short_description.id: Hag adalah sosok perempuan tua keriput dalam cerita rakyat dan dongeng yang berwujud peri, penyihir, atau penjelmaan dewi.
short_description.en: A hag is a wizened old woman in folklore and tales, appearing as a fairy, witch, or manifestation of a goddess.

long_description.id: Hag digambarkan sebagai perempuan tua berkerut atau makhluk serupa peri dan penyihir dalam cerita rakyat serta dongeng seperti Hansel and Gretel. Sosok ini kerap dipandang jahat, namun juga menjadi wujud pilihan dewi pengubah wujud seperti The Morrígan atau Badb.
long_description.en: A hag is portrayed as a wizened old woman or a type of fairy or witch in folklore and tales such as Hansel and Gretel. While often seen as malevolent, hags also serve as forms for shapeshifting deities such as The Morrígan or Badb.

long_description.id: Istilah ini berasal dari bahasa Middle English sebagai kependekan dari hægtesse dalam Old English yang berarti penyihir, seakar dengan heks dalam bahasa Dutch dan Hexe dalam German dari Proto-Germanic *hagatusjon-. Kata hag juga digunakan bersinonim dengan kata witch.
long_description.en: The term stems from Middle English as a shortening of Old English hægtesse, cognate with Dutch heks and German Hexe from Proto-Germanic *hagatusjon-. The word hag can also be synonymous for a witch.

short_description.id: Amaterasu adalah dewi matahari utama dalam Shinto, penguasa Takama no Hara, dan leluhur ilahi keluarga kekaisaran Japan.
short_description.en: Amaterasu is the chief sun goddess of Shinto, ruler of Takama no Hara, and divine ancestor of Japan's imperial family.

long_description.id: Amaterasu Omikami berarti 'dewa agung yang menerangi langit'. Kisah kelahirannya menempatkannya muncul dari mata kiri Izanagi, dan ia adalah kakak Susanoo sang dewa badai. Ia memerintah dataran langit Takama no Hara.
long_description.en: Amaterasu Omikami means 'great divinity illuminating heaven'. In one birth story she emerges from Izanagi's left eye, and she is the elder sister of the storm god Susanoo. She rules the celestial plain Takama no Hara.

long_description.id: Dalam cerita gua, tindakan Susanoo membuat Amaterasu bersembunyi sehingga dunia gelap. Para dewa menyiapkan cermin dan perhiasan pada pohon sakaki; Uzume menari hingga mereka tertawa. Tajikarao lalu menarik Amaterasu keluar dan terang kembali.
long_description.en: In the cave story, Susanoo's actions cause Amaterasu to hide, leaving the world dark. The gods set a mirror and jewels on a sakaki tree; Uzume dances and they laugh. Tajikarao then pulls Amaterasu out and light returns.

long_description.id: Amaterasu memberi Ninigi tiga benda yang kemudian menjadi lambang kekaisaran Japan. Situs resmi Ise Jingu menyebut Amaterasu sebagai kami leluhur keluarga kekaisaran dan menyatakan cermin suci ditempatkan di Naiku. Lebih dari 1.500 ritual diadakan setiap tahun di kompleks itu.
long_description.en: Amaterasu gives Ninigi three objects that become Japan's imperial regalia. The Ise Jingu shrine describes Amaterasu as the imperial family's ancestral kami and says her sacred mirror is housed at Naiku. More than 1,500 rituals take place at the shrine complex each year.

long_description.id: Amaterasu (bahasa Jepang: 天照, Amaterasu-ōmikami; 天照大御神, atau Ōhiru-menomuchi-no-kami; 大日孁貴神) dalam mitologi Jepang adalah dewi matahari yang menerangi seluruh jagat raya. Karena tugasnya ini, Amaterasu merupakan dewi (神; kami) yang penting dalam kepercayaan Shinto; para kaisar Jepang dikatakan memiliki garis keturunan dari Amaterasu.
long_description.en: Amaterasu Ōmikami (天照大（御）神; Japanese pronunciation: [ä́.mä̀.tè̞.ɾä̀.sɨ̀ | ò̞ó̞.mʲí.kä̀.mʲì, ó̞ó̞.-]), often called Amaterasu ([ä́.mä̀.tè̞.ɾä̀.sɨ̀]) for short, also known as Amateru Kami (天照神) and Ōhirume no Muchi (大日孁貴), is the goddess of the sun in Japanese mythology. Often considered the chief deity (kami) of the Shinto pantheon, she is also portrayed in Japan's earliest literary texts, the Kojiki (c. 712 CE) and the Nihon Shoki (720 CE), as the ruler (or one of the rulers) of the heavenly realm Takamagahara and as the mythical ancestress of the Imperial House of Japan via her grandson Ninigi. Along with two of her siblings (the moon deity Tsukuyomi and the impetuous storm-god Susanoo) she ranks as one of the "Three Precious Children" (三貴子, mihashira no uzu no miko / sankishi), the three most important offspring of the creator god Izanagi. Amaterasu's chief place of worship, the Grand Shrine of Ise in Ise, Mie Prefecture, is one of Shinto's holiest sites and a major pilgrimage center and tourist spot. As with other Shinto kami, she is also enshrined in a number of Shinto shrines throughout Japan.

short_description.id: Amaterasu adalah dewi matahari utama dalam Shinto, penguasa Takama no Hara, dan leluhur ilahi keluarga kekaisaran Japan.
short_description.en: Amaterasu is the chief sun goddess of Shinto, ruler of Takama no Hara, and divine ancestor of Japan's imperial family.

long_description.id: Amaterasu Omikami berarti 'dewa agung yang menerangi langit'. Kisah kelahirannya menempatkannya muncul dari mata kiri Izanagi, dan ia adalah kakak Susanoo sang dewa badai. Ia memerintah dataran langit Takama no Hara.
long_description.en: Amaterasu Omikami means 'great divinity illuminating heaven'. In one birth story she emerges from Izanagi's left eye, and she is the elder sister of the storm god Susanoo. She rules the celestial plain Takama no Hara.

long_description.id: Dalam cerita gua, tindakan Susanoo membuat Amaterasu bersembunyi sehingga dunia gelap. Para dewa menyiapkan cermin dan perhiasan pada pohon sakaki; Uzume menari hingga mereka tertawa. Tajikarao lalu menarik Amaterasu keluar dan terang kembali.
long_description.en: In the cave story, Susanoo's actions cause Amaterasu to hide, leaving the world dark. The gods set a mirror and jewels on a sakaki tree; Uzume dances and they laugh. Tajikarao then pulls Amaterasu out and light returns.

long_description.id: Amaterasu memberi Ninigi tiga benda yang kemudian menjadi lambang kekaisaran Japan. Situs resmi Ise Jingu menyebut Amaterasu sebagai kami leluhur keluarga kekaisaran dan menyatakan cermin suci ditempatkan di Naiku. Lebih dari 1.500 ritual diadakan setiap tahun di kompleks itu.
long_description.en: Amaterasu gives Ninigi three objects that become Japan's imperial regalia. The Ise Jingu shrine describes Amaterasu as the imperial family's ancestral kami and says her sacred mirror is housed at Naiku. More than 1,500 rituals take place at the shrine complex each year.

long_description.id: Amaterasu (bahasa Jepang: 天照, Amaterasu-ōmikami; 天照大御神, atau Ōhiru-menomuchi-no-kami; 大日孁貴神) dalam mitologi Jepang adalah dewi matahari yang menerangi seluruh jagat raya. Karena tugasnya ini, Amaterasu merupakan dewi (神; kami) yang penting dalam kepercayaan Shinto; para kaisar Jepang dikatakan memiliki garis keturunan dari Amaterasu.
long_description.en: Amaterasu Ōmikami (天照大（御）神; Japanese pronunciation: [ä́.mä̀.tè̞.ɾä̀.sɨ̀ | ò̞ó̞.mʲí.kä̀.mʲì, ó̞ó̞.-]), often called Amaterasu ([ä́.mä̀.tè̞.ɾä̀.sɨ̀]) for short, also known as Amateru Kami (天照神) and Ōhirume no Muchi (大日孁貴), is the goddess of the sun in Japanese mythology. Often considered the chief deity (kami) of the Shinto pantheon, she is also portrayed in Japan's earliest literary texts, the Kojiki (c. 712 CE) and the Nihon Shoki (720 CE), as the ruler (or one of the rulers) of the heavenly realm Takamagahara and as the mythical ancestress of the Imperial House of Japan via her grandson Ninigi. Along with two of her siblings (the moon deity Tsukuyomi and the impetuous storm-god Susanoo) she ranks as one of the "Three Precious Children" (三貴子, mihashira no uzu no miko / sankishi), the three most important offspring of the creator god Izanagi. Amaterasu's chief place of worship, the Grand Shrine of Ise in Ise, Mie Prefecture, is one of Shinto's holiest sites and a major pilgrimage center and tourist spot. As with other Shinto kami, she is also enshrined in a number of Shinto shrines throughout Japan.

removed_artwork.prompt: Use case: historical-scene. One square detailed painterly naturalistic encyclopedia illustration of Amaterasu Omikami, revered Japanese Shinto sun goddess. Depict ONE adult Japanese female deity emerging from the mouth of a rocky heavenly cave; her whole figure is comfortably visible, dressed in dignified layered traditional flowing Japanese robes, with long dark hair and calm authoritative expression. Bright sacred golden sunlight radiates from her, transforming the dark cave entrance to luminous heaven. Beside the entrance place a green sakaki tree decorated with a round sacred mirror, comma-shaped magatama jewels and strips of white cloth, as in the documented cave legend. Those objects belong to the tree, not extra body limbs. Mood: divine majesty, benevolent awe, sacred reverence, radiant celestial presence. Naturalistic rich painted textures and restrained Japanese historical visual language, no anime. This is an interpretive depiction of the documented emergence scene; avoid fabricated weapons, armor, horns, wings or extra arms. One goddess only, no other characters, no text or watermark. Square composition with margins and clear central silhouette.

long_description.id: Amaterasu (bahasa Jepang: 天照, Amaterasu-ōmikami; 天照大御神, atau Ōhiru-menomuchi-no-kami; 大日孁貴神) dalam mitologi Jepang adalah dewi matahari yang menerangi seluruh jagat raya. Karena tugasnya ini, Amaterasu merupakan dewi (神; kami) yang penting dalam kepercayaan Shinto; para kaisar Jepang dikatakan memiliki garis keturunan dari Amaterasu.
long_description.en: Amaterasu Ōmikami (天照大（御）神; Japanese pronunciation: [ä́.mä̀.tè̞.ɾä̀.sɨ̀ | ò̞ó̞.mʲí.kä̀.mʲì, ó̞ó̞.-]), often called Amaterasu ([ä́.mä̀.tè̞.ɾä̀.sɨ̀]) for short, also known as Amateru Kami (天照神) and Ōhirume no Muchi (大日孁貴), is the goddess of the sun in Japanese mythology. Often considered the chief deity (kami) of the Shinto pantheon, she is also portrayed in Japan's earliest literary texts, the Kojiki (c. 712 CE) and the Nihon Shoki (720 CE), as the ruler (or one of the rulers) of the heavenly realm Takamagahara and as the mythical ancestress of the Imperial House of Japan via her grandson Ninigi. Along with two of her siblings (the moon deity Tsukuyomi and the impetuous storm-god Susanoo) she ranks as one of the "Three Precious Children" (三貴子, mihashira no uzu no miko / sankishi), the three most important offspring of the creator god Izanagi. Amaterasu's chief place of worship, the Grand Shrine of Ise in Ise, Mie Prefecture, is one of Shinto's holiest sites and a major pilgrimage center and tourist spot. As with other Shinto kami, she is also enshrined in a number of Shinto shrines throughout Japan.

removed_artwork.prompt: Use case: historical-scene. One square detailed painterly naturalistic encyclopedia illustration of Amaterasu Omikami, revered Japanese Shinto sun goddess. Depict ONE adult Japanese female deity emerging from the mouth of a rocky heavenly cave; her whole figure is comfortably visible, dressed in dignified layered traditional flowing Japanese robes, with long dark hair and calm authoritative expression. Bright sacred golden sunlight radiates from her, transforming the dark cave entrance to luminous heaven. Beside the entrance place a green sakaki tree decorated with a round sacred mirror, comma-shaped magatama jewels and strips of white cloth, as in the documented cave legend. Those objects belong to the tree, not extra body limbs. Mood: divine majesty, benevolent awe, sacred reverence, radiant celestial presence. Naturalistic rich painted textures and restrained Japanese historical visual language, no anime. This is an interpretive depiction of the documented emergence scene; avoid fabricated weapons, armor, horns, wings or extra arms. One goddess only, no other characters, no text or watermark. Square composition with margins and clear central silhouette.

short_description.id: Amaterasu adalah dewi matahari utama dalam Shinto, penguasa Takama no Hara, dan leluhur ilahi keluarga kekaisaran Japan.
short_description.en: Amaterasu is the chief sun goddess of Shinto, ruler of Takama no Hara, and divine ancestor of Japan's imperial family.

long_description.id: Amaterasu Omikami berarti 'dewa agung yang menerangi langit'. Kisah kelahirannya menempatkannya muncul dari mata kiri Izanagi, dan ia adalah kakak Susanoo sang dewa badai. Ia memerintah dataran langit Takama no Hara.
long_description.en: Amaterasu Omikami means 'great divinity illuminating heaven'. In one birth story she emerges from Izanagi's left eye, and she is the elder sister of the storm god Susanoo. She rules the celestial plain Takama no Hara.

long_description.id: Dalam cerita gua, tindakan Susanoo membuat Amaterasu bersembunyi sehingga dunia gelap. Para dewa menyiapkan cermin dan perhiasan pada pohon sakaki; Uzume menari hingga mereka tertawa. Tajikarao lalu menarik Amaterasu keluar dan terang kembali.
long_description.en: In the cave story, Susanoo's actions cause Amaterasu to hide, leaving the world dark. The gods set a mirror and jewels on a sakaki tree; Uzume dances and they laugh. Tajikarao then pulls Amaterasu out and light returns.

long_description.id: Amaterasu memberi Ninigi tiga benda yang kemudian menjadi lambang kekaisaran Japan. Situs resmi Ise Jingu menyebut Amaterasu sebagai kami leluhur keluarga kekaisaran dan menyatakan cermin suci ditempatkan di Naiku. Lebih dari 1.500 ritual diadakan setiap tahun di kompleks itu.
long_description.en: Amaterasu gives Ninigi three objects that become Japan's imperial regalia. The Ise Jingu shrine describes Amaterasu as the imperial family's ancestral kami and says her sacred mirror is housed at Naiku. More than 1,500 rituals take place at the shrine complex each year.

Often considered the chief deity (kami) of the Shinto pantheon, she is also portrayed in Japan's earliest literary texts, the Kojiki (c. 712 CE) and the Nihon Shoki (720 CE), as the ruler (or one of the rulers) of the heavenly realm Takamagahara and as the mythical ancestress of the Imperial House of Japan via her grandson Ninigi. Along with two of her siblings (the moon deity Tsukuyomi and the impetuous storm-god Susanoo) she ranks as one of the "Three Precious Children" (三貴子, mihashira no uzu no miko / sankishi), the three most important offspring of the creator god Izanagi. Amaterasu's chief place of worship, the Grand Shrine of Ise in Ise, Mie Prefecture, is one of Shinto's holiest sites and a major pilgrimage center and tourist spot. As with other Shinto kami, she is also enshrined in a number of Shinto shrines throughout Japan.

long_description.id: Benzaiten berasal dari Sarasvatī, dewi air India. Di Jepang ia dikenal sebagai pelindung musik dan kefasihan, serta termasuk dalam tujuh dewa keberuntungan. Ia juga masuk ke dalam tradisi Shinto dan Buddha. Pada masa Muromachi, kelompok tujuh dewa keberuntungan mulai dikenal di Jepang.
long_description.en: Benzaiten derives from Sarasvatī, an Indian water goddess. In Japan she is a patron of music and eloquence and is counted among the Seven Gods of Good Fortune. She was also adopted into Shinto and Buddhist traditions. The grouping of seven fortune deities emerged in Japan during the Muromachi period.

long_description.id: Pemujaan Benzaiten mengambil bentuk khas di Jepang. Ia berpadu dengan Ugajin menjadi Uga Benten; penggambaran ini dapat memiliki delapan lengan dan ular putih berkepala manusia di atas kepalanya. Bentuk itu berbeda dari gambaran Benzaiten dalam sutra lain. Pemujaan Uga Benzaiten menyebar dari Chikubujima ke tempat seperti Itsukushima, Enoshima, dan Tenkawa.
long_description.en: Worship of Benzaiten developed distinctive forms in Japan. She merged with Ugajin as Uga Benten, a form portrayed with eight arms and a white snake with a human face on her head. This differs from other sutra depictions of Benzaiten. Worship of Uga Benzaiten spread from Chikubujima to places including Itsukushima, Enoshima, and Tenkawa.

long_description.id: Benzaiten (弁才天, 弁財天, juga disebut Benten) adalah nama Jepang untuk Dewi Saraswati dalam kepercayaan Hindu. Pemujaan Benzaiten hadir di Jepang selama abad ke-6 hingga ke-8, terutama melalui penerjemahan Sutra Cahaya Emas dari bahasa Tionghoa, yang ada pembahasan mengenainya. Dia juga disebut dalam Sutra Teratai dan sering digambarkan memegang biwa, semacam kecapi tradisional Jepang, berbeda dengan Saraswati yang memegang alat musik petik yang dikenal sebagai veena. Benzaiten adalah entitas yang sinkretis dengan ajaran Buddha maupun Shinto.
long_description.en: Benzaiten (弁才天／弁財天; Japanese pronunciation: [ben.(d)zaꜜi.teɴ]), or simply Benten, is an East Asian Buddhist dharmapāla (wrathful goddess) who is similar in the Hindu goddess Saraswati, the patroness of speech, the arts, and learning. Worship of Benzaiten arrived in Japan during the sixth to eighth centuries, mainly via Classical Chinese translations of the Golden Light Sutra (Sanskrit: Suvarṇaprabhāsa Sūtra), which has a section devoted to her. Benzaiten was also syncretized with Japanese kami and adopted into the Shinto religion, with several Shinto shrines dedicated to her. As such, she is now also associated with dragons, snakes, many local deities, wealth, fortune, protection from disease and danger, and the protection of the state.

short_description.id: Yama-uba adalah yōkai perempuan pegunungan Jepang yang dalam kisah dapat menakutkan atau menolong manusia.
short_description.en: Yama-uba is a Japanese mountain woman yōkai who may frighten or help people in different stories.

long_description.id: Yama-uba, juga disebut yamamba, adalah yōkai perempuan dalam kisah Jepang yang tinggal di pegunungan. Ia dapat muncul sebagai perempuan tua atau muda yang menawarkan tempat bermalam kepada pelancong, lalu memperlihatkan wujud mengerikannya. Kisah lain menggambarkannya memangsa pedagang yang melintasi jalur gunung. Namun, tidak semua kisah menempatkannya sebagai ancaman: ada pula yama-uba yang memberi keberuntungan kepada orang yang memperlakukannya dengan baik.
long_description.en: Yama-uba, also called yamamba, is a female yōkai of Japanese mountain stories. She may appear as an old or young woman who offers a traveler shelter, then reveals a frightening form. Other tales describe her preying on merchants crossing mountain routes. Yet some stories instead say that she rewards people who treat her kindly.

long_description.id: Sisi keibuan tokoh itu tampak dalam legenda Kintarō. Sebuah lukisan karya Nagasawa Rosetsu memperlihatkan yama-uba dan anak angkatnya Kintarō, yang menurut cerita dibesarkan di Gunung Hakone dan memiliki tenaga luar biasa. Lukisan itu disumbangkan ke Kuil Itsukushima pada 1797. Yama-uba juga hadir dalam drama Noh dan seni lukis, kadang dengan rambut terurai dan pakaian compang-camping, kadang digambarkan sebagai perempuan cantik. Berbagai rupa ini memperlihatkan tokoh yang berubah menurut medium dan kisahnya.
long_description.en: The maternal side of the figure appears in Kintarō’s legend. A painting by Nagasawa Rosetsu shows yama-uba with her adopted child Kintarō, whom a tale says she raised on Mount Hakone and who possessed extraordinary strength. The painting was donated to Itsukushima Shrine in 1797. Yama-uba also appears in Noh drama and painting, sometimes with disheveled hair and ragged clothes, sometimes as a beauty. Her appearance varies with the story and medium.

long_description.id: Yamauba (山姥, nenek gunung) atau dibaca Yamamba adalah wanita tua golongan yōkai yang hidup di tengah hutan di gunung dalam legenda dan cerita rakyat Jepang. Ia digambarkan bertubuh tinggi, rambutnya panjang beruban semua, sudut luar mata tertarik ke atas, dan mulutnya lebar hingga ke telinga. Nama lain untuknya adalah onibaba (鬼婆, nenek oni) dan kijo (鬼女). Menjelma sebagai wanita berparas cantik, yamauba akan menawarkan tempat menginap kepada pelancong atau yang kemalaman di tengah gunung. Orang itu juga akan ditawari makan dan minum. long_description.en: Yamauba (山姥, 山うば, or 山女郎), yamamba, and yamanba are variations on the name of a yōkai found in Japanese folklore. Mostly said to resemble women, yamauba may be depicted as predatory monsters or benevolent beings.

long_description.en: In a broad sense, Goryō (御霊; Japanese: [ɡoɾʲoː]) is an honorific for a spirit, especially one that causes hauntings, and the term is used as a synonym for onryō (怨霊, vengeful Japanese ghosts). In a narrower sense, it refers to a noble or accomplished person who lost a political power struggle or died prematurely from an epidemic or other disease, becoming an onryō that brings pestilence or famine and is later enshrined as a kami in Shinto shrines. For example, the "Sandai Jitsuroku" (a historical Japanese document) mentions that six Shinto shrines were dedicated to the worship of goryō, which were the spirits of those who died from non-natural causes. Later on, two more shrines were added, bringing the total to eight. Goryō Shinko (御霊信仰, Belief in goryō) refers to the belief that the onryō of people who have died unfortunate deaths cause hauntings and disasters, and the belief that they are enshrined as kami to appease them.

long_description.id: Noderabō (bahasa Jepang Kanji: 野寺坊, Hiragana: のでらぼう - pendeta kuil terpencil) adalah yokai berwujud pendeta dalam cerita rakyat Jepang. Ia muncul di malam hari, di kuil-kuil yang telah lama ditinggalkan, atau di reruntuhan kuil. Menurut legenda, noderabo dahulu merupakan pendeta yang melakukan kejahatan dan meninggal dengan cara yang tidak wajar. Ia kemudian berubah menjadi yokai yang menghantui kuil-kuil di pedesaan. Toriyama Sekien menggambarkan Noderabo sebagai biarawan dengan pakaian lusuh, kotor, dan tak terawat, yang berdiri di samping lonceng besar, yang mana lonceng tersebut merujuk pada lonceng milik Kuil Nodera yang telah lama hilang.
long_description.en: The noderabō is a Japanese yōkai from Toriyama Sekien's Gazu Hyakki Yagyō and is thought to be a yōkai that appears at abandoned temples. The Gazu Hyakki Yagyō depicts a yōkai that looks like a monk wearing a tattered kasa standing next to a temple bell, but there is no explanation from Sekien about what this is about, so it is not known what characteristics this yōkai was intended to have. Beginning in the Shōwa period, literature about yōkai often explained that they are a yōkai that appear at deserted dilapidated temples or that they are resulting the grudges turned yōkai of a chief priest whose temple became dilapidated from lack of donations from villagers, which would then appear at evenings at the dilapidated temple and ring the bell alone at the deserted temple.

long_description.en: Arikura-no-baba (蟻鞍の婆, ant-saddle hag) is a character from the folklore of Gifu Prefecture, Japan. She was an old woman with supernatural powers who lived in Takayama. She used a prayer to stop the eruption of a mountain after it had been rumbling for seven days, and turned the hot water of an onsen cold by throwing a horse's hoof into it.

short_description.en: Apsaras are a class of celestial female beings in Hindu and Buddhist traditions.

long_description.id: Apsara adalah kelompok makhluk perempuan surgawi dalam tradisi Hindu dan Buddha. Mereka dikenal sebagai penari istana Indra.
long_description.en: Apsaras are a class of celestial female beings in Hindu and Buddhist traditions. They are known as dancers at Indra's court.

long_description.id: Gandharva berhubungan dengan mereka sebagai musisi dan pasangan. Sebagian kisah memberi mereka kemampuan mengubah wujud. Indra mengirim apsara menggoda resi yang bertapa dalam sejumlah cerita. Urvashi, Menaka, Rambha, Tilottama, dan Ghritachi termasuk apsara yang dikenal. Di Jepang, nama Tennin dan Tennyo digunakan untuk sosok terkait apsara. Etimologi Monier-Williams menghubungkan namanya dengan bergerak di air atau di antara air awan. Uraian awal membandingkan apsara dengan nimfa air. Rigveda memuat dialog Urvashi dengan kekasih manusia Pururavas. Kaushitaki Upanishad mengaitkan apsara dengan minyak wangi, rangkaian bunga, pakaian, dan wewangian bubuk. Ramayana dan Purana menghubungkan asal apsara dengan pengadukan lautan. Mahabharata menuturkan Tilottama menyelamatkan dunia dari Sunda dan Upasunda. Mackenzie menuturkan apsara menari ketika Gandharva memainkan alat musik ilahi.
long_description.en: Gandharvas are associated with them as musicians and partners. Some accounts give them the ability to change shape. Indra sends apsaras to tempt ascetic sages in several stories. Urvashi, Menaka, Rambha, Tilottama, and Ghritachi are among the known apsaras. In Japan, the names Tennin and Tennyo are used for figures associated with apsaras. Monier Williams's etymology connects the name with moving in water or among cloud waters. Early descriptions compare apsaras to water nymphs. The Rigveda contains Urvashi's dialogue with her mortal lover Pururavas. The Kaushitaki Upanishad associates apsaras with ointments, garlands, clothes, and powdered aromatics. The Ramayana and Puranas connect the origin of apsaras with the churning of the ocean. The Mahabharata recounts Tilottama saving the world from Sunda and Upasunda. Mackenzie recounts apsaras dancing when Gandharvas play divine instruments.

long_description.id: Bidadari (Dewanagari: विध्यधरी; ,IAST: Vidhyadharī,; juga disebut dengan istilah apsara atau apsari) menurut kepercayaan Hindu, adalah makhluk gaib berwujud manusia berjenis kelamin wanita yang tinggal di kahyangan (surga) dan menjadi istri para gandarwa. Kepercayaan tersebut juga tersebar di kawasan yang mendapatkan pengaruh Hindu, antara lain Asia Selatan dan Tenggara. Tugas dan fungsi mereka, menurut agama Hindu, adalah menjadi penyampai pesan para dewa kepada manusia, sebagaimana para malaikat dalam kepercayaan Semit. Adakalanya mereka diutus untuk menguji sejauh mana ketekunan seseorang (pria) dalam bertapa, dengan cara mencoba membangunkan para petapa dari tapa mereka. Para bidadari memanfaatkan kecantikan fisik mereka untuk menguji para petapa.
long_description.en: Apsaras (Sanskrit: अप्सरस्, IAST: Apsaras, Khmer: អប្សរា, Pali: अच्छरा, romanized: Accharā, Thai: อัปสร) are a class of celestial beings in Hindu and Buddhist culture. They were originally a type of female spirit associated with clouds and water, but, later came to play the role of a "nymph" or "fairy". They figure prominently in the sculpture, dance, literature and paintings of many South Asian and Southeast Asian cultures. The apsaras are described as being beautiful, youthful and elegant, and are said to be able to change their shape at will; making anyone fall for their beauty. There are two types of apsaras—laukika (worldly) and daivika (divine). They are said to excel at dancing, and are often considered the wives of the gandharvas, the court musicians of Indra. The apsaras reside in the palaces of the gods and entertain them by dancing to the music of the Gandharvas. The 26 apsaras of Indra's court are each said to symbolise a different facet of the performing arts, drawing comparisons to the Muses of Ancient Greece. They are also renowned for seducing rishis in order to prevent them from attaining divine powers. Famous apsaras include Urvashi, Menaka, Rambha, Tilottama and Ghritachi. In Japan, Apsara are known as "Tennin" (天人); "Tennyo" (天女) for "female Tennin" and "Tennan" (天男) for "male Tennin".

long_description.id: Bidadari (Dewanagari: विध्यधरी; ,IAST: Vidhyadharī,; juga disebut dengan istilah apsara atau apsari) menurut kepercayaan Hindu, adalah makhluk gaib berwujud manusia berjenis kelamin wanita yang tinggal di kahyangan (surga) dan menjadi istri para gandarwa. Kepercayaan tersebut juga tersebar di kawasan yang mendapatkan pengaruh Hindu, antara lain Asia Selatan dan Tenggara. Tugas dan fungsi mereka, menurut agama Hindu, adalah menjadi penyampai pesan para dewa kepada manusia, sebagaimana para malaikat dalam kepercayaan Semit. Adakalanya mereka diutus untuk menguji sejauh mana ketekunan seseorang (pria) dalam bertapa, dengan cara mencoba membangunkan para petapa dari tapa mereka. Para bidadari memanfaatkan kecantikan fisik mereka untuk menguji para petapa.
long_description.en: Apsaras (Sanskrit: अप्सरस्, IAST: Apsaras, Khmer: អប្សរា, Pali: अच्छरा, romanized: Accharā, Thai: อัปสร) are a class of celestial beings in Hindu and Buddhist culture. They were originally a type of female spirit associated with clouds and water, but, later came to play the role of a "nymph" or "fairy". They figure prominently in the sculpture, dance, literature and paintings of many South Asian and Southeast Asian cultures. The apsaras are described as being beautiful, youthful and elegant, and are said to be able to change their shape at will; making anyone fall for their beauty. There are two types of apsaras—laukika (worldly) and daivika (divine). They are said to excel at dancing, and are often considered the wives of the gandharvas, the court musicians of Indra. The apsaras reside in the palaces of the gods and entertain them by dancing to the music of the Gandharvas. The 26 apsaras of Indra's court are each said to symbolise a different facet of the performing arts, drawing comparisons to the Muses of Ancient Greece. They are also renowned for seducing rishis in order to prevent them from attaining divine powers. Famous apsaras include Urvashi, Menaka, Rambha, Tilottama and Ghritachi. In Japan, Apsara are known as "Tennin" (天人); "Tennyo" (天女) for "female Tennin" and "Tennan" (天男) for "male Tennin".

long_description.id: Bidadari (Dewanagari: विध्यधरी; ,IAST: Vidhyadharī,; juga disebut dengan istilah apsara atau apsari) menurut kepercayaan Hindu, adalah makhluk gaib berwujud manusia berjenis kelamin wanita yang tinggal di kahyangan (surga) dan menjadi istri para gandarwa. Kepercayaan tersebut juga tersebar di kawasan yang mendapatkan pengaruh Hindu, antara lain Asia Selatan dan Tenggara. Tugas dan fungsi mereka, menurut agama Hindu, adalah menjadi penyampai pesan para dewa kepada manusia, sebagaimana para malaikat dalam kepercayaan Semit. Adakalanya mereka diutus untuk menguji sejauh mana ketekunan seseorang (pria) dalam bertapa, dengan cara mencoba membangunkan para petapa dari tapa mereka. Para bidadari memanfaatkan kecantikan fisik mereka untuk menguji para petapa.
long_description.en: Apsaras (Sanskrit: अप्सरस्, IAST: Apsaras, Khmer: អប្សរា, Pali: अच्छरा, romanized: Accharā, Thai: อัปสร) are a class of celestial beings in Hindu and Buddhist culture. They were originally a type of female spirit associated with clouds and water, but, later came to play the role of a "nymph" or "fairy". They figure prominently in the sculpture, dance, literature and paintings of many South Asian and Southeast Asian cultures. The apsaras are described as being beautiful, youthful and elegant, and are said to be able to change their shape at will; making anyone fall for their beauty. There are two types of apsaras—laukika (worldly) and daivika (divine). They are said to excel at dancing, and are often considered the wives of the gandharvas, the court musicians of Indra. The apsaras reside in the palaces of the gods and entertain them by dancing to the music of the Gandharvas. The 26 apsaras of Indra's court are each said to symbolise a different facet of the performing arts, drawing comparisons to the Muses of Ancient Greece. They are also renowned for seducing rishis in order to prevent them from attaining divine powers. Famous apsaras include Urvashi, Menaka, Rambha, Tilottama and Ghritachi. In Japan, Apsara are known as "Tennin" (天人); "Tennyo" (天女) for "female Tennin" and "Tennan" (天男) for "male Tennin".

long_description.id: Dakini (Dewanagari: डाकिनी; ,IAST: ḍākinī, डाकिनी) adalah sejenis makhluk gaib dalam kepercayaan Hindu dan Buddha. Konsep tentang Dakini berbeda-beda tergantung konteks dan juga tradisi. Sebagai contoh, dalam kitab-kitab Hindu Kuno dan juga naskah Buddhis Tionghoa, istilah tersebut merujuk kepada golongan setan betina yang memangsa daging dan/atau bagian vital manusia. Dalam sastra Tantra Hindu, Dakini adalah nama seorang dewi yang sering dikaitkan dengan salah satu dari enam cakra atau tujuh unsur penting (dhatu) pada tubuh manusia. Dalam kepercayaan Buddhisme di Nepal dan Tibet, dakini dapat mengacu kepada sosok feminin dengan energi tercerahkan berwujud mengerikan, atau wanita yang telah mencapai beberapa tingkatan spiritual, yang kedua-duanya dapat memicu cara-cara Tantra dalam mencapai pencerahan.
long_description.en: A dakini is a type of goddess in Hinduism and Buddhism. The concept of the dakini somewhat differs depending on the context and the tradition. For example, in earlier Hindu texts and East Asian esoteric Buddhism, the term denotes a race of demonesses who ate the flesh and vital essence of humans. In Hindu Tantric literature, Ḍākinī is the name of a goddess often associated with one of the six chakras or the seven fundamental elements (dhātu) of the human body. Meanwhile, in Nepalese and Tibetan Buddhism, dakini (or wisdom dakini) can refer to both what can be best described as fierce-looking female embodiments of enlightened energy, and to human women with a certain amount of spiritual development, both of whom can help Tantric initiates in attaining enlightenment. In Japan, the ḍākinīs – held in the East Asian Buddhist tradition to have been subjugated and converted to Buddhism by the buddha Vairocana under the guise of the god Mahākāla (Daikokuten in Japanese) – were eventually coalesced into a single deity called Dakiniten, who, after becoming syncretized with the native agricultural deity Inari, became linked to the fox (kitsune) iconography associated with the latter.

short_description.id: Ysbaddaden Bencawr ("Ysbaddaden, Kepala Para Raksasa") adalah raksasa kejam dan tokoh antagonis utama roman Wales Culhwch and Olwen, ayah Olwen.
short_description.en: Ysbaddaden Bencawr ('Ysbaddaden, Chief of Giants') is the vicious giant and main antagonist of the Welsh romance Culhwch and Olwen, father of Olwen.

long_description.id: Ysbaddaden Bencawr, "Ysbaddaden, Kepala Para Raksasa" (dari akar kata yang berarti "hawthorn" atau "mandul", atau mungkin keduanya), adalah antagonis utama roman Wales (Welsh) Culhwch and Olwen. Ia raksasa kejam yang tinggal di kastel yang hampir tak terjangkau, ayah Olwen dan paman Goreu fab Custennin. Ibu tiri Culhwch mengutuknya agar hanya dapat menikahi Olwen, putri Ysbaddaden, sehingga Culhwch mencari bantuan sepupunya Arthur. Ysbaddaden telah merampas tanah saudaranya, gembala Custennin, dan membunuh dua puluh tiga anaknya karena kekejaman.
long_description.en: Known as Ysbaddaden Bencawr, 'Chief of Giants', a name whose roots may mean 'hawthorn', 'infertile' or both, he is the chief villain of the Welsh romance Culhwch and Olwen. A cruel giant in a castle almost impossible to reach, he is Olwen's father and uncle of Goreu fab Custennin. Culhwch's stepmother curses him to wed no one but Olwen, Ysbaddaden's daughter, so Culhwch seeks help from his cousin Arthur. Ysbaddaden had seized the lands of his brother, the shepherd Custennin, and out of cruelty killed twenty-three of his children.

long_description.id: Ketika Culhwch dan kawan-kawannya memasuki aulanya, Ysbaddaden mencoba membunuh Culhwch dengan anak panah beracun tetapi dikalahkan dan dilukai oleh Bedwyr, penyihir Menw, dan Culhwch sendiri. Akhirnya ia setuju menyerahkan putrinya dengan syarat Culhwch menyelesaikan sejumlah tugas mustahil (anoethau), termasuk memburu Twrch Trwyth. Menurut artikel de, kelopak matanya begitu berat sehingga seorang pelayan harus mengangkatnya dengan garpu bila ia ingin melihat seseorang (bandingkan Balor), dan kastelnya bergerbang sembilan.
long_description.en: When Culhwch and his companions enter his hall, Ysbaddaden tries to kill Culhwch with a poisoned dart but is outwitted and wounded by Bedwyr, the enchanter Menw and Culhwch himself. At last he agrees to give up his daughter if Culhwch completes a series of impossible tasks (anoethau), among them hunting Twrch Trwyth. According to the de article his eyelids are so heavy that a servant must lift them with a fork when he wants to look at someone (compare Balor), and his castle has nine gates.

long_description.id: Nefilim (bahasa Inggris: Nephilim; bahasa Ibrani: נְפִילִים‎, ne-fi-lim, bentuk tunggal נָפִיל, Nafíl atau Naphil) adalah orang-orang yang dilahirkan dari hasil perkawinan ketika "Para Fallen Angel (Malaikat Pembangkang) menghampiri anak-anak perempuan manusia" sebelum terjadinya Air Bah raksasa menurut catatan Alkitab Ibrani dan Perjanjian Lama di Alkitab Kristen terutama pada Kejadian 6:4. Nama ini juga digunakan untuk merujuk kepada orang-orang raksasa yang menghuni Kanaan pada zaman Musa seperti yang dicatat dalam Bilangan 13:33. Sebuah kata bahasa Ibrani yang serupa dengan penandaan suara huruf hidup yang berbeda dijumpai pada Yehezkiel 32:27 untuk menyebut prajurit-prajurit Filistin yang mati.
long_description.en: The Nephilim (; Hebrew: נְפִילִים, romanized: Nəfīlīm) are enigmatic figures mentioned in several passages of the Hebrew Bible and later Jewish and Christian literature. They are traditionally associated with extraordinary size, strength, or status, though the biblical texts provide only brief and ambiguous descriptions. The earliest reference appears in Genesis 6:1–4, where the Nephilim are linked to the "mighty men of old" and to the marital relations between the "sons of God" and the "daughters of men". Their identity, origin, and role in early biblical history have been the subject of extensive debate among scholars, theologians, and interpreters. The meaning of the term Nephilim is uncertain. Many translations render the word as "giants," influenced by the Septuagint’s use of the Greek term gigantes, though this may reflect later interpretive traditions rather than the original Hebrew sense. Some scholars derive the term from the Hebrew root n-p-l ("to fall"), leading to interpretations such as "fallen ones" or "those who cause others to fall," while others propose meanings related to violence, domination, or social oppression. Because the biblical text does not define the term explicitly, later Jewish and Christian writings played a major role in shaping the modern understanding of the Nephilim. The Nephilim appear again in Numbers 13:33, where ten of the Twelve Spies report encountering formidable inhabitants in Canaan described as descendants of the Nephilim. This passage has contributed to the longstanding association of the Nephilim with great physical stature, though some scholars argue that the spies’ report may reflect exaggeration, fear, or rhetorical emphasis rather than literal description. Interpretations of the Nephilim vary widely across religious and academic traditions. One influential view, preserved in Second Temple literature such as 1 Enoch and Jubilees, identifies the Nephilim as the offspring of rebellious angels (the Watchers) and human women, portraying them as destructive giants whose corruption contributed to the moral decline preceding the flood. Another major interpretation, found in some early Jewish and Christian commentaries, understands the Nephilim as powerful human rulers or warriors, possibly arising from intermarriage between the righteous line of Seth and the unrighteous line of Cain. A third approach views the Nephilim as legendary or symbolic figures reflecting ancient Near Eastern traditions about semi-divine heroes or primordial beings. Outside the canonical Hebrew Bible, related terms or concepts appear in several deuterocanonical books—including Judith 16:6, Sirach 16:7, Baruch 3:26–28, and Wisdom 14:6—and possibly in Ezekiel 32, where scholars debate whether the term refers directly to the Nephilim or to a related class of fallen warriors. These texts contributed to the development of later Jewish and Christian traditions about ancient giants, divine-human unions, and the pre-flood world. In modern scholarship, the Nephilim are studied within the broader context of ancient Near Eastern mythology, comparative linguistics, and the history of biblical interpretation. Parallels have been drawn between the Nephilim and regional traditions involving giant clans, heroic demigods, or semi-divine figures, though the extent of these connections remains debated. The Nephilim have also become prominent in contemporary popular culture, appearing in novels, films, video games, and speculative theories, where they are often reimagined as hybrid beings, ancient superhuman races, or remnants of a lost primordial world.

short_description.id: Bean-nighe ("perempuan pencuci") adalah roh perempuan dalam cerita rakyat Skotlandia, pertanda kematian yang mencuci pakaian orang yang akan meninggal di sungai sepi.
short_description.en: The bean-nighe ('washerwoman') is a female spirit of Scottish folklore, an omen of death who washes the clothes of the soon-to-die in lonely streams.

long_description.id: Bean-nighe (Gaelik Skotlandia/Scottish Gaelic untuk "perempuan pencuci") adalah roh perempuan dalam cerita rakyat Skotlandia (Scottish folklore), dianggap pertanda kematian dan utusan dari Dunia Lain (Otherworld). Ia sejenis ban-sìth (Irlandia/Irish: bean sídhe, dianglisisasi banshee) yang menghantui sungai sepi dan mencuci pakaian orang yang akan meninggal; Les Lavandières adalah sebutan Prancis (French) untuk para pencuci malam ini. Ia juga disebut nigheag, "pencuci kecil", nigheag na h-ath, "pencuci kecil di arungan", dan nigheag bheag a bhroin, "pencuci kecil kesedihan".
long_description.en: The bean-nighe (Scottish Gaelic for 'washerwoman') is a female spirit of Scottish folklore, held to be an omen of death and a messenger of the Otherworld. She is a kind of ban-sìth (Irish bean sídhe, anglicised banshee) haunting lonely streams and washing the clothes of the soon-to-die; Les Lavandières is the French name for these night washerwomen. Other names for her are nigheag ('little washer'), nigheag na h-ath (the little washer at the ford) and nigheag bheag a bhroin (the little washer of sorrow).

long_description.id: Ia terlihat di tempat sepi di tepi sungai atau kolam, mencuci darah dari linen dan kain kubur orang yang akan meninggal; sifatnya berbeda menurut daerah, dan ada yang menyebutnya dapat memberi pengetahuan atau mengabulkan permintaan bila didekati dengan hati-hati. Mnathan-nighe konon arwah perempuan yang meninggal saat melahirkan dan harus bekerja sampai hari ajal mereka semestinya tiba. Di Mull dan Tiree, orang yang mendekatinya dari belakang dan mengaku anak susuannya akan diberi pengetahuan yang diinginkan. Menurut artikel de, ban-sìth dan bean sídhe berasal dari bahasa Irlandia Kuno ben síde, "perempuan peri".
long_description.en: She is seen in lonely spots beside a stream or pool washing blood from the linen and grave-clothes of those about to die; her traits vary by place, and some traditions say she can impart knowledge or grant wishes if approached with care. Mnathan-nighe are said to be spirits of women who died in childbirth, bound to their task until the day they would have died naturally. On Mull and Tiree, one who approaches her from behind and claims to be her foster-child will be told whatever he wishes to know. According to the de article ban-sìth and bean sídhe come from Old Irish ben síde, 'woman of the fairies'.

famous_for.en: Spirits of women who died in childbirth.

short_description.id: Knocker adalah makhluk mitos mirip gnome yang hidup di bawah tanah dalam cerita rakyat Cornwall dan Devon, penghuni tambang yang mengetuk dinding untuk memperingatkan penambang.
short_description.en: The knocker is a mythical gnome-like underground creature of Cornish and Devon folklore, a mine-dweller that knocks on walls to warn miners.

long_description.id: Knocker, Knacker, atau Tommyknocker (AS) adalah makhluk mitos mirip gnome yang hidup di bawah tanah dalam cerita rakyat Cornwall (Cornish) dan Devon. Padanannya di Wales (Welsh) adalah coblyn, dan ia berkerabat dekat dengan leprechaun Irlandia (Irish), kloker dari Kent (Kentish), dan brownie Inggris dan Skotlandia (English and Scottish). Orang Cornwall menggambarkannya bertinggi sekitar 61 cm, berkepala besar tak seimbang, berlengan panjang, berkulit keriput, berjanggut putih, berpakaian penambang mini, dan suka mengusili seperti mencuri perkakas dan makanan penambang.
long_description.en: The Knocker, Knacker or Tommyknocker (US) is a mythical gnome-like underground being of Cornish and Devon folklore. Its Welsh counterpart is the coblyn, and it is close kin to the Irish leprechaun, the Kentish kloker and the English and Scottish brownie. The Cornish picture it about 61 cm tall, with an oversized head, long arms, wrinkled skin and white whiskers, dressed as a tiny miner and given to random mischief such as stealing miners' tools and food left lying about.

long_description.id: Penambang Cornwall percaya knocker kecil menuntun mereka ke urat timah yang kaya, dan kemudian mengetuk dinding tambang untuk memperingatkan runtuhan. Umumnya dianggap baik, mereka juga usil, menyembunyikan perkakas dan memadamkan lilin. Satu tafsiran menganggap mereka arwah orang Yahudi yang bekerja di tambang pada abad ke-11 dan ke-12, tafsiran lain arwah korban tambang; sebagai ungkapan terima kasih penambang melempar gigitan terakhir pasty mereka ke dalam tambang. Pada 1820-an penambang Wales dan Cornwall membawa kisah Tommyknocker ke Pennsylvania dan kemudian ke Colorado, Nevada, dan California. Menurut artikel de, nama mereka berasal dari kebiasaan mengetuk dinding tambang.
long_description.en: Cornish miners believed the little knockers led them to rich tin lodes, and later that they knocked on mine walls to warn of collapse. Mostly thought kindly, they were also pranksters who hid tools and snuffed candles. Some say they are the ghosts of Jewish miners of the 11th and 12th centuries, another the spirits of those killed underground; in thanks miners tossed the last bite of their pasties into the mine. In the 1820s Welsh and Cornish miners carried Tommyknocker tales to Pennsylvania and later to Colorado, Nevada and California. According to the de article their name comes from their habit of knocking on mine walls.

did_you_know.en: Cornish miners tossed the last bite of their pasties into the mine as thanks to the knockers.

long_description.en: Qareen as an accompanying spirit is distinguished from Qarinah, a female childbed demon. According to the article, hadith clearly associates Qareen with spiritual company. Az-Zukhruf 43:36 assigns a devil as companion to someone ignoring remembrance of the All-beneficent; interpretations of that companion differ.

long_description.id: Qarīn (Arab: قرين, Qarīn) adalah istilah yang digunakan untuk menunjuk kepada jin (golongan setan) yang mendampingi setiap manusia. Istilah ini digunakan di dalam Al-Qur'an dan dikatakan bahwa qarin itu mengikuti manusia sejak lahir hingga mengalami ajalnya, makhluk itu dianggap sebagai "kembaran setiap manusia." jin dan manusia. Menurut keyakinan umat Muslim, pada umumnya jin qarin ini bertugas mendorong dampingannya untuk berbuat kejahatan. Dia membisikkan was-was, melalaikan salat, berat ketika hendak membaca Al-Quran dan sebagainya dan ia bekerja sekuat tenaga untuk menghalang dampingannya membuat ibadah dan kebaikan. Untuk mengimbangi adanya pendamping jahat, Allah mengutus malaikat qarin yang selalu membisikkan hal-hal kebenaran dan mengajak membuat kebaikan. Dalam beberapa hadits dikatakan bahwa jin qarin yang mendampingi Nabi Muhammad telah memeluk Islam, sehingga Nabi Muhammad selalu terjaga dari kesalahan. - Dalam Al-Qur'an, qarin terdapat penjelasan dalam Surat Qaf ayat 17, 18, 23 dan 27, dijelaskan manusia dalam hidupnya disertai qarin dari jenis malaikat yaitu 2 malaikat yang senantiasa mencatat seluruh amal perbuatannya (Raqib & Atid), dan 1 lagi qarin dari jenis jin setan untuk menggoda manusia agar tidak taat kepada Allah. Allah Subhanahu Wa Ta'ala berfirman: اِذْ يَتَلَقَّى الْمُتَلَقِّيٰنِ عَنِ الْيَمِيْنِ وَعَنِ الشِّمَا لِ قَعِيْدٌ iz yatalaqqol-mutalaqqiyaani 'anil-yamiini wa 'anisy-syimaali qo'iid "(lngatlah) ketika dua malaikat mencatat (perbuatannya), yang satu duduk di sebelah kanan dan yang lain di sebelah kiri." (QS. Qaf 50: Ayat 17) Allah Subhanahu Wa Ta'ala berfirman: مَا يَلْفِظُ مِنْ قَوْلٍ اِلَّا لَدَيْهِ رَقِيْبٌ عَتِيْدٌ maa yalfizhu ming qoulin illaa ladaihi roqiibun 'atiid "Tidak ada suatu kata yang diucapkannya melainkan ada di sisinya malaikat pengawas yang selalu siap (mencatat)." (QS. Qaf 50: Ayat 18) Allah Subhanahu Wa Ta'ala berfirman: وَقَا لَ قَرِيْـنُهٗ هٰذَا مَا لَدَيَّ عَتِيْدٌ wa qoola qoriinuhuu haazaa maa ladayya 'atiid "Dan (malaikat) yang menyertainya berkata, "Inilah (catatan perbuatan) yang ada padaku."" (QS. Qaf 50: Ayat 23) Allah Subhanahu Wa Ta'ala berfirman: قَا لَ قَرِيْنُهٗ رَبَّنَا مَاۤ اَطْغَيْتُهٗ وَلٰـكِنْ كَا نَ فِيْ ضَلٰلٍۢ بَعِيْدٍ qoola qoriinuhuu robbanaa maaa athghoituhuu wa laaking kaana fii dholaalim ba'iid "(Setan) yang menyertainya berkata (pula), "Ya Tuhan kami, aku tidak menyesatkannya, tetapi dia sendiri yang berada dalam kesesatan yang jauh."" (QS. Qaf 50: Ayat 27) Via Al-Qur'an Indonesia https://quran-id.com
long_description.en: A qareen (Arabic: قرين, romanized: qarīn, lit. 'constant companion') is a spiritual double of a human, either part of the human themself or a complementary creature in a parallel realm. The qareen belongs to the jinn in regards to its ghostly nature, yet distinct from jinn. Although the qareen can be either a devil or an angel, they are more often associated with malevolent spirits tempting into sin. The idea of a spiritual double accompanying humans might be a remnant of older Near Eastern beliefs, such as the Egypt kꜣ which in turn resembles the Babylonian idea of an undefined personal deity accompanying a person. The Qareen as an accompanying spirit should not be confused with the Qarinah, a female "childbed demon" in Middle Eastern traditions.

short_description.id: Di sma undar jordi ("yang kecil di bawah tanah") adalah makhluk mirip vættir dalam cerita rakyat Gotland, Swedia, yang menjaga pertanian selama tidak dibuat marah.
short_description.en: Di sma undar jordi ('the little ones underground') are vættir-like beings in the folklore of Gotland, Sweden, who look after farms as long as they are not angered.

long_description.id: Di sma undar jordi, atau singkatnya di sma, adalah makhluk legenda mirip vættir dari cerita rakyat pulau Gotland, Swedia. Namanya dalam bahasa Gutnish berarti "yang kecil di bawah tanah", dan mereka merupakan varian lokal dari kepercayaan yang lebih luas tentang "orang tersembunyi" atau makhluk bawah tanah (underjordiska) di daratan Swedia.
long_description.en: Di sma undar jordi, or just di sma, are legendary vættir-like beings from the folklore of the island of Gotland, Sweden. In Gutnish the name means 'the little ones underground', and they are the local form of the wider belief in the 'hidden people' or subterraneans (underjordiska) of mainland Sweden.

long_description.id: Menurut kepercayaan rakyat, mereka tinggal di dekat manusia dan pertanian mereka, serta merawat pertanian beserta penghuni dan hewan-hewannya selama tidak dibuat marah. Cara klasik membuat mereka murka adalah menyiram air panas ke luar rumah tanpa peringatan sehingga mereka tersiram. Mereka juga dianggap memastikan manusia merawat tanah yang diolahnya.
long_description.en: Folk belief holds that they live near people and their farms, tending the farm, its people and its animals so long as they are not angered. The classic way to anger them is to throw hot water outdoors without warning and scald them. They are also seen as making sure people care for the land they farm.

long_description.en: Di sma undar jordi (Gutnish, Swedish: de små under jorden, lit. 'the small (ones) underground'), or simply di sma, are legendary vættir-like creatures found in folklore from the island of Gotland, Sweden. It is really the regional variation of the broader folklore of the "hidden people" (mainland Swedish: underjordiska, "subterraneans"). Di sma are said to take care of farms and the people and animals that live there, as long as one does not anger them. The most classical example of doing so is to mindlessly scald them when disposing hot water outdoors. According to Gotlandic tales, di sma can only be seen by looking through a hole in a sheet of paper. The Swedish rauk'n'roll band Di sma undar jårdi, active in the 1980s, was named after these creatures.

short_description.id: Orang lumut (Moosleute) adalah golongan peri dalam cerita rakyat Jerman, bertubuh kecil, berbalut lumut, dan hidupnya terikat erat pada pohon dan hutan.
short_description.en: Moss people (Moosleute) are a class of fairy-folk in German folklore, small in size, clad in moss and bound closely to trees and the forest.

long_description.id: Orang lumut, juga disebut orang kayu (Holzleute), orang hutan (Waldleute), atau orang liar, adalah golongan peri dalam cerita rakyat Jerman yang dibandingkan dengan kurcaci, elf, atau roh. Kata Schrat dan Waldschrat juga dipakai untuk mereka. Moosweiblein, yang perempuan, dikenal di Sachsen, Thüringen, Harz, Vogtland, Oberpfalz, Bayerischen Wald, Franken, Riesengebirge, hingga Westfalen.
long_description.en: Moss people, also called wood folk (Holzleute), forest folk (Waldleute) or wild folk, are a class of fairy-folk in German folklore compared with dwarfs, elves or spirits. The words Schrat and Waldschrat are used for them too. The female Moosweiblein are known in Saxony, Thuringia, the Harz, the Vogtland, the Upper Palatinate, the Bavarian Forest, Franconia, the Giant Mountains and as far as Westphalia.

long_description.id: Mereka biasanya sebesar anak-anak, kelabu dan tampak tua, berbulu, dan berpakaian lumut, meski kadang lebih besar atau malah cantik. Hidup mereka terikat pada pohon: bila kulit dalam sebuah pohon terkelupas karena gesekan, seorang perempuan hutan mati. Mereka tinggal di rongga tanah, pohon berlubang, atau pondok lumut, tidur di atas lumut, dan bisa menikah serta beranak.
long_description.en: They are usually the size of children, grey and old-looking, hairy and dressed in moss, though sometimes larger or even pretty. Their lives are bound to trees: if a tree's inner bark is rubbed loose, a wood-woman dies. They live in earth holes, hollow trees or moss huts, sleep on moss, and can marry and have children.

long_description.id: Mereka kadang meminjam barang atau meminta bantuan manusia dan selalu membalas dengan murah hati, sering dengan nasihat atau roti, tetapi mudah tersinggung bila hadiahnya ditolak atau bila diberi roti jintan, yang mereka benci. Sebagian mitos menyebut mereka meminta ASI untuk bayi mereka atau mencuri anak manusia. Perempuan lumut dapat menyebarkan wabah, tetapi juga menunjukkan tanaman obat untuk menyembuhkannya.
long_description.en: They sometimes borrow things or ask people for help and always repay generously, often with advice or bread, but are easily offended if their gifts are spurned or if given caraway bread, which they hate. Some myths have them asking for breast milk for their young or stealing human children. Moss women can spread plague, yet also show people the healing herbs against it.

long_description.id: Mereka sering menjadi buruan perburuan liar. Untuk menyelamatkan diri, mereka berlindung di tunggul pohon yang ditandai tiga salib oleh penebang saat pohon itu tumbang.
long_description.en: They are often the quarry of the Wild Hunt. To escape, they take refuge on tree stumps that a woodsman marked with three crosses while the tree was falling.

role.en: Their lives are bound to trees.

statement.en: Moosweiblein appear in Sachsen, Thüringen, an der Saale, Orlagau, Harz, Vogtland, Oberpfalz, Bayerischen Wald, Franken, Oberfranken, Böhmerwald, around Warnsdorf in Nordtschechien, Riesengebirge and Westfalen (Saxony, Thuringia, Upper Palatinate, Bavarian Forest, Franconia, Giant Mountains, Westphalia).

claims.quote: Die Moosweiblein leben im Wald. Sie wohnen auf der Heide, an dunklen Orten im Holz oder im tiefsten Wald. Ihre Behausung ist ein Erdloch, ein hohler Baum, ein Häuslein aus Baumwurzeln oder eine Mooshütte. Sie schlafen auf Moos und betten auch ihre Kinder auf Moos oder Rinde.

statement.id: Moosweiblein tinggal di hutan, di padang, di tempat gelap, atau di hutan terdalam; rumahnya rongga tanah, pohon berlubang, pondok dari akar, atau pondok lumut; mereka tidur di atas lumut dan membaringkan anak-anaknya di atas lumut atau kulit kayu.
statement.en: Moosweiblein live in the forest, on heaths, in dark places or the deepest woods; they dwell in earth holes, hollow trees, root huts or moss huts, sleep on moss and bed their children on moss or bark.

claims.quote: In Thuringia, the only place where a Moosweibchen "little moss woman") is safe from the wild huntsman (German wilder Jäger) chasing her kind in the afternoon and at night is a tree stump marked with three crosses by a woodsman while the tree was still falling.

statement.en: In Thuringia the only refuge for a Moosweibchen from the wild huntsman (the Wild Hunt; wilder Jäger) is a stump marked with three crosses by a woodsman while the tree was still falling.

long_description.en: The moss people or moss folk (German: Moosleute, "moss folk", German: [ˈmoːsˌlɔɪ̯tə], wilde Leute, "wild folk", German: [ˈvɪldə ˈlɔɪ̯tə]), also referred to as the wood people or wood folk (Holzleute, "wood folk", German: [ˈhɔltsˌlɔɪ̯tə]) or forest folk (Waldleute, "forest-folk", German: [ˈvaltˌlɔɪ̯tə]), are a class of fairy-folk, variously compared to dwarfs, elves, or spirits, described in German folklore as having an intimate connection to trees and the forest. In German, the words Schrat and Waldschrat are also used for a moss person. (Compare Old Norse skratti, "goblin".) The diminutive Schrätlein also serves as synonym for a nightmare creature.

short_description.id: Bergsrå ("rå gunung") adalah roh atau makhluk gunung dalam kepercayaan rakyat Nordik yang menguasai bijih di dalam gunung dan memikat manusia masuk ke kediamannya.
short_description.en: The Bergsrå ('mountain rå') is a mountain spirit of Nordic folk belief that rules the ore within the mountain and lures people into its dwelling.

long_description.id: Bergsrå, juga disebut bergatrollet ("troll gunung") atau bergakungen ("raja gunung"), adalah makhluk gaib dalam kepercayaan rakyat Nordik yang tinggal di dalam gunung dan menguasai bijih logamnya. Ia bisa laki-laki maupun perempuan, dan dalam banyak cerita dikelilingi keluarga serta istana para troll.
long_description.en: The Bergsrå, also called bergatrollet ('mountain troll') or bergakungen ('mountain king'), is a supernatural being of Nordic folk belief who lives inside the mountain and rules over its ore. It could be male or female, and in many tales is surrounded by its family and a court of trolls.

long_description.id: Bergsrå sering mengacaukan penglihatan orang yang kebetulan menemukan endapan bijih sehingga mereka tak bisa menemukannya lagi. Ia juga terkenal memikat manusia masuk ke gunung; orang yang diambil itu disebut bergtagen ("diambil ke dalam gunung"), dan hubungan antara manusia dan bergsrå lama dianggap nyata.
long_description.en: The Bergsrå often confuses the sight of people who chance upon ore deposits so that they can never find them again. It is also known for luring humans into the mountain; someone taken this way was called bergtagen ('taken into the mountain'), and dealings between humans and a bergsrå were long thought to be real.

long_description.id: Pada 1691 seorang buruh tani remaja, Sven Andersson dari Västergötland, dijatuhi hukuman mati karena mengaku bersetubuh dengan bergsrå perempuan. Ia bercerita pernah tertidur di hutan dekat sebuah gunung saat mencari kambing yang lepas, lalu dibawa masuk ke gunung oleh seorang perempuan berbaju putih yang memberinya makan dan minum.
long_description.en: In 1691 a teenage farmhand, Sven Andersson of Västergötland, was sentenced to death for confessing to intercourse with a female bergsrå. He said he had fallen asleep in the forest by a mountain while looking for a stray goat and had been taken into the mountain by a woman in white, who gave him food and drink.

did_you_know.id: Pada 1691 seorang pemuda dari Västergötland dijatuhi hukuman mati karena mengaku bersetubuh dengan bergsrå perempuan di dalam gunung.
did_you_know.en: In 1691 a young man from Västergötland was sentenced to death for confessing to intercourse with a female bergsrå inside a mountain.

description.en: Twists the sight of ore finders so they cannot find it again.

claims.quote: The bergsrå could be either masculine or feminine. It lived in the mountain with a court of relatives and sometimes surrounded by trolls. It was a common phenomenon in the mythology about the bergsrå to trick people into their dwellings in the mountain and to become bergtagen

claims.quote: Bergsrået, eller bergatrollet eller bergakungen, var i nordisk folktro ett övernaturligt väsen, som bor i berget och råder över dess malm. statement.en: Bergsrået (bergatrollet, bergakungen) in Nordic (nordisk) folk belief is a supernatural being living in the mountain and ruling its ore; it often twists the sight of those who find ore deposits so they cannot find them again, and in many tales is surrounded by family and a court of trolls.

claims.quote: Umgänge mellan människor och bergrå var något som långt fram i tiden sågs som en realitet: en människa som hade gjort detta blev tagen in i berget, något som kallades bergtagning och var ett känt fenomen inom mytologin kring bergsrået.

statement.id: Hubungan antara manusia dan bergrå lama dianggap nyata; orang yang melakukannya diambil ke dalam gunung, disebut bergtagning, fenomena terkenal dalam mitologi bergsrå.
statement.en: Dealings between humans and a bergrå were long seen as real; one who had them was taken into the mountain, called bergtagning, a known phenomenon in bergsrå lore.

claims.quote: År 1691 dömdes en dräng, Sven Andersson från Vättle härad i Västergötland, till döden för att ha haft samlag med ett kvinnligt bergrå .

statement.en: In 1691 farmhand Sven Andersson of Vättle hundred in Västergötland was sentenced to death for intercourse with a female bergrå.

The bergsrå could be either masculine or feminine. It lived in the mountain with a court of relatives and sometimes surrounded by trolls. It was a common phenomenon in the mythology about the bergsrå to trick people into their dwellings in the mountain and to become bergtagen (literary: "taken into the mountain"). These bergtagnings (Swedish: abduction into the mountain) are usual are done by lone males and their victims tend to be women. A typical description of such a claimed occurrence was given by Sven Andersson in 1691 when he was on trial for having sexual intercourse with a female bergsrå.

short_description.id: Witte Wiwer ("perempuan putih" dalam bahasa Jerman Rendah) adalah makhluk legenda dari cerita rakyat Jerman (Rendah) yang mirip, tetapi berbeda dari, Weiße Frauen; mereka tinggal di bawah tanah dan bisa menukar bayi dengan anak ganti.
short_description.en: The witte Wiwer ("white women" in Low German) are legendary beings of (Low) German folklore similar to but distinct from the weiße Frauen; they live underground and may swap babies for changelings.

long_description.id: Witte Wiwer (juga witte Wîwer, witte Wiewer, atau witte Wiver; semuanya berarti "perempuan putih" dalam bahasa Jerman Rendah, Jerman baku weiße Weiber) adalah makhluk legenda dari cerita rakyat Jerman (Rendah) yang mirip tetapi berbeda dari Weiße Frauen. Nama lain mereka adalah unterirdische Weiber (perempuan bawah tanah) di Mecklenburg dan Sibyllen di Jerman barat laut. Artikel tentang Weiße Frauen menyebut witte Wiwer sebagai padanan Jerman Rendah dari Weiße Frauen.
long_description.en: The witte Wiwer (also witte Wîwer, witte Wiewer or witte Wiver; all meaning "white women" in Low German, Standard German weiße Weiber) belong to (Low) German folk legend and resemble the weiße Frauen without being the same beings. Other names are unterirdische Weiber (subterranean women) in Mecklenburg and Sibyllen in northwestern Germany. The article on the Weiße Frauen calls the witte Wiwer their Low German equivalent.

long_description.id: Witte Wiwer di Mecklenburg tinggal di dalam tanah, di bawah semak, di bukit kecil, di tanah lapang hutan, atau di bawah akar pohon tua. Di Westphalia mereka tinggal di lubang dengan mata air jernih yang dikelilingi hutan kecil, disebut Wittewiwerskule, atau di gua berpintu; mereka juga dikatakan tinggal di pegunungan, dan di pulau Rügen memakai terowongan bawah tanah. Mereka memainkan musik riang dan bersuara sangat merdu.
long_description.en: The witte Wiwer of Mecklenburg make their homes underground: beneath bushes, inside low hills, in woodland glades or among the roots of old trees. In Westphalia they dwell in a pit with a clear spring ringed by a grove, the Wittewiwerskule, or in a cave with a door; they are also said to live in mountains, and on the island of Rügen they use underground tunnels. They play merry music and have very fine voices.

long_description.id: Mereka menukar bayi yang belum dibaptis dengan anak ganti (Wechselbälge) bila tidak ada lampu menyala di samping buaian pada malam hari, dan kadang membawa pergi perempuan yang baru melahirkan. Pada senja hari setiap bulan baru mereka mungkin meminjam kuali pembuat bir, lalu tiga malam kemudian mengembalikannya berisi bir buatan mereka sebagai bayaran. Mereka diburu oleh perburuan liar (wilde Jagd) yang dipimpin pemburu perempuan Fru Waur. Ketika witte Wiwer di Mönchgut di Rügen diusir, pohon ek yang terkait dengan mereka layu, dan mereka meramalkan akan kembali bila pohon itu bertunas lagi.
long_description.en: They swap unbaptized newborns for changelings (Wechselbälge) if no light burns beside the cradle at night, and sometimes carry off women just out of childbed. At twilight each new moon they may borrow the brewing copper and, three evenings later, return it filled with their own beer as payment. They are hunted by the wild hunt (wilde Jagd) led by the huntress Fru Waur. When the witte Wiwer of Mönchgut on Rügen were driven away, the oak tied to them withered, and they foretold their return when it sprouted again.

long_description.en: The witte Wiwer, witte Wîwer, witte Wiewer or witte Wiver (pronounced [ˈvɪtə ˈviːvɐ]; all meaning 'white women' in Low German; Standard German: weiße Weiber, pronounced [ˈvaɪsə ˈvaɪbɐ]; sg. witt Wif or weißes Weib) are legendary creatures from (Low) German folklore similar to but distinct from the weiße Frauen. Other names are unterirdische Weiber (subterranean women) in Mecklenburg and Sibyllen (sibyls; sg. Sibylle) in Northwestern Germany. The witte Wiwer of Mecklenburg dwell in the earth, under shrubs, in small hills, in forest clearings, or beneath the roots of old trees. They might also live beneath the cow stable in some places in Mecklenburg. In Westphalia, the witte Wiwer dwell in a pit with a clear fountain inside surrounded by a grove which is called the Wittewiwerskule (white women's pit), otherwise described as a cave with a door. They are also said to dwell in mountains. On the island of Rügen, they further use subterranean tunnels to get from one place to another. The witte Wiwer play merry music and have very fine voices. They exchange unbaptized newborn children for changelings (German Wechselbälge, sg. Wechselbalg) if there is no light burning beside the cradle at night, warding them off. They might also take away women just out of childbed and bring them to their dwelling, threatening the woman to stay there or else they would wring her neck. The witte Wiwer might ask to borrow the brewing copper every new moon during twilight hour, taking it away unseen if obliged. Three evenings later, they will return it the very same hour filled with some cans of the beer brewed by them as payment. They might also ask to get some sweet porridge, too, if a wedding takes place in somebody's house. They are chased by the wild hunt (German wilde Jagd) from which they flee with flying hair. The wild hunt consists of the wilde Jägerin (wild huntswoman) and her pack of hounds. The wild huntswoman, known as de oll Fru Waur (the old Lady Waur) or de oll Węderhex Waur (the old hag [literally: weather-witch] Waur), carries the witte Wiwer she caught off on her horse, either one placed before her or – if she has caught two of them – with their hair bound together, hanging from the horse. If the witt Wif flees from Fru Waur unkempt, unwashed, and sweaty, the wild huntress will first need to wash up to catch her, using her own water and drying off with her long hunting dress. This seems corrupted, for usually it is the wild huntsman who has not washed up yet and thus has no power over his victims rather than them being unwashed. When the witte Wiwer of Mönchgut in Rügen were driven away, the oak tree connected to them withered. They prophesied their return when the withered oak would sprout again.

short_description.id: Kurcaci (dwarf) adalah makhluk gaib berwujud manusia dalam cerita rakyat Jermanik, yang umumnya tinggal di gunung atau batu dan dikenal sebagai perajin yang mahir.
short_description.en: A dwarf is a supernatural human-shaped being of Germanic folklore, commonly said to live in mountains or stones and known as a skilled craftsman.

long_description.id: Kurcaci (dwarf) adalah makhluk gaib berwujud manusia dalam cerita rakyat Jermanik (Germanic). Gambaran tentang mereka sangat beragam sepanjang sejarah; umumnya, tetapi tidak selalu, mereka tinggal di gunung atau batu dan merupakan perajin yang mahir. Dalam sumber sastra awal hanya lelaki yang secara tegas disebut kurcaci, meski mereka disebut punya saudari dan anak perempuan. Kata Inggris dwarf berasal dari dweorg (Old English), sekerabat dengan dvergr (Old Norse) dan twerg (Old High German).
long_description.en: A dwarf is a supernatural human-shaped being of Germanic folklore. Accounts of dwarfs vary widely through history; they are commonly, though not always, said to live in mountains or stones and to be skilled craftsmen. In early literary sources only males are explicitly called dwarfs, though they are said to have sisters and daughters. The English word dwarf comes from Old English dweorg, related to Old Norse dvergr and Old High German twerg.

long_description.id: Menurut Edda Prosa, para kurcaci mula-mula tumbuh seperti belatung dalam daging raksasa Ymer, lalu atas keputusan para dewa memperoleh akal dan rupa manusia, tetapi tetap harus tinggal di dalam tanah dan batu; Modsogner dan Durin adalah dua di antaranya. Syair Völuspá juga menyebut bahwa Motsognir adalah yang terkuat di antara para kurcaci, dan Durin berikutnya. Para sarjana menduga Svartálfar ("elf hitam") dalam Edda Prosa adalah makhluk yang sama dengan kurcaci, karena keduanya disebut tinggal di Svartálfheimr.
long_description.en: According to the Prose Edda, the dwarfs first quickened like maggots in the flesh of the giant Ymer, then by the gods' decision gained understanding and the likeness of men, yet still had to dwell in earth and rocks; Modsogner and Durin were two of them. The poem Völuspá likewise calls Motsognir the mightiest of the dwarfs, with Durin next. Scholars take the Svartálfar ("black elves") of the Prose Edda to be the same beings as dwarfs, since both are said to live in Svartálfheimr.

long_description.id: Dalam sumber Edda, kurcaci membuat harta ajaib bagi para dewa, seperti Mjölnir, rambut Sif, Draupnir, Gullinbursti, Skíðblaðnir, Gleipnir, dan Gungnir, serta Brísingamen bagi Freyja; mereka juga membuat mead puisi dari darah Kvasir. Dalam kesusastraan Jerman banyak kurcaci dapat menjadi tak kasatmata, biasanya dengan Tarnkappe (jubah tak kasatmata), dan bisa bersikap bermusuhan atau bersahabat terhadap manusia. Kurcaci Alberich dalam Nibelungenlied menjaga harta Nibelung dan sekuat dua belas lelaki.
long_description.en: The Eddic dwarfs are the makers of the gods' wonders, among them Gungnir, Gleipnir, Draupnir, Mjölnir, Gullinbursti, Skíðblaðnir and the golden hair of Sif, as well as Freyja's Brísingamen; they also brewed the mead of poetry from Kvasir's blood. In German literature many dwarfs can become invisible, usually with a Tarnkappe (cloak of invisibility), and may be hostile or friendly to humans. The dwarf Alberich in the Nibelungenlied guards the Nibelung treasure and has the strength of twelve men.

long_description.id: Dalam sumber Nordik awal kurcaci tidak disebut kecil, tetapi dalam saga legenda dan cerita rakyat kemudian mereka sering digambarkan pendek; sebagian dapat berubah wujud, seperti Andvari yang hidup sebagai ikan tombak. Dalam syair Alvissmol, kurcaci Alvis yang ingin menikahi putri Thor dipaksa menjawab banyak pertanyaan hingga fajar, lalu Thor berkata "hari telah menangkapmu, kurcaci" ketika matahari bersinar di aula. Menurut artikel id, kurcaci tinggal di gua di pegunungan atau di bawah tanah, dapat melihat dengan baik dalam gelap, menambang emas, perak, dan besi, dan merupakan pandai besi yang mahir; dalam mitologi Nordik mereka membuat rantai yang mampu mengikat serigala Fenrir.
long_description.en: In early Norse sources dwarfs are not said to be small, but in the legendary sagas and later folklore they are often described as short; some can change shape, like Andvari who lived as a pike. In the poem Alvissmol, the dwarf Alvis, wishing to marry Thor's daughter, is made to answer question after question until dawn, and Thor says "the day has caught thee, dwarf" as the sun shines in the hall. According to the id article, dwarfs live in caves in the mountains or underground, see well in the dark, mine gold, silver and iron, and are skilled smiths; in Norse mythology they made the chain able to bind the wolf Fenrir.

long_description.id: Kurcaci tetap muncul dalam cerita rakyat modern wilayah berbahasa Jermanik, misalnya Simonside Dwarfs di Northumberland yang konon memakai cahaya untuk menyesatkan orang seperti will-o'-the-wisp. Dalam budaya populer mereka tampil dalam karya J. R. R. Tolkien dan Terry Pratchett, dan dalam dongeng Putih Salju digambarkan sebagai bangsa pekerja keras yang polos tetapi melindungi.
long_description.en: Dwarfs remain in the modern folklore of Germanic-speaking regions, such as the Simonside Dwarfs of Northumberland, said to use lights to lure people off paths like a will-o'-the-wisp. In popular culture they appear in the works of J. R. R. Tolkien and Terry Pratchett, and in the tale of Snow White they are a hard-working, simple but protective people.

long_description.id: Kurcaci (bahasa Inggris: dwarf) adalah manusia kerdil dalam mitologi Nordik. Kurcaci juga sering diadopsi sebagai tokoh dalam kisah-kisah fiksi fantasi, film, dan permainan video.
long_description.en: A dwarf (pl. dwarfs or dwarves) is a type of supernatural human-shaped being in Germanic folklore. Accounts of dwarfs vary significantly throughout history. They are commonly, but not exclusively, presented as living in mountains or stones and being skilled craftsmen. In early literary sources, only males are explicitly referred to as dwarfs. However, they are described as having sisters and daughters, while male and female dwarfs feature in later saga literature and folklore. Dwarfs are sometimes described as short; however, scholars have noted that this is neither explicit, nor relevant to their roles in the earliest sources. Dwarfs continue to feature in modern popular culture, such as in the works of J. R. R. Tolkien and Terry Pratchett, where they are often, but not exclusively, presented as distinct from elves.
