long_description.en: A dwarf is a supernatural human-shaped being of Germanic folklore. Accounts of dwarfs vary widely through history; they are commonly, though not always, said to live in mountains or stones and to be skilled craftsmen. In early literary sources only males are explicitly called dwarfs, though they are said to have sisters and daughters. The English word dwarf comes from Old English dweorg, related to Old Norse dvergr and Old High German twerg.

long_description.id: Menurut Edda Prosa, para kurcaci mula-mula tumbuh seperti belatung dalam daging raksasa Ymer, lalu atas keputusan para dewa memperoleh akal dan rupa manusia, tetapi tetap harus tinggal di dalam tanah dan batu; Modsogner dan Durin adalah dua di antaranya. Syair Völuspá juga menyebut bahwa Motsognir adalah yang terkuat di antara para kurcaci, dan Durin berikutnya. Para sarjana menduga Svartálfar ("elf hitam") dalam Edda Prosa adalah makhluk yang sama dengan kurcaci, karena keduanya disebut tinggal di Svartálfheimr.
long_description.en: According to the Prose Edda, the dwarfs first quickened like maggots in the flesh of the giant Ymer, then by the gods' decision gained understanding and the likeness of men, yet still had to dwell in earth and rocks; Modsogner and Durin were two of them. The poem Völuspá likewise calls Motsognir the mightiest of the dwarfs, with Durin next. Scholars take the Svartálfar ("black elves") of the Prose Edda to be the same beings as dwarfs, since both are said to live in Svartálfheimr.

long_description.id: Dalam sumber Edda, kurcaci membuat harta ajaib bagi para dewa, seperti Mjölnir, rambut Sif, Draupnir, Gullinbursti, Skíðblaðnir, Gleipnir, dan Gungnir, serta Brísingamen bagi Freyja; mereka juga membuat mead puisi dari darah Kvasir. Dalam kesusastraan Jerman banyak kurcaci dapat menjadi tak kasatmata, biasanya dengan Tarnkappe (jubah tak kasatmata), dan bisa bersikap bermusuhan atau bersahabat terhadap manusia. Kurcaci Alberich dalam Nibelungenlied menjaga harta Nibelung dan sekuat dua belas lelaki.
long_description.en: The Eddic dwarfs are the makers of the gods' wonders, among them Gungnir, Gleipnir, Draupnir, Mjölnir, Gullinbursti, Skíðblaðnir and the golden hair of Sif, as well as Freyja's Brísingamen; they also brewed the mead of poetry from Kvasir's blood. In German literature many dwarfs can become invisible, usually with a Tarnkappe (cloak of invisibility), and may be hostile or friendly to humans. The dwarf Alberich in the Nibelungenlied guards the Nibelung treasure and has the strength of twelve men.

long_description.id: Dalam sumber Nordik awal kurcaci tidak disebut kecil, tetapi dalam saga legenda dan cerita rakyat kemudian mereka sering digambarkan pendek; sebagian dapat berubah wujud, seperti Andvari yang hidup sebagai ikan tombak. Dalam syair Alvissmol, kurcaci Alvis yang ingin menikahi putri Thor dipaksa menjawab banyak pertanyaan hingga fajar, lalu Thor berkata "hari telah menangkapmu, kurcaci" ketika matahari bersinar di aula. Menurut artikel id, kurcaci tinggal di gua di pegunungan atau di bawah tanah, dapat melihat dengan baik dalam gelap, menambang emas, perak, dan besi, dan merupakan pandai besi yang mahir; dalam mitologi Nordik mereka membuat rantai yang mampu mengikat serigala Fenrir.
long_description.en: In early Norse sources dwarfs are not said to be small, but in the legendary sagas and later folklore they are often described as short; some can change shape, like Andvari who lived as a pike. In the poem Alvissmol, the dwarf Alvis, wishing to marry Thor's daughter, is made to answer question after question until dawn, and Thor says "the day has caught thee, dwarf" as the sun shines in the hall. According to the id article, dwarfs live in caves in the mountains or underground, see well in the dark, mine gold, silver and iron, and are skilled smiths; in Norse mythology they made the chain able to bind the wolf Fenrir.

long_description.id: Kurcaci tetap muncul dalam cerita rakyat modern wilayah berbahasa Jermanik, misalnya Simonside Dwarfs di Northumberland yang konon memakai cahaya untuk menyesatkan orang seperti will-o'-the-wisp. Dalam budaya populer mereka tampil dalam karya J. R. R. Tolkien dan Terry Pratchett, dan dalam dongeng Putih Salju digambarkan sebagai bangsa pekerja keras yang polos tetapi melindungi.
long_description.en: Dwarfs remain in the modern folklore of Germanic-speaking regions, such as the Simonside Dwarfs of Northumberland, said to use lights to lure people off paths like a will-o'-the-wisp. In popular culture they appear in the works of J. R. R. Tolkien and Terry Pratchett, and in the tale of Snow White they are a hard-working, simple but protective people.

long_description.id: Kurcaci (bahasa Inggris: dwarf) adalah manusia kerdil dalam mitologi Nordik. Kurcaci juga sering diadopsi sebagai tokoh dalam kisah-kisah fiksi fantasi, film, dan permainan video.
long_description.en: A dwarf (pl. dwarfs or dwarves) is a type of supernatural human-shaped being in Germanic folklore. Accounts of dwarfs vary significantly throughout history. They are commonly, but not exclusively, presented as living in mountains or stones and being skilled craftsmen. In early literary sources, only males are explicitly referred to as dwarfs. However, they are described as having sisters and daughters, while male and female dwarfs feature in later saga literature and folklore. Dwarfs are sometimes described as short; however, scholars have noted that this is neither explicit, nor relevant to their roles in the earliest sources. Dwarfs continue to feature in modern popular culture, such as in the works of J. R. R. Tolkien and Terry Pratchett, where they are often, but not exclusively, presented as distinct from elves.

short_description.id: Aos sí adalah nama Irlandia untuk ras gaib dalam cerita rakyat Gaelik, mirip elf, yang konon keturunan Tuatha Dé Danann dan tinggal di gundukan peri (sí).
short_description.en: Aos sí is the Irish name for a supernatural race of Gaelic folklore, similar to elves, said to descend from the Tuatha Dé Danann and to live in fairy mounds (sí).

long_description.id: Aos sí atau aos sídhe adalah nama Irlandia untuk ras gaib dalam cerita rakyat Gaelik (Gaelic folklore), mirip elf. Mereka dikatakan keturunan Tuatha Dé Danann atau dewa-dewa mitologi Irlandia. Istilah aos sí berarti "bangsa sí", yaitu gundukan tempat mereka tinggal, yang dipandang sebagai gerbang ke Dunia Lain; dalam bahasa Inggris tempat itu disebut fairy mounds atau hollow hills. Mereka berinteraksi dengan manusia dan disebut sebagai leluhur, roh alam, atau dewi dan dewa.
long_description.en: In Irish, aos sí or aos sídhe names an elf-like otherworldly people of Gaelic lore, held to be the offspring of the Tuatha Dé Danann or of the old Irish gods. The term means "folk of the sí", the mounds they dwell in, seen as gateways to an Otherworld; in English these are called fairy mounds or hollow hills. They deal with humans and are variously called ancestors, nature spirits, or goddesses and gods.

long_description.id: Nama lainnya daoine sí, juga "orang gundukan peri"; dalam bahasa Inggris mereka sering disebut "the Sidhe". Pada abad ke-7 uskup Tírechán menyebut kaum sídh sebagai "dewa-dewa bumi", dan Fiacc's Hymn abad ke-8 menyebut orang Irlandia memuja mereka sebelum kedatangan Santo Patrick. Dalam cerita rakyat Irlandia, peri bisa berasal dari malaikat yang jatuh tetapi dosanya tak cukup berat untuk neraka, atau dari Tuatha Dé Danann yang mundur ke Dunia Lain setelah kalah dari putra-putra Míl Espáine. Mereka sering ditenangkan dengan persembahan, dan orang berhati-hati agar tak membuat mereka marah.
long_description.en: Another name is daoine sí, likewise "people of the fairy mound"; in English they are often simply "the Sidhe". In the 7th century bishop Tírechán called the sídh folk "earthly gods", and the 8th-century Fiacc's Hymn says the Irish worshipped them before Saint Patrick came. In Irish folklore fairies may be fallen angels whose sins were too slight for hell, or descendants of the Tuatha Dé Danann who withdrew into the Otherworld after losing to the Sons of Míl Espáine. They are often appeased with offerings, and people take care not to anger them.

long_description.id: Menurut artikel id, aos sí adalah ras supranatural dalam mitologi Irlandia dan Skotlandia yang tinggal di bawah tanah atau di dunia tak kasatmata yang berdampingan dengan dunia manusia; Lebor Gabála Érenn menggambarkan dunia itu sebagai alam semesta paralel. Dalam mitologi Skotlandia mereka disebut daoine sìth.
long_description.en: According to the id article, the aos sí are a supernatural race of Irish and Scottish mythology living underground or in an invisible world alongside ours, which the Lebor Gabála Érenn describes as a parallel universe. In Scottish mythology they are called daoine sìth.

long_description.id: Aos sí ([eːs ˈʃiː], bentuk lama aes sídhe [eːs ˈʃiːðʲə]) adalah istilah yang mengacu kepada ras supranatural dalam mitologi Irlandia dan Skotlandia yang mirip dengan peri atau elf. Konon mereka tinggal di bawah tanah atau di dunia kasatmata yang ada bersamaan dengan dunia manusia. Dunia ini dijelaskan di dalam Lebor Gabála Érenn sebagai alam semesta paralel dan aos sí berkeliaran di antara makhluk hidup. Dalam bahasa Irlandia, aos sí berarti "orang-orang gundukan" (gundukan dalam bahasa Irlandia disebut "sídhe"). Dalam sastra Irlandia, orang-orang gundukan juga disebut daoine sídhe [ˈdiːnʲə ˈʃiːə]; sementara dalam mitologi Skotlandia mereka dinamai daoine sìth. Mereka telah dideskripsikan sebagai nenek moyang, roh di alam, peri, atau dewa-dewi. Beberapa sumber sekunder dan tersier (termasuk pengarang terkenal seperti W. B. Yeats) menyebut aos sí dengan nama sídhe" saja. Menurut beberapa sumber, aos sí adalah dewa-dewi Tuatha Dé Danann yang selamat dari perang melawan kaum Milesia dan mereka melarikan diri ke dunia lain.
long_description.en: Aos sí or aos sídhe (pronounced [iːsˠ ˈʃiː]; English approximation: eess SHEE) is the Irish name for a supernatural race in Gaelic folklore, similar to elves. They are said to descend from the Tuatha Dé Danann or the gods of Irish mythology. The term aos sí means "folk of the sí"; these are the mounds in which they are said to dwell, which are seen as portals to an Otherworld. Such abodes are referred to in English as "shees", "fairy mounds", "elf mounds" or "hollow hills". The aos sí interact with humans and the human world. They are variously said to be the ancestors, the spirits of nature, or goddesses and gods.

short_description.id: Manannán mac Lir ("anak laut") adalah dewa laut, pejuang, dan raja dunia lain dalam mitologi Gaelik, salah satu Tuatha Dé Danann.
short_description.en: Manannán mac Lir, whose surname means 'son of the Sea', is the Gaelic god of the sea, a warrior and lord of the otherworld, counted among the Tuatha Dé Danann.

long_description.id: Manannán atau Manann, juga Manannán mac Lir ("anak laut"), adalah dewa laut, pejuang, dan raja dunia lain dalam mitologi Gaelik (Gaelic) Irlandia, Man, dan Skotlandia, dan salah satu Tuatha Dé Danann. Ia penguasa dan penjaga dunia lain, yang disebut Emain Ablach ("Pulau Pohon Apel"), Mag Mell ("Dataran Kebahagiaan"), atau Tír Tairngire ("Negeri Perjanjian"). Setelah kedatangan manusia (kaum Milesia), ia menjadi raja atas Tuatha Dé yang tersisa dan memakai kabut gaib (féth fíada) untuk menyembunyikan kediamannya dan sidhe yang lain.
long_description.en: Manannán (or Manann), called Manannán mac Lir, 'son of the Sea', is the sea god, warrior and otherworld king of Irish, Manx and Scottish Gaelic myth, and belongs to the Tuatha Dé Danann. As lord and keeper of the otherworld, his realm goes by several names: Tír Tairngire, the 'Land of Promise'; Mag Mell, the 'Plain of Delights'; and Emain Ablach, the 'Isle of Apple Trees'. After the coming of humans (the Milesians) he became over-king of the remaining Tuatha Dé and uses the mist of invisibility (féth fíada) to hide his home and the other sidhe.

long_description.id: Ia memiliki perahu yang berlayar sendiri, Sguaba Tuinne ("Penyapu Ombak"), kuda Aonbharr yang dapat berlari di atas air dan darat, dan pedang mematikan Fragarach yang menguras kekuatan. Dalam legenda Skotlandia dan Man ia dikenal sebagai Manannan beg mac y Leir, dan Isle of Man (Mannin) umumnya dianggap dinamai menurutnya; ia sekerabat dengan tokoh Wales Manawydan fab Llŷr. Namanya dieja Manandán dalam bahasa Irlandia Kuno dan Mannan dalam bahasa Man. Menurut artikel id, ia dipandang sebagai penjaga dunia lain dan salah satu yang mengantar jiwa ke alam baka, dan juga dikenal sebagai Oirbsiu atau Oirbsen, asal nama Lough Corrib.
long_description.en: He owns a self-sailing boat, Sguaba Tuinne ('Wave-sweeper'), a horse, Aonbharr, that gallops across sea and land alike, and Fragarach, a lethal sword that drains an enemy's strength. In Scottish and Manx legend he is Manannan beg mac y Leir, and the Isle of Man (Mannin) is generally held to be named after him; he is cognate with the Welsh figure Manawydan fab Llŷr. His name is Manandán in Old Irish and Mannan in Manx. According to the id article he is seen as guardian of the otherworld and one who brings souls to the afterlife, and is also known as Oirbsiu or Oirbsen, from whom Lough Corrib takes its name.

famous_for.en: The Isle of Man is named after him.

did_you_know.id: Isle of Man umumnya dianggap dinamai menurut dewa laut Manannán, meski ada yang berpendapat sebaliknya.
did_you_know.en: The Isle of Man is generally thought to be named after the sea god Manannán, though some say the reverse.

long_description.id: 'Manannán atau Manann (Irlandia kuno Manandán), juga dikenal sebagai Manannán mac Lir (Mac Lirberarti "anak laut"), adalah dewa laut dalam mitologi Irlandia. Ia berafiliasi dengan Tuatha Dé Danann dan Fomorians.Dalam cerita, dia berkata memiliki perahu bernamaScuabtuinne("Penyapu Gelombang"), kereta yang berlayar di laut yang ditarik oleh kuda Enbarr, pedang yang kuat bernama Fragarach ("Penjawab"), dan jubah gaib (féth fíada). Ia dipandang sebagai 'the guardian of the Otherworld (penjaga dunia lain) dan salah satu yang membebaskan jiwa-jiwa ke alam baka. Manannán selanjutnya diidentifikasikan dengan sosok penipu dalam Bodach an Chóta Lachtna ("orang kikir dengan jubah yang menjemukan"). Manannán muncul juga di Skotlandia dan legenda Manx, dan beberapa sumber mengatakan Isle of Man (Manainn) dinamai dengan namanya, sementara yang lain mengatakan dia dinamai berdasarkan nama pulau. Dia serumpun dengan tokoh Welsh Manawydan fab Llŷr.
long_description.en: Manannán or Manann, also known as Manannán mac Lir ('son of the Sea'), is a sea god, warrior and king of the otherworld in Gaelic (Irish, Manx and Scottish) mythology who is one of the Tuatha Dé Danann. He is seen as a ruler and guardian of the otherworld and his dominion is referred by such names as Emain Ablach (or Emhain Abhlach, 'Isle of Apple Trees'), Mag Mell ('Plain of Delights'), or Tír Tairngire ('Land of Promise'). He is described as over-king of the surviving Tuatha Dé after the advent of humans (Milesians) and uses the mist of invisibility (féth fíada) to cloak the whereabouts of his home as well as the sidhe dwellings of the others. He is said to own a self-navigating boat named Sguaba Tuinne ('Wave-sweeper'), a horse Aonbharr which can course over water as well as land and a deadly strength-sapping sword named Fragarach, though the list does not end there. Manannán appears also in Scottish and Manx legend, where he is known as Manannan beg mac y Leir ('little Manannan, son of the Sea'). The Isle of Man (Mannin) is generally thought to be named after him, though some have said he is named after the island. He is cognate with the Welsh figure Manawydan fab Llŷr.

short_description.id: Manannán mac Lir ("anak laut") adalah dewa laut, pejuang, dan raja dunia lain dalam mitologi Gaelik, salah satu Tuatha Dé Danann.
short_description.en: Manannán mac Lir, whose surname means 'son of the Sea', is the Gaelic god of the sea, a warrior and lord of the otherworld, counted among the Tuatha Dé Danann.

long_description.id: Manannán atau Manann, juga Manannán mac Lir ("anak laut"), adalah dewa laut, pejuang, dan raja dunia lain dalam mitologi Gaelik (Gaelic) Irlandia, Man, dan Skotlandia, dan salah satu Tuatha Dé Danann. Ia penguasa dan penjaga dunia lain, yang disebut Emain Ablach ("Pulau Pohon Apel"), Mag Mell ("Dataran Kebahagiaan"), atau Tír Tairngire ("Negeri Perjanjian"). Setelah kedatangan manusia (kaum Milesia), ia menjadi raja atas Tuatha Dé yang tersisa dan memakai kabut gaib (féth fíada) untuk menyembunyikan kediamannya dan sidhe yang lain.
long_description.en: Manannán (or Manann), called Manannán mac Lir, 'son of the Sea', is the sea god, warrior and otherworld king of Irish, Manx and Scottish Gaelic myth, and belongs to the Tuatha Dé Danann. As lord and keeper of the otherworld, his realm goes by several names: Tír Tairngire, the 'Land of Promise'; Mag Mell, the 'Plain of Delights'; and Emain Ablach, the 'Isle of Apple Trees'. After the coming of humans (the Milesians) he became over-king of the remaining Tuatha Dé and uses the mist of invisibility (féth fíada) to hide his home and the other sidhe.

long_description.id: Ia memiliki perahu yang berlayar sendiri, Sguaba Tuinne ("Penyapu Ombak"), kuda Aonbharr yang dapat berlari di atas air dan darat, dan pedang mematikan Fragarach yang menguras kekuatan. Dalam legenda Skotlandia dan Man ia dikenal sebagai Manannan beg mac y Leir, dan Isle of Man (Mannin) umumnya dianggap dinamai menurutnya; ia sekerabat dengan tokoh Wales Manawydan fab Llŷr. Namanya dieja Manandán dalam bahasa Irlandia Kuno dan Mannan dalam bahasa Man. Menurut artikel id, ia dipandang sebagai penjaga dunia lain dan salah satu yang mengantar jiwa ke alam baka, dan juga dikenal sebagai Oirbsiu atau Oirbsen, asal nama Lough Corrib.
long_description.en: He owns a self-sailing boat, Sguaba Tuinne ('Wave-sweeper'), a horse, Aonbharr, that gallops across sea and land alike, and Fragarach, a lethal sword that drains an enemy's strength. In Scottish and Manx legend he is Manannan beg mac y Leir, and the Isle of Man (Mannin) is generally held to be named after him; he is cognate with the Welsh figure Manawydan fab Llŷr. His name is Manandán in Old Irish and Mannan in Manx. According to the id article he is seen as guardian of the otherworld and one who brings souls to the afterlife, and is also known as Oirbsiu or Oirbsen, from whom Lough Corrib takes its name.

He is described as over-king of the surviving Tuatha Dé after the advent of humans (Milesians) and uses the mist of invisibility (féth fíada) to cloak the whereabouts of his home as well as the sidhe dwellings of the others. He is said to own a self-navigating boat named Sguaba Tuinne ('Wave-sweeper'), a horse Aonbharr which can course over water as well as land and a deadly strength-sapping sword named Fragarach, though the list does not end there. Manannán appears also in Scottish and Manx legend, where he is known as Manannan beg mac y Leir ('little Manannan, son of the Sea'). The Isle of Man (Mannin) is generally thought to be named after him, though some have said he is named after the island. He is cognate with the Welsh figure Manawydan fab Llŷr.

short_description.id: Kurcaci Natal (Christmas elf) adalah elf kecil yang dalam budaya berbahasa Inggris tinggal bersama Sinterklas di Kutub Utara dan membantunya membuat mainan.
short_description.en: Christmas elves are diminutive elves that, in English-speaking cultures, live with Santa Claus at the North Pole and help him make toys.

long_description.id: Dalam budaya berbahasa Inggris (English-speaking), Christmas elves adalah elf kecil yang tinggal bersama Santa Claus (Sinterklas) di Kutub Utara (North Pole) dan menjadi pembantunya. Mereka biasanya digambarkan berpakaian hijau atau merah, bertelinga besar dan runcing, dan bertopi runcing; kebanyakan berwujud humanoid, kadang mamalia berbulu dan berekor. Mereka sering dikatakan membuat mainan di bengkel Santa dan merawat rusa kutubnya.
long_description.en: Across the English-speaking world, Christmas elves are tiny elves who serve as Santa Claus's assistants in his North Pole home. They are usually shown in green or red with large pointed ears and pointed hats; mostly humanoid, sometimes furry, tailed mammals. They are often said to make toys in Santa's workshop and to tend his reindeer.

long_description.id: Kaitan hadiah Natal (Christmas) dengan elf berakar pada nisse atau tomte Skandinavia pada paruh pertama abad ke-19, dan Saint Nicholas sendiri disebut elf dalam A Visit from St. Nicholas (1823): "a right jolly old elf". Gambaran elf di bengkel dipopulerkan Godey's Lady's Book lewat sampul edisi Natal 1873 yang menampilkan Santa dikelilingi mainan dan elf. Di Swedia, pada 1891 sang santo telah menyatu dengan Tomten, penjaga pertanian mirip elf atau kurcaci, dan lewat karya Jenny Nyström tokoh itu dikenal sebagai Jultomten. Menurut artikel id, kurcaci Natal dikenal dalam budaya Amerika, Kanada, Irlandia, dan Inggris.
long_description.en: The link between Christmas presents and elves has precedents in the Scandinavian nisse or tomte in the first half of the 19th century, while the 1823 poem A Visit from St. Nicholas even calls the saint "a right jolly old elf". The image of elves in a workshop was popularized by Godey's Lady's Book, whose 1873 Christmas cover showed Santa surrounded by toys and elves. In Sweden, by 1891 the saint had merged with Tomten, an elfish or dwarfish farm guardian, and through Jenny Nyström's work the figure became Jultomten. According to the id article, Christmas elves are known in American, Canadian, Irish and British culture.

short_description.id: Hobgoblin adalah roh rumah tangga dalam cerita rakyat Inggris, dahulu dianggap penolong tetapi sejak penyebaran Kristen sering dianggap jahil.
short_description.en: The hobgoblin is a household spirit of English folklore, once thought helpful but since the spread of Christianity often seen as mischievous.

long_description.id: Hobgoblin adalah roh rumah tangga dalam cerita rakyat Inggris (English folklore) yang dahulu dianggap suka menolong, tetapi sejak Kristen (Christianity) menyebar sering dipandang jahil. Shakespeare menyebut tokoh Puck dalam A Midsummer Night's Dream sebagai hobgoblin. Istilah ini berasal dari kata hob dan tercatat sekitar 1530. Menurut artikel fr, hobgoblin adalah makhluk legenda Britania (britannique) yang ramah dan kadang suka menolong, tinggal di rumah-rumah pedesaan; dalam cerita rakyat Inggris yang lebih kemudian ia kadang digambarkan sebagai roh jahat dan dicampuradukkan dengan goblin.
long_description.en: The hobgoblin is a household spirit of English folklore, once thought of as helpful but, after Christianity spread, often treated as a nuisance. Shakespeare names Puck in A Midsummer Night's Dream as a hobgoblin. The word grows out of hob and is recorded from around 1530. According to the fr article, the hobgoblin is a legendary British (britannique) creature, friendly and sometimes helpful, living in country homes; in later English folklore it is at times pictured as an evil spirit and confused with the goblin.

long_description.id: Hobgoblin tampaknya lelaki kecil berbulu yang, seperti kerabat dekatnya brownie, sering tinggal di rumah manusia dan mengerjakan tugas kecil seperti membersihkan debu dan menyetrika ketika keluarga tidur, cukup dengan imbalan makanan. Mereka lebih gemar bercanda daripada brownie, mudah tersinggung, dan bisa jahil, menakutkan, bahkan berbahaya; memberi mereka pakaian sering membuat mereka pergi untuk selamanya. Di Lancashire dan Yorkshire, menurut folklorist Elizabeth Mary Wright, hobgoblin juga disebut dobby. Menurut artikel fr, nama Hob mungkin berasal dari kata Wales (gallois) hob "melompat" atau kata Inggris hob "perapian", dan Hob juga nama kecil Robert/Robin yang mungkin mengaitkannya dengan Robin Goodfellow (Puck).
long_description.en: Hobgoblins seem to be small, hairy men who, like their close kin the brownies, often live in human houses and do small chores such as dusting and ironing while the family sleeps, usually paid only in food. They are fonder of pranks than brownies, quick to take offence and can be mischievous, frightening, even dangerous; giving them clothes often drives them away for good. In Lancashire and Yorkshire, according to folklorist Elizabeth Mary Wright, a hobgoblin is also called a dobby. According to the fr article, the name Hob may come from Welsh (gallois) hob 'to hop' or English hob 'hearth', and Hob is also a pet form of Robert/Robin, perhaps tying the hobgoblin to Robin Goodfellow (Puck).

short_description.id: Hobgoblin adalah roh rumah tangga dalam cerita rakyat Inggris, dahulu dianggap penolong tetapi sejak penyebaran Kristen sering dianggap jahil.
short_description.en: The hobgoblin is a household spirit of English folklore, once thought helpful but since the spread of Christianity often seen as mischievous.

long_description.id: Hobgoblin adalah roh rumah tangga dalam cerita rakyat Inggris (English folklore) yang dahulu dianggap suka menolong, tetapi sejak Kristen (Christianity) menyebar sering dipandang jahil. Shakespeare menyebut tokoh Puck dalam A Midsummer Night's Dream sebagai hobgoblin. Istilah ini berasal dari kata hob dan tercatat sekitar 1530. Menurut artikel fr, hobgoblin adalah makhluk legenda Britania (britannique) yang ramah dan kadang suka menolong, tinggal di rumah-rumah pedesaan; dalam cerita rakyat Inggris yang lebih kemudian ia kadang digambarkan sebagai roh jahat dan dicampuradukkan dengan goblin.
long_description.en: The hobgoblin is a household spirit of English folklore, once thought of as helpful but, after Christianity spread, often treated as a nuisance. Shakespeare names Puck in A Midsummer Night's Dream as a hobgoblin. The word grows out of hob and is recorded from around 1530. According to the fr article, the hobgoblin is a legendary British (britannique) creature, friendly and sometimes helpful, living in country homes; in later English folklore it is at times pictured as an evil spirit and confused with the goblin.

long_description.id: Hobgoblin tampaknya lelaki kecil berbulu yang, seperti kerabat dekatnya brownie, sering tinggal di rumah manusia dan mengerjakan tugas kecil seperti membersihkan debu dan menyetrika ketika keluarga tidur, cukup dengan imbalan makanan. Mereka lebih gemar bercanda daripada brownie, mudah tersinggung, dan bisa jahil, menakutkan, bahkan berbahaya; memberi mereka pakaian sering membuat mereka pergi untuk selamanya. Di Lancashire dan Yorkshire, menurut folklorist Elizabeth Mary Wright, hobgoblin juga disebut dobby. Menurut artikel fr, nama Hob mungkin berasal dari kata Wales (gallois) hob "melompat" atau kata Inggris hob "perapian", dan Hob juga nama kecil Robert/Robin yang mungkin mengaitkannya dengan Robin Goodfellow (Puck).
long_description.en: Hobgoblins seem to be small, hairy men who, like their close kin the brownies, often live in human houses and do small chores such as dusting and ironing while the family sleeps, usually paid only in food. They are fonder of pranks than brownies, quick to take offence and can be mischievous, frightening, even dangerous; giving them clothes often drives them away for good. In Lancashire and Yorkshire, according to folklorist Elizabeth Mary Wright, a hobgoblin is also called a dobby. According to the fr article, the name Hob may come from Welsh (gallois) hob 'to hop' or English hob 'hearth', and Hob is also a pet form of Robert/Robin, perhaps tying the hobgoblin to Robin Goodfellow (Puck).

short_description.id: Elf adalah makhluk peri dari cerita rakyat European dan mitologi Norse; gambaran mereka berubah dari sosok ambigu dalam tradisi lama menjadi tokoh fantasi yang lebih seragam.
short_description.en: Elves are fairy beings of European folklore and Norse myth; their older ambiguous portrayal differs from more standardized modern fantasy versions.

long_description.id: Dalam sumber Norse, elf atau álfar disebut bersama dewa dalam puisi, tetapi kisah pribadi mereka jarang dicatat. Mereka dikaitkan dengan keterampilan, pembuatan benda berharga, dan sifat yang tidak selalu baik atau jahat. Batas antara elf, kurcaci, dan makhluk lain dalam sumber lama tidak selalu tegas.
long_description.en: In Norse sources, elves or álfar accompany gods in poetry, but individual stories about them are scarce. They are linked with skill, precious crafts, and moral ambiguity. Boundaries among elves, dwarves, and other beings were not always firm in older sources.

long_description.id: Snorri membedakan elf terang di Alfheim dari elf gelap yang terkait tanah, meski hubungannya dengan kurcaci diperdebatkan. Wayland atau Völund adalah tokoh elf pandai besi yang kisah balas dendamnya muncul dalam Poetic Edda. Teks pengobatan lama juga mengaitkan elf dengan penyakit, sehingga mereka tidak hanya digambarkan ramah.
long_description.en: Snorri distinguishes light elves in Alfheim from dark elves linked to the ground, though their relation to dwarves is debated. Wayland or Völund is an elven smith whose revenge story appears in the Poetic Edda. Older medical writings also associate elves with illness, so they were not always portrayed as friendly.

long_description.id: Sebuah wawancara menempatkan elf dan peri dalam sejarah budaya European serta menyoroti pengaruh sastra modern yang membentuk elf sebagai makhluk kuat. Ringkasan penelitian mencatat bahwa penulis gereja medieval pernah menggolongkan mereka sebagai demon, sedangkan telinga runcing khas fantasi modern tidak jelas berasal dari tradisi awal.
long_description.en: An interview places elves and fairies in European cultural history and describes modern literature's role in portraying elves as powerful. A research abstract notes that medieval church writers sometimes categorized them as demons, while pointed ears characteristic of modern fantasy are not securely an early trait.

long_description.en: An elf (pl. elves) is a type of humanoid supernatural being in Germanic folklore. Elves appear especially in North Germanic mythology, being mentioned in the Icelandic Poetic Edda and the Prose Edda. In medieval Germanic-speaking cultures, elves were thought of as beings with magical powers and supernatural beauty, ambivalent towards everyday people, and capable of either helping or hindering them. Beliefs varied considerably over time and space and flourished in both pre-Christian and Christian cultures. The word elf is found throughout the Germanic languages. It seems originally to have meant 'white being'. However, reconstructing the early concept depends largely on texts written by Christians, in Old and Middle English, medieval German, and Old Norse. These associate elves variously with the gods of Norse mythology, with causing illness, with magic, and with beauty and seduction. After the medieval period, the word elf became less common throughout the Germanic languages, losing out to terms like Zwerg ('dwarf') in German and huldra ('hidden being') in North Germanic languages, and to loan-words like fairy (borrowed from French). Still, belief in elves persisted in the early modern period, particularly in Scotland and Scandinavia, where elves were thought of as magically powerful people living, usually invisibly, alongside human communities. They continued to be associated with causing illnesses and with sexual threats. For example, several early modern ballads in the British Isles and Scandinavia, originating in the medieval period, describe elves attempting to seduce or abduct human characters. With modern urbanisation and industrialisation, belief in elves declined rapidly, though Iceland has some claim to continued popular belief. Elves started to be prominent in the literature and art of educated elites from the early modern period onwards. These literary elves were imagined as tiny, playful beings, with William Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream a key development of this idea. In the eighteenth century, German Romantic writers were influenced by this notion of the elf, and re-imported the English word elf into the German language. From the Romantic notion came the elves of modern popular culture. Christmas elves are a relatively recent creation, popularized during the late 19th century in the United States. Elves entered the twentieth-century high fantasy genre in the wake of J. R. R. Tolkien's works; these re-popularised the idea of elves as human-sized and humanlike beings. Elves remain a prominent feature of fantasy media today.

short_description.id: Obake adalah istilah Jepang bagi makhluk gaib atau penampakan yang berkaitan dengan perubahan bentuk.
short_description.en: Obake is a Japanese term for supernatural beings or apparitions associated with transformation.

long_description.id: Obake bukan nama satu makhluk, melainkan sebutan bagi kelompok penampakan atau yōkai. Makna harfiahnya berkaitan dengan sesuatu yang berubah; terjemahan Inggris dapat berupa hantu, monster, atau penampakan. Sumber museum menyebut cakupannya luas: benda rumah tangga yang hidup, hewan berkekuatan gaib, setan, dan roh pendendam. Dalam penjelasan Japan Society, manusia, hewan, bahkan benda yang ditinggalkan dapat menjadi obake; contoh benda itu disebut tsukumogami.
long_description.en: Obake is a category, not the name of one creature. Its literal sense relates to something transformed; English renderings include ghost, monster, or apparition. A museum account gives a broad range: animated household objects, supernatural animals, demons, and vengeful spirits. Japan Society explains that people, animals, and abandoned objects can become obake; the object type is called tsukumogami.

long_description.id: Luasnya pemakaian kata ini membuatnya sukar dipadankan tepat dengan satu golongan makhluk. Sebuah kajian bahasa menempatkan obake dan bakemono sebagai istilah Jepang untuk golongan yōkai yang terkait perubahan wujud. Museum menerangkan makhluk seperti itu sudah lama hadir dalam lukisan, cetakan, ukiran netsuke, dan panggung kabuki; cetakan yang dibahasnya berasal dari pertengahan abad ke-19. Japan Society juga mencatat bahwa dalam pemakaian masa kini kata obake bisa merujuk lebih luas pada sosok seram, termasuk gambaran horor yang datang dari luar Jepang.
long_description.en: The word’s broad use makes it difficult to match with one fixed creature class. A language study places obake and bakemono among Japanese terms for yōkai associated with transformation. A museum notes depictions in paintings, prints, netsuke carvings, and kabuki, including mid-nineteenth-century prints. Japan Society also reports broader current use of obake for spooky figures, including imported horror imagery.

long_description.id: Obake (お化け) atau bakemono (化け物) adalah sejenis yōkai dalam cerita rakyat Jepang. Arti harfiah dari kata obake adalah sesuatu yang sangat besar atau sesuatu yang bentuknya aneh. Istilah bakemono sering diterjemahkan dalam kamus sebagai hantu atau setan, tetapi istilah ini umumnya dipakai untuk makhluk hidup atau makhluk supranatural yang dapat melakukan transformasi untuk sementara. Oleh karena itu, bakemono berbeda dari arwah orang mati. Meskipun demikian, istilah obake juga sinonim dengan yūrei atau hantu dari arwah orang yang telah meninggal dunia. Bentuk sebenarnya bakemono dapat berupa hewan seperti rubah (kitsune), anjing rakun (tanuki), musang (mujina), kucing yang dapat mengubah bentuk (bakeneko), arwah tumbuh-tumbuhan kodama, atau benda mati yang dipercaya memiliki arwah dalam kepercayaan Shinto dan tradisi animisme lainnya. Obake yang berasal dari perabot rumah tangga disebut tsukumogami. Bakemono biasanya menyamar sebagai manusia atau muncul sebagai bentuk yang aneh atau menakutkan, seperti halnya seorang hitotsume-kozō, ōnyūdō, atau makhluk berwajah datar tanpa mata, hidung, dan mulut (noppera-bō). Semua penampakan yang menakutkan umumnya dapat disebut bakemono atau obake, tanpa memandang apakah subjek tersebut dapat berubah menjadi bentuk lain atau tidak. Oleh karena itu, bakemono secara garis besar sering disamakan dengan yōkai.
long_description.en: Obake (お化け) and bakemono (化け物) are a class of yōkai, preternatural creatures in Japanese folklore. Literally, the terms mean a thing that changes, referring to a state of transformation or shapeshifting. These words are often translated as "ghost", but primarily they refer to living things or supernatural beings who have taken on a temporary transformation, and these bakemono are distinct from the spirits of the dead. However, as a secondary usage, the term obake can be a synonym for yūrei, the ghost of a deceased human being. A bakemono's true form may be an animal such as a fox (kitsune), a raccoon dog (bake-danuki), a badger (mujina), a transforming cat (bakeneko), the spirit of a plant—such as a kodama, or an inanimate object which may possess a soul in Shinto. Obake derived from household objects are often called tsukumogami. A bakemono usually either disguises itself as a human or appears in a strange or terrifying form such as a hitotsume-kozō, an ōnyūdō, or a noppera-bō. In common usage, any bizarre apparition can be referred to as a bakemono or an obake whether it is believed to have some other form, making the terms roughly synonymous with yōkai.

short_description.id: Ubume adalah roh ibu yang meninggal saat melahirkan dan dalam cerita meminta orang lain menggendong bayinya.
short_description.en: Ubume is the spirit of a mother who died in childbirth and asks others to hold her baby in stories.

long_description.id: Ubume adalah sosok gaib yang paling sering digambarkan sebagai roh perempuan yang meninggal saat melahirkan. Ceritanya memiliki rupa dan identitas yang berbeda-beda. Dalam satu pola kisah, ia tampak seperti perempuan biasa yang menggendong bayi, meminta pejalan kaki memegang anak itu, lalu menghilang. Setelah itu, bayi tersebut ternyata hanya seikat daun atau sebongkah batu. Penjelasan dari kalangan museum juga memasukkan ibu yang meninggalkan anak kecil sebagai bagian dari gambaran ubume.
long_description.en: Ubume is a supernatural figure most often described as the spirit of a woman who died in childbirth. Her identity and appearance vary across stories. In one common pattern she looks like an ordinary woman with a baby, asks a passerby to hold the child, and disappears. The apparent baby turns out to be leaves or a rock. A museum lecture also includes women who left behind young children in its account of ubume.

long_description.id: Ubume dapat disebut yōkai maupun hantu ibu. Kisahnya berkaitan dengan pandangan sosial dan agama tentang persalinan serta kehilangan ibu. Sebuah ringkasan perpustakaan universitas menyebut bahwa pada akhir abad pertengahan, sebagian masyarakat menganggap kematian ibu saat hamil atau melahirkan sebagai dosa dan menyalahkan ibu atas kematian janin. Pengertian itu adalah sikap masa lampau yang dicatat sebagai latar kepercayaan, bukan penilaian atas ibu yang meninggal. Dalam pembahasan seni, kisah hantu, lukisan ukiyo-e, dan kabuki dipandang sebagai media yang mengembangkan tema hantu perempuan.
long_description.en: Ubume may be called both a yōkai and a mother ghost. Her tales are connected with social and religious views about childbirth and maternal loss. A university library summary says that in the late medieval period some people viewed a mother’s death in late pregnancy or childbirth as a sin and blamed her for a fetus’s death. That is a historical attitude reported as context, not a judgment on mothers who died. An art lecture notes that ghost tales, ukiyo-e painting, and kabuki developed ghost themes.

long_description.en: Ubume (Japanese: 産女) (also ubumedori (姑獲鳥) or ubumetori (産女鳥)) are Japanese yōkai, ghosts of women who died in childbirth, but may have borne a child alive. short_description.id: Ubume adalah roh ibu yang meninggal saat melahirkan dan dalam cerita meminta orang lain menggendong bayinya.
short_description.en: Ubume is the spirit of a mother who died in childbirth and asks others to hold her baby in stories.

long_description.id: Ubume adalah sosok gaib yang paling sering digambarkan sebagai roh perempuan yang meninggal saat melahirkan. Ceritanya memiliki rupa dan identitas yang berbeda-beda. Dalam satu pola kisah, ia tampak seperti perempuan biasa yang menggendong bayi, meminta pejalan kaki memegang anak itu, lalu menghilang. Setelah itu, bayi tersebut ternyata hanya seikat daun atau sebongkah batu. Penjelasan dari kalangan museum juga memasukkan ibu yang meninggalkan anak kecil sebagai bagian dari gambaran ubume.
long_description.en: Ubume is a supernatural figure most often described as the spirit of a woman who died in childbirth. Her identity and appearance vary across stories. In one common pattern she looks like an ordinary woman with a baby, asks a passerby to hold the child, and disappears. The apparent baby turns out to be leaves or a rock. A museum lecture also includes women who left behind young children in its account of ubume.

long_description.id: Ubume dapat disebut yōkai maupun hantu ibu. Kisahnya berkaitan dengan pandangan sosial dan agama tentang persalinan serta kehilangan ibu. Sebuah ringkasan perpustakaan universitas menyebut bahwa pada akhir abad pertengahan, sebagian masyarakat menganggap kematian ibu saat hamil atau melahirkan sebagai dosa dan menyalahkan ibu atas kematian janin. Pengertian itu adalah sikap masa lampau yang dicatat sebagai latar kepercayaan, bukan penilaian atas ibu yang meninggal. Dalam pembahasan seni, kisah hantu, lukisan ukiyo-e, dan kabuki dipandang sebagai media yang mengembangkan tema hantu perempuan.
long_description.en: Ubume may be called both a yōkai and a mother ghost. Her tales are connected with social and religious views about childbirth and maternal loss. A university library summary says that in the late medieval period some people viewed a mother’s death in late pregnancy or childbirth as a sin and blamed her for a fetus’s death. That is a historical attitude reported as context, not a judgment on mothers who died. An art lecture notes that ghost tales, ukiyo-e painting, and kabuki developed ghost themes.

short_description.id: Korpokkur adalah kaum kecil dalam cerita rakyat Ainu yang dikaitkan dengan naungan daun butterbur.
short_description.en: Korpokkur are little people in Ainu folklore associated with shelter beneath butterbur leaves.

long_description.id: Korpokkur, juga ditulis koropokkur, adalah kaum kecil dalam cerita rakyat Ainu di kepulauan utara. Sebuah uraian folklor menyebut mereka hidup di lubang beratap daun butterbur, pandai memancing, dan pernah bertukar hasil buruan atau ikan dengan orang Ainu. Dalam kisah itu mereka enggan terlihat dan meninggalkan pemberian pada malam hari. Seorang lelaki muda kemudian menangkap tangan salah satu dari mereka untuk melihatnya; setelah peristiwa itu kaum korpokkur dikisahkan tidak terlihat lagi. Ini adalah cerita asal-usul dalam folklor, bukan keterangan sejarah tentang suatu populasi yang terbukti ada.
long_description.en: Korpokkur, also spelled koropokkur, are little people in the folklore of the Ainu of northern islands. One account says they lived in pits roofed with butterbur leaves, fished well, and exchanged game or fish with Ainu people. In that tale they avoided being seen and left gifts at night. A young man then grabbed one by the hand to see it, after which the korpokkur were said to disappear from view. This is a folkloric account, not a confirmed history of a real population.

long_description.id: Hubungan dengan daun butterbur masih terlihat dalam representasi modern: sebuah museum seni menampilkan lukisan tahun 1977 berjudul Little Korpokkur Under the Butterbur Leaves sebagai bagian seri lukisan yang berangkat dari sastra lisan Ainu. Karya seni tersebut menunjukkan kelanjutan penggambaran korpokkur, tetapi tidak membuktikan ciri fisik atau tempat tinggal mereka sebagai fakta sejarah.
long_description.en: The association with butterbur leaves remains visible in modern representations: an art museum displayed a 1977 painting titled Little Korpokkur Under the Butterbur Leaves within a series based on Ainu oral literature. The painting shows continued representation of korpokkur, not evidence that their size or dwelling was a historical fact.

long_description.en: The Korpokkur (Ainu: コㇿポックㇽ; Japanese: コロポックル, romanized: Koropokkuru), also written Koro-pok-kuru, korobokkuru, korbokkur, or koropokkur, koro-pok-guru, are a race of little people in folklore of the Ainu people of the northern Japanese islands. The Ainu believe that the korpokkur were the people who lived in the Ainu land before the Ainu themselves lived there. They were short of stature, agile, and skilled at fishing. They lived in pits with roofs made from butterbur leaves. Long ago, the korpokkur were on good terms with the Ainu, and would send them deer, fish, and other game and exchange goods with them. The little people hated to be seen, however, so they would stealthily make their deliveries under the cover of night. One day, a young Ainu man decided he wanted to see a korpokkur for himself, so he waited in ambush by the window where their gifts were usually left. When a korpokkur came to place something there, the young man grabbed it by the hand and dragged it inside. It turned out to be a beautiful korpokkur woman, who was so enraged at the young man's rudeness that her people have not been seen since. Their pits, pottery, and stone implements, the Ainu believe, still remain scattered about the landscape.

long_description.id: Gagoze (Jepang: 元興寺), juga memiliki sebutan lain Gangōji no Oni, Gagoji, Guwagoze, atau Gangō adalah salah satu yokai yang berwujud hantu iblis. Menurut cerita rakyat Jepang, cerita tentang yokai ini muncul berabad-abad yang lalu di Gangō-ji, sebuah kuil di Nara. Ia dideskripsikan sebagai iblis mengerikan yang mengenakan jubah biarawan dan merangkak dengan keempat kakinya. Legendanya disimpan di Kuil Gangō yang didirikan pada tahun 593 oleh Soga no Umako. Gagoze dahulunya merupakan seorang pelayan kuil dengan kepribadiannya yang malas dan jahat. Kisah hantu Gagoze berasal dari teks abad ke-9 yang berjudul Nihon Ryoiki (Catatan Kejadian Hantu Aneh di Jepang).
long_description.en: Gagoze (元興寺), also gagoji, guwagoze, gangō, and gangōji no oni (元興寺の鬼, the oni of gangōji) is a yōkai said to have appeared at Gangō-ji in the Nara Prefecture around the Asuka period. It can also be found in the text of the Heian period Nihon Ryōiki (in the story, 雷の憙を得て生ま令めし子の強き力在る縁," On a Boy of Great Strength Who Was Born of the Thunder’s Rejoicing"), the Honchō Monzui, among others. In classical yōkai drawings such as the Gazu Hyakki Yagyō by Toriyama Sekien, it is depicted as an oni with the appearance of a monk.

long_description.id: Versi yaksha dapat berupa roh alam yang tidak berbahaya atau hantu yang menghadang dan memangsa pelancong. long_description.id: Yaksa (Dewanagari: यक्ष; ,IAST: Yakṣa,; Pali: [yakha] Galat: {{Lang}}: text has italic markup (bantuan)) adalah roh-roh alam yang biasanya baik hati tetapi kadang-kadang usilan atau angin-anginan, dan dikait-kaitkan dengan air, kesuburan, pohon, hutan, harta benda, serta alam liar. Yaksa disebut-sebut di dalam kesusastraan agama Hindu, Jaina, dan Buddha, serta dicitrakan di kuil-kuil Asia Selatan dan Asia Tenggara dari abad kuno maupun abad madya sebagai dewa pelindung. Bentuk feminin dari yaksa adalah "yaksi" atau yaksini (Sanskerta: यक्षिणी, yakṣiṇī; Pali: [yakhini] Galat: {{Lang}}: text has italic markup (bantuan)). Penggambarannya di dalam kesusastraan agama Hindu, Jaina, dan Buddha membuat yakṣa terkesan berkepribadian ganda. Yakṣa dapat disifatkan sebagai peri penunggu hutan atau gunung, tetapi dapat pula disifatkan sebagai butakala, dedemit alam liar yang suka menghadang dan memangsa manusia yang kebetulan lewat, mirip dengan rakṣasa.
long_description.en: The Yakshas (Sanskrit: यक्ष, IAST: Yakṣa, Pali: Yakkha) are a broad class of nature spirits in Hindu mythology which are associated with water, trees, forests, wilderness, treasure, and fertility. They are usually considered benevolent, and sometimes mischievous or capricious. They appear in Hindu, Jain and Buddhist texts, as well as ancient and medieval temples of South Asia and Southeast Asia as guardian deities. The feminine form of the word is IAST: Yakṣī or Yakshini (Sanskrit: यक्षिणी, IAST: Yakṣiṇī; Pali: Yakkhini). In Hindu, Jain and Buddhist texts, the yakṣas have a dual personality. A yakṣa may be an inoffensive nature spirit associated with woods and mountains, or a darker version of the yakṣa which is a kind of Bhoota (ghost) that haunts the wilderness and waylays and devours travellers, similar to the rakṣasas. A unique cultural dance form related to the Yakshas is Yakshagana. Yakshagana is a traditional stage performance, found in Dakshina Kannada, Udupi, Kasaragod district and Uttara Kannada, Shimoga and western Chikmagalur districts, in the state of Karnataka.

long_description.id: Gandarwa (Dewanagari: गन्धर्व; ,IAST: gandharva, गन्धर्व) adalah golongan makhluk gaib (supernatural) berwujud seperti manusia berjenis kelamin pria yang tinggal di kahyangan atau surga dalam kepercayaan agama Hindu dan Buddha. Dalam kepercayaan tersebut, ada juga makhluk gaib yang disebut dengan nama Bidadara, fungsinya sebagai pembawa pesan dari dewa, sedangkan Gandarwa lebih merujuk kepada tugasnya sebagai pemusik surgawi. Tugas dan fungsi mereka adalah menjadi penyampai pesan para dewa kepada manusia, sebagai pemusik surgawi dan penjaga swargaloka, sebagaimana para malaikat dalam agama Islam, Kristen, dan Yahudi.
long_description.en: A gandharva (Sanskrit: गन्धर्व) is a member of a class of celestial beings in Indian religions, such as Hinduism, Buddhism, and Jainism, whose males are divine performers such as musicians and singers, and the females are divine dancers. In Hinduism, they are regarded to be the celestial demigods who serve as the musicians of the devas. It is also a term for skilled singers in Indian classical music. In Buddhism, this term also refers to a being in the intermediate state (between death and rebirth).

long_description.id: Ganesha dan Ganapati berarti penguasa atau pemimpin para gana. Mereka disebut Shivagana atau Rudragana dan padanan perempuan disebut Rudraganika. Shiva Purana mengisahkan penobatan Ganesha setelah Shiva menghidupkannya kembali. LACMA menggambarkan gana sebagai sosok kerdil gemuk yang menari dan memainkan musik untuk Shiva serta Parvati.
long_description.en: Ganesha and Ganapati mean lord or leader of the ganas. They are called Shivaganas or Rudraganas and female equivalents Rudraganikas. The Shiva Purana recounts Ganesha's coronation after Shiva restores his life. LACMA describes ganas as rotund gnomes dancing and playing music for Shiva and Parvati.

long_description.id: Gana (Dewanagari: गण; ,IAST: Gaṇa, गण) adalah suatu kata dalam bahasa Sanskerta dan Pali yang berarti "gerombolan, pasukan, rombongan, kumpulan, kelompok, himpunan, rangkaian, atau kelas". Kata itu juga dapat diartikan "sekelompok pengikut/pelayan" atau "sebuah perkumpulan yang dibentuk demi mencapai suatu tujuan". Kata gana juga dapat merujuk kepada majelis atau dewan dalam hal urusan keagamaan atau topik lainnya. Dalam kepercayaan Hindu, para Gaṇa adalah pengikut sekaligus pelayan Dewa Siwa dan tinggal di Gunung Kailash. Putra Siwa yang berkepala gajah dipilih olehnya sebagai pemimpin mereka. Itulah sebabnya putra Siwa tersebut diberi nama Ganesa atau Ganapati, yang secara harfiah berarti "pemimpin para gana".
long_description.en: In Hinduism, the Gaṇas are attendants of Shiva and live on Mount Kailash. Ganesha was chosen as their leader by Shiva; the deity's title is gaṇeśa or gaṇapati, meaning, "lord or leader of the ganas". They are referred to as Shivaganas or Rudraganas and Rudraganikas are considered the female equivalents. The word gaṇa (Sanskrit: गण Sanskrit pronunciation: [ɡɐ.ɳɐ́]) in Sanskrit and Pali means "flock, troop, multitude, number, tribe, category, series, or clan". It can also be used to refer to a "body of attendants" and can refer to "a company, any assemblage or association of men formed for the attainment of the same aims". The word "gana" can also refer to councils or assemblies convened to discuss matters of religion or other topics.

long_description.id: Vidyadhara adalah golongan makhluk gaib agama India yang memiliki kekuatan sihir. Dalam Hindu mereka mengiringi Shiva dan digolongkan sebagai setengah dewa.
long_description.en: Vidyadharas are a class of Indian religious supernatural beings possessing magical powers. In Hinduism they attend Shiva and are considered demigods.

long_description.id: Epos Hindu menggambarkan mereka sebagai roh udara yang menabur bunga dan bergembira dengan musik. Mereka memiliki kekuatan untuk mengecilkan ukuran tubuh. Narasi Jain menggambarkan mereka sebagai garis keturunan manusia atau semi-ilahi dengan ilmu atau kekuatan vidya. Catatan terjemahan Ramayana Griffith menempatkan Vidyadhara bersama Siddha di udara antara bumi dan matahari.
long_description.en: Hindu epics depict them as air spirits scattering flowers and rejoicing with music. They have powers to diminish their size. Jain narratives describe them as human or semidivine lineages with vidya sciences or powers. Griffith's Ramayana translation note places Vidyadharas with Siddhas in the air between earth and sun.

long_description.id: Bidadara (Dewanagari: विद्याधर; ,IAST: Vidyādhara,; artinya "pembawa kebijaksanaan") adalah sejenis makhluk supernatural dalam mitologi Hindu dan Buddha. Mereka memiliki kekuatan magis dan tinggal di pegunungan Himalaya. Mereka juga merupakan abdi dewa Siwa, yang juga bersemayam di Himalaya. Mereka dianggap sebagai Upadewa, atau dewa tingkatan rendah. Dalam kepercayaan Hindu-Buddha Indonesia, Bidadara cenderung dianggap berjenis kelamin pria, sedangkan pasangannya yang berjenis kelamin perempuan disebut bidadari (vidyādhari), atau sering kali disamakan dengan Apsara. Tugas dan fungsi mereka adalah menjadi penyampai pesan para dewa kepada manusia.

short_description.en: Manohara is a kinnari, a bird woman, and heroine of a Jataka tale.

long_description.id: Manohara adalah kinnari, perempuan-burung, tokoh utama kisah Jataka. Kisahnya muncul dalam Pannasa Jataka, Divyavadana, dan relief Borobudur.
long_description.en: Manohara is a kinnari, a bird woman, and heroine of a Jataka tale. Her story appears in the Pannasa Jataka, Divyavadana, and Borobudur reliefs.

long_description.id: Ia merupakan putri termuda dari tujuh putri raja Kinnara yang tinggal di Kailash. Seorang pemburu menangkapnya dan memberikannya kepada Sudhana, yang kemudian menikahinya. Ketika dituduh membawa kesialan dan diancam mati, ia terbang pulang dan meninggalkan cincin serta petunjuk bagi Sudhana. Sonobudoyo menjelaskan Manohara pada relief Borobudur digambarkan sebagai manusia utuh menyerupai bidadari.
long_description.en: She is the youngest of the Kinnara king's seven daughters living on Kailash. A hunter captures her and gives her to Sudhana, who later marries her. When accused of bringing misfortune and threatened with death she flies home, leaving a ring and directions for Sudhana. Sonobudoyo explains that Manohara on Borobudur reliefs is depicted as a complete human resembling an angel.

claims.quote: Manohara, the youngest of seven daughters of the Kimnara king, lives on Mount Kailash. One day, she travels to the human realm. She is caught by a hunter (using a magic noose in some versions) who gives her to Prince Sudhana. Son of King Adityavamsa and Queen Chandradevi, Sudhana is a renowned archer and heir to the Panchala kingdom.

long_description.id: Manohara (Dewanagari: मनोहरा; ,IAST: Manoharā, मनोहरा) adalah nama salah satu makhluk setengah manusia setengah burung (kinnara) dalam kisah jataka dalam mitologi Buddha. Menurut kisah, ia menikah dengan seorang pangeran manusia yang bernama Sudhana. Relief yang melukiskan kisah Manohara terdapat pada candi Borobudur.
long_description.en: Manoharā (Pali: "captivating", "heart-stealing") or Manoharī is the kinnari (half-woman, half-bird) heroine of one of the Jataka tales. Typically referred to as Manohara and Prince Sudhana, the legend appears in the Paññāsa Jātaka, Divyavadana and is documented by stone reliefs at Borobodur. Versions of the story are reported in the literature of Southeast Asian countries, and similar stories about a bird maiden and a mortal man can also be found in East Asia and other parts of the world.

long_description.en: An Acheri is a spirit of a young girl in the folklore of the southern Himalayas, specifically regions around Kumaon. They often dwell on top of mountains during the day and come down at dusk to hold revel. They are not peaceful, as to come across them, during a revel, could lead to death or molestation. long_description.en: In Hindu and Jain traditions, the muṇḍana ceremony marks a boy's entry into formal education, involving the tying of a sacred thread around the torso and a girdle made of munja grass around the waist, typically at the age of seven. He is known as Munjya when he puts on the munja grass girdle. According to folklore in Maharashtra and the Konkan coast, Munjya is believed to be the ghosts of boys who died after this ceremony but before marriage, inhabiting peepal trees. Munjya's are described as restless bachelor ghosts who roam trees at night, possessing cleverness and multilingual abilities. While most Munjya's are not harmful, they may retaliate against those who defile their tree homes, potentially pelting offenders with stones or causing accidents. Some stories depict more malevolent Munjya's causing harm to humans, such as causing accidents or possessing living beings with dangerous intentions, including forcing them to commit acts of violence. One feasible rationale for the belief in Munjya is that peepal trees, known for their expansive canopies, emit substantial carbon dioxide during the night. The apprehension surrounding Munjya probably deterred individuals from lingering under these trees after dusk.

short_description.id: Korrigan adalah roh peri atau mirip kerdil dalam cerita rakyat Breton, yang dalam sebagian kisah berupa perempuan peri penghuni mata air yang memikat lelaki menuju kematian.
short_description.en: The korrigan is a fairy or dwarf-like spirit of Breton folklore, in some accounts a siren-like female fairy of springs who lures men to their deaths.

long_description.id: Dalam cerita rakyat Breton (Breton folklore), Korrigan adalah roh peri atau mirip kerdil. Kata korrigan dalam bahasa Breton berarti "kerdil kecil" (korr "kerdil", ig pengecil, an akhiran sayang). Namanya berbeda-beda menurut tempat. Théodore de Villemarqué dalam Barzaz Breiz memakai istilah itu bergantian dengan "peri" dan membedakannya dari kerdil, sedangkan Walter Evans-Wentz dalam The Fairy Faith in Celtic Countries berpendapat bahwa di Morbihan tak ada pembedaan jelas antara korrigan dan kerdil.
long_description.en: In Breton folklore a Korrigan is a fairy or dwarfish spirit. In Breton the word means 'small dwarf' (korr dwarf, ig a diminutive, an an affectionate ending). Its name varies from place to place. Théodore de Villemarqué, in Barzaz Breiz, uses the word interchangeably with 'fairy' and sets them apart from dwarves, while Walter Evans-Wentz in The Fairy Faith in Celtic Countries held that Morbihan lore draws no clear line between korrigans and dwarves.

long_description.id: Penulis lain memakai istilah ini hanya untuk peri perempuan mirip siren yang menghuni mata air dan sungai, sangat cantik saat senja atau malam tetapi pada siang hari bermata merah, berambut putih, dan berkulit keriput. Mereka kadang digambarkan sebagai putri atau druid perempuan yang menentang Kristen (Christianity) ketika para Rasul datang ke Brittany. Mereka dapat meramal, berubah wujud, dan bergerak secepat kilat; seperti siren mereka bernyanyi dan menyisir rambut panjang, membuat lelaki jatuh cinta lalu membunuhnya, dan suka mencuri anak manusia serta menggantinya dengan changeling. Menurut artikel de, mereka juga dikatakan dapat menyembuhkan penyakit yang tak tersembuhkan.
long_description.en: Other writers keep the name for siren-like female fairies of springs and rivers, lovely at dusk or night but by day red-eyed, white-haired and wrinkled. They are sometimes cast as princesses or druidesses who resisted Christianity when the Apostles came to convert Brittany. They foretell the future, change shape and move like lightning; like sirens they sing and comb their long hair, make men love them and then kill them, and like to steal human children, leaving changelings. According to the de article they are also said to cure otherwise incurable illnesses.

role.en: Lovely by night, wrinkled by day.

long_description.en: In Breton folklore, a Korrigan (pronounced [kɔˈriːɡãn]) is a fairy or dwarf-like spirit. The word korrigan means in Breton "small-dwarf" (korr means dwarf, ig is a diminutive and the suffix an is a hypocoristic). It is closely related to the Cornish word korrik which means gnome. The name changes according to the place. Among the other names, there are korrig, korred, korrs, kores, couril, crion, goric, kornandon, ozigan, nozigan, teuz, torrigan, viltañs, poulpikan, poulpiquet, and paotred ar sabad.

long_description.id: Gandalf, dalam bahasa Nordik Kuno Gandálfr, adalah seorang dvergr atau kurcaci dalam mitologi Nordik. Namanya muncul dalam apa yang disebut "Daftar Para Kurcaci" di puisi Völuspá dari Edda Puisi, serta dalam Edda Prosa.
long_description.en: Gandalf, Old Norse Gandálfr, is a dvergr or dwarf in Norse mythology. His name appears in the so-called 'Tally of the Dwarves' in the poem Völuspá of the Poetic Edda, and in the Prose Edda.

long_description.id: Namanya berasal dari kata Nordik Kuno gandr, entitas gaib seperti tongkat sihir, dan álfr, "elf", sehingga dapat dimaknai roh pelindung yang memegang tongkat sihir. Nama yang sama juga dipakai untuk seorang raja Nordik dalam Heimskringla.
long_description.en: His name comes from Old Norse gandr, a magical entity such as a wand, and álfr, 'elf', so it can be read as a protective spirit wielding a magic wand. The same name was also borne by a Norse king in the Heimskringla.

long_description.id: J. R. R. Tolkien kemudian menamai tokoh penyihirnya Gandalf menurut kurcaci ini, setelah semula memakai nama itu untuk pemimpin rombongan kurcaci yang akhirnya bernama Thorin Oakenshield.
long_description.en: J. R. R. Tolkien later named his wizard Gandalf after this dwarf, having first used the name for the leader of the dwarf party who was finally called Thorin Oakenshield.

short_description.id: Belsnickel adalah sosok pembawa hadiah Natal berbaju bulu dalam cerita rakyat Pfalz dan sekitarnya di Jerman, yang memberi kue kepada anak baik dan memukul anak nakal dengan ranting.
short_description.en: Belsnickel is a fur-clad Christmas gift-bringer of the folklore of the Palatinate and neighbouring areas of Germany, giving treats to good children and switching naughty ones.

long_description.id: Belsnickel, juga disebut Belschnickel, Belznickel, atau Pelznickel, adalah sosok pembawa hadiah Natal yang pemarah dan berbaju bulu dalam cerita rakyat wilayah Pfalz di barat daya Jerman di sepanjang Rhein, Saarland, dan Odenwald. Ia masih dipertahankan dalam komunitas Pennsylvania Dutch dan komunitas Jerman di Brasil.
long_description.en: Belsnickel, also called Belschnickel, Belznickel or Pelznickel, is a grumpy, fur-clad Christmas gift-bringer in the folklore of the Palatinate in south-western Germany along the Rhine, the Saarland and the Odenwald. He survives among the Pennsylvania Dutch and in German-Brazilian communities.

long_description.id: Ia berkerabat dengan para pendamping Santo Nikolaus dan mungkin bersumber dari Knecht Ruprecht, tetapi tidak mendampingi Nikolaus; ia datang sendiri dan memadukan sisi menakutkan dan sisi baik yang dalam tradisi lain terbagi antara Nikolaus dan pendampingnya. Ia lelaki berbulu, compang-camping dan kumal, membawa ranting untuk memukul anak nakal sekaligus saku penuh kue, permen, dan kacang untuk anak baik.
long_description.en: He is related to Saint Nicholas's companions and may derive from Knecht Ruprecht, but he does not accompany Nicholas; he comes alone and combines the frightening and kindly sides that other traditions split between Nicholas and his helper. He is a fur-wearing man, ragged and unkempt, carrying a switch for naughty children and pockets of cakes, sweets and nuts for good ones.

long_description.id: Para pendatang dari Pfalz membawa tradisi ini ke Pennsylvania, tempat Belsnickel sudah dikenal awal abad ke-19. Ia mendatangi rumah satu atau dua minggu sebelum Natal untuk memeriksa perilaku anak-anak, mengetuk pintu atau jendela dengan tongkatnya, lalu melempar permen ke lantai; anak yang terlalu cepat menyambar bisa terkena rantingnya.
long_description.en: Settlers from the Palatinate brought the custom to Pennsylvania, where Belsnickel was known by the early 1800s. He visited homes one or two weeks before Christmas to check on the children's behaviour, rapping on door or window with his stick and tossing sweets on the floor; children who grabbed too fast might feel his switch.

long_description.id: Di Franken, sosok serupa bernama Pelzmärtel, gabungan tradisi hari Santo Nikolaus dan hari Santo Martin, dengan nama dari kata pelzen, "memukul". Di kota-kota Brasil seperti Guabiruba, ia dikenal sebagai Pelznickel yang konon tinggal di hutan sepanjang tahun dan disebut Papai Noel do Mato.
long_description.en: In Franconia a similar figure is called Pelzmärtel, merging the customs of the feasts of Saint Nicholas and Saint Martin, the name coming from pelzen, 'to beat'. In Brazilian towns such as Guabiruba he is known as Pelznickel, said to live in the forest the rest of the year and called Papai Noel do Mato.

famous_for.en: His switch and pockets full of cakes.

did_you_know.id: Di Brasil, Pelznickel konon tinggal di hutan sepanjang tahun dan dijuluki Papai Noel do Mato, "Sinterklas hutan".
did_you_know.en: In Brazilian towns Pelznickel is said to live in the forest all year and is nicknamed Papai Noel do Mato, 'Santa of the forest'.

claims.quote: Belsnickel (also known as Belschnickel, Belznickle, Belznickel, Pelznikel, Pelznickel, Bell Sniggle) is a crotchety, fur-clad Christmas gift-bringer figure in the folklore of the Palatinate region of southwestern Germany along the Rhine, the Saarland, and the Odenwald area of Baden-Württemberg. The figure is also preserved in Pennsylvania Dutch communities and Brazilian-German communities.

statement.id: Belsnickel (juga Belschnickel, Belznickel, Pelznickel, dan lain-lain) adalah sosok pembawa hadiah Natal yang pemarah dan berbaju bulu dalam cerita rakyat Pfalz di barat daya Jerman di sepanjang Rhein, Saarland, dan Odenwald di Baden-Württemberg, dan juga dipertahankan dalam komunitas Pennsylvania Dutch serta Jerman-Brasil.
statement.en: Belsnickel (also Belschnickel, Belznickel, Pelznickel and others) is a crotchety, fur-clad Christmas gift-bringer in the folklore of the Palatinate of south-western Germany along the Rhine, the Saarland and the Odenwald of Baden-Württemberg, also preserved among the Pennsylvania Dutch and German-Brazilians.

claims.quote: Belsnickel is related to other companions of Saint Nicholas in the folklore of German-speaking Europe. He may have been based on an older German myth, Knecht Ruprecht ... Unlike those figures, Belsnickel does not accompany Saint Nicholas but instead visits alone and combines both the threatening and the benign aspects

statement.id: Belsnickel berkerabat dengan pendamping Santo Nikolaus lain dalam cerita rakyat Eropa berbahasa Jerman dan mungkin bersumber dari mitos Knecht Ruprecht; namun ia tidak mendampingi Nikolaus, melainkan datang sendiri dan memadukan sisi mengancam dan sisi baik.
statement.en: Belsnickel is related to other companions of Saint Nicholas in German-speaking folklore and may be based on the Knecht Ruprecht myth; but he visits alone rather than with Nicholas, combining threatening and benign aspects.

claims.quote: Belsnickel is a man wearing fur. He is typically very ragged and disheveled. He wears torn, tattered, and dirty clothes, and he carries a switch in his hand with which to beat naughty children, but also pockets full of cakes, candies, and nuts for good children.

statement.id: Belsnickel adalah lelaki berbaju bulu yang compang-camping dan kumal, membawa ranting untuk memukul anak nakal sekaligus saku penuh kue, permen, dan kacang untuk anak baik.
statement.en: Belsnickel is a fur-wearing man, ragged and dishevelled, carrying a switch to beat naughty children and pockets full of cakes, sweets and nuts for good ones.

claims.quote: The Belsnickel character originated in the Palatinate. When people immigrated to Pennsylvania, they brought their German traditions with them. Belsnickel was known in Pennsylvania in the early 1800s.

statement.id: Tokoh Belsnickel berasal dari Pfalz; para imigran ke Pennsylvania membawa tradisi Jerman mereka, dan Belsnickel sudah dikenal di Pennsylvania awal abad ke-19.
statement.en: The Belsnickel figure originated in the Palatinate; immigrants to Pennsylvania brought their German traditions, and Belsnickel was known there in the early 1800s.

claims.quote: The traditional Belsnickel showed up at houses 1–2 weeks before Christmas ... He would rap on the door or window with his stick and often the children would have to answer a question for him or sing some type of song. In exchange he would toss candies onto the floor. If the children jumped too quick for the treats, they may end up getting struck with Belsnickel's switch.

statement.id: Belsnickel tradisional datang ke rumah-rumah satu atau dua minggu sebelum Natal, mengetuk pintu atau jendela dengan tongkat, meminta anak menjawab pertanyaan atau bernyanyi, lalu melempar permen ke lantai; anak yang terlalu cepat menyambar bisa terkena rantingnya.
statement.en: The traditional Belsnickel came to houses one or two weeks before Christmas, rapped on door or window with his stick, had children answer a question or sing, then tossed sweets on the floor; those who jumped too fast might be struck with his switch.

claims.quote: Der Pelzmärtel (auch Pelzemärtel, Pelzermärtel, Pelzamärdl, Belzermärdl, Bulzermärtl, Belzemärdl oder Pelzmartin) ist ein in Teilen Frankens (Süddeutschland) verbreiteter Name für den vorweihnachtlichen Gabenbringer. Regional tritt er auch als Pelznickel auf.

claims.quote: Belsnickel (also known as Belschnickel, Belznickle, Belznickel, Pelznikel, Pelznickel, Bell Sniggle) is a crotchety, fur-clad Christmas gift-bringer figure in the folklore of the Palatinate region of southwestern Germany along the Rhine, the Saarland, and the Odenwald area of Baden-Württemberg. short_description.id: Bokkenrijders atau penunggang kambing jantan adalah penyihir dalam cerita rakyat Belanda tenggara dan Belgia timur laut yang terbang dengan kambing pemberian Iblis untuk merampok dan membunuh.
short_description.en: The Buckriders (Bokkenrijders) are witches of south-eastern Dutch and north-eastern Belgian folklore who flew on bucks given by the Devil to rob and murder.

long_description.id: Bokkenrijders (penunggang kambing jantan) adalah bagian dari cerita rakyat Belanda tenggara dan Belgia timur laut. Mereka dipercaya sebagai penyihir yang terbang di langit menunggangi kambing jantan pemberian Iblis untuk merampok dan membunuh rakyat biasa serta merampas harta gereja, dan setahun sekali menghadap tuan mereka, sang Iblis, di Padang Mook.
long_description.en: The Bokkenrijders (Buckriders) belong to south-eastern Dutch and north-eastern Belgian folklore. They were believed to be witches who flew through the sky on bucks given by the Devil to rob and murder common people and plunder church property, and once a year visited their master, the Devil, on the Mook Heath.

long_description.id: Sepanjang abad ke-18, kawanan pencuri dan penjahat memakai kepercayaan ini untuk menakut-nakuti penduduk Limburg selatan dan melancarkan serangan di wilayah Limburg dan sebagian Jerman masa kini. Orang percaya mereka dapat menempuh jarak jauh dengan cepat lewat udara dan pulang sebelum fajar. Sebagai tanggapan, kota-kota di Limburg membangun parit pertahanan.
long_description.en: Throughout the 18th century gangs of thieves exploited the belief to frighten the people of southern Limburg, raiding across Limburg and parts of present-day Germany. People believed they could fly far and fast and be home before dawn. In response, Limburg towns built defensive moats.

long_description.id: Karena dikaitkan dengan ilmu gaib, banyak lelaki yang mungkin tak bersalah dituduh sebagai bokkenrijder, disiksa, lalu dihukum; tuduhan selalu mencakup perampokan sekaligus sihir. Diperkirakan sekitar 1.200 orang dituduh dan sedikitnya 425 sampai 468 dieksekusi antara 1743 dan 1796. Kisah mereka diangkat dalam serial televisi De Legende van de Bokkenrijders (1993) dan wahana Villa Volta di taman hiburan Efteling.
long_description.en: Because of the link to the occult, many possibly innocent men were accused of being buckriders, tortured and convicted; the charges always combined robbery and witchcraft. About 1,200 men are thought to have been accused and at least 425 to 468 executed between 1743 and 1796. Their story inspired the TV series De Legende van de Bokkenrijders (1993) and the Villa Volta ride at the Efteling theme park.

long_description.en: The Buckriders (Dutch: Bokkenrijders; French: Chevaliers du bouc) are a part of South-Eastern Dutch and North-Eastern Belgian folklore. They are witches, who rode through the sky on the back of flying bucks provided to them by the Devil to rob and murder common people and church possessions. The trials against the buckriders differed from 'ordinary' criminal proceedings because in many cases a so-called 'ungodly oath' was involved ("I renounce God and swear submission to the Devil"). Once a year, they would visit their master, the Devil, on the Mook Heath. Throughout the 18th century, groups of thieves and other criminals adopted the belief to frighten the inhabitants of southern Limburg, a province in the southern part of the Netherlands and in parts of what has become since eastern Belgium. Using the name "Bokkenrijders" (buckriders), these criminal bands launched raids across a region that included Limburg, and parts of modern-day Germany. In response to the robberies towns in Limburg started to build defences like moats around them and farms started to develop a closed square building style. The buckriders were feared and despised by the common people throughout the area because of the ruthlessness and violence the robberies were committed by. The belief existed that the buckriders could travel fast and vast distances through the skies to rob in a widespread area and be home before dawn to remain obscured in their crimes. Commonly, the buckriders raided small communities, parsonages, churches and more remote farms. Hundreds of buckriders were convicted and sentenced to death. Because of the link to the occult and witchcraft, authorities accused a large number of potentially innocent men of being buckriders and the majority of suspects were tortured and subsequently convicted of crimes they initially denied having committed. The buckriders were considered both criminals and witches that made a pact with the devil. The witch trials and robbery trials can not be seen separately in that sense: the accusations always included both robbery and witchcraft. It is estimated that about 1200 men were accused and at least between 425 and 468 men were executed between 1743 and 1796 on the conviction of being a Buckrider. The number of deaths might surpass 500 men due to suspects dying under torture when questioned.

short_description.id: Lange Wapper adalah raksasa dan penipu dalam cerita rakyat Flandria, terutama di Antwerpen, yang bisa membesarkan atau mengecilkan diri dan suka mengganggu pemabuk.
short_description.en: Lange Wapper is a giant and trickster of Flemish folklore, above all in Antwerp, who can make himself big or small and likes to torment drunkards.

long_description.id: Lange Wapper adalah tokoh cerita rakyat Flandria, raksasa legendaris sekaligus penipu yang kisahnya terutama diceritakan di kota Antwerpen dan sekitarnya, meski kisah serupa juga ada di kota-kota Flandria lain. Menurut satu versi asal-usulnya, seorang petani menemukannya sebagai bayi dalam kubis merah raksasa di petak peterseli; anak itu diasuh keluarga di Antwerpen dan tumbuh menjadi pemuda kuat yang suka menolong.
long_description.en: Lange Wapper is a figure of Flemish folklore, a legendary giant and trickster whose tales were told especially in Antwerp and nearby towns, though similar stories exist in other Flemish cities. In one account of his origin a farmer found him as a baby inside a giant red cabbage in a parsley bed; the child was raised by an Antwerp family and grew into a strong youth who helped those in need.

long_description.id: Suatu hari ia menyelamatkan seorang nenek dari tenggelam di Sungai Schelde, dan nenek itu memberinya kemampuan membesarkan atau mengecilkan diri; karena lebih suka tampil tinggi, ia dijuluki Lange Wapper. Ia menyamar sebagai anak untuk mendapat air susu, mengganggu pemabuk, dan mencurangi anak-anak dalam permainan, dan tawanya yang mengembik membuat orang menyebutnya "setan air".
long_description.en: After he rescued an old woman who was drowning in the Scheldt, she granted him the power to grow huge or shrink; since he liked best to appear tall, he became known as Lange Wapper. He disguised himself as a child to get breast milk, vexed drunkards and cheated children at games, and his bleating laugh led people to call him 'water devil'.

long_description.id: Dalam satu kisah, seorang lelaki mabuk pulang dari penginapan di Antwerpen dan dikejar sosok misterius; setelah ia bersembunyi di ranjang, Lange Wapper setinggi rumah mengetuk jendelanya dan mengancam akan mematahkan lehernya bila ia mabuk lagi. Satu versi menyebut ia takut pada patung Perawan Maria, yang konon menjelaskan banyaknya patung itu di kota.
long_description.en: In one tale a drunk man walking home from an Antwerp inn is followed by a mysterious figure; after he hides in bed, Lange Wapper, as tall as a house, knocks at his window and threatens to break his neck if he gets drunk again. One version says he feared statues of the Virgin, which supposedly explains how many there are in the city.

did_you_know.id: Proyek jembatan raksasa di Antwerpen dinamai Lange Wapperbrug menurut tokoh ini, tetapi ditolak warga dalam konsultasi publik pada 19 Oktober 2009.
did_you_know.en: A huge bridge project in Antwerp was named Lange Wapperbrug after him, but residents rejected it in a public consultation on 19 October 2009.
