Because he preferred to appear in his tall form, he gained the nickname Lange Wapper.

claims.statement: He disguised himself as a child to get breast milk, vexed drunkards and cheated children at games; his bleating laugh frightened people, who called him 'water devil'.
claims.statement_id: Ia menyamar sebagai anak untuk mendapat air susu, mengganggu pemabuk, dan mencurangi anak-anak dalam permainan; tawanya yang mengembik menakutkan orang sehingga ia disebut "setan air".
claims.quote: He would disguise himself as a child to receive breastmilk to drink, would vex drunkards, and would cheat children in games. His bleating laughter frightened the general public, who began to call him “water devil”.

claims.statement: It is Lange Wapper, as big as a house, who warns: 'If you get drunk again, I will break your neck!'
claims.statement_id: Sosok itu ternyata Lange Wapper, sebesar rumah, yang memperingatkan: "Kalau kau mabuk lagi, akan kupatahkan lehermu!"
claims.quote: It is Lange Wapper, as big as a house, who warns, "If you get drunk again, I will break your neck!"

claims.statement: Lange Wapper (French le Grand Wapper) is a legendary giant who plays tricks on the people of Antwerp, Belgium; he appears at night, pursues those who drank too much, and can make himself very big or very small.
claims.statement_id: Lange Wapper (Prancis: le Grand Wapper) adalah raksasa legenda yang mempermainkan warga Antwerpen, Belgia; ia muncul di malam hari, mengejar orang yang terlalu banyak minum, dan bisa membuat dirinya sangat besar atau sangat kecil.
claims.quote: Le Lange Wapper (en français, le Grand Wapper) est un géant de légende qui joue de mauvais tours aux habitants de la ville d'Anvers, en Belgique. Il apparaît la nuit et poursuit les gens qui ont trop bu. Il sait se faire très grand et très petit.

claims.statement: One version says Lange Wapper feared statues of the Virgin, which would explain their great number in the city.
claims.statement_id: Satu versi menyebut Lange Wapper takut pada patung Perawan Maria, yang konon menjelaskan banyaknya patung itu di kota.
claims.quote: Une version dit aussi que Lange Wapper avait peur des statues de la Vierge et que cela expliquerait le grand nombre de celle-ci dans la ville.

claims.statement: His name was given to a huge bridge project (Lange Wapperbrug) over part of the city, rejected by Antwerp residents in a public consultation on 19 October 2009.
claims.statement_id: Namanya dipakai untuk proyek jembatan raksasa (Lange Wapperbrug) di atas sebagian kota itu, yang ditolak warga Antwerpen dalam konsultasi publik pada 19 Oktober 2009.
claims.quote: Il a aussi donné son nom au projet d'un immense pont (Lange Wapperbrug) surplombant une partie de la même ville. Les Anversois ont rejeté le projet par consultation populaire, le 19 octobre 2009 .

short_description.id: Egil adalah pemanah legendaris dalam Völundarkviða dan Thidreks saga, saudara pandai besi Völund, yang terkenal karena memanah apel dari kepala putranya.
short_description.en: Egil is a legendary archer of the Völundarkviða and Thidreks saga, brother of the smith Völund, famed for shooting an apple from his son's head.

long_description.id: Egil adalah pahlawan legendaris dalam Völundarkviða dan Thidreks saga. Namanya berasal dari bentuk Proto-Jermanik *Agilaz, dan legenda yang sama tercermin pada Ægil di Peti Franks dalam bahasa Inggris Kuno serta Aigil di gesper Pforzen dalam bahasa Alemannik. Bentuk awal legendanya tampaknya tentang pemanah termasyhur yang bersama istrinya Alruna mempertahankan sebuah benteng dari banyak penyerang, adegan yang juga terpahat pada Peti Franks.
long_description.en: Both the Völundarkviða and the Thidreks saga feature Egil as a hero of legend. His name derives from Proto-Germanic *Agilaz, and the same story surfaces in Old English Ægil on the Franks Casket and Alamannic Aigil on the Pforzen buckle. The earliest form of the legend seems to have been about a famous archer who, with his wife Alruna, defended a keep against many attackers, a scene also carved on the Franks Casket.

long_description.id: Dalam Völundarkviða, Egil adalah putra seorang raja Finn, dengan kakak Slagfiðr dan adik Völund. Ketiga bersaudara itu menikahi valkyrie yang mereka temui dalam rupa angsa; Egil menikahi Ölrún, putri Kaisar Romawi. Sebagai saudara Wieland si pandai besi, ia juga termasuk lingkaran legenda Dietrich von Bern.
long_description.en: In the Völundarkviða Egil is a son of a Finnish king, with Slagfiðr as his elder brother and Völund as his younger. The three brothers marry valkyries they meet in swan shape; Egil weds Ölrún, daughter of the Roman Emperor. As a brother of Wieland the smith he also belongs to the legend cycle of Dietrich von Bern.

long_description.id: Dalam Thidreks saga ia pemanah ulung yang dipaksa Raja Nidung memanah apel dari kepala putranya yang berusia tiga tahun; ia menyiapkan lebih dari satu anak panah, dan anak panah pertama sudah membelah apel itu. Ia juga mengumpulkan bulu burung untuk sayap saudaranya Wieland, lalu ketika disuruh menembak Wieland yang melarikan diri di udara, ia sengaja membidik kantong darah di ketiak Wieland sehingga saudaranya selamat.
long_description.en: In the Thidreks saga he is a master bowman whom King Nidung compels to hit an apple placed on his three-year-old son's head; he readied more than one arrow, and the first split the apple. He also gathered bird feathers for the wings of his brother Wieland, and when ordered to shoot Wieland as he fled through the air, he deliberately hit a bladder of blood under Wieland's arm so his brother escaped.

long_description.en: Egil is a legendary hero of the Völundarkviða and the Thidreks saga. The name is from Proto-Germanic *Agilaz, and the same legend is reflected in Old English Ægil [ˈæɡil] of the Franks Casket and Alamannic Aigil of the Pforzen buckle. The Proto-Germanic form of the legend may only be guessed at, but it appears likely that Egil was a renowned archer who defended a keep together with his wife Alruna, against numerous attackers. The testimony of the Pforzen buckle is uncertain beyond naming Aigil and Ailrun, possibly adding that they fought a battle at the Ilz river. The Franks Casket shows the scene of Aegil and his wife enclosed in the keep, with Aegil shooting arrows against attacking troops.

short_description.id: Wiedergänger, "yang berjalan lagi", adalah sebutan Jerman untuk orang mati yang kembali ke dunia orang hidup, sering dalam wujud jasmani, dan biasanya berniat jahat.
short_description.en: Wiedergänger, 'one who walks again', is the German term for the dead who return to the world of the living, often in bodily form and usually ill-disposed.

long_description.id: Dalam bahasa Jerman, Wiedergänger (juga ditulis Widergänger) adalah istilah untuk mayat hidup dan berbagai fenomena hantu dari beragam budaya, berarti "yang berjalan lagi", sekerabat dengan kata Skandinavia gjenganger. Inti mitosnya adalah orang mati yang kembali ke dunia orang hidup, sering dalam wujud jasmani sebagai Untote. Mereka menyeramkan, biasanya berniat jahat, dan kerap menimbulkan masalah bagi orang hidup.
long_description.en: In German, Wiedergänger (also spelled Widergänger) is a term for revenants and various ghost phenomena from many cultures, meaning 're-walker', cognate with Scandinavian gjenganger. The core of the myth is the dead returning to the world of the living, often in bodily form as undead. They are uncanny, usually ill-disposed, and often trouble the living.

long_description.id: Di berbagai wilayah Jerman, sampai awal abad ke-20 orang percaya bahwa orang mati tetap hidup dan memberi pengaruh buruk dari dalam kubur. Karena itu Nachzehrer konon tidak perlu bangkit dari kubur. Mayat hidup lain, Aufhocker, keluar dari kubur dan melompat ke punggung pengembara malam, makin berat sampai korban ambruk kelelahan atau mati.
long_description.en: In various parts of Germany until the early 20th century people believed the dead lived on and exerted a baleful influence from the grave. So the Nachzehrer supposedly did not need to rise from the grave. Other undead, the Aufhocker, left the grave and leapt onto night walkers' backs, growing heavier until the victim collapsed exhausted or dead.

long_description.id: Mediavis Prancis Jean-Claude Schmitt, yang meneliti sumber gambar Eropa Tengah abad ke-12 sampai ke-16, membagi gambaran mayat hidup menjadi tipe Wiedergänger (revenant), Lazarus, jiwa, dan hantu; tipe Wiedergänger tampak seperti orang hidup. Di wilayah Katolik, kepercayaan pada Wiedergänger yang menunggang punggung bercampur dengan kepercayaan pada jiwa.
long_description.en: The French medievalist Jean-Claude Schmitt, who studied Central European images from the 12th to 16th centuries, divides depictions of the undead into revenant, Lazarus, soul and ghost types; the revenant type resembles a living person. In Catholic areas, belief in the back-riding Wiedergänger merged with belief in souls.

Der Kern des Wiedergänger-Mythologems ist die Vorstellung von Verstorbenen, die – oft als körperliche Erscheinung („Untote“) – in die Welt der Lebenden zurückkehren. Sie sind den Lebenden unheimlich und meist böse gesinnt

statement.en: Wiedergänger, also spelled Widergänger, denotes various ghostly apparitions from many cultures; its core is the idea of the dead returning to the living, often in bodily form (undead), uncanny and usually ill-disposed.

claims.quote: In verschiedenen Teilen Deutschlands war bis ins frühe 20. Jahrhundert der Glaube verbreitet, dass Tote nach ihrem Tod trotzdem weiterlebten und einen unheilvollen Einfluss aus dem Grab heraus ausübten. Teilweise geschah dies durch eine telepathische Wirkung (Sympathiezauber), so dass der als Nachzehrer bezeichnete Unhold nicht aus dem Grab steigen musste

statement.id: Di berbagai wilayah Jerman sampai awal abad ke-20 orang percaya orang mati tetap hidup dan memberi pengaruh buruk dari kubur, sebagian lewat pengaruh telepatis, sehingga makhluk jahat yang disebut Nachzehrer tak perlu bangkit dari kubur.
statement.en: In various parts of Germany until the early 20th century people believed the dead lived on and exerted baleful influence from the grave, partly telepathically, so the fiend called Nachzehrer need not leave the grave.

claims.quote: Andere Untote stiegen dem Volksglauben nach aus den Gräbern und sprangen nächtlichen Wanderern auf den Rücken. Diesen Aufhocker, der auch verschiedene Gestalten annehmen konnte, zum Beispiel im Rheinland die des Werwolfs, musste der Mensch tragen ... Dabei wurde der Aufhocker (auch „Huckop“ oder „Huckupp“ genannt) immer schwerer, und das Opfer brach schließlich erschöpft oder gar tot zusammen.

statement.id: Menurut kepercayaan rakyat, mayat hidup lain keluar dari kubur dan melompat ke punggung pengembara malam; Aufhocker ini, yang bisa berubah rupa, misalnya menjadi manusia serigala di Rheinland, harus digendong dan makin berat sampai korban ambruk kelelahan atau mati.
statement.en: In folk belief other undead rose from graves and jumped onto night walkers' backs; this Aufhocker, which could take various shapes such as a werewolf in the Rhineland, had to be carried and grew heavier until the victim collapsed exhausted or dead.

claims.quote: Der französische Mediävist Jean-Claude Schmitt, der mitteleuropäische Bildquellen aus dem 12. bis 16. Jahrhundert untersucht hat, unterteilt Untote je nach Darstellungsweise in Wiedergänger (Revenant), Lazarus-, Seelen- und Gespensttypen. ... gleicht der Wiedergänger einem Lebenden.

statement.en: The French medievalist Jean-Claude Schmitt, studying Central European images of the 12th–16th centuries, divides the undead by depiction into revenant, Lazarus, soul and ghost types; the revenant resembles a living person.

statement.id: Terutama di wilayah Katolik, kepercayaan pada Wiedergänger penunggang punggung bercampur dengan kepercayaan pada jiwa.

long_description.en: In German, the term Wiedergänger (German pronunciation: [ˈviːdɐˌɡɛŋɐ] ) is a term for a revenant and different ghost phenomena from different cultural areas, meaning "re-walker", or by extension, "one who walks again"; cognate to Scandinavian gjenganger ("again-walker"). The core of the wiedergänger myth is the concept of the deceased, who—often in the form of a physical phenomenon—return to the world of the living. They usually cause problems and frighten living people. They exist either to avenge some injustice they experienced while alive, or because their soul is not ready to be released, as a consequence of their former way of life.

short_description.id: Rå adalah roh penjaga tempat atau bentang alam tertentu dalam cerita rakyat Skandinavia dan Sami, yang bisa membawa untung atau sial bagi manusia.
short_description.en: A rå is a spirit that keeps a particular place or landform in Scandinavian and Sami folklore, able to bring good or bad luck to people.

long_description.id: Dalam cerita rakyat Skandinavia, rå (jamak rår), kependekan dari rådare ("penguasa"), dari kata råda ("memerintah, menasihati") dan Nordik Kuno ráða, adalah roh penjaga suatu tempat atau bentang alam. Rå dikenal dalam budaya Nordik maupun Sami, tempat ia disebut radie. Manusia perlu menjaga hubungan baik dengannya, karena ia menguasai kekuatan alam dan hewan di bawah asuhannya serta dapat membawa untung atau sial bagi siapa pun yang mengganggu wilayahnya.
long_description.en: In Scandinavian folklore a rå (plural rår), short for rådare ('ruler'), from råda ('to rule, to advise') and Old Norse ráða, is the keeper of a particular place or landform. It is known in Nordic and Sami culture alike, the Sami calling it radie. People had to keep on good terms with it, since it ruled the natural forces and animals in its care and could bring good or bad luck to anyone meddling with its domain.

long_description.id: Rår dibedakan menurut wilayah alam yang dijaganya, seperti skogsrå atau hulder untuk hutan, sjörå untuk air tawar, havsrå untuk air asin, dan bergsrå untuk gunung. Menurut kepercayaan lama, setiap benda, hewan, dan tumbuhan punya rå pelindungnya sendiri, dan rå juga bisa menjaga tempat dan benda milik manusia, seperti skeppsrået (rå kapal) dan gruvrået (rå tambang). Rår dapat tampil berwujud hewan atau manusia; skogsrå dan bergsrå biasanya digambarkan perempuan.
long_description.en: Rår are distinguished by the sphere of nature they keep, such as the skogsrå or hulder of the forest, the sjörå of fresh water, the havsrå of salt water and the bergsrå of mountains. In old belief every object, animal and plant had its own protecting rå, and a rå might also oversee human places and things, such as the skeppsrået (ship's rå) and gruvrået (mine's rå). Rår may appear as animals or as men or women; the skogsrå and bergsrå are usually described as female.

long_description.en: In Scandinavian folklore, a rå (in Swedish) (pl. rår), short for rådare ("ruler") from råda (to rule, to advise) from old Norse ráða, is a spirit who is the keeper or warden of a particular location or landform. The rå is known both in Nordic culture and in the Sami culture, where it is called radie. It was important for humans to cultivate good relationships with them, since they had power over the natural forces and animals under their care, and could cause both good and bad luck for humans who interfered with the places and creatures under their watch.

short_description.id: Kyrië adalah raja para kabouter (gnom) dalam cerita rakyat Kempen, Brabant Utara, Belanda; setelah ia ditembak seorang pemburu, semua kabouter meninggalkan wilayah itu.
short_description.en: Kyrië is the king of the kabouters (gnomes) in the folklore of the Campine, North Brabant, the Netherlands; after a hunter shot him, all the gnomes left the region.

long_description.id: Menurut cerita rakyat setempat, Raja Kurcaci Kyrië (Kabouterkoning Kyrië) adalah pemimpin kabouter legendaris yang tinggal di wilayah Kempen di Brabant Utara, Belanda. Para kabouter berpangkalan di desa Hoogeloon, dan Kyrië sendiri tinggal di Kerkakkers, di Kabouterberg ("gunung kurcaci") atau Duivelsberg ("gunung setan"), sebuah tumulus.
long_description.en: According to local folklore, Gnome King Kyrië (Kabouterkoning Kyrië) was the leader of the legendary kabouters of the Campine in North Brabant, the Netherlands. The gnomes were based in the village of Hoogeloon, and Kyrië himself lived on the Kerkakkers in the Kabouterberg ('gnome mountain') or Duivelsberg ('devil's mountain'), a tumulus.

long_description.id: Para kabouter Kempen adalah makhluk penolong yang membantu petani dan rumah tangga pada malam hari dan tak ingin dilihat manusia; siapa yang melihat mereka akan dihukum, seperti petani penasaran yang buta sebelah matanya setelah mengintip. Kyrië ditembak seorang pemburu di padang Riethoven, masih sempat mencapai Duivelsberg, dan pemburu itu mendengar kabouter berseru "Kyrië sudah mati"; setelah sang raja dimakamkan di Hoogeloon, semua kabouter pergi ke tempat yang tak diketahui.
long_description.en: The gnomes of the Campine were helpful beings who aided farmers and households at night and did not wish to be seen; those who saw them were punished, like a curious farmer who went blind in one eye after spying. Kyrië was shot by a hunter on the Riethoven heath, managed to reach the Duivelsberg, and the hunter heard the gnomes cry 'Kyrië is dead'; after the king was buried in Hoogeloon, all the gnomes left for an unknown place.

long_description.id: Dalam satu versi, kematian sang raja diumumkan seorang pengembara, struktur cerita yang mungkin berasal dari Plutarkhos. Pada 1985 sebuah pompa desa berpatung Raja Kyrië karya Wim Gubbels didirikan di Valensplein, Hoogeloon, yang menurut kisah kabouter juga tempat sang raja dimakamkan.
long_description.en: In one version the king's death is announced by a traveller, a narrative pattern that may come from Plutarch. In 1985 a village pump with a statue of King Kyrië by Wim Gubbels was set up on the Valensplein in Hoogeloon, which according to the gnome tales is also where the king was buried.

famous_for.en: His death made the gnomes leave.

did_you_know.id: Pada 2001, bersamaan dengan pemindahan patung Raja Kyrië di Hoogeloon, diperkenalkan minuman khusus "Koning Kyrië Kruidenbitter".
did_you_know.en: In 2001, when the King Kyrië statue in Hoogeloon was moved, a special 'Koning Kyrië Kruidenbitter' was introduced.

statement.en: The Campine gnomes were helpful beings aiding farmers and households in the Campine, the Peel and the Meierij; they came at night, did not want to be seen, and punished those who saw them, like a curious farmer blinded in one eye.

statement.id: Pada 9 April 2001 patung itu dipindahkan ke tempat lain di alun-alun yang sama karena penataan ulang Valensplein, dan sekaligus diperkenalkan minuman khusus "Koning Kyrië Kruidenbitter".

long_description.en: Gnome king Kyrië (Dutch: Kabouterkoning Kyrië, pronounced [kaːˈbʌutərˌkoːnɪŋ ˈkiːrijə]) is, according to local folklore, the leader of the legendary gnomes (kabouters) who lived in the Campine region of the province of North Brabant, the Netherlands. These gnomes had their base in the village of Hoogeloon, from which they journeyed into neighboring lands. According to tradition the gnome king Kyrië lived on the Kerkakkers in the Kabouterberg ("gnome mountain"), also known as Duivelsberg ("devil's mountain"), a tumulus located in the Koebosch forest, slightly northeast of Hoogeloon.

short_description.id: Klagmuhme ("bibi peratap") adalah roh perempuan dalam cerita rakyat Jerman yang meratap dan merintih sebagai pertanda kematian, padanan banshee di Jerman.
short_description.en: The Klagmuhme ('wailing aunt') is a female sprite of German folklore whose wailing and whining foretell death, the German counterpart of the banshee.

long_description.id: Klagmuhme atau Klagemuhme ("bibi peratap"), juga disebut Klagmutter ("ibu peratap"), adalah roh perempuan dalam cerita rakyat Jerman. Dengan ratapan dan rintihannya ia mengabarkan kematian yang akan datang, sehingga dianggap padanan banshee di Jerman. Ia pertama tercatat pada abad ke-15 dalam bahasa Jerman Tinggi Pertengahan sebagai klagmuoter, sebutan untuk burung hantu, dan sering disamakan dengan burung itu.
long_description.en: The Klagmuhme or Klagemuhme ('wailing aunt'), also called Klagmutter ('wailing mother'), is a female sprite of German folklore. Through her wailing and whimpering she announces a coming death, making her the German counterpart of the banshee. She is first recorded in 15th-century Middle High German as klagmuoter, a name for the owl, and is often identified with that bird.

long_description.id: Ia sering tampil sebagai hewan: anjing hitam berbulu panjang yang melolong mengitari rumah, angsa putih, merpati di talang, kucing kelabu besar berkerudung, atau domba putih berkaki tiga yang membesar menjadi raksasa bila diganggu. Dalam wujud manusia ia perempuan tua bergaun hitam berkerudung putih, perempuan kecil berwajah tertutup sarang laba-laba, atau sosok setinggi menara gereja berbalut kain kafan; ia juga bisa berupa gumpalan benang biru yang menyemburkan bunga api.
long_description.en: She often takes animal form: a long-haired black dog howling round the house, a white goose, a dove in the gutter, a large grey cat in a headscarf, or a white three-legged sheep that swells to giant size if teased. In human form she is an old woman in a black dress and white scarf, a little woman whose face is veiled in cobwebs, or a figure as tall as a church steeple in a burial robe; she may also be a tangled blue clew spitting sparks.

long_description.id: Ratapannya pertanda maut dan bencana. Bila ia meratap di depan rumah orang sakit, pakaian si sakit dilempar keluar: jika Klagmuhme membawanya pergi, orang itu akan mati; jika ditinggalkannya, ia akan sembuh. Biasanya ia tak terlihat, melayang di atas rumah tanpa pernah masuk, aktif tengah malam, dan rintihannya ("u-u-u!") dapat membuat orang yang ketakutan jatuh sakit saraf, tetapi selain itu ia tidak mencelakai siapa pun.
long_description.en: Her wailing heralds death and disaster. If she wails before a house with a sick person inside, the patient's clothes are thrown out of the door: if the Klagmuhme carries them off, the patient will die; if she leaves them, he will recover. She is usually invisible, hovering over houses without ever going in, active at midnight, and her whimper ('u-u-u!') can give frightened people a nervous illness, though otherwise she harms no one.

long_description.id: Asal-usulnya berbeda menurut daerah: di Austria ia arwah orang mati; di Sachsen arwah ibu malang yang mencari putranya yang tenggelam; di Kärnten dan Swiss ia bagian dari Perburuan Liar; di pegunungan Fichtel ia roh hutan perempuan (Waldweibchen).
long_description.en: Her origin differs by region: in Austria she is the soul of a dead person; in Saxony the soul of an unhappy mother searching for her drowned son; in Carinthia and Switzerland she belongs to the Wild Hunt; in the Fichtel Mountains she is a female wood sprite (Waldweibchen).

famous_for.id: Membawa pergi pakaian orang yang akan mati.
famous_for.en: Carries off the clothes of the doomed.

did_you_know.id: Untuk mengetahui nasib orang sakit, orang melempar pakaiannya ke luar pintu: bila Klagmuhme membawanya pergi, orang itu akan mati.
did_you_know.en: To learn a sick person's fate, people threw his clothes outside the door: if the Klagmuhme took them away, he would die.

description.en: The foretold disaster can be averted by at once telling the Klagmuhme an alternative.

statement.en: The Klagmuhme or Klagemuhme ('wailing aunt'), also called Klagmutter or Klagemutter ('wailing mother'), is a female sprite of German folklore who heralds imminent death by wailing and whining, the German equivalent of the banshee.

claims.quote: Further terms are Klagmütterchen (wailing mother), Winselmutter (whining mother), Haulemutter (wailing mother), Klinselweib (wailing woman), and Klagweh (wailing). The Klagmuhme is first attested in 15th century Middle High German as klagmuoter (wailing mother), denoting an owl.

statement.id: Sebutan lain termasuk Winselmutter ("ibu perintih") dan Haulemutter; Klagmuhme pertama tercatat pada abad ke-15 dalam bahasa Jerman Tinggi Pertengahan (Middle High German) sebagai klagmuoter, yang menunjuk burung hantu.
statement.en: Other names include Winselmutter ('whining mother') and Haulemutter; the Klagmuhme is first attested in 15th-century Middle High German as klagmuoter, meaning an owl.

claims.quote: The Klagmuhme often appears as an animal. So she roves howling around the concerned house in the shape of a longhaired black dog, or she sits whiningly in the corner as a white goose or in the eaves gutter as a dove.

statement.en: The Klagmuhme often takes animal form: a long-haired black dog howling round the house concerned, a white goose whimpering in the corner, or a dove in the eaves gutter.

claims.quote: The Klagmuhme's human appearance is that of an old woman in a black dress with a white scarf. Otherwise, she is described as a small woman with a face covered with cobwebs who is wearing a little three-cornered hat.

statement.id: Dalam wujud manusia Klagmuhme adalah perempuan tua bergaun hitam berkerudung putih, atau perempuan kecil berwajah tertutup sarang laba-laba bertopi tiga sudut.
statement.en: In human form the Klagmuhme is an old woman in a black dress and white scarf, or a small woman with a cobweb-covered face in a little three-cornered hat.

claims.quote: If the Klagmuhme wails in front of a house where an ill person is inside, clothing belonging to the diseased is thrown outside the door. If the Klagmuhme carries the clothing away, the diseased will undoubtedly die; if she leaves it behind, the diseased will recover. The prophesied disaster can be averted by immediately telling the Klagmuhme an alternative.

statement.id: Bila Klagmuhme meratap di depan rumah orang sakit, pakaian si sakit dilempar keluar; jika ia membawanya pergi, orang itu pasti mati, jika ditinggalkan ia sembuh; bencana yang diramalkan dapat dicegah dengan segera menyebutkan alternatif kepadanya.
statement.en: If the Klagmuhme wails before a house with a sick person, the patient's clothes are thrown outside; if she carries them away he will surely die, if she leaves them he will recover; the foretold disaster can be averted by at once telling her an alternative.

claims.quote: She is usually invisible when she gets close to the houses without ever entering them and floats over them. Her whining (which sounds like "u-u-u!") can cause frightened people to fall ill with a nervous disease. Otherwise, she does nobody harm.

statement.id: Biasanya ia tak terlihat saat mendekati rumah, tanpa pernah masuk, dan melayang di atasnya; rintihannya ("u-u-u!") dapat membuat orang yang ketakutan sakit saraf, tetapi selain itu ia tidak mencelakai siapa pun; ia biasanya aktif tengah malam.
statement.en: She is usually invisible as she nears houses, never entering, floating above them; her whine ('u-u-u!') can give frightened people a nervous illness, but otherwise she harms nobody; she is usually active at midnight.

short_description.id: Aufhocker atau Huckup adalah makhluk pengubah wujud dalam cerita rakyat Jerman yang melompat ke punggung pejalan malam dan makin berat di setiap langkah.
short_description.en: The Aufhocker or Huckup is a shapeshifter of German folklore that leaps onto the backs of night travellers and grows heavier with every step.

long_description.id: Aufhocker (bahasa Jerman Hilir Huckup) adalah makhluk pengubah wujud dalam cerita rakyat Jerman yang tak punya bentuk tetap: ia bisa tampil sebagai goblin, perempuan cantik, orang mati, atau berbagai hewan seperti beruang, anak sapi, manusia serigala, atau anjing. Namanya berarti "yang melompat ke atas", sebab ia melompat ke punggung korbannya, sering pencuri dan penjahat yang perlu diberi pelajaran, pejalan sendirian, atau perempuan tua.
long_description.en: The Aufhocker (Low German Huckup) is a shapeshifter of German folklore with no fixed form: goblin, lovely woman, corpse, or a beast such as a bear, calf, werewolf or dog are all among its guises. Its name means 'leap upon', because it springs onto its victims' backs, often thieves and wrongdoers who need a lesson, lone travellers or old women.

long_description.id: Sebagai roh penekan, ia duduk di bahu pejalan malam dan makin berat di setiap langkah, sehingga korbannya lumpuh, sesak, dan tak bisa menoleh; banyak yang mati kelelahan karena ia tak bisa dienyahkan. Korban dapat bebas bila berhasil sampai di rumah, atau bila datang cahaya fajar, doa, atau dentang lonceng. Serangan ini terjadi di tempat tertentu: jembatan, persimpangan, mata air, hutan, jalan cekung, dan pemakaman.
long_description.en: As a pressure spirit it sits on a night walker's shoulders and grows heavier at each step, leaving the victim paralysed, oppressed and unable to turn around; many die of exhaustion because it cannot be shaken off. A victim can be freed by reaching home, or by dawn light, a prayer or the ringing of bells. Such attacks happen at particular places: bridges, crossroads, springs, woods, sunken lanes and cemeteries.

long_description.id: Kepercayaan akan Aufhocker berakar pada ketakutan terhadap mayat hidup (Wiedergänger): laporan tertua berbicara tentang "mayat yang melompat ke punggung", bukan kobold atau hantu. Sebagian versi menyebut ia merobek leher korban, yang dikaitkan dengan vampirisme. Mitos serupa ada di banyak bagian Eropa, seperti Ganipote di Charente-Maritime, Prancis.
long_description.en: Belief in the Aufhocker is rooted in fear of the revenant (Wiedergänger): the oldest reports speak of 'corpses that leap onto one's back', not of kobolds or ghosts. Some versions say it tears out its victims' throats, which links it with vampirism. Similar myths exist across much of Europe, such as the Ganipote of Charente-Maritime in France.

claims.quote: The aufhocker ( German: [ˈaʊfˌhɔkɐ] ) or huckup ( German: [ˈhʊkˌʔʊp] ) is a shapeshifter in German folklore.

statement.id: Aufhocker atau huckup adalah makhluk pengubah wujud dalam cerita rakyat Jerman (German).
statement.en: The aufhocker or huckup is a shapeshifter of German folklore.

claims.quote: The Aufhocker is described in German legend as having an unidentifiable shape because it takes on shapes such as a goblin, a beautiful woman, a dead man, or various animals.

statement.id: Aufhocker digambarkan tak punya bentuk yang dapat dikenali karena mengambil rupa goblin, perempuan cantik, orang mati, atau berbagai hewan.
statement.en: The Aufhocker is said to have no identifiable shape, taking forms such as a goblin, a beautiful woman, a dead man or various animals.

claims.quote: The name Aufhocker means "leap upon". This name is used because according to legend, the Aufhocker would leap upon the back of its victims which are often thieves and criminals that need to be taught a lesson. Other common targets in the Aufhocker legend are lone travelers and old women.

statement.id: Nama Aufhocker berarti "melompat ke atas", karena menurut legenda ia melompat ke punggung korbannya, sering pencuri dan penjahat yang perlu diberi pelajaran, juga pejalan sendirian dan perempuan tua.
statement.en: The name Aufhocker means 'leap upon', since legend says it leaps onto victims' backs, often thieves and criminals needing a lesson, also lone travellers and old women.

claims.quote: The victims often die of exhaustion because the Aufhocker cannot be shaken off or killed. However, it is believed that travelers can free themselves if they are able to make it home before being killed. These attacks often occur in specific locations such as bridges, crossroads, springs, woods, on a path through a hollow, and cemeteries.

statement.id: Korban sering mati kelelahan karena Aufhocker tak bisa dienyahkan atau dibunuh, tetapi pejalan bisa bebas bila sempat sampai di rumah; serangan terjadi di jembatan, persimpangan, mata air, hutan, jalan cekung, dan pemakaman.
statement.en: Victims often die of exhaustion as the Aufhocker cannot be shaken off or killed, but travellers can free themselves by reaching home; attacks occur at bridges, crossroads, springs, woods, hollow paths and cemeteries.

claims.quote: Similar myths can be found in most of Europe. In the Charente-Maritime département of France, the Ganipote is depicted as having similar traits.

statement.id: Mitos serupa ditemukan di sebagian besar Eropa (Europe); di Charente-Maritime, Prancis (France), Ganipote digambarkan bersifat serupa.
statement.en: Similar myths are found across most of Europe; in Charente-Maritime, France, the Ganipote is described with similar traits.

claims.quote: Der Aufhocker (niederdeutsch Huckup, sorbisch Bubak) ist in der Mythologie ein koboldartiger Druckgeist, der Wanderern, die nachts noch unterwegs sind, auf die Schultern oder den Rücken springt und mit jedem Schritt schwerer wird. ... Der Aufhocker bleibt auf dem Wanderer sitzen, bis dieser durch das heraufbrechende Licht, ein Gebet oder Glockenläuten von ihm erlöst wird

statement.id: Aufhocker (Jerman Hilir Huckup, Sorbia Bubak) adalah roh penekan mirip kobold yang melompat ke bahu atau punggung pejalan malam dan makin berat di setiap langkah; ia tetap duduk di sana sampai pejalan dibebaskan oleh cahaya fajar, doa, atau dentang lonceng.
statement.en: The Aufhocker (Low German Huckup, Sorbian Bubak) is a kobold-like pressure spirit that leaps onto the shoulders or back of night travellers and grows heavier each step; it stays there until the traveller is freed by dawn light, a prayer or bells.

claims.quote: Manchmal treten die Aufhocker zunächst als mitleiderregende alte Frauen in Erscheinung; sie können aber auch Tiergestalten wie Bär, Kalb (wie beim Bahkauv), Werwolf (wie beim Stüpp) oder Hund (wie beim Sürthgens Mossel) annehmen.

statement.id: Aufhocker kadang muncul sebagai perempuan tua yang memancing iba, tetapi juga bisa berwujud hewan seperti beruang, anak sapi (Bahkauv), manusia serigala (Stüpp), atau anjing.
statement.en: Aufhockers sometimes first appear as pitiable old women, but can also take animal forms such as a bear, calf (Bahkauv), werewolf (Stüpp) or dog.

claims.quote: Typische Spukorte wie Bäche, Brücken, Seen, Wälder, Gräben, Wegkreuzungen, Hohlwege, Kirchhöfe und Mord- oder Richtstätten sind die übliche Stelle für eine Begegnung mit dem Aufhocker

statement.id: Tempat angker yang khas seperti sungai kecil, jembatan, danau, hutan, parit, persimpangan, jalan cekung, pemakaman, serta tempat pembunuhan atau eksekusi adalah lokasi umum pertemuan dengan Aufhocker.
statement.en: Typical haunted places such as brooks, bridges, lakes, woods, ditches, crossroads, sunken lanes, churchyards and murder or execution sites are where one usually meets the Aufhocker.

claims.quote: Seine Ursprünge hat der Glaube an den Aufhocker jedoch in der Furcht vor dem Wiedergänger, dem Untoten. Die ältesten Berichte über Aufhocker sprechen eindeutig von „aufhuckenden Leichen“ und nicht von Kobolden oder Gespenstern.

statement.id: Kepercayaan akan Aufhocker berakar pada ketakutan terhadap Wiedergänger (mayat hidup); laporan tertua jelas berbicara tentang "mayat yang melompat ke punggung" (aufhuckenden Leichen), bukan kobold atau hantu.
statement.en: Belief in the Aufhocker stems from fear of the Wiedergänger (revenant); the oldest reports clearly speak of 'corpses leaping onto backs' (aufhuckenden Leichen), not kobolds or ghosts.

claims.quote: The Aufhocker is a very dangerous theriomorph that is sometimes said to tear out the throats of humans instead of killing its victims from exhaustion. The version of the Aufhocker that attacks victims' throats is linked to vampirism.

statement.id: Aufhocker kadang dikatakan merobek leher manusia alih-alih membunuh korban dengan kelelahan; versi ini dikaitkan dengan vampirisme.
statement.en: The Aufhocker is sometimes said to tear out human throats rather than exhaust its victims; this version is linked to vampirism.

claims.quote: Um solch einen Aufhocker handelt es sich auch bei dem Hackestüpp von Düren, der seine Opfer zunächst als verspieltes Hündchen begleitet, ihnen dann auf den Rücken springt, sich nicht mehr abschütteln lässt und von Schritt zu Schritt schwerer wird.

statement.id: Hackestüpp dari Düren juga Aufhocker: mula-mula menemani korbannya sebagai anak anjing yang lucu, lalu melompat ke punggung mereka, tak bisa dienyahkan, dan makin berat di setiap langkah.
statement.en: The Hackestüpp of Düren is such an Aufhocker: it first follows victims as a playful puppy, then leaps onto their backs, cannot be shaken off and grows heavier step by step.

claims.quote: Das Bahkauv („Bachkalb“) ist eine Aachener Sagengestalt, die nachts betrunkene Männer erschrecken und sie auffordern soll, sie auf ihren Schultern zu tragen.

statement.id: Bahkauv ("anak sapi sungai") adalah tokoh legenda Aachen (Aachener) yang konon menakuti lelaki mabuk pada malam hari dan meminta digendong di bahu mereka.
statement.en: The Bahkauv ('brook calf') is an Aachen legend figure said to frighten drunken men at night and demand to be carried on their shoulders.

claims.quote: Der Wanderer ist wie gelähmt, leidet unter Beklemmung und ist unfähig sich umzuwenden.

statement.id: Pejalan seperti lumpuh, merasa sesak, dan tak mampu menoleh.
statement.en: The traveller is as if paralysed, feels oppressed and cannot turn around.

short_description.id: Aufhocker atau Huckup adalah makhluk pengubah wujud dalam cerita rakyat Jerman yang melompat ke punggung pejalan malam dan makin berat di setiap langkah.
short_description.en: The Aufhocker or Huckup is a shapeshifter of German folklore that leaps onto the backs of night travellers and grows heavier with every step.

long_description.id: Aufhocker (bahasa Jerman Hilir Huckup) adalah makhluk pengubah wujud dalam cerita rakyat Jerman yang tak punya bentuk tetap: ia bisa tampil sebagai goblin, perempuan cantik, orang mati, atau berbagai hewan seperti beruang, anak sapi, manusia serigala, atau anjing. Namanya berarti "yang melompat ke atas", sebab ia melompat ke punggung korbannya, sering pencuri dan penjahat yang perlu diberi pelajaran, pejalan sendirian, atau perempuan tua.
long_description.en: The Aufhocker (Low German Huckup) is a shapeshifter of German folklore with no fixed form: goblin, lovely woman, corpse, or a beast such as a bear, calf, werewolf or dog are all among its guises. Its name means 'leap upon', because it springs onto its victims' backs, often thieves and wrongdoers who need a lesson, lone travellers or old women.

long_description.id: Sebagai roh penekan, ia duduk di bahu pejalan malam dan makin berat di setiap langkah, sehingga korbannya lumpuh, sesak, dan tak bisa menoleh; banyak yang mati kelelahan karena ia tak bisa dienyahkan. Korban dapat bebas bila berhasil sampai di rumah, atau bila datang cahaya fajar, doa, atau dentang lonceng. Serangan ini terjadi di tempat tertentu: jembatan, persimpangan, mata air, hutan, jalan cekung, dan pemakaman.
long_description.en: As a pressure spirit it sits on a night walker's shoulders and grows heavier at each step, leaving the victim paralysed, oppressed and unable to turn around; many die of exhaustion because it cannot be shaken off. A victim can be freed by reaching home, or by dawn light, a prayer or the ringing of bells. Such attacks happen at particular places: bridges, crossroads, springs, woods, sunken lanes and cemeteries.

long_description.id: Kepercayaan akan Aufhocker berakar pada ketakutan terhadap mayat hidup (Wiedergänger): laporan tertua berbicara tentang "mayat yang melompat ke punggung", bukan kobold atau hantu. Sebagian versi menyebut ia merobek leher korban, yang dikaitkan dengan vampirisme. Mitos serupa ada di banyak bagian Eropa, seperti Ganipote di Charente-Maritime, Prancis.
long_description.en: Belief in the Aufhocker is rooted in fear of the revenant (Wiedergänger): the oldest reports speak of 'corpses that leap onto one's back', not of kobolds or ghosts. Some versions say it tears out its victims' throats, which links it with vampirism. Similar myths exist across much of Europe, such as the Ganipote of Charente-Maritime in France.

claims.quote: Typische Spukorte wie Bäche, Brücken, Seen, Wälder, Gräben, Wegkreuzungen, Hohlwege, Kirchhöfe und Mord- oder Richtstätten sind die übliche Stelle für eine Begegnung mit dem Aufhocker

claims.statement: Belief in the Aufhocker stems from fear of the Wiedergänger (revenant); the oldest reports clearly speak of 'corpses leaping onto backs' (aufhuckenden Leichen), not kobolds or ghosts.
claims.statement_id: Kepercayaan akan Aufhocker berakar pada ketakutan terhadap Wiedergänger (mayat hidup); laporan tertua jelas berbicara tentang "mayat yang melompat ke punggung" (aufhuckenden Leichen), bukan kobold atau hantu.
claims.quote: Seine Ursprünge hat der Glaube an den Aufhocker jedoch in der Furcht vor dem Wiedergänger, dem Untoten. Die ältesten Berichte über Aufhocker sprechen eindeutig von „aufhuckenden Leichen“ und nicht von Kobolden oder Gespenstern.

claims.statement: The Aufhocker is sometimes said to tear out human throats rather than exhaust its victims; this version is linked to vampirism.
claims.statement_id: Aufhocker kadang dikatakan merobek leher manusia alih-alih membunuh korban dengan kelelahan; versi ini dikaitkan dengan vampirisme.
claims.quote: The Aufhocker is a very dangerous theriomorph that is sometimes said to tear out the throats of humans instead of killing its victims from exhaustion. The version of the Aufhocker that attacks victims' throats is linked to vampirism.

claims.statement: The Hackestüpp of Düren is such an Aufhocker: it first follows victims as a playful puppy, then leaps onto their backs, cannot be shaken off and grows heavier step by step.
claims.statement_id: Hackestüpp dari Düren juga Aufhocker: mula-mula menemani korbannya sebagai anak anjing yang lucu, lalu melompat ke punggung mereka, tak bisa dienyahkan, dan makin berat di setiap langkah.
claims.quote: Um solch einen Aufhocker handelt es sich auch bei dem Hackestüpp von Düren, der seine Opfer zunächst als verspieltes Hündchen begleitet, ihnen dann auf den Rücken springt, sich nicht mehr abschütteln lässt und von Schritt zu Schritt schwerer wird.

claims.statement: The Bahkauv ('brook calf') is an Aachen legend figure said to frighten drunken men at night and demand to be carried on their shoulders.
claims.statement_id: Bahkauv ("anak sapi sungai") adalah tokoh legenda Aachen (Aachener) yang konon menakuti lelaki mabuk pada malam hari dan meminta digendong di bahu mereka.
claims.quote: Das Bahkauv („Bachkalb“) ist eine Aachener Sagengestalt, die nachts betrunkene Männer erschrecken und sie auffordern soll, sie auf ihren Schultern zu tragen.

claims.statement: The traveller is as if paralysed, feels oppressed and cannot turn around.
claims.statement_id: Pejalan seperti lumpuh, merasa sesak, dan tak mampu menoleh.
claims.quote: Der Wanderer ist wie gelähmt, leidet unter Beklemmung und ist unfähig sich umzuwenden.

short_description.id: Buschgroßmutter ("nenek semak") adalah roh hutan perempuan tua dalam cerita rakyat Jerman, ibu dan pemimpin para Moosfräulein, yang membalas kebaikan dengan hadiah dan ejekan dengan penyakit.
short_description.en: The Buschgroßmutter ('shrub grandmother') is an aged female forest spirit of German folklore, mother and leader of the Moosfräulein, who rewards kindness with gifts and mockery with sickness.

long_description.id: Buschgroßmutter adalah makhluk legenda Jerman yang terutama dikenal di Thüringen, Sachsen, Silesia, dan Bohemia, dengan nama daerah seperti Pusch-Grohla dan Buschmutter di Silesia serta Buschweibchen di Bohemia. Ia roh hutan yang tinggal di hutan terdalam dan hanya menampakkan diri kepada manusia sekali dalam seratus tahun: kecil, bungkuk, keriput, bermata melotot, berambut panjang seputih salju tetapi kusut dan berkutu, dengan tongkat bengkok dan kaki berlumut.
long_description.en: The Buschgroßmutter is a creature of German legend known chiefly in Thuringia, Saxony, Silesia and Bohemia, under regional names such as Pusch-Grohla and Buschmutter in Silesia and Buschweibchen in Bohemia. She is a forest spirit dwelling in the deepest woods who shows herself to people only once in a hundred years: small, stooped, wrinkled and staring, with long snow-white but tangled, lousy hair, a gnarled stick and moss-grown feet.

long_description.id: Sifatnya mendua. Ia meminta orang menyisir atau mencari kutu di rambutnya, dan yang memenuhinya diberi gulungan benang yang tak habis atau daun yang kelak menjadi emas, meski kepalanya sedingin es. Siapa yang mengejeknya akan dihembus napasnya dan jatuh sakit, biasanya ruam kulit. Kabut yang naik dari pegunungan di musim semi dan gugur dianggap tanda ia sedang memasak.
long_description.en: Her nature is two-sided. She asks people to comb or delouse her hair, and those who do are given an endless clew of yarn or leaves that later turn to gold, though her head is as cold as ice. Whoever mocks her is breathed on and falls ill, usually with a rash. Fog rising from the mountains in spring and autumn is taken as a sign that she is cooking.

long_description.id: Menurut artikel bahasa Jerman, di tepi Saale ia dianggap nyonya dan ibu para Moosweiblein (Moosfräulein), yang berkeliling negeri bersamanya dengan kereta kecil pada malam-malam suci; ia juga dipakai untuk menakut-nakuti anak dan disamakan dengan Frau Holle atau Perchta. Para mitolog abad ke-19 menganggapnya ratu orang lumut, tetapi kini ia lebih dipandang sebagai setan hutan yang sederhana.
long_description.en: According to the German article, by the Saale she is held to be the mistress and mother of the Moosweiblein (Moosfräulein), who roam the land with her in a little cart during the holy nights; she is also used to frighten children and equated with Frau Holle or Perchta. Nineteenth-century mythologists saw her as queen of the moss people, but she is now rather viewed as a primitive forest demon.

role.en: Rewards those who comb her hair.

did_you_know.id: Siapa yang menyisir rambut Buschgroßmutter konon diberi daun hijau atau kuning yang kelak berubah menjadi emas, asalkan tidak dibuang.
did_you_know.en: Anyone who combed the Buschgroßmutter's hair was said to receive green or yellow leaves that would later turn to gold, as long as they were not thrown away.

description.id: Padanan di kalangan Saxon Transilvania: roh hutan berambut kusut, bermata menyala, dan bergigi besar yang dipakai untuk menakut-nakuti anak.
description.en: The Transylvanian Saxon equivalent: a forest sprite with shaggy hair, large fiery eyes and big teeth used to frighten children.

note.en: Mother and leader of the Moosfräulein.

note.id: Disamakan dengan Frau Holle atau Perchta.
note.en: Equated with Frau Holle or Perchta.

claims.quote: is a legendary creature from German folklore, especially found in folktales from the regions Thuringia, Saxony, former German-speaking Silesia and the former German-speaking parts of Bohemia. She is called various regional names such as Pusch-Grohla ("shrub granny" in Silesian German) and Buschmutter ("shrub mother") in Silesia, 's Buschkathel ("th' Shrub-Katie") and Buschweibchen in Bohemia

statement.id: Buschgroßmutter ("nenek semak") adalah makhluk legenda cerita rakyat Jerman (German), terutama di Thüringen (Thuringia), Sachsen (Saxony), Silesia, dan Bohemia, dengan nama daerah Pusch-Grohla dan Buschmutter di Silesia serta Buschweibchen di Bohemia.
statement.en: The Buschgroßmutter ('shrub grandmother') is a legendary creature of German folklore, especially in Thuringia, Saxony, Silesia and Bohemia, called Pusch-Grohla and Buschmutter in Silesia and Buschweibchen in Bohemia.

claims.quote: The Buschgroßmutter is a forest spirit living in the deepest woods which shows herself to humans only once every hundred years. She is as old as the hills, her appearance being small and ducked, wrinkly and ugly. She has staring eyes and is sometimes said to have an iron head, a typical demonic feature. The Buschgroßmutter's hair is long, as white as snow, but messy and full of lice.

statement.id: Buschgroßmutter adalah roh hutan di hutan terdalam yang menampakkan diri hanya sekali tiap seratus tahun; ia sangat tua, kecil, bungkuk, keriput, bermata melotot, berambut panjang seputih salju tetapi kusut dan berkutu.
statement.en: The Buschgroßmutter is a forest spirit of the deepest woods, showing herself only once a century; ancient, small, stooped, wrinkled and staring, with long snow-white but tangled, lice-ridden hair.

claims.quote: When the mountains are "smoking" with fog in spring and autumn, then the Buschweibchen is said to be cooking.

statement.id: Bila pegunungan "berasap" oleh kabut pada musim semi dan gugur, Buschweibchen dikatakan sedang memasak.
statement.en: When the mountains 'smoke' with fog in spring and autumn, the Buschweibchen is said to be cooking.

claims.quote: The character of the Buschgroßmutter is ambivalent, fluctuating between benevolent and malevolent behaviour. She asks people to comb or louse her hair. Those who fulfill her request will be rewarded with a neverending clew of yarn ... or with either green or yellow leaves which will later become gold if not thrown away.

statement.id: Watak Buschgroßmutter mendua antara baik dan jahat; ia meminta orang menyisir atau mencari kutu di rambutnya, dan yang memenuhinya diberi gulungan benang tak habis atau daun hijau atau kuning yang kelak menjadi emas bila tak dibuang.
statement.en: The Buschgroßmutter's character wavers between benevolent and malevolent; she asks people to comb or delouse her hair, and those who comply get an endless clew of yarn or green or yellow leaves that later become gold if kept.

claims.quote: It is but very difficult to clean and tidy the Buschweibchen's hair because her head is as cold as ice, thus leading to a (temporary) freezing of the helper's hands. When she was sneered at, the Buschgroßmutter takes revenge by breathing on the sneerer which will result in illnesses, most commonly rash.

statement.id: Merapikan rambutnya sangat sulit karena kepalanya sedingin es sehingga tangan penolong membeku sementara; bila diejek, Buschgroßmutter membalas dengan menghembuskan napas pada pengejek, yang lalu sakit, biasanya ruam kulit.
statement.en: Tidying her hair is very hard since her head is ice-cold, briefly freezing the helper's hands; when sneered at, the Buschgroßmutter takes revenge by breathing on the mocker, who falls ill, usually with a rash.

claims.quote: Normally the Buschgroßmutter is a solitary figure, but occasionally she is said to be the leader of a horde of Moosfräulein ("moss ladies"), female forest spirits which are said to be her daughters. Accompanied by her daughters, the Buschgroßmutter roams the countryside in holy nights.

statement.id: Biasanya Buschgroßmutter penyendiri, tetapi kadang dikatakan memimpin rombongan Moosfräulein, roh hutan perempuan yang disebut putri-putrinya, dan bersama mereka berkeliling negeri pada malam-malam suci.
statement.en: The Buschgroßmutter is usually solitary, but at times said to lead a band of Moosfräulein, female forest spirits called her daughters, roaming the land with them in the holy nights.

claims.quote: Als Herrin der Moosweiblein wird an der Saale die Buschgroßmutter bezeichnet. Die Buschgroßmutter ist genau genommen die Mutter der Moosweiblein (hier: Moosfräuleins), mit welchen sie im Lande umherzieht, meist in einem kleinen Rollwagen. Sie hat wirres Haar und einen starren Blick. Die Buschgroßmutter ist auch ein Kinderschreck. Sie entspricht der andernorts verbreiteten Frau Holle oder Perchta.

statement.id: Di tepi Saale, Buschgroßmutter disebut nyonya para Moosweiblein; tepatnya ia ibu para Moosweiblein (Moosfräuleins) yang berkeliling negeri bersamanya dengan kereta kecil; rambutnya kusut, tatapannya kaku, ia juga penakut anak, dan sepadan dengan Frau Holle atau Perchta.
statement.en: By the Saale the Buschgroßmutter is called mistress of the Moosweiblein; strictly she is their mother (Moosfräuleins), roaming the land with them, usually in a little cart; with tangled hair and a fixed stare, she is also a bogey for children and corresponds to Frau Holle or Perchta.

claims.quote: In the 19th century, mythologists such as Jacob Grimm or Wilhelm Mannhardt declared the Buschgroßmutter to be the leader or even the queen of the moss people, similar to the elf queen.

statement.id: Pada abad ke-19 para mitolog seperti Jacob Grimm dan Wilhelm Mannhardt menyatakan Buschgroßmutter pemimpin atau bahkan ratu orang lumut, seperti ratu elf.
statement.en: In the 19th century mythologists like Jacob Grimm and Wilhelm Mannhardt made the Buschgroßmutter leader or even queen of the moss people, like an elf queen.

claims.quote: In traditional folktales of the German-speaking Transylvanian Saxons in Transylvania, today part of Romania, there is a similar being called Baschgrîs ("shrub grandmother"), Baschmôter ("shrub mother") or Baschäinjel ("shrub angel") in Transylvanian Saxon dialect.

statement.id: Dalam cerita rakyat Saxon Transilvania (Transylvanian Saxons) berbahasa Jerman di Transilvania, kini bagian Rumania, terdapat makhluk serupa bernama Baschgrîs, Baschmôter, atau Baschäinjel.
statement.en: In folktales of the German-speaking Transylvanian Saxons, in today's Romania, there is a similar being called Baschgrîs, Baschmôter or Baschäinjel.

claims.quote: Während sie von den Mythologen des 19. Jahrhunderts als Königin der Moosleute betrachtet wurde, wird sie doch eher als primitiver Walddämon gesehen.

statement.id: Meski para mitolog abad ke-19 menganggapnya ratu orang lumut (Moosleute), ia lebih dipandang sebagai setan hutan primitif.
statement.en: Though 19th-century mythologists regarded her as queen of the moss people (Moosleute), she is rather seen as a primitive forest demon.

claims.quote: All three names are used to scare children and denote a female wood sprite with shaggy fluttering hair, large fiery eyes and very big teeth.

statement.id: Ketiga nama itu dipakai untuk menakuti anak-anak dan menunjuk roh hutan perempuan berambut kusut berkibar, bermata besar menyala, dan bergigi sangat besar.
statement.en: All three names serve to scare children and denote a female wood sprite with shaggy, fluttering hair, large fiery eyes and very big teeth.

long_description.en: The Buschgroßmutter ("shrub grandmother", in older orthography also Buschgrossmutter; German: [ˈbʊʃˌɡʁoːsˌmʊtɐ]) is a legendary creature from German folklore, especially found in folktales from the regions Thuringia, Saxony, former German-speaking Silesia and the former German-speaking parts of Bohemia. She is called various regional names such as Pusch-Grohla ("shrub granny" in Silesian German) and Buschmutter ("shrub mother") in Silesia, 's Buschkathel ("th' Shrub-Katie") and Buschweibchen in Bohemia, Buschweiblein and Buschweibel in Silesia again. Buschweibchen, Buschweiblein, and Buschweibel all mean "shrub woman", with Weibchen, Weiblein or Weibel being the diminutive of Weib, "woman". The Buschgroßmutter is a forest spirit living in the deepest woods which shows herself to humans only once every hundred years. She is as old as the hills, her appearance being small and ducked, wrinkly and ugly. She has staring eyes and is sometimes said to have an iron head, a typical demonic feature. The Buschgroßmutter's hair is long, as white as snow, but messy and full of lice. The Buschweibchen holds a gnarled stick in her hand. Her feet are overgrown by moss and she walks in a wavering manner. She has tied her apron as if she were transporting something in it and also carries a basket on her back. The Buschmutter is ugly, wearing a tatterered dress and having dishevelled hair, holding a crutch. The Buschweibchen manifests herself in different natural phenomena. When the mountains are "smoking" with fog in spring and autumn, then the Buschweibchen is said to be cooking. Also when a hailstorm comes up in April and the mountains look veiled, then the Buschweibchen climbs over the mountains. The character of the Buschgroßmutter is ambivalent, fluctuating between benevolent and malevolent behaviour. She asks people to comb or louse her hair. Those who fulfill her request will be rewarded with a neverending clew of yarn, with a spindle covered with a hundred strands of yarn which might vanish through cussing or with either green or yellow leaves which will later become gold if not thrown away. It is but very difficult to clean and tidy the Buschweibchen's hair because her head is as cold as ice, thus leading to a (temporary) freezing of the helper's hands. When she was sneered at, the Buschgroßmutter takes revenge by breathing on the sneerer which will result in illnesses, most commonly rash. Alternatively she will perch herself on the sneerer, also leading to negative effects. When called Buschmutter, this woman of the woods is simply evil, e.g. when she attacks children picking berries to steal their harvest and break their jars used to hold the gathered berries. She also steals the milk of a herdsman's cows by milking them dry and wakes up napping cowherds by hitting them ruggedly with her crutch. The Buschgroßmutter is regionally used to scare the children as is the Buschmutter. Normally the Buschgroßmutter is a solitary figure, but occasionally she is said to be the leader of a horde of Moosfräulein ("moss ladies"), female forest spirits which are said to be her daughters. Accompanied by her daughters, the Buschgroßmutter roams the countryside in holy nights. At those times, she travels in a little cart or waggon and people try to stay out of her way. Robert Eisel summarizes the typical characteristics of the Buschgroßemutter, as he calls her, in his Sagenbuch des Voigtlandes (Book of Folk Tales from the Voigtland): "Near Leutenberg, during the holy nights, the Buschgroßemutter wanders around the country with her daughters, the Moosfräuleins. You can recognize her by the staring eyes, the shaggy hair, and her small cart, and it would not be advisable to encounter her." (Translated from the German text) A folk tale from the Bavarian Forest gives a hint on how much older the Buschgroßmutter might be compared to her descendants. A Moosweibel ("moss woman") traversing the forest at night, described as being hunchbacked and half blind, found three charburners asleep in the forest, their heads placed on a sack of moss and their feet stretched out in different directions. Feeling them, the Moosweibel got the impression of having found a creature with six legs and a single head, the likes of which she had never seen before despite being so old that the knew the Bohemian Forest nine times as pure forest and nine times as consisting of both meadows and forest. So impressed she was, that she hurried home to tell her grandmother, who she said was nine times as old as herself. In the 19th century, mythologists such as Jacob Grimm or Wilhelm Mannhardt declared the Buschgroßmutter to be the leader or even the queen of the moss people, similar to the elf queen. Ludwig Bechstein, another mythologist of the 19th century, declared her to be identical with legendary creatures such as Hulda or Bertha, which were interpreted as ancient goddesses at that time, basically on the same level as the historically recorded Germanic goddesses. This view was abandoned in early 20th century, thus defining Buschgroßmutter and Buschweibchen as forest demons of the most primitive kind.

short_description.id: Fenixmännlein adalah roh tanah dan kurcaci dalam cerita rakyat Jerman dari Silesia dan Lusatia, penghuni bukit yang terkenal suka memanggang kue dan menukar bayi manusia dengan anak tukar.
short_description.en: The Fenixmännlein are earth sprites and dwarfs of German folklore from Silesia and Lusatia, hill-dwellers famed for baking cake and for swapping human babies with changelings.

long_description.id: Fenixmännlein, juga disebut Fenixmännel, Fenskemännel, atau Fenesleute, adalah roh tanah dan kurcaci dari cerita rakyat Jerman yang dahulu dikenal di Silesia, terutama di Oderské vrchy dan Hrubý Jeseník, serta di bagian Lusatia milik Sachsen. Mereka lebih besar dari kurcaci tetapi lebih kecil dari manusia, sehingga namanya mungkin terkait dengan Venedigermännlein, "lelaki kecil dari Venesia". Mereka hidup berkelompok di bukit dan semak.
long_description.en: The Fenixmännlein, also called Fenixmännel, Fenskemännel or Fenesleute, are earth sprites and dwarfs of German folklore once known in Silesia, especially the Oderské vrchy and Hrubý Jeseník, and in the Saxon part of Lusatia. They are bigger than dwarfs but smaller than people, so their name may be linked with the Venedigermännlein, 'little Venetian men'. They live in groups in hills and shrubbery.

long_description.id: Di dalam gunung mereka berpesta besar, dan mereka konon pemilik asli resep kue streusel Silesia; asap yang naik dari lubang tanah menandakan mereka sedang memanggang. Para petani yang meminta sepotong kue kadang mendapatkannya, tetapi harus memakannya di atas "meja besi", misalnya mata bajak, dan kue itu bisa berubah menjadi timah, debu, atau emas.
long_description.en: Deep inside the mountains they hold great feasts, and Silesian streuselkuchen is said to have been their recipe first; whenever smoke drifts up from holes in the ground, they are baking. Farmhands who asked for a piece of cake were sometimes given one, but had to eat it on an 'iron table', such as a ploughshare, and the cake might turn to lead, dust or gold.

long_description.id: Mereka kadang menukar bayi manusia dengan anak tukar mereka sendiri dan suka menculik perempuan yang baru melahirkan untuk mengasuh anak-anak mereka. Untuk menyelamatkan korban, sang penyelamat harus berkuda secepatnya sambil melempar rami, sisir, dan sabun di belakangnya agar para kurcaci sibuk. Menurut berbagai tradisi, mereka akhirnya meninggalkan negeri itu karena jalur kereta api, peterseli dalam masakan, atau dentang lonceng gereja.
long_description.en: They sometimes swap human babies for their own changelings and like to abduct women in childbed to nurse their children. To save a victim, the rescuer must ride as fast as he can, throwing flax, a comb and soap behind him to keep the dwarfs busy. Various traditions say they finally left the land because of the railways, parsley in people's food or the ringing of church bells.

role.en: Owners of the Silesian streuselkuchen recipe.

did_you_know.id: Fenixmännlein konon pemilik asli resep kue streusel Silesia, dan asap dari lubang tanah menandakan mereka sedang memanggang.

long_description.en: The Fenixmännlein (sg., pl.; German: [ˈfeːnɪksˌmɛnlaɪ̯n]; Männlein = little man), also called Fenixmännel, Fenskemännel, Feensmännel (all sg., pl.;Männel = little man in Silesian German) or Fenesleute (pl.; Leute = people) among other names are earth sprites and dwarves from German folklore. They were historically known in Silesia, particularly in the Oderské vrchy and Hrubý Jeseník as well as in the part of Lusatia belonging to Saxony. The first element of the name, Fenix- or variants, might either come from a Middle High German expression ein wenigez mennelin (= a little diminutive man) or from legendary beings called Venedigermännlein (sg., pl.; little Venetian men) or Walen (pl., sg. Wale), a kind of mythical miners or prospectors often said to hail from Venice. The latter option is supported by the fact that both Fenixmännlein and Venedigermännlein are supposed to be bigger than dwarves (German Zwerge, sg. Zwerg) but smaller than humans. The Fenixmännlein are collective beings dwelling in hills and shrubbery. Inside the mountains, they throw big parties. The Fenismannla (pl. Mannla = little men in Silesian German) are said to be the original owners of the recipe for Silesian streuselkuchen. When the Fänismännchen (sg., pl.;Männchen = little man) are baking cake in their caves, smoke is rising from earth holes and from beneath clods. They also can be heard kneading dough and forming cakes. But not only the male Fenixmännlein know how to bake, their female equivalent, the Venusweiblein (sg., pl.; Weiblein = little woman), do too. The Fenichmännchen or Fenskemännchen (both sg., pl.) cook as well. The same is true for the Fenskeweibel (sg., pl.; Weibel = little woman in Silesian German) who also gather wood and grind coffee with a coffee grinder. Furthermore, the Vensmännel dry their linen on the riverbank.

short_description.id: Sjörå ("penjaga danau") atau Sjöfru adalah roh danau dalam kepercayaan rakyat Swedia, perempuan menggoda yang memberi tangkapan melimpah kepada nelayan yang baik dan menenggelamkan yang tak hormat.
short_description.en: The sjörå ('keeper of the lake') or Sjöfru is a lake spirit of Swedish folk belief, a seductive woman who grants good catches to kind fishermen and drowns the disrespectful.

long_description.id: Sjörå atau Sjöfru ("nyonya danau") adalah makhluk danau dalam kepercayaan rakyat Swedia: roh atau penguasa yang menjaga sebuah telaga, danau, atau bahkan seluruh sistem danau. Ia padanan air dari skogsrå, dan dapat membantu nelayan seperti skogsrå membantu pemburu, meski air membuatnya lebih enggan bergaul dengan manusia.
long_description.en: The sjörå or Sjöfru ('mistress of the lake') is a lake being of Swedish folk belief: the spirit or ruler watching over a pond, a lake or even a whole lake system. She is the watery counterpart of the skogsrå and can help fishermen as the skogsrå helps hunters, though the water makes her less willing to mix with people.

long_description.id: Ia biasanya roh air perempuan berwujud manusia yang menggoda, sering duduk di batu menyisir rambutnya yang panjang dan gelap, kadang berpunggung berongga atau sebagian bersisik. Ia memikat dan menenggelamkan lelaki yang tidak ramah, tidak setia, atau tidak hormat kepadanya atau danaunya, tetapi berbeda dengan näcken jarang menenggelamkan orang karena dengki semata. Kepada yang baik hati ia memberi tangkapan melimpah, menyelamatkan mereka dari tenggelam, dan memperingatkan badai. Ia mudah diusir dengan benda logam, misalnya pisau ikan yang dilempar ke depan kakinya.
long_description.en: She is usually a seductive, humanlike female water spirit, often sitting on a stone combing her long dark hair, sometimes hollow-backed or partly scaled. She lures and drowns men who are unkind, unfaithful or disrespectful to her or her lake, but unlike the näck she seldom drowns people out of sheer malice. To the kind she grants rich catches, rescues them from drowning and warns of storms. She can easily be driven off with metal, such as a fishing knife thrown before her feet.

long_description.id: Kisah populer menceritakan nelayan yang memberi sarung tangan kepada sjörå yang menjulurkan tangan dari air pada musim dingin, lalu diberi tangkapan melimpah dan diperingatkan saat badai datang; kisah ini dicatat Olaus Magnus. Ia juga memelihara ternak danau (sjönöt), berupa sapi belang di tepi air atau ikan perch dan pike besar. Sjörå laki-laki digambarkan lebih mirip troll, dan salah satunya, Håvålen, menikahi perempuan manusia sebelum kembali ke air di akhir hidupnya.
long_description.en: A popular tale tells of a fisherman who gave a mitten to a sjörå reaching her hand out of the water in winter and was rewarded with rich catches and warnings of storms; the story is recorded by Olaus Magnus. She also keeps lake cattle (sjönöt), striped cows by the shore or large perch and pike. Male sjörå are described as more troll-like, and one of them, Håvålen, took a human wife and lived among people, going back to the lake only when his life drew to a close.

role.id: Memberi tangkapan melimpah kepada yang baik.
role.en: Grants good catches to the kind.

did_you_know.id: Nelayan yang memberi sarung tangan kepada sjörå yang menjulurkan tangan dari air konon dibalas dengan tangkapan melimpah dan peringatan badai.
did_you_know.en: A fisherman who gave a mitten to a sjörå reaching out of the water was said to be repaid with rich catches and storm warnings.

description.id: Melempar pisau ikan ke depan kakinya membuatnya lenyap.
description.en: Throwing a fishing knife before her feet makes her vanish.

note.id: Sjörå adalah padanan air dari skogsrå.
note.en: The sjörå is the watery counterpart of the skogsrå.

note.id: Sjörå dan näcken saling tidak suka dan jarang berbagi perairan.
note.en: The sjörå and the näck dislike each other and rarely share waters.

claims.quote: The sjörå (in Swedish) , (lake Sjö) or the Sjöfru (Mistress of the Lake) was a mythical creature of the lake, or sjö, in Swedish folklore.

statement.id: Sjörå atau Sjöfru ("nyonya danau") adalah makhluk mitis danau dalam cerita rakyat Swedia (Swedish).
statement.en: The sjörå or Sjöfru ('Mistress of the Lake') was a mythical lake creature in Swedish folklore.

claims.quote: Sjörå are considered to be the aquatic equivalent of the skogsrå, in that they can help fishermen the same way the skogsrå can help hunters. They are generally less willing to become involved with humans than skogsrå due to the separation provided by the water.

statement.id: Sjörå dianggap padanan air dari skogsrå: dapat membantu nelayan seperti skogsrå membantu pemburu, tetapi umumnya lebih enggan bergaul dengan manusia karena dipisahkan air.
statement.en: Sjörå are considered the aquatic equivalent of the skogsrå, helping fishermen as the skogsrå helps hunters, but generally less involved with humans because of the water's separation.

claims.quote: She is a seductive creature, often featured sitting and combing her long, sweeping hair with delight, and often lures and drowns men who are unkind, unfaithful or otherwise disrespectful to her or the lake. Like all other rå (keepers) she protects her domain and awards those kind to her with prosperous fishing and good luck, by rescuing them from drowning and warning of incoming storms.

statement.id: Ia makhluk penggoda yang sering duduk menyisir rambut panjangnya dengan gembira, dan sering memikat serta menenggelamkan lelaki yang tidak ramah, tidak setia, atau tidak hormat kepadanya atau danau; seperti rå lain ia menjaga wilayahnya dan memberi yang baik kepadanya tangkapan melimpah, menyelamatkan dari tenggelam, dan memperingatkan badai.
statement.en: She is a seductive creature, often shown happily combing her long hair, who lures and drowns men unkind, unfaithful or disrespectful to her or the lake; like all rå she guards her domain and rewards the kind with good fishing, rescue from drowning and storm warnings.

claims.quote: Male sjörå are described as appearing more like trolls, and are as protective of the water as female sjörå. Some stories have them attempt to drown or blind humans. One particular male sjörå named Håvålen lived amongst humans married a human woman before returning to the water at the end of his life.

statement.id: Sjörå laki-laki digambarkan lebih mirip troll dan sama protektifnya terhadap air; sebagian kisah menyebut mereka mencoba menenggelamkan atau membutakan manusia; seorang sjörå laki-laki bernama Håvålen tinggal di antara manusia, menikahi perempuan manusia, lalu kembali ke air di akhir hidupnya.
statement.en: Male sjörå look more troll-like and are as protective of the water; some tales have them try to drown or blind people; one male sjörå, Håvålen, lived among humans and married a human woman before returning to the water at life's end.

claims.quote: Sjörået är i nordisk folktro namnet på den ande eller rådare som vakar över en tjärn, en insjö eller – om det är ett mäktigt sjörå – över ett helt sjösystem.

statement.id: Dalam kepercayaan rakyat Nordik (nordisk), sjörå adalah nama roh atau penguasa yang menjaga telaga, danau, atau, bila sjörå itu kuat, seluruh sistem danau.
statement.en: In Nordic (nordisk) folk belief, the sjörå is the spirit or ruler watching over a pond, a lake or, if mighty, a whole lake system.

claims.quote: Liksom skogsrået var hon en förförisk kvinnlig humanoid, som ibland kunde ha ihålig rygg eller vara delvis täckt med fjäll. ... För att undvika närkontakt med henne kunde man lätt skrämma bort henne med ett metallföremål. Ett sådant knep var att kasta fiskekniven framför hennes fötter och vips var hon försvunnen.

statement.id: Seperti skogsrå ia perempuan berwujud manusia yang menggoda, kadang berpunggung berongga atau sebagian bersisik; ia mudah diusir dengan benda logam, misalnya pisau ikan yang dilempar ke depan kakinya.
statement.en: Like the skogsrå she was a seductive humanlike female, sometimes hollow-backed or partly scaled; she was easily scared off with a metal object, such as a fishing knife thrown before her feet.

claims.quote: En populär sägen är en om en fiskare som ger en vante (eller strumpa) till sjörået och till tack får god fiskelycka och varnas av henne vid annalkande storm. Berättelsen återges av Olaus Magnus i Historia om de nordiska folken.

statement.id: Legenda populer menceritakan nelayan yang memberi sarung tangan (atau kaus kaki) kepada sjörå dan sebagai balasan mendapat tangkapan melimpah serta diperingatkan saat badai datang; kisah ini dicatat Olaus Magnus dalam Historia om de nordiska folken.
statement.en: A popular legend tells of a fisherman who gives a mitten (or stocking) to the sjörå and in thanks gets good fishing and a warning of approaching storms; Olaus Magnus records it in his History of the Northern Peoples.

claims.quote: Till skillnad från exempelvis näcken så lurade hon sällan folk att drunkna av ren illvilja, utan detta skedde bara som vedergällning för en oförrätt. Till på köpet ogillade dessa båda varelser varandra varför de sällan förekom i varandras vatten.

statement.id: Berbeda dengan näcken, sjörå jarang memikat orang tenggelam karena dengki semata, melainkan hanya sebagai balasan atas kesalahan; keduanya juga saling tidak suka sehingga jarang ada di perairan yang sama.
statement.en: Unlike the näck, she seldom lured people to drown out of pure malice, only as revenge for a wrong; the two beings also disliked each other and rarely shared waters.

claims.quote: Sjörået höll sig ibland med kreatur som kallades sjönöt eller sjökreatur. Dessa kunde vara brokiga eller strimmiga kor som betade i strandkanten, men kunde också förekomma som abborrar eller gäddor som tillhörde hennes sjö.

statement.id: Sjörå kadang memelihara ternak yang disebut sjönöt atau sjökreatur: sapi belang atau bergaris yang merumput di tepi danau, atau ikan perch dan pike milik danaunya.
statement.en: The sjörå sometimes kept cattle called sjönöt or sjökreatur: mottled or striped cows grazing at the shore, or perch and pike belonging to her lake.

claims.quote: Andra namn på sjörået är nixa, nikse, sjöfru eller sjöfröken.

statement.id: Nama lain sjörå adalah nixa, nikse, sjöfru, atau sjöfröken.
statement.en: Other names for the sjörå are nixa, nikse, sjöfru or sjöfröken.

claims.quote: Hon visade sig nästan enbart för ensamma män, som vistades i sjöns närhet, där hon med förtjusning brukade sitta på en sten och kamma sitt långa, mörka svepande hår.

statement.id: Ia menampakkan diri hampir hanya kepada lelaki sendirian di dekat danau, sambil duduk di batu dengan gembira menyisir rambut panjang gelapnya.
statement.en: She showed herself almost only to lone men near the lake, delightedly sitting on a stone combing her long dark hair.

short_description.id: Changeling (juga auf atau oaf) adalah makhluk mirip manusia dalam cerita rakyat Eropa: pengganti yang ditinggalkan makhluk gaib ketika menculik manusia, biasanya bayi.
short_description.en: A changeling (also auf or oaf) is a human-like creature of European folklore: a substitute left by a supernatural being when it kidnapped a human, usually a baby.

long_description.id: Changeling, dulu juga disebut auf atau oaf, adalah makhluk mirip manusia yang dikenal di sebagian besar cerita rakyat Eropa (European folklore). Menurut cerita rakyat, changeling adalah pengganti yang ditinggalkan makhluk gaib ketika menculik manusia; kadang berupa sepotong kayu yang disihir menyerupai korbannya, tetapi lebih sering makhluk gaib yang disihir agar tampak seperti manusia yang diculik. Pelaku penculikan bisa peri, iblis, troll, nereid, dan makhluk lain; korbannya biasanya anak-anak, tetapi di Skandinavia dan Irlandia orang dewasa juga diambil.
long_description.en: Known in older English as an auf or oaf, the changeling is a human-looking being that turns up across most of Europe's folk traditions. According to folklore it was a substitute left by a supernatural being when it kidnapped a human; sometimes a piece of wood magically made to resemble the victim, but more often a supernatural being magically made to look like the stolen person. The kidnappers could be fairies, demons, trolls, nereids and others; victims were usually children, but in Scandinavia and Ireland adults were taken too.

long_description.id: Dalam legenda Irlandia, anak peri bisa tampak sakit-sakitan dan tidak tumbuh seperti anak biasa, berjanggut atau bergigi panjang, dan menunjukkan kecerdasan jauh di atas usianya. Jimat sederhana seperti mantel yang dibalik atau gunting besi terbuka di dekat tempat tidur anak dipercaya menangkalnya. Sebagian sarjana modern berpendapat kisah anak yang ditukar berasal dari penjelasan rakyat atas autisme atau kondisi perkembangan lain; kasus Bridget Cleary, yang dibunuh suaminya karena dianggap changeling, adalah salah satu yang paling terkenal.
long_description.en: In Irish legend a fairy child may look sickly and fail to grow like a normal child, have a beard or long teeth, and show intelligence far beyond its years. People guarded a sleeping child with simple charms, for instance a coat turned inside out or a pair of open iron scissors. Some modern scholars argue that tales of swapped children began as folk explanations of autism or other developmental conditions; the case of Bridget Cleary, killed by her husband who thought her a changeling, is among the best known.

long_description.id: Menurut artikel de, dalam takhayul Eropa abad pertengahan Wechselbalg adalah bayi yang ditukarkan makhluk iblis dengan bayi seorang ibu baru untuk mengganggu dan merugikan manusia; dalam kepercayaan non-Kristen ia dilahirkan Druden, kurcaci, atau elf, sedangkan dalam kepercayaan Kristen ia anak penyihir atau bahkan Iblis, yang terutama mengincar bayi belum dibaptis. Istilah Wechselbalg pertama muncul awal abad ke-11.
long_description.en: According to the de article, in medieval European superstition the Wechselbalg was an infant swapped by a demonic being for a new mother's own baby, to harass and harm people; in non-Christian belief it was fathered by Druden, dwarfs or elves, while in Christian belief it was the child of witches or even the Devil, who especially sought unbaptized babies. The term Wechselbalg first appears in the early 11th century.

who.id: Pengganti bayi yang diculik makhluk gaib.
who.en: Substitute for a baby stolen by supernatural beings.

origin.en: Looks sickly and fails to grow.

role.id: Ditangkal gunting besi atau mantel terbalik.
role.en: Warded off by iron scissors or an inverted coat.

did_you_know.id: Gunting besi terbuka di dekat tempat tidur bayi dipercaya dapat menangkal penukaran bayi oleh peri.
did_you_know.en: Open iron scissors by a baby's bed were believed to ward off fairies swapping the child.

description.id: Disihir agar tampak seperti manusia yang diculik.
