claims.quote: Supernatural beings blamed for stealing children included fairies, demons, trolls, nereids and many others. Usually, the kidnapped human was a child; but there were cases, particularly in Scandinavia and Ireland, where adults were taken.

statement.id: Penculiknya peri, iblis, troll, nereid; korbannya biasanya anak, tetapi di Skandinavia (Scandinavia) dan Irlandia (Ireland) orang dewasa juga.

statement.id: Dalam takhayul (Aberglauben) Eropa abad pertengahan, Wechselbalg adalah bayi (Säugling) yang ditukar makhluk iblis (dämonisches Wesen) untuk mengganggu dan merugikan manusia (Menschen).

claims.quote: In nichtchristlichen Glaubensvorstellungen wurde der Wechselbalg von Druden, Zwergen oder Elfen gezeugt und untergeschoben.

statement.en: In Christian (christlichen) belief the Wechselbalg was a child of witches (Hexen) or the Devil (Teufels), who sought unbaptized children (ungetaufte Kinder).

claims.quote: Der für das Böse und Unheimliche stehende Begriff Wechselbalg taucht Anfang des 11. Jahrhunderts erstmals auf.

statement.id: Istilah (Begriff) Wechselbalg pertama muncul awal abad ke-11 (11. Jahrhunderts).
statement.en: The term (Begriff) Wechselbalg first appears in the early 11th century (11. Jahrhunderts).

claims.quote: Die verängstigte Mutter betrachtete wiederum die Taufe als den besten Schutz vor einem Wechselbalg.

long_description.en: A changeling, also historically referred to as an auf or oaf, is a human-like creature found throughout much of European folklore. According to folklore, a changeling was a substitute left by a supernatural being when kidnapping a human being. Although sometimes it was a "stock" (a piece of wood made magically to resemble the kidnapped human), more often the changeling was a supernatural being made magically to look like the kidnapped human. Supernatural beings blamed for stealing children included fairies, demons, trolls, nereids and many others. Usually, the kidnapped human was a child; but there were cases, particularly in Scandinavia and Ireland, where adults were taken. Some modern scholars have argued these stories of replaced children originated as folklore explanations for autism or other developmental conditions.

short_description.id: Pixie (juga pisky atau piskie) adalah makhluk mitos cerita rakyat Britania, terutama di dataran tinggi Cornwall dan Devon, yang kecil, usil, dan gemar menari semalaman.
short_description.en: The pixie (also pisky or piskie) is a mythical creature of British folklore, mainly of the Cornwall and Devon moorlands, small, mischievous and fond of dancing all night.

long_description.id: Pixie (juga pisky, pixy, pixi, pizkie, piskie, atau pigsie di sebagian Cornwall dan Devon) adalah makhluk mitos cerita rakyat Britania (British folklore). Pixie diduga paling banyak di dataran tinggi sekitar Cornwall dan Devon, yang mengisyaratkan asal-usul Kelt bagi kepercayaan dan namanya, meski kata pixie juga dijumpai di Dorset, Somerset, dan beberapa daerah lain. Seperti Aos Sí Irlandia dan Skotlandia, pixie dipercaya mendiami situs bawah tanah kuno seperti lingkaran batu, barrow, dolmen, ringfort, atau menhir.
long_description.en: Known locally in Cornwall and Devon by names such as pisky, piskie or pigsie, the pixie is a mythical being of British folklore. Pixies are thought to cluster in the high moorland around Cornwall and Devon, hinting at a Celtic origin for the belief and the name, though the word also turns up in Dorset, Somerset and elsewhere. Like the Irish and Scottish Aos Sí, pixies are thought to dwell beneath old monuments: menhirs, dolmens, barrows, ringforts and stone circles.

long_description.id: Dalam cerita tradisional, pixie umumnya tidak jahat, usil, bertubuh pendek, dan kekanak-kanakan; mereka suka menari dan bergulat di luar sepanjang malam. Di era modern mereka biasanya digambarkan bertelinga runcing, berpakaian hijau, dan bertopi runcing. Asal kata pixie tidak pasti; mungkin dari pyske dalam dialek Swedia atau dari akar Kelt untuk "kecil", dan secara bersama mereka disebut Pobel Vean ("orang kecil"). Di Penwith barat, spriggan dibedakan dari pixie karena sifatnya yang jahat.
long_description.en: In traditional lore pixies are generally harmless, mischievous, short and childlike, fond of dancing and wrestling outdoors through the night. In modern times they are usually shown with pointed ears, green clothes and a pointed hat. The origin of the word is unclear; perhaps Swedish dialect pyske or a Celtic root for "little", and collectively they are called Pobel Vean ("little people"). In west Penwith spriggans are told apart from pixies by their malevolence.

long_description.id: Menurut artikel de, pixie adalah makhluk dongeng kecil dari cerita rakyat Inggris yang mirip kobold dan peri, dengan kisah yang tersebar di Devon dan Cornwall. Ada beberapa mitos asal-usul: mereka makhluk yang tak cukup baik untuk surga dan tak cukup jahat untuk neraka sehingga harus tinggal di bumi selamanya, atau para druid yang menolak masuk Kristen dan dikecilkan Tuhan sebagai hukuman.
long_description.en: According to the de article, pixies are small fabulous beings of English folklore resembling kobolds and fairies, with stories spread in Devon and Cornwall. There are several origin myths: they were beings not good enough for heaven nor bad enough for hell and so had to stay on earth forever, or druids who refused Christianity and were shrunk by God as punishment.

who.en: Little fairy of Cornwall and Devon.

famous_for.id: Tinggal di situs kuno bawah tanah.

did_you_know.en: One myth says pixies were beings not good enough for heaven nor bad enough for hell, so they must stay on earth forever.

note.en: Irish and Scottish counterpart.
Told apart from pixies by malevolence.

claims.quote: A pixie (also called pisky, pixy, pixi, pizkie, piskie, or pigsie in parts of Cornwall and Devon) is a mythical creature of British folklore.

statement.id: Pixie (pisky, pixy, pixi, pizkie, piskie, pigsie di Cornwall dan Devon) adalah makhluk mitos cerita rakyat Britania (British folklore).
statement.en: A pixie (pisky, pixy, piskie or pigsie in Cornwall and Devon) is a mythical creature of British folklore.

claims.quote: Pixies are speculated to be particularly concentrated in the high moorland areas around Cornwall and Devon, suggesting some Celtic origin for the belief and name. However, the word 'pixie' (under various forms) also appears in Dorset, Somerset and to a lesser extent in Sussex, Wiltshire and Hampshire.

statement.id: Pixie terutama di dataran tinggi Cornwall dan Devon, mengisyaratkan asal Kelt (Celtic); kata pixie juga ada di Dorset, Somerset, dan lain-lain.
statement.en: Pixies cluster in the moorlands of Cornwall and Devon, suggesting a Celtic origin; the word also appears in Dorset, Somerset and elsewhere.

claims.quote: Similar to the Irish and Scottish Aos Sí (also spelled Aos Sidhe), pixies are believed to inhabit ancient underground sites such as stone circles, barrows, dolmens, ringforts, or menhirs.

statement.id: Seperti Aos Sí Irlandia dan Skotlandia (Irish, Scottish), pixie mendiami situs bawah tanah kuno seperti lingkaran batu, barrow, dolmen, ringfort, menhir.
statement.en: Like the Irish and Scottish Aos Sí, pixies inhabit ancient underground sites such as stone circles, barrows, dolmens, ringforts or menhirs.

claims.quote: In traditional regional lore, pixies are generally benign, mischievous, short of stature, and childlike; they are fond of dancing and wrestling outdoors, which they perform through the night.

statement.id: Pixie umumnya tak jahat, usil, pendek, kekanak-kanakan, suka menari dan bergulat sepanjang malam.
statement.en: Pixies are generally benign, mischievous, short and childlike, dancing and wrestling outdoors through the night.

claims.quote: The term Pobel Vean (Little People) is often used to refer to them collectively.

statement.id: Sebutan Pobel Vean (Little People, orang kecil) dipakai untuk mereka secara bersama.
statement.en: The term Pobel Vean (Little People) is used for them collectively.

claims.quote: In west Penwith, the area of late survival of the Cornish language, spriggans are distinguished from pixies by their malevolent nature

statement.id: Di Penwith barat (west Penwith), spriggan dibedakan dari pixie karena jahat.
statement.en: In west Penwith spriggans are distinguished from pixies by their malevolence.

claims.quote: Pixies sind kleine Fabelwesen aus der englischen Folklore, deren Charakteristika denen von Kobolden und Feen ähneln. Geschichten über diese Wesen sind im Südwesten Englands, in den Regionen Devon und Cornwall, verbreitet.

statement.id: Pixies makhluk dongeng kecil (kleine Fabelwesen) cerita rakyat Inggris (englischen Folklore) mirip kobold (Kobolden) dan peri (Feen), di Devon dan Cornwall.
statement.en: Pixies are small fabulous beings (kleine Fabelwesen) of English folklore (englischen Folklore) like kobolds (Kobolden) and fairies (Feen), in Devon and Cornwall.

claims.quote: So sollen die pixies Wesen sein, die nicht gut genug für das Paradies und nicht schlecht genug für die Hölle waren und daher für ewig auf der Erde bleiben mussten. Nach einer anderen Geschichte sind die pixies Druiden, die nicht zum Christentum konvertierten und zur Strafe von Gott so lange geschrumpft wurden, bis sie sich zum Christentum bekannten.

statement.id: Pixies makhluk yang tak cukup baik untuk surga (Paradies) dan tak cukup jahat untuk neraka (Hölle), atau druid (Druiden) yang tak masuk Kristen (Christentum). Dikecilkan oleh Tuhan (Gott) sebagai hukuman.
statement.en: Pixies were beings not good enough for paradise (Paradies) nor bad enough for hell (Hölle), or druids (Druiden) who did not convert to Christianity (Christentum).

claims.quote: The origin of the word pixie is uncertain. It could have come from the Swedish dialectal pyske, meaning 'small fairy'.

statement.id: Asal kata pixie tidak pasti; mungkin dari pyske dialek Swedia (Swedish), "peri kecil".
statement.en: The origin of pixie is uncertain; perhaps Swedish dialect pyske, 'small fairy'.

Similar to the Irish and Scottish Aos Sí (also spelled Aos Sidhe), pixies are believed to inhabit ancient underground sites such as stone circles, barrows, dolmens, ringforts, or menhirs. In traditional regional lore, pixies are generally benign, mischievous, short of stature, and childlike; they are fond of dancing and wrestling outdoors, which they perform through the night. In the modern era, they are usually depicted with pointed ears, often wearing a green outfit and pointed hat. Traditional stories describe them as wearing dirty, ragged bundles of rags, which they discard for gifts containing new clothes. In other depictions, their eyes are described as being pointed upwards at the outer end. These, however, are Victorian era conventions and not part of the older mythology.

short_description.id: Gremlin adalah makhluk usil rekaan yang diciptakan pada awal abad ke-20 untuk menjelaskan kerusakan pesawat terbang dan mesin lain, populer di kalangan penerbang Perang Dunia II.
short_description.en: A gremlin is a mischievous fictional creature invented in the early 20th century to explain malfunctions in aircraft and other machinery, popular among World War II airmen.

long_description.id: Gremlin adalah makhluk usil rekaan yang diciptakan pada awal abad ke-20, mula-mula untuk menjelaskan kerusakan pesawat terbang, lalu mesin, proses, dan operatornya. Gambarannya sangat beragam. Pemakaian kata ini untuk makhluk yang menyabotase pesawat pertama kali muncul dalam slang Royal Air Force (RAF) di kalangan pilot Britania yang ditempatkan di Malta, Timur Tengah, dan India pada 1920-an, dengan catatan cetak tertua berupa puisi dalam jurnal Aeroplane in Malta pada 10 April 1929.
long_description.en: A gremlin is a mischievous fictional creature invented early in the 20th century, at first to account for aircraft malfunctions and later for machines, processes and their operators. Depictions vary widely. The word for a creature that sabotages aircraft first appeared in Royal Air Force (RAF) slang among British pilots in Malta, the Middle East and India in the 1920s, the earliest printed record being a poem in the journal Aeroplane in Malta on 10 April 1929.

long_description.id: Asal namanya diperdebatkan: ada yang menurunkannya dari kata Inggris Kuno gremian ("menjengkelkan"), dan ada pula yang menganggapnya gabungan kata goblin dengan Fremlin, merek bir yang paling banyak tersedia di RAF pada 1920-an. Pada Perang Dunia II (World War II), awak pesawat RAF menyalahkan gremlin atas kecelakaan yang tak dapat dijelaskan; pesawat musuh ternyata mengalami masalah serupa, sehingga gremlin dianggap pengganggu yang tidak memihak. Menurut artikel de, penulis Roald Dahl, yang pernah bertugas di RAF, menerbitkan The Gremlins pada 1943, dan gremlin seperti banyak jenis kobold lain gemar berbuat usil, terutama di bidang mesin dan teknik.
long_description.en: The name's origin is disputed: some derive it from the Old English gremian ("to vex"), others see a blend of goblin with Fremlin, the beer most widely available in the RAF in the 1920s. In World War II RAF crews blamed gremlins for otherwise inexplicable accidents; enemy aircraft turned out to have the same troubles, so gremlins were seen as even-handed tricksters. According to the de article, the writer Roald Dahl, who had served in the RAF, published The Gremlins in 1943, and like many kinds of kobold the gremlin loves mischief, above all with machines and technology.

long_description.en: A gremlin is a mischievous fictional creature invented at the beginning of the 20th century originally to explain malfunctions in aircraft, and later in other machinery, processes and their operators. Depictions of these creatures vary widely. Stories about them and references to them as the causes of especially inexplicable technical and mental problems of pilots were especially popular during and after World War II. Use of the term in the sense of a mischievous creature that sabotages aircraft first arose in Royal Air Force (RAF) slang among British pilots stationed in Malta, the Middle East and India in the 1920s, with the earliest printed record in a poem published in the journal Aeroplane in Malta on 10 April 1929. Later sources have sometimes claimed that the concept goes back to World War I, but there is no print evidence of this. There is evidence of an even earlier reference in the 1920s, stating that the term was used in the RAF to refer to a lowly menial person, such as a low-ranking officer or enlisted man saddled with oppressive assignments.

short_description.id: Huldufólk ("orang tersembunyi") adalah makhluk gaib cerita rakyat Islandia dan Faroe yang mirip manusia tetapi hidup di dunia sejajar dan dapat menampakkan diri sesuka hati.
short_description.en: The huldufólk ('hidden folk') are supernatural beings of Icelandic and Faroese folklore who resemble humans but live in a parallel world and can show themselves at will.

long_description.id: Dalam cerita rakyat Nordik (Nordic folklore), termasuk Northern Isles, hidden-folk (Faroe dan Islandia/Faroese and Icelandic: huldufólk; Norwegia/Norwegian: huldrefolk) adalah sebutan kolektif untuk kelompok longgar elf, wight, brownie (nisse), troll, dan sejenisnya. Mereka makhluk gaib yang hidup di alam, rupa dan perilakunya mirip manusia tetapi tinggal di dunia sejajar, dan dapat menampakkan diri sesuka hati. Konrad von Maurer mengutip sumber Islandia abad ke-19 bahwa satu-satunya beda yang terlihat adalah philtrum (lekuk di bawah hidung) mereka yang cembung, bukan cekung.
long_description.en: In Nordic folklore, the Northern Isles included, the hidden-folk (Faroese and Icelandic huldufólk; Norwegian huldrefolk) is a group name for a loose gathering of elves, wights, brownies (nisse), trolls and the like. These beings live in nature, look and act much like people yet dwell in a parallel world, and can become visible when they choose. Konrad von Maurer cites a 19th-century Icelandic source saying the only visible difference is a convex rather than concave philtrum beneath the nose.

long_description.id: Dalam dongeng Faroe (Faroese) mereka bertubuh besar, berpakaian serba kelabu, berambut hitam, dan tinggal di gundukan; sebagian dongeng Islandia memperingatkan agar tidak melempar batu karena bisa mengenai mereka. Pada abad ke-19 istilah huldufólk dipakai sebagai sinonim álfar (elf); menurut Jón Árnason keduanya sama kecuali álfar bernada merendahkan. Menurut artikel fr, Huldufólk berarti "orang tersembunyi" (peuple caché) dan terdiri atas elf, troll, dan orang tak kasat mata yang terutama tinggal di gunung dan batu tempat mereka membangun kota, Álagablettur; jalan di Kópavogur konon dibelokkan agar tidak merusak tempat tinggal mereka.
long_description.en: In Faroese tales they are large, dressed all in grey, black-haired and living in mounds; some Icelandic tales warn against throwing stones lest they hit the hidden people. In the 19th century huldufólk was used as a synonym of álfar (elves); Jón Árnason found the words equivalent except that álfar was disparaging. According to the fr article, Huldufólk means 'hidden people' (peuple caché) and covers elves, trolls and invisible people who live mostly in mountains and rocks where they build their towns, the Álagablettur; a road at Kópavogur was reportedly routed to avoid destroying their home.

long_description.en: In Nordic folklore, including the Northern Isles, hidden-folk (Faroese and Icelandic: huldufólk; Norwegian: huldrefolk), mound-folk (Danish: højfolk, Swedish: högfolk), mountain-folk (Danish: bjærgfolk, Swedish: bergfolk, bergafolk; Finnish: vuoren väki), subterraneans (Norwegian: underjordiske, Swedish: underjordiska; Gutnish: di sma undar jordi, "the small underground"; Finnish: maahiset, roughly "grounders"), among other names (Swedish: oknytt, Insular Scots: trow, drow), are collective names for a loose race or conglomeration of elves, wights, brownies (Nordic: nisse), trolls, and thereof. They are supernatural beings that live in nature. They look and behave similarly to humans, but live in a parallel world. They can make themselves visible at will. Konrad von Maurer cites a 19th-century Icelandic source claiming that the only visible difference between normal people and outwardly human-appearing huldufólk is, the latter have a convex rather than concave philtrum (Icelandic: vuldulág) below their noses. An analog myth are the trolls being discerned by their large noses. In Faroese folk tales, hidden people are said to be "large in build, their clothes are all grey, and their hair black (the same description is also given for draugrs in Faroese folklore). Their dwellings are in mounds, and they are also called Elves." Some Icelandic folk tales caution against throwing stones, as it may hit the hidden people. The term huldufólk was taken as a synonym of álfar (elves) in 19th-century Icelandic folklore. Jón Árnason found that the terms are synonymous, except álfar is a pejorative term. Konrad von Maurer contends that huldufólk originates as a euphemism to avoid calling the álfar by their real name. There is, however, some evidence that the two terms have come to be taken as referring to two distinct sets of supernatural beings in contemporary Iceland. Katrin Sontag found that some people do not differentiate elves from hidden people, while others do. A 2006 survey found that "54% of respondents did not distinguish between elves and hidden people, 20% did and 26% said they were not sure."

short_description.id: Landvættir adalah roh tanah dalam agama Nordik Kuno, kepercayaan rakyat kemudian, dan Heathenry modern, yang terikat pada tempat tertentu dan menentukan kesuburan tanahnya.
short_description.en: Landvættir are land spirits of Old Nordic religion, later folk belief and modern Heathenry, bound to particular places and needed for the land to be fruitful.

long_description.id: Landvættir, "roh tanah", dikenal dalam agama Nordik Kuno, kepercayaan rakyat sesudahnya, dan Heathenry modern. Mereka terikat erat pada tempat tertentu, dan kesejahteraan mereka dianggap syarat agar tanah yang mereka huni subur. Dalam sumber Nordik Kuno mereka bisa berbahaya, sanggup mengusir orang yang tak diinginkan, tetapi juga dapat ditakut-takuti, misalnya dengan hiasan kepala kapal atau níðstöng.
long_description.en: Landvættir, 'land spirits', figure in Old Nordic religion, in the folk belief that followed it and in present-day Heathenry. Each is bound to a particular place, and the fruitfulness of that land was thought to depend on their wellbeing. Old Norse sources show them as potentially dangerous, able to drive away unwanted people, yet capable of being frightened by things like carved ship figureheads or a níðstöng.

long_description.id: Hukum kafir lama Islandia melarang kapal mendekati daratan dengan kepala berukir yang menganga agar roh tanah tidak takut. Landnámabók menceritakan tak seorang pun berani tinggal di tempat Hjörleif menetap karena landvættir, dan para perempuan membawa makanan ke tumpukan batu agar landvættir membuat mereka makmur. Hukum Gulating Norwegia abad ke-13 melarang kepercayaan bahwa gundukan kubur, hutan, dan air terjun dihuni landvættir sebagai bidah.
long_description.en: The old heathen law of Iceland forbade ships to approach land with gaping carved heads lest the land spirits be scared. Landnámabók says that fear of the landvættir kept anyone from living on Hjörleif's former land, and women took food to stone piles hoping the landvættir would make them prosperous. Norway's 13th-century Gulating laws banned the belief that howes, woods and waterfalls were inhabited by landvættir as heresy.

long_description.id: Dalam sebuah kisah saga, seorang penyihir utusan Raja Harald berwujud paus melihat semua gunung dan bukit Islandia penuh roh penjaga, lalu diusir di tiap sisi pulau oleh naga, burung besar, banteng, dan raksasa gunung (bergrisi). Keempat sosok ini kini dipandang sebagai pelindung empat wilayah Islandia dan tampil pada lambang negara serta koin króna.
long_description.en: In a saga account a warlock sent by King Harald in the shape of a whale saw all the mountains and hills of Iceland full of guardian spirits, and was driven off on each side of the island by a dragon, a great bird, a bull and a mountain giant (bergrisi). These four figures are now regarded as protectors of Iceland's four quarters and appear on the coat of arms and the króna coins.

long_description.id: Sebagian sarjana menganggap landvættir roh chthonic atau arwah orang mati, sedangkan yang lain memandangnya roh alam karena kadang mereka menghuni tanah yang tak pernah didiami manusia. Mereka juga dikaitkan dengan elf, kurcaci, dan landdísir.
long_description.en: Some scholars consider landvættir chthonic spirits of the dead, while others see them as nature spirits because they sometimes live in land never settled by people. They have also been linked with elves, dwarfs and landdísir.

long_description.en: Landvættir ("land spirits" or "land wights") are spirits of the land in Old Nordic religion, later folk belief and modern Heathenry. They are closely associated with specific locations and their wellbeing is presented as being required for the land they inhabit to be fruitful. In Old Norse sources, they are depicted as being potentially harmful and capable of driving away unwanted individuals and capable of being frightened through human actions such as usage of carved figureheads on ships or níðstangs. Good relationships between humans and landvættir were believed to be fostered through acts like leaving out food for them. However upon the establishment of the church, the practice was labelled heretical and explicitly forbidden in the Norwegian Gulating law codes. Landvættir have been variously connected by scholars to other beings believed to inhabit the land such as elves, dwarfs and landdísir, with which they were potentially identified at different points in history. Their belief and veneration has been revived in the modern period as part of the practice of modern Heathens.

In Old Norse sources, they are depicted as being potentially harmful and capable of driving away unwanted individuals

statement.id: Landvættir ("roh tanah") adalah roh tanah dalam agama Nordik Kuno, kepercayaan rakyat sesudahnya, dan Heathenry modern; mereka terikat pada tempat tertentu, kesejahteraannya syarat kesuburan tanah, dan dalam sumber Nordik Kuno mereka bisa berbahaya serta mampu mengusir orang yang tak diinginkan.
statement.en: Landvættir ('land spirits') are spirits of the land in Old Nordic religion, later folk belief and modern Heathenry; tied to specific places, their wellbeing is needed for the land to be fruitful, and Old Norse sources show them as potentially harmful and able to drive away unwanted people.

claims.quote: Translation: It was the beginning of the preamble of the heathen laws that men should not take ships to sea with carved figure heads upon their sterns, but if they did, they should take them off before they came in sight of land

statement.id: Pembukaan hukum kafir menyatakan orang tidak boleh berlayar dengan kepala berukir di kapalnya, dan bila ada, harus melepasnya sebelum daratan terlihat.
statement.en: The preamble of the heathen laws said men should not sail with carved figureheads, and if they did, should remove them before land came in sight.

claims.quote: Later, the book states that no one dared live where Hjörleif had settled because of the landvættir.

statement.id: Landnámabók kemudian menyatakan tak seorang pun berani tinggal di tempat Hjörleif menetap karena landvættir.
statement.en: The book later states no one dared live where Hjörleif had settled because of the landvættir.

claims.quote: In this account, the women take food to stone piles or flat stones, hoping that in return the landvættir would make them prosperous.

statement.id: Dalam catatan itu, para perempuan membawa makanan ke tumpukan batu atau batu datar dengan harapan landvættir membuat mereka makmur.
statement.en: In this account, women take food to stone piles or flat stones hoping the landvættir will make them prosperous.

claims.quote: The Norwegian Gulating laws, written in the latter half of the 13th century, made illegal the belief that howes, wooded areas and waterfalls, were inhabited by landvættir, considering it a heresy and belonging to the heathen religion.

statement.id: Hukum Gulating Norwegia dari paruh kedua abad ke-13 melarang kepercayaan bahwa gundukan kubur, hutan, dan air terjun dihuni landvættir, karena dianggap bidah dan bagian agama kafir.
statement.en: Norway's Gulating laws of the later 13th century outlawed the belief that howes, woods and waterfalls were inhabited by landvættir, deeming it heresy and heathen.

claims.quote: King Harald told a warlock to hie to Iceland in some altered shape, and to try what he could learn there to tell him: and he set out in the shape of a whale. ... where he saw all the mountains and hills full of guardian-spirits, some great, some small.

statement.id: Raja Harald menyuruh seorang penyihir pergi ke Islandia dalam wujud lain; ia berangkat sebagai paus dan melihat semua gunung dan bukit penuh roh penjaga, besar dan kecil.
statement.en: King Harald sent a warlock to Iceland in altered shape; he went as a whale and saw all the mountains and hills full of guardian spirits, great and small.

claims.quote: First on the East side by a large dragon followed by snakes, toads and lizards who blew atter, or poison, at him, then on the North side by a great bird with many smaller birds, next in the West a large bull followed by beasts and other landvættir, and finally a huge bergrisi with an iron staff in the South

statement.id: Ia diusir di sisi timur oleh naga besar yang diikuti ular, kodok, dan kadal penyembur racun, di utara oleh burung besar, di barat oleh banteng besar beserta landvættir lain, dan di selatan oleh bergrisi raksasa bertongkat besi.
statement.en: He was driven off in the east by a great dragon with poison-blowing snakes, toads and lizards, in the north by a great bird, in the west by a great bull with other landvættir, and in the south by a huge bergrisi with an iron staff.

claims.quote: Les quatre Landvættir sont aujourd'hui considérés comme les protecteurs des quatre quartiers d'Islande : le dragon (Dreki) dans le Nord-Est, l'aigle ou griffon (Gammur) dans de Nord-Ouest, le taureau (Griðungur) dans le Sud-Ouest, et le géant (Bergrisi) dans le Sud-Est. Les quatre Landvættir de l'Islande sont représentés sur les Armoiries de l'Islande et sur l'envers des pièces

statement.id: Empat landvættir kini dianggap pelindung empat wilayah Islandia: naga (Dreki), elang atau griffin (Gammur), banteng (Griðungur), dan raksasa (Bergrisi); keempatnya tampil pada lambang Islandia dan sisi belakang koin króna.
statement.en: The four landvættir are now regarded as protectors of Iceland's four quarters: the dragon (Dreki), eagle or griffin (Gammur), bull (Griðungur) and giant (Bergrisi); they appear on the Icelandic arms and the reverse of króna coins.

claims.quote: Some scholars have suggested that landvættir are chthonic and spirits of the dead, but others have interpreted them as nature spirits, since they sometimes live in land that has never been populated.

statement.id: Sebagian sarjana menduga landvættir adalah roh chthonic dan arwah orang mati, sedangkan yang lain menafsirkannya sebagai roh alam karena kadang menghuni tanah yang tak pernah didiami.
statement.en: Some scholars suggest landvættir are chthonic spirits of the dead, while others interpret them as nature spirits because they sometimes live in never-populated land.

claims.quote: Landvættir have been variously connected by scholars to other beings believed to inhabit the land such as elves, dwarfs and landdísir, with which they were potentially identified at different points in history.

statement.id: Para sarjana mengaitkan landvættir dengan makhluk lain penghuni tanah seperti elf, kurcaci, dan landdísir, yang mungkin pernah disamakan dengannya pada masa berbeda.
statement.en: Scholars have linked landvættir to other land-dwelling beings such as elves, dwarfs and landdísir, with which they may have been identified at different times.

claims.quote: As a compound, land-vættir has been variously translated as "guardian spirits of a country", "land-spirits", "landwights" or "nature spirits".

statement.id: Sebagai kata majemuk, land-vættir diterjemahkan antara lain sebagai "roh penjaga negeri", "roh tanah", atau "roh alam".
statement.en: As a compound, land-vættir has been rendered 'guardian spirits of a country', 'land-spirits', 'landwights' or 'nature spirits'.

summary.id: Roh chthonic dan arwah orang mati.
summary.en: Chthonic spirits of the dead.

summary.id: Roh alam.
summary.en: Nature spirits.

long_description.en: Landvættir ("land spirits" or "land wights") are spirits of the land in Old Nordic religion, later folk belief and modern Heathenry. They are closely associated with specific locations and their wellbeing is presented as being required for the land they inhabit to be fruitful. In Old Norse sources, they are depicted as being potentially harmful and capable of driving away unwanted individuals and capable of being frightened through human actions such as usage of carved figureheads on ships or níðstangs. Good relationships between humans and landvættir were believed to be fostered through acts like leaving out food for them. However upon the establishment of the church, the practice was labelled heretical and explicitly forbidden in the Norwegian Gulating law codes. Landvættir have been variously connected by scholars to other beings believed to inhabit the land such as elves, dwarfs and landdísir, with which they were potentially identified at different points in history. Their belief and veneration has been revived in the modern period as part of the practice of modern Heathens.

short_description.id: Myling adalah arwah anak yang dibunuh dan tidak dikuburkan dengan layak dalam cerita rakyat Skandinavia, yang meminta dibawa ke tanah suci pemakaman.
short_description.en: In Scandinavian folklore a myling is the ghost of a murdered child left unburied, who demands to be carried to consecrated ground.

long_description.id: Dalam cerita rakyat Skandinavia, mylingar adalah penjelmaan arwah anak-anak yang terpaksa berkeliaran di bumi sampai mereka dapat membujuk seseorang untuk menguburkan mereka dengan layak. Menurut kepercayaan rakyat Swedia, myling adalah mayat hidup bayi yang belum dibaptis, dibunuh dan disembunyikan ibunya; kadang bayi itu bahkan dikubur di bawah lantai kayu pondok untuk menutupi kelahiran yang tak diinginkan.
long_description.en: In Scandinavian folklore mylingar are the ghostly forms of children's souls forced to wander the earth until they can persuade someone to bury them properly. In Swedish folk belief a myling is the revenant of an unbaptised newborn murdered and hidden by its mother, sometimes even buried under the wooden floor of the cottage to conceal the unwanted birth.

long_description.id: Myling, yang dikenal juga sebagai utburd di Norwegia, útburður di Islandia, serta ihtiriekko dan liekkiö di Finlandia, konon mengejar pengembara yang sendirian di malam hari dan melompat ke punggung mereka, meminta dibawa ke pemakaman. Ia makin berat saat mendekati pemakaman sampai pembawanya bisa terbenam ke tanah, dan bila orang itu gagal mencapai pemakaman, myling membunuhnya dengan murka.
long_description.en: The myling, also called utburd in Norwegian, útburður in Icelandic and ihtiriekko or liekkiö in Finnish, reportedly pursues people walking alone after dark, leaps onto their backs and insists on being taken to the graveyard. It grows heavier as the graveyard nears until its bearer may sink into the soil, and if the person fails to reach the cemetery, the myling kills them in rage.

long_description.id: Nyanyiannya di malam hari dapat membongkar kejahatan sang ibu. Myling dapat ditolong dengan memberinya nama, misalnya bila ia berseru "beri aku nama!", atau dengan menemukan jasadnya dan menguburkannya di tanah suci pemakaman.
long_description.en: Its singing at night can reveal the mother's crime. A myling can be helped by giving it a name, for instance when it cries 'give me a name!', or by finding its body and burying it in hallowed ground.

long_description.id: Kata myling berasal dari bahasa Swedia myrding atau mörding, dari bahasa Swedia Kuno myrða, "membunuh", sehingga berarti "yang dibunuh"; kata ini tercatat dalam bahasa Swedia sejak 1647. Keyakinan bahwa myling murka dan menuntut balas membuatnya dianggap salah satu jenis hantu paling mengancam dalam cerita rakyat Skandinavia.
long_description.en: The word myling comes from Swedish myrding or mörding, from Old Swedish myrða, 'to murder', and so means 'the murdered one'; it is attested in Swedish since 1647. The belief that mylingar are enraged and vengeful made them one of the most menacing kinds of ghost in Scandinavian folklore.

who.en: The ghost of a murdered infant.

role.en: Demands to be carried to the graveyard.

claims.quote: The myling (also known as utburd in Norwegian, útburður in Icelandic and ihtiriekko and liekkiö in Finnish) is said to chase lone wanderers at night and jump on their backs, demanding to be carried to the graveyard ... apparently grow heavier as they near the graveyard ... claims.quote: Das ungetaufte Kind konnte man ebenfalls um Hilfe rufen hören mit den Worten: „Gib mir einen Namen!“ und man konnte das Kind retten, indem man antwortete: „Du kannst meinen haben, ich heiße N. N.“

statement.id: Bayi yang belum dibaptis itu bisa terdengar berseru "beri aku nama!", dan orang dapat menyelamatkannya dengan menjawab "ambillah namaku" sambil menyebut namanya sendiri.
statement.en: The unbaptised child could be heard crying 'give me a name!', and one could save it by answering 'you can have mine' and giving one's own name.

claims.quote: Das Wort stammt vom schwedischen myrding bzw. mörding, abgeleitet von altschwedisch: myrða mit der Bedeutung „morden“. Myling bedeutet also „Ermordetes“. Das Wort ist im schwedischen Sprachgebrauch seit 1647 belegt.

statement.en: The word comes from Swedish myrding or mörding, from Old Swedish myrða, 'to murder', so myling means 'the murdered one'; it is attested in Swedish since 1647.

short_description.id: Myling adalah arwah anak yang dibunuh dan tidak dikuburkan dengan layak dalam cerita rakyat Skandinavia, yang meminta dibawa ke tanah suci pemakaman.
short_description.en: In Scandinavian folklore a myling is the ghost of a murdered child left unburied, who demands to be carried to consecrated ground.

long_description.id: Dalam cerita rakyat Skandinavia, mylingar adalah penjelmaan arwah anak-anak yang terpaksa berkeliaran di bumi sampai mereka dapat membujuk seseorang untuk menguburkan mereka dengan layak. Menurut kepercayaan rakyat Swedia, myling adalah mayat hidup bayi yang belum dibaptis, dibunuh dan disembunyikan ibunya; kadang bayi itu bahkan dikubur di bawah lantai kayu pondok untuk menutupi kelahiran yang tak diinginkan.
long_description.en: In Scandinavian folklore mylingar are the ghostly forms of children's souls forced to wander the earth until they can persuade someone to bury them properly. In Swedish folk belief a myling is the revenant of an unbaptised newborn murdered and hidden by its mother, sometimes even buried under the wooden floor of the cottage to conceal the unwanted birth.

long_description.id: Myling, yang dikenal juga sebagai utburd di Norwegia, útburður di Islandia, serta ihtiriekko dan liekkiö di Finlandia, konon mengejar pengembara yang sendirian di malam hari dan melompat ke punggung mereka, meminta dibawa ke pemakaman. Ia makin berat saat mendekati pemakaman sampai pembawanya bisa terbenam ke tanah, dan bila orang itu gagal mencapai pemakaman, myling membunuhnya dengan murka.
long_description.en: The myling, also called utburd in Norwegian, útburður in Icelandic and ihtiriekko or liekkiö in Finnish, reportedly pursues people walking alone after dark, leaps onto their backs and insists on being taken to the graveyard. It grows heavier as the graveyard nears until its bearer may sink into the soil, and if the person fails to reach the cemetery, the myling kills them in rage.

long_description.id: Nyanyiannya di malam hari dapat membongkar kejahatan sang ibu. Myling dapat ditolong dengan memberinya nama, misalnya bila ia berseru "beri aku nama!", atau dengan menemukan jasadnya dan menguburkannya di tanah suci pemakaman.
long_description.en: Its singing at night can reveal the mother's crime. A myling can be helped by giving it a name, for instance when it cries 'give me a name!', or by finding its body and burying it in hallowed ground.

long_description.id: Kata myling berasal dari bahasa Swedia myrding atau mörding, dari bahasa Swedia Kuno myrða, "membunuh", sehingga berarti "yang dibunuh"; kata ini tercatat dalam bahasa Swedia sejak 1647. Keyakinan bahwa myling murka dan menuntut balas membuatnya dianggap salah satu jenis hantu paling mengancam dalam cerita rakyat Skandinavia.
long_description.en: The word myling comes from Swedish myrding or mörding, from Old Swedish myrða, 'to murder', and so means 'the murdered one'; it is attested in Swedish since 1647. The belief that mylingar are enraged and vengeful made them one of the most menacing kinds of ghost in Scandinavian folklore.

short_description.id: Kabouter adalah makhluk mirip gnom dalam cerita rakyat Belanda dan Flandria: orang mungil berjanggut dan bertopi runcing yang membantu pekerjaan rumah tetapi menghukum siapa pun yang mengintipnya.
short_description.en: The kabouter is a gnome-like creature of the folklore of the Netherlands and Flanders: a tiny bearded person in a pointed hat who helps with chores but punishes anyone who spies on it.

long_description.id: Kabouter adalah makhluk mirip gnom dalam cerita rakyat Belanda, sekerabat dengan leprechaun Irlandia, tomte atau nisse Skandinavia, hob Inggris, brownie Skotlandia, dan Klabauter atau kobold Jerman. Dalam cerita rakyat Negeri-Negeri Rendah, kabouter adalah orang mungil setinggi sekitar 10–15 cm yang tinggal di dalam atau dekat rumah dan kandang, atau di bukit, hutan, dan padang; banyak kisah menyebut kerajaan kabouter yang luas.
long_description.en: The kabouter is a gnome-like being of Dutch folklore, comparable to the Irish leprechaun, the English hob, the Scottish brownie, the Scandinavian tomte or nisse and the German Klabauter or kobold. Across the Low Countries, folk tradition pictures kabouters as little people only some 10–15 cm high, dwelling in or by houses and stables, or in hills, woods and heaths; many tales speak of vast kabouter kingdoms.

long_description.id: Kabouter dapat dipandang sebagai roh yang membantu di rumah dengan bekerja di malam hari dan merawat ternak, misalnya memerah susu. Yang jantan berjanggut panjang, dan semuanya memakai topi tinggi runcing, biasanya merah atau hijau. Mereka pemalu dan sering menghukum orang yang mengintip mereka, misalnya dengan membutakan, mengasamkan susu, menghitamkan biji-bijian, atau menakut-nakuti ternak; meninggalkan susu dan roti untuk mereka dapat memperbaiki hubungan.
long_description.en: Kabouters can be seen as spirits who help at home by working at night and tending animals, for example milking them. The males have long beards, and all wear tall pointed hats, usually red or green. They are shy and often punish people who spy on them, by blinding, souring milk, blackening grain or scaring livestock; leaving out milk and bread helps keep good relations.

long_description.id: Sebuah kisah terkenal menceritakan para kabouter menghilang dari Kempen ke tempat tak dikenal setelah seorang pemburu menembak raja mereka, Kyrië. Dalam Legenda Sepatu Kayu, seorang kabouter mengajari orang Belanda membuat tiang pancang dan sepatu kayu. Ilustrator Belanda Rien Poortvliet berperan besar dalam citra kabouter modern lewat bukunya Leven en werken van de Kabouter (1976) dengan teks Wil Huygen.
long_description.en: A well-known tale tells how the kabouters vanished from the Campine to an unknown place after a hunter shot their king Kyrië. In the Legend of the Wooden Shoes a kabouter teaches a Dutchman to make piles and wooden shoes. The Dutch illustrator Rien Poortvliet shaped the modern kabouter image through his 1976 book Leven en werken van de Kabouter, with text by Wil Huygen.

origin.en: Folklore of the Netherlands and Flanders.

role.id: Membantu pekerjaan rumah di malam hari.
role.en: Helps with household tasks at night.

did_you_know.en: In French-speaking Belgium the kabouter is called nuton.

summary.en: After a local hunter shot their king Kyrië, the kabouters vanished from the Campine to an unknown place.

long_description.en: The Kabouter (Dutch pronunciation: [kaːˈbʌutər] ) is a gnome-like creature in Dutch folklore. The Dutch Kabouter is akin to the Irish leprechaun, Scandinavian tomte or nisse, the English hob, the Scottish brownie and the German Klabauter or kobold. In the folklore of the Low Countries, kabouters are tiny people, about 10–15 cm tall, who live in or near houses and stables, or in hills, in forests or on heaths. Many stories refer to vast kabouter kingdoms with specific locations where they were seen more often or resided. In modern children's stories, Kabouters live in mushrooms or sometimes underground. Kabouters can be regarded as spirits who help in the home by doing tasks at night and care for the animals like milking them. Descriptions of kabouters vary throughout time and place. Often kabouters are associated with red squirrels. The males have long, full beards and they all wear tall, pointed hats, generally of a red or green colour. Kabouters are shy of humans and in stories often punish people for spying on them. Kabouters are sometimes associated with collecting gold or treasure, but this seems mostly connected to their association with lost objects. Often they would also steal livestock for themselves if those were left unattended by the farmers. Blinding was a common punishment for spying on the gnomes, but they could also make life more difficult by souring the milk, blackening the grain, making objects disappear, or scaring the livestock. Leaving milk and bread out for kabouters was a way to improve relationships with them. Kabouters could become very old and many are depicted with grey hair. Throughout Flanders and the Netherlands, they exist under a number of different local names such as alvermanneke or auwelke. A well known story is about the disappearance of kabouters from the Campine to an unknown place after a local hunter shot their king Kyrië. Other stories about the disappearance of the Kabouters exist as well. About the disappearance of kabouters from East Flanders and West Flanders, telling of the boy that kept losing cows until he held onto a cow tail and was taken with the cow into a kabouter kingdom, after which he spoke so beautifully that the kabouters gave him gold and his 15 cows for him to marry his love, after which the kabouters forever disappeared to the other side of the Rhine where they still live to this day. In the Legend of the Wooden Shoes, an old Dutch folktale, a kabouter teaches a Dutch man how to make piles and wooden shoes. The Dutch illustrator Rien Poortvliet played an important part in modern Kabouter lore with his publication of Leven en werken van de Kabouter (The Life and Works of the Gnome), later translated into English and published as Gnomes. In popular culture today, the business Travelocity uses a Rien Poortvliet-style statue of a kabouter for commercials. They call him the Travelocity Roaming Gnome.

short_description.id: Türst adalah sosok legenda dari komunitas petani Luzern, "pemburu mengerikan" yang meniup terompet berburunya di desa-desa pada bulan-bulan berbadai menjelang Epifani, diiringi anjing-anjing berkaki tiga.
short_description.en: Türst is a legendary figure of the farming communities of Lucerne, a 'dreadful huntsman' who blows his hunting horn through villages in the stormy months before Epiphany, followed by three-legged hounds.

long_description.id: Türst, juga Dürst, adalah tokoh cerita rakyat dari komunitas petani Luzern yang diyakini berasal dari masa pra-Kristen. Ia digambarkan sebagai "pemburu mengerikan" yang harus diwaspadai saat cuaca buruk; pada bulan-bulan berbadai menjelang Epifani ia meniup terompet berburu menembus desa-desa bersama sekawanan anjing berkaki tiga yang menyalak.
long_description.en: Türst, also Dürst, is a folk figure of the farming communities of Lucerne believed to date from pre-Christian times. He is described as a 'dreadful huntsman' to beware of in stormy weather; in the tempestuous months before Epiphany he blows his hunting horn through the villages with a baying pack of three-legged hounds.

long_description.id: Ciri khasnya adalah ancaman "drü Schritt rechts, gang uswägs" ("tiga langkah ke kanan, minggir"): pejalan kaki yang tidak menyingkir tepat waktu diubah menjadi salah satu anjingnya. Pintu lumbung harus dibiarkan terbuka agar ia bisa berburu menembus lumbung tanpa halangan, dan menurut kisah lain ia membuat sapi perah ketakutan sampai sakit dan berhenti menghasilkan susu.
long_description.en: His hallmark is the threat 'drü Schritt rechts, gang uswägs' ('three steps right, get out of the way'): a walker who fails to step aside in time is turned into one of his dogs. Barn doors should be left open so he can hunt through unhindered, and other tales say he frightens dairy cows until they sicken and stop giving milk.

long_description.id: Kisahnya berbeda dari daerah ke daerah. Di Horw ia diiringi anjing-anjing kecil yang dipimpin anjing bermata satu, istrinya Sträggele si penyihir buruk rupa, dan Pfaffenkellnerin, hantu bermata menyala. Di Rickenbach ia memakai pakaian berburu hijau dengan kawanan setengah anjing setengah babi, dan di Wolhusen warga mendirikan salib untuk menghindarinya.
long_description.en: His tales vary by region. In Horw he is followed by small dogs led by a one-eyed hound, his wife Sträggele, a hideous witch, and the Pfaffenkellnerin, a ghost with glowing eyes. In Rickenbach he wears a green hunting costume with a pack of half-dog, half-pig beasts, and in Wolhusen people put up crosses to keep him away.

role.id: Berburu menembus desa saat musim badai.
role.en: Hunts through villages in stormy seasons.

did_you_know.id: Menurut kisah Wolhusen, bila salib penangkal Türst roboh, para petani akan sial sampai salib itu ditegakkan kembali.
did_you_know.en: In Wolhusen lore, if a cross set up against Türst fell, the farmers had bad luck until it stood upright again.

He is described as a "dreadful huntsman", of whom people should be wary in stormy weather. short_description.en: Dáinn, 'the dead one', is a figure of Norse mythology, mostly a dwarf and sometimes king of the elves, who with Nabbi forged Freyja's golden boar Hildisvíni.

long_description.id: Dáinn (Nordik Kuno, "yang mati") atau Dain adalah tokoh dalam mitologi Nordik; kebanyakan kisah menyebutnya kurcaci, sebagian lainnya raja para elf. Ia disebut kurcaci dalam daftar kurcaci Völuspá dan dalam bait Sigvatr Þórðarson, tetapi dalam Hávamál ia elf yang mengukir rune: "Odin bagi Æsir, dan Dain bagi para elf".
long_description.en: Dáinn (Old Norse 'dead') or Dain is a figure of Norse mythology; most tales make him a dwarf, some a king of elves. He is called a dwarf in the Völuspá's dwarf list and in a stanza by Sigvatr Þórðarson, but in the Hávamál he is an elf who carved runes: 'Odin for the Aesir, and Dain for the elves'.

long_description.id: Dalam Hyndluljóð ia bersama kurcaci Nabbi membuat babi hutan emas Hildisvíni milik Freyja. Namanya juga terdapat pada pedang Raja Högni, Dáinsleif ("warisan Dáinn"), yang dikutuk agar selalu membunuh seseorang setiap kali dihunus. Berbeda dari kurcaci lain, Dáinn cukup sering disebut dalam teks-teks lama.
long_description.en: In the Hyndluljóð he and the dwarf Nabbi made Freyja's golden boar Hildisvíni. His name is also found on King Högni's sword Dáinsleif ('Dáinn's legacy'), cursed always to kill a man whenever drawn. Unlike other dwarfs, Dáinn is mentioned comparatively often in the old texts.

short_description.id: Heinzelmännchen adalah roh rumah tangga penolong, sejenis kobold, yang dikaitkan dengan kota Köln dan konon mengerjakan semua pekerjaan warga di malam hari.
short_description.en: The Heinzelmännchen are helpful household spirits or kobolds associated with Cologne, said to have done all the citizens' work at night.

long_description.id: Heinzelmännchen adalah roh rumah tangga penolong atau kobold yang dikaitkan dengan kota Köln di Jerman, mirip brownie dari Skotlandia. Menurut sage Köln, makhluk-makhluk kecil ini mengerjakan pekerjaan warga di malam hari saat mereka tidur, sehingga penduduk Köln bisa bermalas-malasan di siang hari. Ukurannya yang kecil, topi runcingnya, dan kerajinannya menunjukkan mereka segolongan dengan kobold, Wichtel, dan kurcaci.
long_description.en: The Heinzelmännchen are helpful household spirits or kobolds tied to the city of Cologne in Germany, comparable to the brownies of Scotland. In the Cologne legend these little beings did the townspeople's work at night while they slept, letting the people of Cologne idle away the day. Their small size, pointed caps and diligence mark them as kin of kobolds, Wichtel and dwarfs.

long_description.id: Kebiasaan itu berakhir ketika istri seorang penjahit begitu ingin melihat mereka sehingga menaburkan kacang polong di lantai bengkel agar mereka terpeleset. Makhluk-makhluk itu murka, menghilang, dan tak pernah kembali, sehingga sejak itu warga Köln harus bekerja sendiri. Kisah ini pertama kali ditulis guru Köln Ernst Weyden pada 1826 dan menjadi populer lewat balada August Kopisch tahun 1836.
long_description.en: This ended when a tailor's wife, eager to catch sight of them, scattered peas on the workshop floor to make them slip. The angered creatures vanished and never came back, so from then on Cologne's citizens had to do their own work. The tale was first written down by the Cologne teacher Ernst Weyden in 1826 and became popular through August Kopisch's 1836 ballad.

long_description.id: Ahli folklor Marianne Rumpf (1976) mengajukan dua penjelasan asal nama: Heinzelmännlein sebagai sebutan boneka akar mandragora yang dipakai sebagai roh rumah, dan Heinz atau Heinzenkunst sebagai nama alat pembuang air di pertambangan, sehingga para operatornya mungkin disebut Heinzelmänner. Dalam dialek Köln namanya Heizemännche.
long_description.en: The folklorist Marianne Rumpf (1976) offered two explanations of the name: Heinzelmännlein as a name for mandrake dolls used as house spirits, and Heinz or Heinzenkunst as names of a mine-draining device, whose operators may have been called Heinzelmänner. In the Cologne dialect the name is Heizemännche.

long_description.en: The Heinzelmännchen (German pronunciation: [ˈhaɪntsl̩ˌmɛnçɛn] ) are helpful household spirits or kobolds associated with the city of Cologne in Germany, akin to brownies of Scotland. It has become traditional to tell their story during Christmas-tide. The creatures are also loosely referred to as "elves", rather in the sense of "The Elves and the Shoemaker". The little house gnomes are said to have done all the work of the citizens of Cologne during the night, so that the inhabitants of Cologne could be very lazy during the day. According to the legend, this went on until a tailor's wife got so curious to see the gnomes that she scattered peas onto the floor of the workshop to make the gnomes slip and fall. This infuriated the gnomes, who disappeared and never returned. From that time on, the citizens of Cologne had to do all their work by themselves.

short_description.id: Mótsognir adalah kurcaci pertama dan penguasa para kurcaci dalam mitologi Nordik, yang menurut Völuspá menjadi yang paling agung di antara mereka.
short_description.en: Mótsognir is the first dwarf and ruler of the dwarfs in Norse mythology, named in the Völuspá as the greatest of them.

long_description.id: Dalam mitologi Nordik, Mótsognir ("yang meminum kekuatan"), juga Móðsognir dalam naskah Hauksbók ("yang meminum keberanian"), adalah penguasa para kurcaci. Völuspá 10 menyebutnya "penguasa semua kurcaci". Menurut Gylfaginning 14 karya Snorri, para kurcaci mula-mula berwujud belatung di daging Ymir, lalu atas keputusan para dewa memperoleh akal dan rupa manusia; Mótsognir adalah kurcaci pertama dan Durinn yang kedua.
long_description.en: In Norse mythology Mótsognir ('he who drinks in might'), also Móðsognir in the Hauksbók manuscript ('he who drinks in courage'), is the ruler of the dwarfs. Völuspá 10 calls him 'lord of all the dwarves'. According to Snorri's Gylfaginning 14, the dwarfs first took shape as maggots in Ymir's flesh, then by the gods' decision gained reason and human form; Mótsognir was the first dwarf and Durinn the second.

long_description.id: Menurut Völuspá 9, para dewa memutuskan membentuk kurcaci dari darah Brimir dan tulang Bláinn, ungkapan yang biasa ditafsirkan sebagai darah dan daging raksasa purba Ymir. Para sarjana memperdebatkan tafsiran Snorri karena teks baitnya berbeda dari naskah lain. Arti namanya juga diperdebatkan; satu tafsiran mengusulkan "yang lelah, yang tak bertenaga", dan menyatakan tidak ada sumber yang menegaskan ia raja para kurcaci.
long_description.en: According to Völuspá 9, the gods resolved to make the dwarfs from Brimir's blood and Bláinn's bones, usually read as the blood and flesh of the primordial giant Ymir. Scholars dispute Snorri's interpretation because his text of the verse differs from other manuscripts. The meaning of the name is also disputed; one reading proposes 'the tired, powerless one', and no source confirms him as king of the dwarfs.

long_description.en: In Norse mythology, Mótsognir (Old Norse: [ˈmoːtˌsoɣnez̠], "he who drinks in might"), also found as Móðsognir ([ˈmoːðˌsoɣnez̠]; Hauksbók manuscript variant), "he who drinks in courage", is the ruler of the dwarves. In Völuspà 10, he is identified as mæztr um orðinn dverga allra, "lord of all the dwarves". According to Snorri Sturluson in Gylfaginning 14, which seeks to explain this verse, "the dwarfs had taken shape first and acquired life in the flesh of Ymir and were then maggots, but by decision of the gods they became conscious with intelligence and had the shape of men though they live in the earth and in rocks. Modsognir was a dwarf and the second was Durinn."

short_description.id: Vörðr adalah roh penjaga dalam mitologi Nordik yang diyakini mengikuti jiwa (hugr) setiap orang sejak lahir sampai mati.
short_description.en: The vörðr is a warden spirit of Norse mythology believed to follow every person's soul (hugr) from birth to death.

long_description.id: Dalam mitologi Nordik, vǫrðr ("pemelihara" atau "penjaga") adalah roh penjaga yang diyakini mengikuti jiwa atau hugr setiap orang sejak lahir sampai mati. Dalam bahasa Swedia Kuno kata padanannya varþer, dan dalam bahasa Swedia modern vård; kepercayaan pada roh penjaga ini tetap kuat dalam cerita rakyat Skandinavia sampai beberapa abad terakhir.
long_description.en: In Norse mythology the vǫrðr ('caretaker' or 'guardian') is a warden spirit believed to follow every person's soul, or hugr, from birth to death. Old Swedish had the matching word varþer and modern Swedish vård; belief in such guardian spirits stayed strong in Scandinavian folklore until the last few centuries.

long_description.id: Kadang roh penjaga ini menampakkan diri sebagai cahaya kecil atau sebagai sosok orang yang dijaganya. Merasakan penjaga orang lain bisa menimbulkan sensasi fisik seperti gatal di tangan atau hidung, dan penjaga itu bisa tiba sebelum orangnya sendiri. Penjaga orang yang sudah meninggal dapat menjadi hantu yang menghuni tempat atau orang tertentu, berbeda dari mayat hidup yang lebih sadar seperti draugar.
long_description.en: At times the warden showed itself as a small light or in the shape of its person. Sensing another's warden could cause bodily feelings such as an itching hand or nose, and the warden might arrive before the person did. A dead person's warden could become a revenant haunting particular places or people, distinct from more conscious undead such as the draugar.

long_description.id: Pohon tua yang tumbuh di pekarangan, sering linden, ash, atau elm, dapat dijuluki "pohon penjaga" (Swedia: vårdträd) dan diyakini melindungi pertanian dari nasib buruk; mematahkan daun atau rantingnya dianggap pelanggaran berat. Kata Inggris wraith diturunkan dari vǫrðr. Di bawah pengaruh Kristen, sebagian orang memandang roh ini seperti hati nurani baik dan buruk, sebagian lagi sebagai malaikat pelindung.
long_description.en: An old tree on the farmstead, often a linden, ash or elm, might be called a 'warden tree' (Swedish vårdträd) and was believed to protect the farm from bad luck; breaking a leaf or twig from it was a serious offence. The English word wraith is derived from vǫrðr. Under Christian influence some came to see the spirit as a good and a bad conscience, others as guardian angels.

role.en: Follows a person's soul for life.

short_description.id: Nis Puk adalah sejenis kobold atau roh rumah dari wilayah berbahasa Denmark, Jerman Rendah, dan Frisia Utara di Schleswig, yang menjaga rumah dan ternak asalkan diberi bubur pada hari Natal.
short_description.en: Nis Puk is a kind of kobold or house spirit from the Danish-, Low German- and North Frisian-speaking lands of Schleswig, who guards house and livestock if given porridge at Christmas.

long_description.id: Nis Puk (juga Niß Puk) adalah makhluk legenda sejenis kobold dari wilayah berbahasa Denmark, Jerman Rendah, dan Frisia Utara di Jerman utara dan Denmark selatan, termasuk Schleswig. Di Denmark ia juga dikenal sebagai nis pug, varian dari nisse. Tergantung tempatnya, ia bisa tampil sebagai roh rumah tangga atau berperan seperti Drak atau kobold, roh dari neraka yang membuat pemiliknya kaya dengan membawakan barang curian.
long_description.en: A legendary being of the kobold type, Nis Puk (also Niß Puk) belongs to the borderland of southern Denmark and northern Germany, including Schleswig, where Danish, Low German and North Frisian are spoken. In Denmark it is also known as nis pug, a variant of the nisse. Depending on place, it may appear as a household spirit or play the role of a Drak or kobold, an infernal spirit enriching its owner with stolen goods.

long_description.id: Namanya menggabungkan Nisse dan Puk, dua kata yang bermakna sama; Niß konon berasal dari nama Nikolaus, sedangkan Puk dari bahasa Denmark Kuno puge, dari Nordik Kuno púki, "kobold". Menurut sage, Nis Puk tinggal di loteng atau lumbung, tak terlihat oleh orang dewasa dan menjaga rumah, halaman, serta ternak bila penghuni memperlakukan anak dan hewan mereka dengan baik.
long_description.en: His name joins Nisse and Puk, two words meaning the same; Niß is said to come from the name Nikolaus, and Puk from Old Danish puge, from Old Norse púki, 'kobold'. By the legends Nis Puk lives in the attic or barn, invisible to adults and looks after house, yard and animals if the household treats its own children and animals well.

long_description.id: Setahun sekali, saat Natal, Nis Puk harus diberi semangkuk bubur dengan mentega; bila tidak, ia pindah ke desa lain dan rumah itu terancam kerusakan dan malapetaka. Penulis Boy Lornsen mengangkatnya dalam beberapa buku anak, dan di depan sekolah Neukirchen berdiri patung kecil Nis Puk.
long_description.en: Once a year, at Christmas, Nis Puk must be given a bowl of porridge with butter; otherwise he moves to another village and the house is exposed to decay and misfortune. The author Boy Lornsen featured him in several children's books, and a small statue of Nis Puk stands in front of the school at Neukirchen.

statement.en: Nis Puk looks after house, yard and animals; he lives in the attic or barn, unseen by adults, and once a year at Christmas must get a bowl of porridge with butter, or he moves to another village.

statement.en: Nis Puk (Sylt Frisian Nes Pük; Danish Nis Pug, Nis Puge) is a folk-tale figure, and a small statue of him stands in front of the school in Neukirchen.

statement.id: Figur ini memadukan nisse Denmark-Skåne-Norwegia dengan puk Inggris; ia menjaga rumah dan hewan bila penghuni bersedia memperlakukan anak dan hewan mereka dengan baik; tanpa bubur rumah itu terancam kerusakan dan malapetaka; pepatah Sylt berbunyi "Hi glüüret üs en pük" (ia menatap seperti Nis Puk), dan ia muncul dalam buku-buku anak Boy Lornsen.
statement.en: The figure combines the Danish-Scanian-Norwegian nisse with the English puk; he looks after house and animals if the occupants treat their own children and animals well; without porridge the house faces decay and misfortune; a Sylt saying runs 'Hi glüüret üs en pük' (he stares like a Nis Puk), and he features in Boy Lornsen's children's books.

long_description.en: The Nis Puk (sometimes also Niß Puk (German: [ˈnɪs pʊk])) is a legendary creature, a kind of Kobold, from Danish-, Low German- and North Frisian-speaking areas of Northern Germany and Southern Denmark, among them Schleswig, today divided into the German Southern Schleswig and Danish Northern Schleswig. It is also known in Denmark itself as nis pug, as a variant of nisse. An earlier saying says Nissen does not want to go over the Eideren, i.e. not to Holstein to the South of Schleswig. Depending on the place, it can either appear as a domestic spirit or take on the role of a being generally called Drak or Kobold in Danish and German mythology, an infernal spirit making its owner wealthy by bringing them stolen goods. The term combines the terms Nisse and Puck. The Nis Puk or Niß Puk can also be referred to as just Niß, Nis or Puk. The figure of the Nisse is widespread in Denmark, Norway, Scania, Halland and Blekinge (here as Goanisse or Godnisse≈the good Nisse), the figure of the Puk can further be found in the (formerly) German-speaking regions of Pomerania and Neumark, belonging partially or completely to Poland today.

short_description.id: Erlking (Erlkönig) adalah elf jahat dalam cerita rakyat Eropa yang berkeliaran di hutan dan membunuh anak-anak dengan sekali sentuh; ia terkenal lewat puisi Goethe.
short_description.en: The Erlking (Erlkönig) is a sinister elf of European folklore who haunts the woods and kills children with a single touch; he is famous from Goethe's poem.

long_description.id: Dalam cerita rakyat dan mitos Eropa, Erlking adalah elf jahat yang berdiam di hutan; ia mengintai anak-anak yang terlalu lama di hutan dan membunuh mereka dengan sekali sentuh. Nama "Erlking" (Jerman: Erlkönig, harfiah "raja pohon alder") dipakai dalam Romantisisme Jerman untuk roh atau "raja para peri", dan umumnya dianggap turunan dari ellekonge, "raja elf", dalam cerita rakyat Denmark.
long_description.en: Woodland is the haunt of the Erlking, a malevolent elf of European myth and folklore who watches for children lingering too long among the trees and slays them with one touch. German Romanticism used 'Erlking' (German Erlkönig, literally 'alder-king') for a spirit or 'king of the fairies', and the name is commonly traced to the ellekonge, 'elf-king', of Danish folk tradition.

long_description.id: Nama ini pertama kali dipakai Johann Gottfried Herder dalam baladanya Erlkönigs Tochter (1778), saduran balada rakyat Denmark Hr. Oluf han rider (1739), lalu diambil Johann Wolfgang von Goethe dalam puisinya Erlkönig (1782) yang digubah menjadi musik oleh Schubert. Goethe memberi makna baru, karena "Erl" berarti pohon alder hitam, bukan elf. Menurut Jacob Grimm, istilah ini berasal dari kata Skandinavia ellekonge, "raja elf".
long_description.en: Johann Gottfried Herder introduced the name in his 1778 ballad Erlkönigs Tochter, a reworking of the 1739 Danish folk ballad Hr. Oluf han rider; Johann Wolfgang von Goethe then used it for his 1782 poem Erlkönig, later set to music by Schubert. Goethe gave it a new sense, since 'Erl' means black alder, not elf. According to Jacob Grimm the term comes from the Scandinavian word ellekonge, 'king of the elves'.

long_description.id: Dalam kisah yang diceritakan Herder, Sir Oluf berkuda menuju pernikahannya tetapi terpikat musik para elf; putri raja elf mengajaknya menari, dan ketika ia menolak tawaran serta hadiah emasnya, sang elf memukulnya hingga jatuh. Esok paginya pengantinnya menemukannya mati. Dalam sastra, Erlkönig digambarkan sebagai makhluk jahat yang menghantui hutan dan menyeret para pengembara menuju kematian.
long_description.en: In the tale as Herder told it, Sir Oluf rides to his wedding but is drawn by elfin music; the elf-king's daughter invites him to dance, and when he refuses her offer and her gifts of gold she strikes him down. Next morning his bride finds him dead. In literature the Erlkönig is portrayed as an evil creature haunting the forests and leading travellers to their death.

long_description.en: In European folklore and myth, the Erlking is a sinister elf who lingers in the woods. He stalks children who stay in the woods for too long and kills them with a single touch. The name "Erlking" (German: Erlkönig, lit. 'alder-king'; German: [ˈɛʁlkøːnɪç, -nɪk]) is a name used in German Romanticism for the figure of a spirit or "king of the fairies". It is usually assumed that the name is a derivation from the ellekonge (older elverkonge, i.e. "Elf-king") in Danish folklore. The name was first used by Johann Gottfried Herder in his ballad Erlkönigs Tochter (1778), an adaptation of the Danish folk ballad Hr. Oluf han rider (1739), and was taken up by Johann Wolfgang von Goethe in his poem Erlkönig (1782), which was set to music by Schubert and others. Goethe added a new meaning, as "Erl" means not "elf" but "black alder", and the poem about the Erlenkönig is set in the area of an alder quarry in the Saale Valley, in Thuringia. In English translations of Goethe's poem, the name is sometimes rendered as Erl-king.

short_description.id: Brân the Blessed (Bendigeidfran, "Gagak yang Diberkati") adalah raksasa dan raja Britania dalam mitologi Wales, yang kepalanya tetap berbicara setelah dipenggal.
short_description.en: In Welsh myth Brân the Blessed (Bendigeidfran, 'Blessed Crow') is a giant who reigned over Britain, and his cut-off head kept on talking.

long_description.id: Brân the Blessed (Wales/Welsh: Bendigeidfran atau Brân Fendigaidd, harfiah "Gagak yang Diberkati") adalah raksasa dan raja Britania (Britain) dalam mitologi Wales. Ia muncul dalam beberapa Welsh Triads, tetapi perannya terpenting ada di Cabang Kedua Mabinogi, Branwen ferch Llŷr. Ia putra Llŷr dan Penarddun serta saudara Brânwen, Manawydan, Nisien, dan Efnysien. Nama Brân biasanya diartikan gagak; ia dianggap dewa laut sekaligus dewa puisi dan para bard.
long_description.en: Brân the Blessed (Welsh Bendigeidfran or Brân Fendigaidd, 'Blessed Crow') is a giant who ruled Britain in Welsh myth. Several Welsh Triads mention him, though his main part is in the Second Branch of the Mabinogi, Branwen ferch Llŷr. Llŷr and Penarddun were his parents, and Brânwen, Manawydan, Nisien and Efnysien his siblings. Brân is usually rendered crow or raven; he is held to be a sea god and also a god of poetry and of bards.

long_description.id: Dalam Mabinogion, ia memberi raja Irlandia (Irish) Matholwch sebuah kuali ajaib yang dapat menghidupkan orang mati sebagai ganti rugi atas penghinaan Efnysien. Ketika Branwen dianiaya di Irlandia, Brân mengarungi Laut Irlandia (Irish Sea) untuk menyelamatkannya. Setelah perang yang hanya menyisakan tujuh orang, Brân yang terluka parah menyuruh mereka memenggal kepalanya dan membawanya pulang ke Britania; kepala itu terus berbicara dan menghibur mereka selama tujuh tahun di Harlech. Akhirnya kepala itu dikubur di Gwynfryn, "Bukit Putih" (diduga lokasi Tower of London), menghadap Prancis (France) untuk menangkal serbuan. Menurut artikel de, nama Bran sering menjadi sinonim untuk "pejuang" (Krieger).
long_description.en: In the Mabinogion he gives the Irish king Matholwch a magic cauldron able to revive the dead, as amends for Efnysien's insult. When Branwen is ill-treated in Ireland, Brân wades the Irish Sea to save her. After a war that leaves just seven men alive, the dying Brân tells them to cut off his head and carry it back to Britain; the head goes on talking and entertains them for seven years at Harlech. It is finally buried at the Gwynfryn, the 'White Hill' (thought to be the site of the Tower of London), facing France to ward off invasion. According to the de article the name Bran is often a synonym for 'warrior' (Krieger).

short_description.id: Puck, juga disebut Goodfellows atau Robin Goodfellow, adalah demon atau peri dalam cerita rakyat Inggris, berupa roh rumah tangga atau roh alam.
short_description.en: Puck, also called the Goodfellows or Robin Goodfellow, is a demon or fairy of English folklore, a household or nature sprite.

long_description.id: Dalam cerita rakyat Inggris (English folklore), Puck, juga dikenal sebagai Goodfellows, adalah demon atau peri yang dapat berupa roh rumah tangga maupun roh alam. Asal-usul katanya tidak pasti: kata Inggris ini sudah tercatat dalam bahasa Inggris Kuno (Old English) sebagai puca, dan kata serupa muncul dalam bahasa Norse Kuno (Old Norse) púki serta bahasa Kelt seperti pwca (Wales), bucca (Cornwall), dan púca (Irlandia). Oxford English Dictionary condong ke asal Skandinavia, sedangkan Erin Sebo dari Flinders University berpendapat kata itu berasal dari Irlandia.
long_description.en: In English folklore the Puck, also known as the Goodfellows, is a demon or fairy that may be a household sprite or a nature sprite. The word's origin is unclear: it is already found in Old English as puca, and similar words appear in Old Norse púki and in Celtic tongues as pwca (Welsh), bucca (Cornish) and púca (Irish). The Oxford English Dictionary leaned to a Scandinavian source, while Erin Sebo of Flinders University argues it came from Irish.

long_description.id: Puck juga dapat disebut Goodfellows atau Hobgoblin, dengan Hob sebagai ganti Rob atau Robin, merujuk pada tokoh Robin Goodfellow. Seperti sebutan "the good folk" untuk peri, nama itu mencerminkan upaya menyenangkan para peri, yang suka pujian meski jahil. Rujukan tertua "Robin Goodfellow" menurut Oxford English Dictionary berasal dari 1531. Menurut artikel de tentang Puk, makhluk kerdil dalam legenda Nordik (nordischen Volkssagen) yang tinggal bersama manusia; bila diberi makan dan minum teratur ia membawa kemakmuran, tetapi bila diperlakukan buruk ia mendatangkan kerugian besar; artikel itu juga mengaitkannya dengan púca dari Kelt.
long_description.en: Puck may also be called the Goodfellows or Hobgoblin, Hob standing in for Rob or Robin, after the figure Robin Goodfellow. Like calling fairies 'the good folk', the name aimed to please beings fond of flattery despite their mischief. The oldest 'Robin Goodfellow' reference cited by the Oxford English Dictionary dates from 1531. The de article describes the Puk as a dwarfish figure of Nordic legend (nordischen Volkssagen) living alongside people; fed and given drink regularly it brings prosperity, but mistreated it causes grave harm; that article also links it with the Celtic púca.

did_you_know.id: Nama Robin Goodfellow bagi Puck dimaksudkan untuk menyenangkan para peri yang gemar pujian, serupa sebutan "the good folk".
did_you_know.en: The name Robin Goodfellow for Puck was meant to please fairies who loved flattery, much like calling them 'the good folk'.

Rujukan tertua "Robin Goodfellow" menurut Oxford English Dictionary berasal dari 1531. Menurut artikel de tentang Puk, makhluk kerdil dalam legenda Nordik (nordischen Volkssagen) yang tinggal bersama manusia; bila diberi makan dan minum teratur ia membawa kemakmuran, tetapi bila diperlakukan buruk ia mendatangkan kerugian besar; artikel itu juga mengaitkannya dengan púca dari Kelt.
long_description.en: Puck may also be called the Goodfellows or Hobgoblin, Hob standing in for Rob or Robin, after the figure Robin Goodfellow. Like calling fairies 'the good folk', the name aimed to please beings fond of flattery despite their mischief. The oldest 'Robin Goodfellow' reference cited by the Oxford English Dictionary dates from 1531. The de article describes the Puk as a dwarfish figure of Nordic legend (nordischen Volkssagen) living alongside people; fed and given drink regularly it brings prosperity, but mistreated it causes grave harm; that article also links it with the Celtic púca.

did_you_know.id: Nama Robin Goodfellow bagi Puck dimaksudkan untuk menyenangkan para peri yang gemar pujian, serupa sebutan "the good folk".
did_you_know.en: The name Robin Goodfellow for Puck was meant to please fairies who loved flattery, much like calling them 'the good folk'.

short_description.id: Clurichaun adalah peri jahil dalam cerita rakyat Irlandia yang sangat gemar minum dan suka menghantui tempat pembuatan bir, kedai, dan gudang anggur.
short_description.en: The clurichaun is a mischievous fairy of Irish folklore with a great love of drink, given to haunting breweries, pubs and wine cellars.

long_description.id: Clurichaun atau clúrachán (dari Irlandia/Irish clobhair-ceann) adalah peri jahil dalam cerita rakyat Irlandia yang terkenal gemar minum dan suka menghantui tempat pembuatan bir, kedai, serta gudang anggur. Ia berkerabat dengan leprechaun dan kadang dicampuradukkan dengannya sebagai tukang sepatu dan penjaga harta terpendam, sehingga sebagian folklorist menganggapnya leprechaun yang sedang mabuk-mabukan. Seperti leprechaun, ia peri penyendiri, bukan peri yang berkelompok. Menurut artikel de, Thomas Crofton Croker pada 1825 berpendapat kata itu berasal dari luchramán, "kerdil", dan kumpulan dongengnya diterjemahkan Grimm bersaudara pada 1826 sebagai Irische Elfenmärchen.
long_description.en: The clurichaun or clúrachán (from Irish clobhair-ceann) is a mischievous fairy of Irish folklore, famous for loving drink and for haunting breweries, pubs and wine cellars. He is kin to the leprechaun and is at times mixed up with him as a shoemaker and keeper of hidden treasure, leading some folklorists to see him as a leprechaun on a drinking binge. Like the leprechaun he is a solitary fairy rather than one of the trooping kind. According to the de article, Thomas Crofton Croker claimed in 1825 that the word comes from luchramán, 'dwarf', and his tales were translated by the Brothers Grimm in 1826 as Irische Elfenmärchen.

long_description.id: Dalam dongeng "The Haunted Cellar" yang dicatat Croker pada 1825, clurichaun bernama Naggeneen menghantui gudang anggur seorang bangsawan Irlandia; ia digambarkan lelaki kecil setinggi sekitar 15 cm, berwajah seperti apel layu, berhidung merah keunguan karena banyak minum, bertopi tidur merah dan bersepatu bergesper perak besar. Dalam "Master and Man", seorang clurichaun memaksa Billy Mac Daniel melayaninya tujuh tahun satu hari, tetapi Billy terbebas dengan menyebut berkat Tuhan. Clurichaun dapat melewati lubang kunci, mengubah rumput rawa menjadi kuda tunggangan, dan terbang menunggangi rumput itu seperti penyihir dengan sapu.
long_description.en: In 'The Haunted Cellar', recorded by Croker in 1825, a clurichaun called Naggeneen haunts an Irish lord's wine cellar; he is a little man about 15 cm tall with a face like a withered apple, a nose red and purple from drink, a red nightcap and shoes with big silver buckles. In 'Master and Man' a clurichaun forces Billy Mac Daniel to serve him for seven years and a day, but Billy breaks free by calling on God's blessing. Clurichauns can slip through keyholes, turn bog rushes into horses to ride, and fly on rushes much as witches ride brooms.

long_description.en: The clurichaun () or clúrachán (from Irish: clobhair-ceann) is a mischievous fairy in Irish folklore known for his great love of drinking and a tendency to haunt breweries, pubs and wine cellars. He is related to the leprechaun and has sometimes been conflated with him as a shoemaker and a guardian of hidden treasure. This has led some folklorists to suppose that the clurichaun is merely a leprechaun on a drinking spree, while others regard them as regional variations of the same being. Like the leprechaun, the clurichaun is a solitary fairy, encountered alone rather than in groups, as distinct from the trooping fairies.
