short_description.id: Ksatria Ålleberg adalah arwah para ksatria dalam legenda Swedia yang tidur di dalam gunung Ålleberg dekat Falköping, menunggu perang baru untuk bangkit menyelamatkan negeri.
short_description.en: The Knights of Ålleberg are ghostly knights of Swedish legend who sleep inside the mountain Ålleberg near Falköping, waiting for a new war to wake them to save the country.

long_description.id: Menurut legenda Swedia, Ksatria Ålleberg adalah arwah dua belas ksatria yang gugur dalam Pertempuran Åsle tahun 1389, di dalam atau sekitar Falköping, antara pasukan Raja Albert dari Swedia dan Margaret I dari Denmark. Legenda ini contoh motif "raja yang tidur di dalam gunung" dalam cerita rakyat.
long_description.en: According to Swedish legend, the Knights of Ålleberg are the ghosts of twelve knights who fell at the Battle of Åsle in 1389, fought in or near Falköping between the forces of King Albert of Sweden and Margaret I of Denmark. The legend is an instance of the folklore motif of the king asleep in the mountain.

long_description.id: Arwah-arwah itu terkurung di dalam gunung Ålleberg, menunggu perang baru yang akan membangunkan mereka untuk berjuang menyelamatkan negeri; gunung itu juga dipercaya dihuni troll. Artikel Swedia mencatat bahwa jumlah penunggang dalam legenda disebut "ribuan demi ribuan", dan angka dua belas berasal dari "dua belas penunggang emas" yang konon bergabung dengan pasukan Nordik dalam pertempuran Åsle.
long_description.en: The ghosts are shut inside the mountain Ålleberg, waiting for a new war to wake them so they can fight for the country; the mountain is also believed to house trolls. The Swedish article notes that legends put the riders at 'thousands upon thousands', and that the figure twelve comes from the 'twelve golden riders' said to have joined the Nordic army at Åsle.

long_description.id: Versi paling umum menceritakan seorang petani yang membawa muatan gandum ke pasar Falköping. Seorang lelaki asing membeli semua muatannya dan membawanya ke sebuah aula di dalam gunung, tempat para ksatria tidur berbaju zirah lengkap. Petani itu tak sengaja membenturkan tali kekang hingga berdenting; para penunggang terbangun dan bertanya apakah sudah tiba waktunya, tetapi lelaki itu meyakinkan mereka untuk tidur lagi. Pada pertengahan abad ke-19 Horace Marryat juga mencatat salah satu versi legenda yang beredar di Falköping.
long_description.en: The commonest version tells of a farmer taking a load of grain to market in Falköping. A stranger bought the whole load and led him into a hall within the mountain, where the knights lay asleep in full armour. The farmer accidentally knocked a bridle so that it jingled; the riders woke and asked whether it was time, but the stranger assured them they could sleep on. In the mid-19th century Horace Marryat also wrote down one of the versions told in Falköping.

short_description.id: Eckart yang Setia (der treue Eckart) adalah tokoh legenda heroik Jermanik dan cerita rakyat Jerman: wali para Harlung dalam kisah Dietrich von Bern, dan pemberi peringatan yang berjalan di depan Perburuan Liar.
short_description.en: Faithful Eckart (der treue Eckart) is a figure of Germanic heroic legend and German folklore: guardian of the Harlungs in the Dietrich von Bern legends, and the warner who walks ahead of the Wild Hunt.

long_description.id: Dalam legenda heroik, Eckart (juga Eckehart atau Eckewart) adalah wali dua pemuda Harlung yang mewarisi Breisgau, Kastel Breisach, dan harta tak terhingga dari ayah mereka, Diether. Ia sendiri seorang Harlung dan termasyhur karena kesetiaannya. Ketika Raja Ermenrich, paman mereka, menghasut oleh penasihat Sibeche, merebut Breisach saat Eckart tak ada, menggantung kedua keponakannya dan merampas hartanya, Eckart membalas dendam: ia menyeret Sibeche ke tiang gantungan dalam pertempuran Rabenschlacht dan bersama para pahlawan lain membunuh Ermenrich.
long_description.en: In heroic legend, Eckart (also Eckehart or Eckewart) is the guardian of two young Harlungs who inherited the Breisgau, Breisach Castle and boundless treasure from their father Diether. He is himself a Harlung and famed for his loyalty. When King Ermenrich, their uncle, egged on by his adviser Sibeche, seized Breisach while Eckart was away, hanged his nephews and took their wealth, Eckart avenged them: he dragged Sibeche to the gallows during the Rabenschlacht and, with other heroes, killed Ermenrich.

long_description.id: Harta para Harlung konon disihir dan disembunyikan di gunung Bürglenberg dekat Breisach, dijaga arwah Eckart yang memperingatkan setiap pemburu harta bahwa harta itu ditakdirkan jatuh ke tangan ahli waris sah. Karena itulah orang Jerman punya pepatah "Du bist der treue Eckart, du warnest jedermann", yang dipakai untuk orang yang suka memperingatkan semua orang.
long_description.en: The Harlungs' treasure is said to be enchanted and hidden in the Bürglenberg near Breisach, guarded by Eckart's spirit, who tells every treasure-seeker that it is destined for the rightful heir. Hence the German proverb "Du bist der treue Eckart, du warnest jedermann", said of anyone who warns everybody.

long_description.id: Di Thüringen, Eckart berjalan di depan Perburuan Liar (wütendes Heer) yang dipimpin Frau Holle pada Dua Belas Malam Natal, menyuruh orang menyingkir agar tidak celaka. Ia digambarkan sebagai lelaki tua bertongkat putih. Saat rombongan itu tinggal di dalam gunung Hörselberg, Eckart duduk di depan guanya dan memperingatkan siapa pun agar tidak memasuki alam Frau Venus, tempat tiada jalan kembali; peran ini sudah dikenal sejak 1453.
long_description.en: In Thuringia, Eckart walks ahead of the Wild Hunt (wütendes Heer) led by Frau Holle during the Twelve Nights of Christmas, telling people to step aside so they come to no harm. He is pictured as an old man with a white staff. When the host stays inside the Hörselberg, Eckart sits before the cave warning everyone not to enter the realm of Frau Venus, from which there is no return; this role has been known since 1453.

who.en: The faithful guardian of the Harlungs.

role.en: Warns people of the Wild Hunt.

famous_for.en: Guards the entrance to the Venusberg.

did_you_know.id: Dalam legenda Thüringen, Eckart mengisi kembali kendi bir anak-anak yang diminum rombongan Perburuan Liar, dan bir itu tetap penuh selama mereka merahasiakan pertemuan tersebut.
did_you_know.en: In a legend from Thuringia, Eckart refilled the beer jugs that the Wild Hunt had drunk from some children, and the beer stayed full as long as they kept the encounter secret.

description.id: Di Denmark ia memperingatkan orang sebelum memasuki rumah bordil, dan sebuah kronik 1566 menempatkannya sebagai hakim di gerbang neraka.
description.en: In Denmark he warns people before they enter a brothel, and a chronicle of 1566 sets him as a judge at the gates of hell.

claims.quote: is a character of Germanic heroic legend, particularly the legends about Dietrich von Bern, and also features in German legends about the wild hunt.

statement.id: Eckart, biasa disebut der treue Eckart atau treuer Eckart ("Eckart yang setia"), adalah tokoh legenda heroik Jermanik (Germanic), khususnya legenda Dietrich von Bern, dan juga muncul dalam legenda Jerman (German) tentang Perburuan Liar (wild hunt).
statement.en: Eckart, commonly der treue Eckart or treuer Eckart ('the faithful Eckart'), is a figure of Germanic heroic legend, especially the Dietrich von Bern legends, and also features in German legends of the Wild Hunt.

claims.quote: In heroic legend, Eckart, also called Eckehart or Eckewart, is the guardian of the Harlungs, two young men whose late father Diether bequeathed them the Breisgau territory, Breisach Castle, and immeasurable treasure. He is a Harlung himself, and has great renown for his loyalty and faithfulness

statement.id: Dalam legenda heroik, Eckart (Eckehart, Eckewart) adalah wali para Harlung, dua pemuda yang mewarisi wilayah Breisgau, Kastel Breisach, dan harta tak terhingga dari mendiang ayah mereka Diether; ia sendiri Harlung dan termasyhur karena kesetiaannya; para Harlung adalah sepupu Dietrich von Bern.
statement.en: In heroic legend Eckart (Eckehart, Eckewart) is the guardian of the Harlungs, two young men left the Breisgau, Breisach Castle and vast treasure by their late father Diether; he is a Harlung himself and renowned for loyalty; the Harlungs are cousins of Dietrich von Bern.

claims.quote: During the Rabenschlacht battle, Eckart took Sibeche captive and dragged him away on horseback to be hung on the gallows. He also took revenge for the demise of his charges when he and other heroes slew Ermenrich.

statement.id: Dalam pertempuran Rabenschlacht, Eckart menawan Sibeche dan menyeretnya dengan kuda ke tiang gantungan; ia membalas kematian anak-anak asuhnya dengan membunuh Ermenrich bersama pahlawan lain.
statement.en: In the Rabenschlacht Eckart captured Sibeche and dragged him on horseback to the gallows; he avenged his wards by killing Ermenrich with other heroes.

claims.quote: The rich treasure of the Harlungs, the Harlungenhort, is said to be enchanted and hidden inside the mountain Bürglenberg near Breisach. This treasure is guarded by the spirit of treuer Eckart who warns every treasure seeker that this treasure is fated to fall into the hands of the true heir of the Harlungs

statement.id: Harta Harlung (Harlungenhort) konon disihir dan disembunyikan di gunung Bürglenberg dekat Breisach, dijaga arwah Eckart yang memperingatkan setiap pemburu harta bahwa harta itu ditakdirkan bagi ahli waris sejati; dari sini lahir pepatah "Du bist der treue Eckart, du warnest jedermann".
statement.en: The Harlungs' treasure (Harlungenhort) is said to be enchanted in the Bürglenberg near Breisach, guarded by Eckart's spirit, who warns every treasure-seeker that it is fated for the true heir; hence the saying 'Du bist der treue Eckart, du warnest jedermann'.

claims.quote: In Thuringia, der treue Eckart is connected with the wild hunt, locally called wütendes Heer or furious host. Leader of the wild hunt is Frau Holle ... who roams the countryside with the furious host during Christmas, namely the Zwölften, that is the Twelve Nights of Christmas. Der treue Eckart goes ahead of the wild hunt, warning the people to step out of the way so they will suffer no harm.

statement.id: Di Thüringen (Thuringia), Eckart terkait dengan Perburuan Liar (wild hunt; wütendes Heer) yang dipimpin Frau Holle pada Dua Belas Malam Natal (Twelve Nights of Christmas); ia berjalan di depannya, menyuruh orang menyingkir agar tidak celaka.
statement.en: In Thuringia Eckart is tied to the Wild Hunt (wütendes Heer) led by Frau Holle over the Twelve Nights of Christmas; he goes ahead of it, telling people to step aside so they come to no harm.

claims.quote: His appearance is that of an old man with a staff. When the furious host doesn’t travel and stays inside Hörselberg Mountain, der treue Eckart sits outside the cave, warning everybody against entering the realm of Frau Venus from where there is no return.

statement.id: Ia berwujud lelaki tua bertongkat; saat rombongan itu tinggal di dalam gunung Hörselberg, Eckart duduk di luar gua memperingatkan semua orang agar tidak memasuki alam Frau Venus (Venusberg), tempat tiada jalan kembali.
statement.en: He looks like an old man with a staff; when the host stays inside the Hörselberg, Eckart sits outside the cave warning all against entering the realm of Frau Venus (the Venusberg), whence none return.

claims.quote: Der Getreue Eckart oder Treue Eckart (auch in den diversen Namensvarianten von „Eckart“ wie „Eckhart“, „Eckehard“ usw.) ist eine Figur mit Wurzeln in der germanischen Sagenwelt, zugleich ein Stoff der Literatur und Kunst.

statement.id: Getreuer Eckart atau Treue Eckart adalah tokoh berakar dalam dunia legenda Jermanik dan juga bahan sastra serta seni.
statement.en: The Getreue Eckart or Treue Eckart is a figure rooted in Germanic legend and also a subject of literature and art.

claims.quote: That der treue Eckart guards the entrance to the Venusberg, i.e. the mountain of Frau Venus, and advises people against entering is known since 1453 if not longer, giving rise to the saying mentioned above. In Denmark, he also is found warning people before entering a brothel, and a chronicle from 1566 places him as a judge at the gates of hell.

statement.id: Peran Eckart menjaga pintu Venusberg dan menasihati orang agar tidak masuk dikenal setidaknya sejak 1453; di Denmark ia memperingatkan orang sebelum memasuki rumah bordil, dan kronik tahun 1566 menempatkannya sebagai hakim di gerbang neraka.
statement.en: Eckart's guarding of the Venusberg entrance and warning people off is known since at least 1453; in Denmark he warns people before entering a brothel, and a chronicle of 1566 makes him a judge at the gates of hell.

claims.quote: Der Getreue Eckart macht sie ihnen wieder voll und verspricht, sie würden immer voll bleiben, solange die Kinder über das Geschaute Schweigen bewahrten.

statement.id: Eckart mengisi kembali kendi bir anak-anak yang diminum rombongan Perburuan Liar dan berjanji kendi itu akan selalu penuh selama mereka merahasiakan apa yang mereka lihat (Thüringen).
statement.en: Eckart refilled the children's beer jugs drunk by the Wild Hunt and promised they would stay full as long as the children kept silent about what they had seen (Thüringen).

statement.id: Jörg Wickram memakai Eckart dalam lakon Der trew Eckart (1532), dan Johann Wolfgang Goethe menjadikannya tokoh utama balada Der getreue Eckart (1813).
statement.en: Jörg Wickram used Eckart in the play Der trew Eckart (1532), and Johann Wolfgang Goethe made him the hero of the ballad Der getreue Eckart (1813).

statement.id: Suatu hari saat Eckart tak ada, Raja Ermenrich, paman para Harlung, terdorong ketamakan akan warisan keponakannya dan fitnah penasihatnya Sibeche, merebut Kastel Breisach, menggantung keponakannya, dan merampas harta mereka.
statement.en: One day while Eckart was away, King Ermenrich, the Harlungs' uncle, driven by greed for their inheritance and his adviser Sibeche's slanders, seized Breisach Castle, hanged his nephews and took their property.

claims.statement: Eckart, commonly der treue Eckart or treuer Eckart ('the faithful Eckart'), is a figure of Germanic heroic legend, especially the Dietrich von Bern legends, and also features in German legends of the Wild Hunt.
claims.statement_id: Eckart, biasa disebut der treue Eckart atau treuer Eckart ("Eckart yang setia"), adalah tokoh legenda heroik Jermanik (Germanic), khususnya legenda Dietrich von Bern, dan juga muncul dalam legenda Jerman (German) tentang Perburuan Liar (wild hunt).
claims.quote: is a character of Germanic heroic legend, particularly the legends about Dietrich von Bern, and also features in German legends about the wild hunt.

claims.statement: In heroic legend Eckart (Eckehart, Eckewart) is the guardian of the Harlungs, two young men left the Breisgau, Breisach Castle and vast treasure by their late father Diether; he is a Harlung himself and renowned for loyalty; the Harlungs are cousins of Dietrich von Bern.
claims.statement_id: Dalam legenda heroik, Eckart (Eckehart, Eckewart) adalah wali para Harlung, dua pemuda yang mewarisi wilayah Breisgau, Kastel Breisach, dan harta tak terhingga dari mendiang ayah mereka Diether; ia sendiri Harlung dan termasyhur karena kesetiaannya; para Harlung adalah sepupu Dietrich von Bern.
claims.quote: In heroic legend, Eckart, also called Eckehart or Eckewart, is the guardian of the Harlungs, two young men whose late father Diether bequeathed them the Breisgau territory, Breisach Castle, and immeasurable treasure. He is a Harlung himself, and has great renown for his loyalty and faithfulness

claims.statement: In the Rabenschlacht Eckart captured Sibeche and dragged him on horseback to the gallows; he avenged his wards by killing Ermenrich with other heroes.
claims.statement_id: Dalam pertempuran Rabenschlacht, Eckart menawan Sibeche dan menyeretnya dengan kuda ke tiang gantungan; ia membalas kematian anak-anak asuhnya dengan membunuh Ermenrich bersama pahlawan lain.
claims.quote: During the Rabenschlacht battle, Eckart took Sibeche captive and dragged him away on horseback to be hung on the gallows. He also took revenge for the demise of his charges when he and other heroes slew Ermenrich.

claims.statement: The Harlungs' treasure (Harlungenhort) is said to be enchanted in the Bürglenberg near Breisach, guarded by Eckart's spirit, who warns every treasure-seeker that it is fated for the true heir; hence the saying 'Du bist der treue Eckart, du warnest jedermann'.
claims.statement_id: Harta Harlung (Harlungenhort) konon disihir dan disembunyikan di gunung Bürglenberg dekat Breisach, dijaga arwah Eckart yang memperingatkan setiap pemburu harta bahwa harta itu ditakdirkan bagi ahli waris sejati; dari sini lahir pepatah "Du bist der treue Eckart, du warnest jedermann".
claims.quote: The rich treasure of the Harlungs, the Harlungenhort, is said to be enchanted and hidden inside the mountain Bürglenberg near Breisach. This treasure is guarded by the spirit of treuer Eckart who warns every treasure seeker that this treasure is fated to fall into the hands of the true heir of the Harlungs

claims.statement: In Thuringia Eckart is tied to the Wild Hunt (wütendes Heer) led by Frau Holle over the Twelve Nights of Christmas; he goes ahead of it, telling people to step aside so they come to no harm.
claims.statement_id: Di Thüringen (Thuringia), Eckart terkait dengan Perburuan Liar (wild hunt; wütendes Heer) yang dipimpin Frau Holle pada Dua Belas Malam Natal (Twelve Nights of Christmas); ia berjalan di depannya, menyuruh orang menyingkir agar tidak celaka.
claims.quote: In Thuringia, der treue Eckart is connected with the wild hunt, locally called wütendes Heer or furious host. Leader of the wild hunt is Frau Holle ... who roams the countryside with the furious host during Christmas, namely the Zwölften, that is the Twelve Nights of Christmas. Der treue Eckart goes ahead of the wild hunt, warning the people to step out of the way so they will suffer no harm.

claims.statement: He looks like an old man with a staff; when the host stays inside the Hörselberg, Eckart sits outside the cave warning all against entering the realm of Frau Venus (the Venusberg), whence none return.
claims.statement_id: Ia berwujud lelaki tua bertongkat; saat rombongan itu tinggal di dalam gunung Hörselberg, Eckart duduk di luar gua memperingatkan semua orang agar tidak memasuki alam Frau Venus (Venusberg), tempat tiada jalan kembali.
claims.quote: His appearance is that of an old man with a staff. When the furious host doesn’t travel and stays inside Hörselberg Mountain, der treue Eckart sits outside the cave, warning everybody against entering the realm of Frau Venus from where there is no return.

claims.statement: The Getreue Eckart or Treue Eckart is a figure rooted in Germanic legend and also a subject of literature and art.
claims.statement_id: Getreuer Eckart atau Treue Eckart adalah tokoh berakar dalam dunia legenda Jermanik dan juga bahan sastra serta seni.
claims.quote: Der Getreue Eckart oder Treue Eckart (auch in den diversen Namensvarianten von „Eckart“ wie „Eckhart“, „Eckehard“ usw.) ist eine Figur mit Wurzeln in der germanischen Sagenwelt, zugleich ein Stoff der Literatur und Kunst.

claims.statement: Eckart's guarding of the Venusberg entrance and warning people off is known since at least 1453; in Denmark he warns people before entering a brothel, and a chronicle of 1566 makes him a judge at the gates of hell.
claims.statement_id: Peran Eckart menjaga pintu Venusberg dan menasihati orang agar tidak masuk dikenal setidaknya sejak 1453; di Denmark ia memperingatkan orang sebelum memasuki rumah bordil, dan kronik tahun 1566 menempatkannya sebagai hakim di gerbang neraka.
claims.quote: That der treue Eckart guards the entrance to the Venusberg, i.e. the mountain of Frau Venus, and advises people against entering is known since 1453 if not longer, giving rise to the saying mentioned above. In Denmark, he also is found warning people before entering a brothel, and a chronicle from 1566 places him as a judge at the gates of hell.

claims.statement: Eckart refilled the children's beer jugs drunk by the Wild Hunt and promised they would stay full as long as the children kept silent about what they had seen (Thüringen).
claims.statement_id: Eckart mengisi kembali kendi bir anak-anak yang diminum rombongan Perburuan Liar dan berjanji kendi itu akan selalu penuh selama mereka merahasiakan apa yang mereka lihat (Thüringen).
claims.quote: Der Getreue Eckart macht sie ihnen wieder voll und verspricht, sie würden immer voll bleiben, solange die Kinder über das Geschaute Schweigen bewahrten.

claims.statement: Jörg Wickram used Eckart in the play Der trew Eckart (1532), and Johann Wolfgang Goethe made him the hero of the ballad Der getreue Eckart (1813).
claims.statement_id: Jörg Wickram memakai Eckart dalam lakon Der trew Eckart (1532), dan Johann Wolfgang Goethe menjadikannya tokoh utama balada Der getreue Eckart (1813).
claims.quote: Jörg Wickram använde Eckart i pjäsen Der trew Eckart från 1532. Johann Wolfgang Goethe gjorde honom till huvudperson i balladen Der getreue Eckart från 1813

claims.statement: One day while Eckart was away, King Ermenrich, the Harlungs' uncle, driven by greed for their inheritance and his adviser Sibeche's slanders, seized Breisach Castle, hanged his nephews and took their property.

claims.quote: One day, when Eckart was absent, King Ermenrich, uncle of the Harlungs, driven by both greed for his nephews’ heritage and his advisor Sibeche’s slanderous, fraudulent remarks

short_description.id: Bergmönch ("biarawan gunung") adalah roh pertambangan dalam cerita rakyat Jerman, raksasa bertudung biarawan yang menghuni lubang tambang, menghukum penambang jahat dan menolong yang baik.
short_description.en: The Bergmönch ('mountain monk') is a mining spirit of German folklore, a giant in a monk's cowl who haunts the mine shafts, punishing wicked miners and helping good ones.

long_description.id: Bergmönch adalah roh gunung dalam cerita rakyat Jerman, juga dikenal sebagai Meister Hämmerling. Ia sebesar raksasa, berambut putih, bermata menyala, dan memakai jubah bertudung hitam seperti biarawan, dari mana namanya berasal; ia juga bisa berpakaian penambang, menjelma kuda berleher panjang, atau menjadi tak terlihat. Artikel bahasa Jerman menyebutnya tokoh yang sangat kontradiktif, kadang dianggap hantu seorang kepala tambang yang tak bisa berpisah dari pekerjaannya.
long_description.en: The Bergmönch is a mountain spirit of German folklore, also known as Meister Hämmerling. He is giant-sized, white-haired and fiery-eyed, wearing a black hooded cowl like a monk, which gave him his name; he may also dress as a miner, turn into a long-necked horse or become invisible. The German article calls him a deeply contradictory figure, sometimes held to be the ghost of a mine master who could not part with his work.

long_description.id: Ia tinggal di lubang dan terowongan tambang di pegunungan, sibuk terutama pada hari Jumat memindahkan bijih dari satu ember ke ember lain. Ia mudah marah dan berbahaya: napasnya beracun dan dapat membunuh dua belas orang sekaligus, dan siapa pun yang mengolok-olok kerjanya yang sia-sia akan dihukum. Ia juga dapat meruntuhkan terowongan atau menimbulkan banjir dan ledakan gas tambang.
long_description.en: He lives in the pits and galleries of mountain mines and is busiest on Fridays, shifting ore from one bucket to another. He is hot-tempered and dangerous: his poisonous breath can kill twelve people at once, and anyone who mocks his pointless labour is punished. He can also bring galleries down or cause floods and firedamp.

long_description.id: Namun ia juga bisa adil dan suka menolong, melindungi penambang yang baik dan menghukum yang jahat, seperti mandor yang kejam, serta kebiasaan bersiul, mengumpat, egois, dan malas. Ia memberi minyak lampu yang tak pernah habis selama rahasianya dijaga, menggali bijih bagi penambang kesayangannya, dan menunjukkan urat emas dan perak.
long_description.en: Yet he can also be fair and helpful, guarding good miners and punishing bad ones, such as a cruel foreman, along with whistling, cursing, selfishness and idleness. He gives lamp oil that never runs out as long as the secret is kept, digs ore for his favourite miners and shows them hidden veins of gold and silver.

who.en: A mining spirit in a monk's cowl.

role.id: Napas beracunnya membunuh dua belas orang.

famous_for.id: Memberi minyak lampu yang tak habis.
famous_for.en: Gives lamp oil that never runs out.

did_you_know.id: Minyak lampu pemberian Bergmönch konon tak pernah habis selama bertahun-tahun, asalkan penambang tak membuka rahasia asal minyak itu.
did_you_know.en: Lamp oil from the Bergmönch was said to last for years without running out, so long as the miner never revealed where it came from.

claims.quote: The Bergmönch ("mountain monk"; German: [ˈbɛʁkˌmœnç] ) is a mountain spirit from German folklore. He is also known as Meister Hämmerling ("master hammering guy").

statement.id: Bergmönch ("biarawan gunung") adalah roh gunung dari cerita rakyat Jerman (German), juga dikenal sebagai Meister Hämmerling.
statement.en: The Bergmönch ('mountain monk') is a mountain spirit of German folklore, also called Meister Hämmerling.

claims.quote: He has white hair and fiery looking eyes as large as dining plates. The mountain spirit wears a black hooded cowl as used by monks; this gave rise to his name Bergmönch. He also can be dressed like a miner. As such he is called Meister Hämmerling. Additionally, he can take the shape of a horse with long neck and terrible looking eyes, and is also able to become invisible.

statement.id: Bergmönch berambut putih, bermata menyala sebesar piring, berjubah bertudung hitam seperti biarawan; ia bisa berpakaian penambang (Meister Hämmerling), menjelma kuda berleher panjang, dan menjadi tak terlihat.
statement.en: The Bergmönch is white-haired, with fiery plate-sized eyes and a black monk's hooded cowl; he can dress as a miner (Meister Hämmerling), become a long-necked horse and turn invisible.

claims.quote: The residence of the Bergmönch are pits and mines in the mountains. There he is active as well deep in the pits as up on the surface. Especially on Fridays this mountain spirit is very busy. He fills the excavated ores from one bucket to another.

statement.id: Bergmönch tinggal di lubang dan tambang di pegunungan, aktif di kedalaman maupun permukaan, terutama sibuk pada hari Jumat (Fridays) memindahkan bijih dari satu ember ke ember lain.
statement.en: The Bergmönch dwells in mountain pits and mines, active deep down and at the surface, busiest on Fridays, moving ore from one bucket to another.

claims.quote: The mountain spirit generally is an erratic and dangerous being. His breath is poisonous, able to kill twelve people at once.

statement.id: Roh gunung ini umumnya makhluk yang tak menentu dan berbahaya; napasnya beracun dan dapat membunuh dua belas orang sekaligus.
statement.en: The mountain spirit is generally an erratic, dangerous being; his poisonous breath can kill twelve people at once.

claims.quote: The Bergmönch can also be just and helpful, guarding the good miners and punishing the evil ones. He punishes vices such as whistling and cursing, egoism, infidelity and idleness. For example, the mountain spirit killed an evil foreman of miners by crushing his head invisibly with his knees.

statement.id: Bergmönch juga bisa adil dan menolong, melindungi penambang baik dan menghukum yang jahat; ia menghukum kebiasaan bersiul, mengumpat, egois, tidak setia, dan malas, misalnya membunuh mandor jahat dengan meremukkan kepalanya secara tak terlihat.
statement.en: The Bergmönch can also be just and helpful, guarding good miners and punishing evil ones; he punishes whistling, cursing, egoism, infidelity and idleness, once killing an evil foreman by invisibly crushing his head.

claims.quote: This oil never diminishes and burns steadily even for years when the miner never reveals the secret that he got lamp oil from the Bergmönch. He also has favorite miners whose work he does, excavating ores for them.

statement.id: Minyak lampu pemberiannya tak pernah berkurang dan menyala bertahun-tahun selama penambang tak membuka rahasianya; ia juga mengerjakan pekerjaan penambang kesayangannya, menggali bijih bagi mereka.
statement.en: The oil he gives never diminishes and burns for years so long as the miner keeps the secret; he also does the work of favourite miners, digging ore for them.

claims.quote: Besonders der Bergmönch wurde zu einer ausgesprochen widersprüchlichen Figur: anstatt in der Gestalt eines Mönches erscheint er auch als Riese mit Kapuze (mit sprühenden Augen, groß wie Kutschenräder), in der Gestalt eines Steigers oder Bergmeisters (mit einem silbernen Grubenlicht) oder noch häufiger als Geschworener.

statement.id: Bergmönch menjadi tokoh yang sangat kontradiktif: selain sebagai biarawan, ia tampil sebagai raksasa bertudung dengan mata berkilat sebesar roda kereta, sebagai mandor atau kepala tambang (Bergmeister) dengan lampu tambang perak, atau sebagai pengawas tambang.
statement.en: The Bergmönch became a highly contradictory figure: besides a monk he appears as a hooded giant with sparkling eyes as big as coach wheels, as a foreman or mine master (Bergmeister) with a silver lamp, or as a mine juror.

claims.quote: Tatsächlich wird er in manchen Sagen für das Gespenst eines toten Bergmeisters gehalten, der sich nicht von seiner geliebten Arbeit trennen konnte, und nun für immer in den Stollen und Gruben umgehen muss. Noch immer ist er gefährlich, wie ein Bergteufel, und tötet mit seinem Gifthauch die Bergleute, die sich über ihn beschweren.

statement.id: Dalam sebagian legenda ia dianggap hantu kepala tambang (Bergmeister) yang tak bisa berpisah dari pekerjaannya dan kini selamanya bergentayangan di terowongan; ia tetap berbahaya, membunuh dengan napas beracun penambang yang mengeluhkannya.
statement.en: Some legends hold him to be the ghost of a dead mine master (Bergmeister) unable to leave his beloved work, now haunting the galleries forever; still dangerous, he kills complaining miners with his poisonous breath.

claims.quote: He also shows his favourite miners hidden lodes of gold and silver but the miner has to throw some of his mining tools in the offered lode or it will be closed to never being seen by human eyes again.

statement.id: Ia menunjukkan urat emas dan perak tersembunyi kepada penambang kesayangannya, tetapi penambang harus melempar sebagian alatnya ke urat itu, atau urat itu akan tertutup selamanya.
statement.en: He shows favourite miners hidden lodes of gold and silver, but the miner must throw some tools into the lode or it closes, never to be seen again.

claims.quote: Er lässt Stollen einstürzen oder verursacht Wassereinbrüche und Schlagwetter.

statement.id: Ia meruntuhkan terowongan atau menimbulkan banjir dan ledakan gas tambang.
statement.en: He makes galleries collapse or causes inrushes of water and firedamp.

claims.quote: The appearance of the Bergmönch is like a giant in size.

statement.id: Bergmönch berukuran seperti raksasa.
statement.en: The Bergmönch is giant-like in size.

summary.id: Sebesar piring.
summary.en: As large as dining plates.

summary.id: Sebesar roda kereta.
summary.en: As large as coach wheels.

long_description.en: The Bergmönch ("mountain monk"; German: [ˈbɛʁkˌmœnç]) is a mountain spirit from German folklore. He is also known as Meister Hämmerling ("master hammering guy"). The appearance of the Bergmönch is like a giant in size. He has white hair and fiery looking eyes as large as dining plates. The mountain spirit wears a black hooded cowl as used by monks; this gave rise to his name Bergmönch. He also can be dressed like a miner. As such he is called Meister Hämmerling. Additionally, he can take the shape of a horse with long neck and terrible looking eyes, and is also able to become invisible. The residence of the Bergmönch are pits and mines in the mountains. There he is active as well deep in the pits as up on the surface. Especially on Fridays this mountain spirit is very busy. He fills the excavated ores from one bucket to another. The Bergmönch should be given his head because he will violate anyone who dares to scold his futile effort. The mountain spirit generally is an erratic and dangerous being. His breath is poisonous, able to kill twelve people at once. Also, he sometimes grasps a miner and puts him down at another place with so much strength that the miner's limbs are shattered. The mountain spirit loves hoaxing and is known as a very hot-tempered person. He doesn't like being denied or joked about and will surely punish those who deny him. The Bergmönch can also be just and helpful, guarding the good miners and punishing the evil ones. He punishes vices such as whistling and cursing, egoism, infidelity and idleness. For example, the mountain spirit killed an evil foreman of miners by crushing his head invisibly with his knees. The Bergmönch sometimes gives miners whose mining lamps are in danger of going out some of the oil from his giant pit lamp. This oil never diminishes and burns steadily even for years when the miner never reveals the secret that he got lamp oil from the Bergmönch. He also has favorite miners whose work he does, excavating ores for them. This spirit is able to excavate more ores in one hour than miners are able to excavate in one week. He also shows his favourite miners hidden lodes of gold and silver but the miner has to throw some of his mining tools in the offered lode or it will be closed to never being seen by human eyes again.

short_description.id: Elder Mother adalah makhluk penjaga pohon elder dalam cerita rakyat Inggris dan Skandinavia, yang harus dimintai izin sebelum kayu elder diambil.
short_description.en: The Elder Mother is a being that guards the elder tree in English and Scandinavian folklore, whose leave must be asked before elder wood is taken.

long_description.id: Elder Mother, yang dikenal di Denmark sebagai Hyldemoer dan di Lincolnshire sebagai Old Lady atau Old Girl, adalah makhluk penjaga pohon elder dalam cerita rakyat Inggris dan Skandinavia. Hingga belum lama ini, di berbagai bagian Inggris dan Skandinavia orang mengatakan bahwa sebelum mengambil kayu elder seseorang harus meminta izin kepadanya, atau nasib sial akan menimpa si penebang.
long_description.en: The Elder Mother, called Hyldemoer in Denmark and the Old Lady or Old Girl in Lincolnshire, is a being that guards the elder tree in English and Scandinavian folklore. Until recently, people in parts of England and Scandinavia said that before taking elder wood one had to ask her permission, or misfortune would strike the woodcutter.

long_description.id: Di Denmark, Hyldemoer atau Hyldequinde ("perempuan elder") adalah roh mirip nimfa hutan atau dryad yang tinggal di pohon elder, dan konon menghantui orang yang membangun dengan kayu elder tanpa meminta izin. Ada dugaan bahwa kepercayaan ini berasal dari Skandinavia dan dibawa ke Inggris oleh bangsa Viking pada masa Danelaw.
long_description.en: Danish tradition knows her as the Hyldemoer or Hyldequinde ('elder woman'), a dryad-like spirit dwelling in the elder tree, who is said to plague anyone building with its wood without first asking leave. It has been suggested that the belief came from Scandinavia and was brought to England by the Vikings in the time of the Danelaw.

long_description.id: Dalam kisah-kisah kemudian, Elder Mother bergeser menjadi penyihir. Di Somerset seorang petani melihatnya dalam wujud pohon elder sedang memerah sapinya; tembakan peluru peraknya meleset, tetapi nenek tua di rumah melempar bara ke pohon itu hingga terbakar dan sang penyihir mati. Kisah lain menyebut penyihir pohon elder menyelamatkan Inggris dengan mengubah seorang raja dan para ksatrianya menjadi Batu Rollright, lalu ia sendiri menjadi pohon elder.
long_description.en: In later tales the Elder Mother shifts into a witch. In Somerset a farmer saw her, in the form of an elder tree, milking his cow; his silver bullet missed, but the old grandmother of the house threw burning coals at the tree so that it burned and the witch died. Another tale has the elder-tree witch saving England by turning a king and his knights into the Rollright Stones, then turning herself into an elder tree.

short_description.id: Feuermann ("manusia api") adalah hantu berapi dalam cerita rakyat Jerman, arwah pendosa yang menebus kesalahannya dan muncul di ladang pada malam hari, lebih besar daripada api pelita (will-o'-the-wisp).
short_description.en: The Feuermann ('fire man') is a fiery ghost of German folklore, the soul of a sinner atoning for its misdeeds who appears in the fields at night, larger than a will-o'-the-wisp.

long_description.id: Feuermann, juga disebut Brennender, Brünnling, Züsler, Glühender, atau Feuerputz, adalah hantu berapi dalam cerita rakyat Jerman yang dibedakan dari Irrlicht (api pelita) karena ukurannya yang besar. Wujudnya beragam: kerangka manusia yang menyala dari dalam, lelaki hitam dalam tiang api, penunggang tanpa kepala di atas kuda berapi, atau pembajak berapi; ia juga bisa berupa berkas jerami raksasa, bola api, atau roda api, dan dapat mengubah ukurannya sesuka hati.
long_description.en: The Feuermann, also called Brennender, Brünnling, Züsler, Glühender or Feuerputz, is a fiery ghost of German folklore set apart from the Irrlicht (will-o'-the-wisp) by its large size. Its forms vary: a human skeleton ablaze inside, a black man within a pillar of fire, a headless rider on a fiery horse or a fiery ploughman; it may also be a giant sheaf of straw, a fireball or a fiery wheel, and can change its size at will.

long_description.id: Ia dianggap pendosa yang masih bergentayangan di bumi untuk menebus dosa-dosanya; nyalanya adalah api penyuciannya. Sering ia seorang Grenzfrevler, orang yang dulu memindahkan batu batas dengan niat jahat dan kini harus menghantui batas itu, tetapi bisa juga koster pencuri uang kolekte, pembakar, atau pengkhianat. Ia hanya muncul pada sore atau malam hari, terutama di ladang dan batas ladang serta padang rumput berawa.
long_description.en: It is seen as a sinner still haunting the earth to atone for the sins of its life; its fire is its purgatory. Often it is a Grenzfrevler, someone who moved a boundary stone with criminal intent and must now haunt that boundary, but it may also be a sexton who stole from the collection bag, an arsonist or a traitor. It appears only in the evening or at night, mostly in fields, field borders and swampy meadows.

long_description.id: Biasanya tak berbahaya, Feuermann bahkan menerangi jalan orang pada malam hari dengan imbalan sedikit uang atau ucapan "Vergelt's Gott", yang sudah cukup untuk menebusnya. Namun ia membalas bila imbalan yang dijanjikan tidak diberikan atau bila dipermainkan: menyesatkan orang, melompat ke punggung mereka, atau membakar jerami di gerobak bahkan rumah mereka. Menyentuh tangannya berbahaya, karena akan meninggalkan cap tangan hitam yang terbakar.
long_description.en: Usually harmless, the Feuermann may even light people's way at night for a small coin or the words 'Vergelt's Gott', which is enough to redeem it. But it takes revenge if denied a promised reward or made a fool of: it leads people astray, leaps onto their backs, or sets the straw on their wagon or even their house alight. Touching its hand is dangerous, as it leaves a black, burnt handprint.

who.en: The fiery ghost of a sinner.

role.en: Lights the way for a 'Vergelt's Gott'.

did_you_know.id: Ucapan sederhana "Vergelt's Gott" ("semoga Tuhan membalasnya") konon cukup untuk menebus Feuermann yang telah menerangi jalan seseorang.
did_you_know.en: A simple 'Vergelt's Gott' ('may God reward it') was said to be enough to redeem a Feuermann that had lit someone's way.

description.id: Mengubah tingginya dari raksasa hingga kecil, dan tampil dalam berbagai wujud berapi.
description.en: Changes its height from giant to tiny and appears in many fiery forms.

description.id: Dapat naik ke udara dan melayang di atas pucuk pohon.
description.en: Can rise into the air and hover above the treetops.

description.id: "Vergelt's Gott", doa, dan misa menebus Feuermann.
description.en: 'Vergelt's Gott', prayers and masses redeem the Feuermann.

description.id: Umpatan mengusirnya.
description.en: Swearing drives it away.

claims.quote: is a fiery ghost from German folklore, which is different from the will-o'-the-wisp (German Irrlicht) owing to its size: Feuermänner are rather big, while Irrlichter are rather small.

statement.id: Feuermann ("manusia api"; juga Brennender, Brünnling, Züsler, Glühender, glühende Männer) adalah hantu berapi dari cerita rakyat Jerman (German) yang berbeda dari will-o'-the-wisp (Irrlicht) karena ukurannya: Feuermänner agak besar, Irrlichter agak kecil.
statement.en: The Feuermann ('fire man'; also Brennender, Brünnling, Züsler, Glühender, glühende Männer) is a fiery ghost of German folklore, unlike the will-o'-the-wisp (Irrlicht) in size: Feuermänner are big, Irrlichter small.

claims.quote: Some are described as rather humanoid, such as a human skeleton whose insides are blazing with fire, or as a leaden manikin wearing a leaden mantle blazing with fire underneath. Another description is of a black man inside a tall, wide pillar of fire, or a Feuermann who is half black, half fiery. It is able to change its height at will, varying from gigantic to diminutive.

statement.id: Sebagian digambarkan mirip manusia, seperti kerangka yang menyala dari dalam atau lelaki kecil bermantel timah dengan api di bawahnya; ada pula lelaki hitam di dalam tiang api; ia dapat mengubah tingginya sesuka hati dari raksasa hingga kecil.
statement.en: Some are humanlike, such as a skeleton blazing inside or a leaden manikin with fire under its mantle; others a black man in a pillar of fire; it can change its height at will from gigantic to tiny.

claims.quote: Alternatively, the Feuermann also appears more or less shapeless like a (sometimes gigantic) sheaf or bundle of straw, a big floating light, a fiery ball, a pyramid, a snake, or a fiery wheel. The Feuermann is very quick and able to rise in the air so that it hovers above the treetops.

long_description.en: The Feuermann (fire man; German: [ˈfɔɪ̯ɐˌman]; pl. Feuermänner), also Brennender, Brünnling, Brünnlinger, Brünnlig (all: burning one), brünnigs Mannli (burning manikin), Züsler (sg., pl.; flickering one or arsonist), and Glühender (glowing one), is a fiery ghost from German folklore, which is different from the will-o'-the-wisp (German Irrlicht) owing to its size: Feuermänner are rather big, while Irrlichter are rather small. An often recurring term for Feuermänner is glühende Männer (pl.; glowing men; die glühenden Männer; in dialect gloinige Männer, glöhnege Männer, glöänige Männer or jlönige Männer).

short_description.id: Vittra adalah sejenis wight dari Swedia utara, orang tak kasatmata yang hidup sejajar dengan manusia, beternak sapi atau rusa kutub, dan hanya menunjukkan sifat gaibnya bila ternaknya diperlakukan buruk.
short_description.en: The vittra is a kind of wight from northern Sweden, an invisible folk living alongside humans and herding cattle or reindeer, who only reveal their supernatural nature if their livestock are mistreated.

long_description.id: Vittra (jamak vittror) adalah sejenis wight, makhluk gaib, dari Swedia utara. Menurut artikel bahasa Swedia, vittra atau vitter adalah bentuk sampingan dari vätte dan merujuk pada bangsa mitis dalam kepercayaan budaya padang penggembalaan musim panas (fäbod) di Nordik utara, atau makhluk tak kasatmata dan bawah tanah yang lebih sering perempuan, sebanding dengan skogsrå atau peri. Batas selatan kepercayaan ini kira-kira melintasi Hälsingland dan Dalarna, dan juga dikenal di Norwegia dan Finlandia.
long_description.en: The vittra (plural vittror) is a kind of wight, a supernatural being, from northern Sweden. According to the Swedish article, vittra or vitter is a side form of vätte and refers to a mythical people in the folk belief of the northern Nordic summer-pasture (fäbod) culture, or to an invisible, underground, mostly female being comparable to the skogsrå or elves. The southern limit of the belief runs roughly through Hälsingland and Dalarna, and it is also known in Norway and Finland.

long_description.id: Vittra dikaitkan dengan penggembalaan sapi atau rusa kutub; mereka dipercaya hidup seperti biasa di antara manusia dan hanya menampakkan sifat gaib bila ternak mereka diperlakukan buruk. Mereka tampak, hidup, dan berpakaian seperti manusia, dan berbeda dari banyak makhluk lain, mereka bisa mati. Mereka tinggal di padang penggembalaan pada musim dingin ketika manusia tidak ada, memelihara sapi sendiri yang disebut vitterkor, dan memiliki jalur sendiri, vitterstråk; celakalah orang yang membangun rumah tepat di atas jalur itu, sebab vittra akan melintasi rumahnya bersama ternaknya.
long_description.en: The vittra are associated with herding cattle or reindeer; they were believed to live ordinarily among humans and to reveal their supernatural nature only if their livestock were mistreated. They look, live and dress like people and, unlike many other beings, are mortal. They stay on the summer pastures in winter when people are away, keep their own cows called vitterkor, and have their own paths, vitterstråk; woe to anyone who builds a house right on such a path, for the vittra will drive their cattle straight through it.

long_description.id: Seperti hulder dan skogsrå, vittra juga dikaitkan dengan kerinduan dan hasrat: ia tampil sebagai wight perempuan cantik yang menggoda lelaki di hutan. Kata vittra berkerabat dengan vätte, dari Nordik Kuno vættr, yang berarti "makhluk (gaib)".
long_description.en: Like the hulder and the skogsrå, the vittra also stands for longing and desire: she takes the form of a lovely female wight who lures men among the trees. The word vittra is related to vätte, from Old Norse vættr, meaning '(supernatural) being'.

literal_meaning.id: berkerabat dengan vätte, dari Nordik Kuno vættr, "makhluk (gaib)"
literal_meaning.en: related to vätte, from Old Norse vættr, '(supernatural) being'

statement.en: The vittra stay on the summer pasture (fäbodvallen) in winter when people are absent, and keep their own cattle called vitterkor, considered especially enchanted.

claims.quote: Vittras vägar kallas för vitterstråk, och på många platser finns det kartor över dessa från förr. Illa går det för den som bygger sitt hus rakt på ett vitterstråk, då går vittra med sin boskap tvärs genom huset.

statement.id: Jalur vittra disebut vitterstråk, dan di banyak tempat ada peta lamanya; celakalah yang membangun rumah tepat di atas vitterstråk, sebab vittra akan berjalan dengan ternaknya menembus rumah itu.
statement.en: The vittra's paths are called vitterstråk, and many places have old maps of them; woe to whoever builds a house right on a vitterstråk, for the vittra will walk their cattle straight through it.

claims.quote: A vittra (plural: vittror) is a type of wight (a term for supernatural beings) from northern Sweden. claims.statement: Like the hulder and skogsrå, the vittra is linked with longing and desire, appearing as a beautiful female wight who seduces men in the forest.

claims.statement: Vittra or vitter is a side form of vätte and denotes a mythical people in the folk belief of northern Nordic fäbod culture, or an invisible or underground, rather female supernatural being of Norrland belief, comparable to the skogsrå or elves (älvor).
claims.statement_id: Vittra atau vitter adalah bentuk sampingan dari vätte dan merujuk bangsa mitis dalam kepercayaan budaya fäbod Nordik utara, atau makhluk gaib tak kasatmata atau bawah tanah yang lebih sering perempuan dalam kepercayaan Norrland, sebanding dengan skogsrå atau peri (älvor).
claims.quote: Vittra eller vitter är en sidoform till vätte (vätter) och avser ett mytiskt folk inom den norra nordiska fäbodkulturens folktro, ibland särskilt som vitterfolk, eller ett övernaturligt osynligt eller underjordiskt snarare kvinnligt väsen i norrländsk folktro, jämförbart med skogsrå eller älvor

claims.statement: The southern limit of vittra belief runs roughly through Hälsingland and Dalarna, and it exists in Norway (Norge) and Finland too; vittra legends recall the Norwegian huldrefolk and the Gutnish tales of di sma undar jordi.

claims.quote: Sydgränsen för vittertron går ungefär genom Hälsingland och Dalarna, och finns även i Norge och Finland. Sägnerna om vittra påminner om de i Norge förekommande om huldrefolket, och gutniska berättelser om di sma undar jordi.

short_description.id: Weiße Frauen ("Perempuan Putih") adalah roh mirip elf dalam cerita rakyat Jerman, makhluk cantik dan tersihir yang muncul di siang hari, menjaga harta atau menghantui kastel.
short_description.en: The Weiße Frauen ("White Women") are elf-like spirits of German folklore, beautiful enchanted beings who appear at noon and guard treasure or haunt castles.

long_description.id: Dalam cerita rakyat Jerman, Weiße Frauen ("Perempuan Putih") adalah roh mirip elf yang mungkin berasal dari paganisme Jermanik, dalam bentuk legenda elf cahaya (Ljósálfar). Mereka digambarkan sebagai makhluk cantik dan tersihir yang muncul pada tengah hari dan terlihat duduk di bawah sinar matahari sambil menyisir rambut atau mandi di sungai kecil. Mereka mungkin menjaga harta atau menghantui kastel, dan memohon manusia mematahkan sihir mereka, tetapi upaya itu selalu gagal. Mitologi ini setidaknya berasal dari Abad Pertengahan.
long_description.en: In German folklore, the Weiße Frauen ("White Women") are elf-like spirits, perhaps rooted in Germanic paganism through tales of the light elves (Ljósálfar). They are described as beautiful, enchanted beings who appear at noon and may be spotted in the sun combing their hair, or bathing in a stream. They may guard treasure or haunt castles, and they beg mortals to break their spell, but this always fails. The mythology goes back at least to the Middle Ages.

long_description.id: Jacob Grimm menduga kaitan mereka dengan warna putih dan sinar matahari berasal dari elf cahaya Ljósálfar yang tinggal di Álfheim di bawah dewa Freyr; mereka juga mungkin mewakili kepercayaan lama tentang roh leluhur atau dewi kuno seperti Holda, Berhta, dan Ostara. Menurut Grimm, sihir yang menimpa mereka mungkin melambangkan larangan yang dijatuhkan Kekristenan atas dewa-dewa kepercayaan lama.
long_description.en: Jacob Grimm thought their link with white and sunlight came from the light elves (Ljósálfar) who lived in Álfheim under the god Freyr; they may also reflect older beliefs in ancestral spirits or ancient goddesses such as Holda, Berhta and Ostara. According to Grimm, the enchantment they suffer may symbolize the ban Christianity laid on the gods of the older faith.

long_description.id: Mereka memiliki padanan di negeri tetangga: di Belanda disebut Witte Wieven, di Prancis Dames Blanches, dan padanan dalam bahasa Jerman rendah (Low German) adalah Witte Wiwer; di wilayah Alpen Austria dan Jerman Selatan mereka disebut Salige Frauen. Di Belanda, witte wieven adalah perempuan dalam legenda yang kadang baik, kadang jahat, yang sering dikaitkan dengan penyihir atau hantu dan diyakini tinggal di bukit kubur dan hunebed.
long_description.en: They have counterparts in neighbouring lands: in the Netherlands the Witte Wieven, in France the Dames Blanches, and their Low German equivalent is the Witte Wiwer; in the Alpine parts of Austria and the south of Germany they go by Salige Frauen. In the Netherlands the witte wieven are women of legend, sometimes kind and sometimes wicked, often linked with witches or ghosts and believed to live in burial mounds and hunebeds.

long_description.en: In German folklore, the Weiße Frauen (German: [ˈvaɪsə ˈfʁaʊən], meaning White Women) are elf-like spirits which may derive from Germanic paganism in the form of legends of light elves (Old Norse: Ljósálfar). The Dutch Witte Wieven are traceable at least as far back as the 7th century, and their mistranslation as White Women instead of the original Wise Women can be explained by the Dutch word wit also meaning white. They are described as beautiful and enchanted creatures who appear at noon and can be seen sitting in the sunshine brushing their hair or bathing in a brook. They may be guarding treasure or haunting castles. They entreat mortals to break their spell, but this is always unsuccessful. The mythology dates back at least to the Middle Ages and was known in the present-day area of Germany.

short_description.id: Ysätters-Kajsa (Ysätter-Kaisa) adalah troll atau penyihir angin dari Närke yang diabadikan Lagerlöf, makhluk usil yang menari di tengah angin puyuh.
short_description.en: Ysätters-Kajsa (Ysätter-Kaisa) is a wind troll or witch of Närke immortalised by Lagerlöf, a mischievous being who dances in the whirlwind.

long_description.id: Ysätters-Kajsa (Ysätter-Kaisa) adalah troll atau penyihir angin dari provinsi Närke yang menurut Lagerlöf tak ada bandingannya di tempat lain. Lagerlöf menampilkannya dalam novel tentang perjalanan Nils Holgersson. Ia dinamai Kaisa karena penyihir angin biasa disebut demikian, dan julukan Ysätter berasal dari rawa Ysätter di paroki Asker; ia tampaknya tinggal di Asker, tetapi bisa muncul di mana saja di Närke. Lagerlöf menutup kisahnya dengan mengatakan bahwa orang kini menganggapnya sudah mati seperti troll lain, tetapi hal itu hampir mustahil dipercaya.
long_description.en: Ysätters-Kajsa (Ysätter-Kaisa) is a wind troll or witch of the province of Närke who, according to Lagerlöf, had no equal elsewhere. Lagerlöf featured her in her novel about the journey of Nils Holgersson. She was called Kaisa because wind witches bear that name, and her byname came from Ysätter swamp in Asker parish; she seemed to live at Asker but could turn up anywhere in Närke. Lagerlöf ends by saying people now think her dead like all other trolls, but that this is almost impossible to believe.

long_description.id: Menurut Lagerlöf, ia bukan troll yang muram melainkan riang dan suka bermain, dan paling senang bila angin badai; ia berdiri di tengah angin puyuh di dataran Närke, rambut panjangnya berputar di antara awan dan roknya menyeret seperti badai debu. Di musim dingin ia menimbulkan badai salju, di musim panas ia mendatangkan hujan saat panen jerami, dan ia meniup tungku arang yang tak dijaga. Namun ia tak jahat sepenuhnya: ia paling keras terhadap orang yang suka bertengkar dan jahat, sering melindungi orang jujur dan anak-anak miskin, dan konon pernah memadamkan kebakaran gereja Asker.
long_description.en: In Lagerlöf's telling she was not a gloomy troll but a merry, playful one who loved a real gale; she stood at the heart of the whirlwinds on the Närke plain, her long hair whirling among the clouds and her skirt trailing like a dust storm. In winter she raised snowstorms, in summer she sent rain on the hay harvest, and she fanned unguarded charcoal kilns. Yet she was not wicked to the bone: she was hardest on the quarrelsome and wicked, often protected honest folk and poor children, and is said once to have put out a fire at the church of Asker.

did_you_know.id: Konon Ysätters-Kajsa pernah memadamkan kebakaran gereja Asker dengan bersarang di tengah asap dan api di atapnya.
did_you_know.en: Ysätters-Kajsa is said to have once put out a fire at Asker church by nestling among the smoke and flames on its roof.

long_description.en: Ysätters-Kajsa was a wind-troll that people in the Swedish province of Närke used to believe in; probably the only one of her kind in Scandinavia. The Swedish writer Selma Lagerlöf immortalised Ysätters-Kajsa in the first part of Chapter 24 of her famous novel The Wonderful Adventures of Nils (1906–1907). She wrote that in the Swedish province of Närke, in the old days, there lived a troll named Ysätters-Kajsa. She was named Kajsa because wind-trolls used to be called by that name. Her cognomen Ysätter came from the swamp Ysätter (59°08′N 15°33′E) in Asker parish where she was born. She appeared to have lived in Asker parish, but she played jokes on people all over Närke and was unique to that region.

Normal human body, two arms raised to direct wind, two legs, human ears. Strong joyful mischievous yet protective presence, not gloomy evil troll. Full figure clear against curling cloud and reeds. short_description.id: Vamana (Wamana) adalah awatara kelima Dewa Wisnu dalam agama Hindu, brahmana kerdil yang merebut kembali tiga dunia dari raja daitya Mahabali dengan tiga langkah.
short_description.en: Vamana is the fifth avatar of the Hindu god Vishnu, a dwarf brahmin who won back the three worlds from the daitya king Mahabali with three steps.

long_description.id: Vamana (Sanskerta वामन, "kerdil"), juga dikenal sebagai Trivikrama ("tiga langkah"), Urukrama, dan Upendra, adalah awatara dewa Hindu Wisnu (Vishnu). Ia awatara kelima Wisnu dan Dashavatara pertama pada Treta Yuga, sesudah Narasimha. Pertama disebut dalam Weda, Vamana paling sering dikaitkan dalam epos dan Purana Hindu dengan kisah merebut kembali tiga dunia (Trailokya) dari raja daitya Mahabali dengan tiga langkah, untuk memulihkan tatanan kosmos dan mendorong Mahabali ke dunia bawah. Ia yang termuda di antara para aditya, putra Aditi dan resi Kashyapa.
long_description.en: Vamana (Sanskrit वामन, "dwarf"), also called Trivikrama ("three steps"), Urukrama and Upendra, is an avatar of the Hindu god Vishnu. Coming after Narasimha, he is the fifth of Vishnu's avatars and the first Dashavatara of the Treta Yuga. Already named in the Vedas, Vamana is best known in the Hindu epics and Puranas to the tale of reclaiming the three worlds (Trailokya) from the daitya king Mahabali with three steps, restoring the cosmic order and pushing Mahabali into the netherworld. He is the youngest of the adityas, sons of Aditi and the sage Kashyapa.

long_description.id: Menurut artikel id, Wamana dilukiskan sebagai brahmana berraga anak kecil yang membawa kamandalu dan payung. Kisahnya dimuat dalam Bhagawatapurana, Brahmapurana, Padmapurana, Wamanapurana, dan Mahapurana lain: Raja Bali mengundang semua brahmana untuk diberi hadiah, dan meski dinasihati Sukracarya, ia mengabulkan permintaan brahmana kecil itu atas tanah seluas tiga langkah. Brahmana itu lalu membesar; langkah pertamanya menginjak swarga, langkah kedua bumi, dan untuk langkah ketiga Bali menyerahkan kepalanya. Terkesan oleh kedermawanannya, Wamana memberinya gelar Mahabali dan berjanji ia kelak menjadi Indra pada Manwantara berikutnya.
long_description.en: According to the id article, Wamana is pictured as a brahmin in a child's body carrying a kamandalu and an umbrella. His story is in the Bhagawatapurana, Brahmapurana, Padmapurana, Wamanapurana and other Mahapuranas: King Bali invited all brahmins to receive gifts, and despite Sukracarya's warning he granted the little brahmin's request for land three strides wide. The brahmin then grew; his first stride covered heaven (swarga), the second the earth, and for the third Bali offered his head. Impressed by his generosity, Wamana gave him the title Mahabali and promised he would become Indra in the next Manwantara.

long_description.id: Kisah Wamana dan Raja Bali diperingati setiap tahun dalam perayaan Onam di Kerala, India, tempat juga terdapat kuil khusus untuknya; kuil Wamana lain antara lain ada di Kanchipuram, dekat kuil Kamakshi.
long_description.en: The story of Wamana and King Bali is commemorated every year at the Onam festival in Kerala, India, where there is also a temple devoted to him; other Wamana temples include one in Kanchipuram near the Kamakshi temple.

long_description.id: Wamana (Dewanagari: वामन ; ,IAST: Vāmana, वामन ) adalah salah satu awatara (penjelmaan) Dewa Wisnu dalam agama Hindu, yang berwujud pendeta kerdil, lahir pada masa Tretayuga sebagai putra Dewi Aditi dan Resi Kasyapa. Wamana dilukiskan sebagai brahmana dengan raga anak kecil yang membawa kamandalu dan payung. Wamana kadang-kadang dikenal juga dengan sebutan Upendra (Dewanagari: उपेन्द्र; ,IAST: Upendra, उपेन्द्र) yang berarti "adik Indra". Dia memiliki julukan Triwikrama (Dewanagari: त्रिविक्रम; ,IAST: Trivikrama,; arti: "tiga langkah") karena langkah kakinya dapat memijak bumi, patala (dunia bawah), dan swarga (kahyangan) sekaligus. Menurut keyakinan Hindu, Wisnu turun ke dunia pada zaman Tretayuga untuk menegakkan kebenaran dan memberi pelajaran kepada Raja Bali (Mahabali), seorang asura, cucu dari Prahlada. Dalam sastra Hindu dikisahkan bahwa Raja Bali (Mahabali) telah merebut swarga dari kekuasaan Dewa Indra sehingga itu Wisnu selaku dewa pemelihara semesta turun tangan dan menjelma ke dunia, memberi hukuman pada Raja Bali.
long_description.en: Vamana (Sanskrit: वामन, lit. 'Dwarf', IAST: Vāmana), also known as Trivikrama (lit. 'three steps'), Urukrama (lit. 'far-stepping'), Upendra (lit. 'Indra’s younger brother/Superior to Indra'), Dadhivamana (Sanskrit: दधिवामन, lit. 'milk-dwarf', IAST: Dadhivāmana), Ulagalanthan (lit. 'the one who measured the world) and Balibandhana (lit. 'binder or killer of Bali'), is an avatar of the Hindu deity Vishnu. He is the fifth avatar of Vishnu and the first Dashavatara in the Treta Yuga, after Narasimha. First mentioned in the Vedas, Vamana is most commonly associated in the Hindu epics and Puranas with the story of taking back the three worlds (collectively referred to as the Trailokya) from the daitya-king Mahabali by taking three steps to restore the cosmic order and push Mahabali into the netherworld. He is the youngest among the adityas, the sons of Aditi and the sage Kashyapa.

short_description.id: Vamana (Wamana) adalah awatara kelima Dewa Wisnu dalam agama Hindu, brahmana kerdil yang merebut kembali tiga dunia dari raja daitya Mahabali dengan tiga langkah.
short_description.en: Vamana is the fifth avatar of the Hindu god Vishnu, a dwarf brahmin who won back the three worlds from the daitya king Mahabali with three steps.

long_description.id: Vamana (Sanskerta वामन, "kerdil"), juga dikenal sebagai Trivikrama ("tiga langkah"), Urukrama, dan Upendra, adalah awatara dewa Hindu Wisnu (Vishnu). Ia awatara kelima Wisnu dan Dashavatara pertama pada Treta Yuga, sesudah Narasimha. Pertama disebut dalam Weda, Vamana paling sering dikaitkan dalam epos dan Purana Hindu dengan kisah merebut kembali tiga dunia (Trailokya) dari raja daitya Mahabali dengan tiga langkah, untuk memulihkan tatanan kosmos dan mendorong Mahabali ke dunia bawah. Ia yang termuda di antara para aditya, putra Aditi dan resi Kashyapa.
long_description.en: Vamana (Sanskrit वामन, "dwarf"), also called Trivikrama ("three steps"), Urukrama and Upendra, is an avatar of the Hindu god Vishnu. Coming after Narasimha, he is the fifth of Vishnu's avatars and the first Dashavatara of the Treta Yuga. Already named in the Vedas, Vamana is best known in the Hindu epics and Puranas to the tale of reclaiming the three worlds (Trailokya) from the daitya king Mahabali with three steps, restoring the cosmic order and pushing Mahabali into the netherworld. He is the youngest of the adityas, sons of Aditi and the sage Kashyapa.

long_description.id: Menurut artikel id, Wamana dilukiskan sebagai brahmana berraga anak kecil yang membawa kamandalu dan payung. Kisahnya dimuat dalam Bhagawatapurana, Brahmapurana, Padmapurana, Wamanapurana, dan Mahapurana lain: Raja Bali mengundang semua brahmana untuk diberi hadiah, dan meski dinasihati Sukracarya, ia mengabulkan permintaan brahmana kecil itu atas tanah seluas tiga langkah. Brahmana itu lalu membesar; langkah pertamanya menginjak swarga, langkah kedua bumi, dan untuk langkah ketiga Bali menyerahkan kepalanya. Terkesan oleh kedermawanannya, Wamana memberinya gelar Mahabali dan berjanji ia kelak menjadi Indra pada Manwantara berikutnya.
long_description.en: According to the id article, Wamana is pictured as a brahmin in a child's body carrying a kamandalu and an umbrella. His story is in the Bhagawatapurana, Brahmapurana, Padmapurana, Wamanapurana and other Mahapuranas: King Bali invited all brahmins to receive gifts, and despite Sukracarya's warning he granted the little brahmin's request for land three strides wide. The brahmin then grew; his first stride covered heaven (swarga), the second the earth, and for the third Bali offered his head. Impressed by his generosity, Wamana gave him the title Mahabali and promised he would become Indra in the next Manwantara.

long_description.id: Kisah Wamana dan Raja Bali diperingati setiap tahun dalam perayaan Onam di Kerala, India, tempat juga terdapat kuil khusus untuknya; kuil Wamana lain antara lain ada di Kanchipuram, dekat kuil Kamakshi.
long_description.en: The story of Wamana and King Bali is commemorated every year at the Onam festival in Kerala, India, where there is also a temple devoted to him; other Wamana temples include one in Kanchipuram near the Kamakshi temple.

long_description.id: Wamana (Dewanagari: वामन ; ,IAST: Vāmana, वामन ) adalah salah satu awatara (penjelmaan) Dewa Wisnu dalam agama Hindu, yang berwujud pendeta kerdil, lahir pada masa Tretayuga sebagai putra Dewi Aditi dan Resi Kasyapa. Wamana dilukiskan sebagai brahmana dengan raga anak kecil yang membawa kamandalu dan payung. Wamana kadang-kadang dikenal juga dengan sebutan Upendra (Dewanagari: उपेन्द्र; ,IAST: Upendra, उपेन्द्र) yang berarti "adik Indra". Dia memiliki julukan Triwikrama (Dewanagari: त्रिविक्रम; ,IAST: Trivikrama,; arti: "tiga langkah") karena langkah kakinya dapat memijak bumi, patala (dunia bawah), dan swarga (kahyangan) sekaligus. Menurut keyakinan Hindu, Wisnu turun ke dunia pada zaman Tretayuga untuk menegakkan kebenaran dan memberi pelajaran kepada Raja Bali (Mahabali), seorang asura, cucu dari Prahlada. Dalam sastra Hindu dikisahkan bahwa Raja Bali (Mahabali) telah merebut swarga dari kekuasaan Dewa Indra sehingga itu Wisnu selaku dewa pemelihara semesta turun tangan dan menjelma ke dunia, memberi hukuman pada Raja Bali.
long_description.en: Vamana (Sanskrit: वामन, lit. 'Dwarf', IAST: Vāmana), also known as Trivikrama (lit. 'three steps'), Urukrama (lit. 'far-stepping'), Upendra (lit. 'Indra’s younger brother/Superior to Indra'), Dadhivamana (Sanskrit: दधिवामन, lit. 'milk-dwarf', IAST: Dadhivāmana), Ulagalanthan (lit. 'the one who measured the world) and Balibandhana (lit. 'binder or killer of Bali'), is an avatar of the Hindu deity Vishnu. He is the fifth avatar of Vishnu and the first Dashavatara in the Treta Yuga, after Narasimha. First mentioned in the Vedas, Vamana is most commonly associated in the Hindu epics and Puranas with the story of taking back the three worlds (collectively referred to as the Trailokya) from the daitya-king Mahabali by taking three steps to restore the cosmic order and push Mahabali into the netherworld. He is the youngest among the adityas, the sons of Aditi and the sage Kashyapa.

short_description.id: Fionn mac Cumhaill (Finn McCool) adalah pahlawan mitologi Irlandia dan cerita rakyat Skotlandia serta Man, pemimpin kelompok pemburu-pejuang Fianna, juga peramal dan penyair.
short_description.en: Fionn mac Cumhaill (Finn McCool) is a hero of Irish mythology and later Scottish and Manx folklore, leader of the Fianna hunter-warrior bands, and also a seer and poet.

long_description.id: Fionn mac Cumhaill (juga Finn mac Cumhaill, Finn McCool, atau MacCool) adalah pahlawan dalam mitologi Irlandia (Irish mythology) serta cerita rakyat Skotlandia dan Man kemudian. Ia pemimpin kelompok pemburu-pejuang muda Fianna, sekaligus peramal dan penyair, dan konon memiliki ibu jari ajaib yang memberinya kebijaksanaan besar. Ia sering digambarkan berburu bersama anjingnya Bran dan Sceólang serta bertarung dengan tombak dan pedang. Kisah-kisahnya membentuk Siklus Fianna (Fenian Cycle), sebagian besar dituturkan oleh putranya, penyair Oisín.
long_description.en: Fionn mac Cumhaill (also Finn mac Cumhaill, Finn McCool or MacCool) is a hero of Irish mythology and of later Scottish and Manx folklore. He leads the Fianna, bands of young roving hunter-warriors, and is also a seer and poet, said to have a magic thumb that grants him great wisdom. He is often shown hunting with his hounds Bran and Sceólang and fighting with spear and sword. His tales make up the Fenian Cycle, much of it told by his son, the poet Oisín.

long_description.id: Dalam bahasa Irlandia Kuno finn berarti "putih, terang, elok". Fionn adalah putra anumerta Cumhall, pemimpin Fianna, dan Muirne; Cumhall dibunuh Goll mac Morna dalam Battle of Cnucha setelah melarikan Muirne. Menurut artikel de, Fionn adalah pahlawan Irlandia dari epos abad pertengahan dan tokoh utama Siklus Finn; ia memiliki "tangan penyembuh" sehingga siapa pun yang diberinya air akan sembuh, belajar ilmu bertarung dari bibinya, dan menerima pedang Mac an Luinn dari ibunya. Dalam kisah-kisah kemudian, seperti Diarmuid und Gráinne, menjelang akhir hidupnya ia digambarkan iri dan pendendam.
long_description.en: In Old Irish finn means "white, bright, fair". Fionn was the posthumous son of Cumhall, leader of the Fianna, and Muirne; Cumhall was killed by Goll mac Morna at the Battle of Cnucha after carrying Muirne off. According to the de article, Fionn is an Irish hero of medieval epic and the namesake of the Finn Cycle; he has "healing hands", so that anyone he gives water to recovers, learns fighting arts from his aunt, and receives the sword Mac an Luinn from his mother. In later tales such as Diarmuid und Gráinne he is shown, near the end of his life, as envious and vengeful.

long_description.en: Fionn mac Cumhaill (alternatively spelled Finn mac Cumhaill), sometimes anglicised Finn McCool or MacCool, is a hero in Irish mythology, as well as in later Scottish and Manx folklore. He is the leader of the Fianna bands of young roving hunter-warriors, as well as being a seer and poet. He is said to have a magic thumb that bestows him with great wisdom. He is often depicted hunting with his hounds Bran and Sceólang, and fighting with his spear and sword. The tales of Fionn and his fiann form the Fianna Cycle or Fenian Cycle (an Fhiannaíocht), much of it narrated by Fionn's son, the poet Oisín; it has become the most important part of the c. 12th-century narrative Acallam na Senórach, and has also been told in other ancient Irish texts.

long_description.id: Imp adalah makhluk mitologi Eropa (European) yang mirip peri atau iblis, sering digambarkan dalam cerita rakyat dan takhayul. Imp biasanya digambarkan merepotkan dan usil, bukan ancaman serius, dan dianggap makhluk rendahan; para pengiring Iblis kadang disebut imp. Mereka biasanya lincah dan bertubuh kecil. Berbeda dengan cerita rakyat Kristen, iblis dalam legenda Jermanik tidak selalu jahat, dan imp sering lebih usil daripada berbahaya; dalam sebagian kepercayaan mereka pelayan para dewa.
long_description.en: Folklore and superstition often speak of the imp, a being somewhere between a fairy and a demon. Imps are usually troublesome and mischievous rather than seriously dangerous, and are counted as lesser beings; the devil's attendants are sometimes called imps. They are usually lively and small. Unlike in Christian folklore, demons in Germanic legend were not always evil, and imps were often mischievous rather than harmful; in some religions they served the gods.

long_description.id: Kata benda impa dalam bahasa Inggris Kuno berarti tunas muda tanaman, kemudian keturunan keluarga bangsawan atau anak; sejak abad ke-16 dipakai dalam ungkapan seperti "imp of hell" dan "imp of the devil", dan pada abad ke-17 berarti iblis kecil, familiar seorang penyihir. Legenda Lincolnshire dari abad ke-14 mengisahkan Iblis yang kesal dengan selesainya katedral Lincoln datang bersama dua imp yang merusak gedung itu; seorang malaikat menyuruh mereka berhenti, dan imp yang melempar batu kepadanya seketika membatu. Lincoln Imp kini menjadi simbol kota itu.
long_description.en: The Old English noun impa meant a young shoot of a plant, later the scion of a noble house or a child; from the 16th century it appears in phrases like "imp of hell" and "imp of the devil", and by the 17th century it meant a small demon, a witch's familiar. A 14th-century Lincolnshire legend tells how the devil, vexed at the finished Lincoln Cathedral, came with two imps who wrecked the building; an angel ordered them to stop, and the imp that threw a stone at it was turned to stone on the spot. The Lincoln Imp is now a symbol of the city.

Berbeda dengan cerita rakyat Kristen, makhluk-makhluk yang digolongkan sebagai iblis dalam legenda Jermanik tidak selalu jahat. Sosok imp sering kali lebih bersifat usil daripada jahat atau berbahaya. Dalam beberapa kepercayaan, mereka merupakan pelayan para dewa.

short_description.id: Wight adalah kata Jermanik untuk makhluk atau benda; dalam bahasa Inggris Pertengahan kemudian berkembang menjadi sebutan bagi makhluk gaib, dan dalam fantasi modern sering berarti mayat hidup.
short_description.en: A wight is a Germanic word for a being or thing; in later English it came to mean supernatural beings, and in modern fantasy it often means an undead.

long_description.id: Wight berarti makhluk atau benda; makna umum ini dimiliki kata-kata serumpunnya dalam bahasa Jermanik (Germanic) lain, tetapi pemakaiannya sangat beragam menurut zaman dan daerah. Dalam bahasa Inggris Kuno kata itu dapat merujuk pada apa saja yang ada, lalu menjadi lebih khusus dalam bahasa Inggris Pertengahan, dan dalam fantasi modern wight sering secara khusus berarti mayat hidup. Wight berasal dari wiht (Old English), sekerabat dengan Wicht dalam bahasa Jerman dan vættr dalam bahasa Nordik Kuno, leluhur vätte Swedia dan vætte Denmark.
long_description.en: A wight is a being or thing; this general meaning is shared by its cognates in other Germanic languages, though their use varies greatly by time and place. In Old English it could refer to anything that exists, became more specific in Middle English, and in modern fantasy wights are often specifically undead. The word comes from Old English wiht, cognate with German Wicht and Old Norse vættr, the ancestor of Swedish vätte and Danish vætte.

long_description.id: Dalam Old English, wiht dipakai untuk makhluk seperti kurcaci dalam mantra XCIIIB serta eoten Grendel dan naga dalam Beowulf, dan sejak Lindisfarne Gospels abad ke-8 mulai bermakna makhluk gaib atau tak duniawi. Menurut artikel de, Wichtel, bentuk kecil dari Wicht, adalah makhluk dalam dongeng dan legenda yang mirip manusia tetapi jauh lebih kecil, hidup berkelompok di bawah tanah, di gua, atau di sudut rumah, umumnya ramah dan diam-diam membantu pekerjaan sehari-hari, dan kadang menukar bayi manusia dengan bayi mereka.
long_description.en: Old English writers applied wiht to the dwarf in the XCIIIB charm and, in Beowulf, to both Grendel and the dragon, and from the 8th-century Lindisfarne Gospels it began to mean supernatural or unearthly beings. According to the de article, the Wichtel, a diminutive of Wicht, is a being of tales and legends that looks human but is much smaller, lives in groups underground, in caves or in hidden corners of houses, is usually friendly and helps unasked with daily work, and sometimes swaps a human baby for its own.

short_description.id: Nibelung (Old Norse: Niflungr) adalah nama pribadi atau nama klan dengan berbagai makna dalam legenda kepahlawanan Jermanik, dan juga bangsa kurcaci pemilik harta Nibelung.
short_description.en: Nibelung (Old Norse Niflungr) is a personal or clan name with several meanings in Germanic heroic legend, and also a race of dwarfs owning the Nibelung hoard.

long_description.id: Istilah Nibelung (Jerman) atau Niflungr (Old Norse) adalah nama pribadi atau nama klan dengan beberapa pemakaian yang saling bersaing dan bertentangan dalam legenda kepahlawanan Jermanik (Germanic). Asal katanya tidak jelas, tetapi sering dikaitkan dengan akar kata Jerman Nebel ("kabut"). Istilah ini memberi nama pada epos Middle High German Nibelungenlied. Pemakaian yang paling luas merujuk keluarga kerajaan Burgundia, juga disebut Gibichungen atau Gjúkingar: saudara-saudara raja yang dipimpin Gunther atau Gunnar, yang bertanggung jawab atas kematian Siegfried atau Sigurd dan kemudian dihancurkan di istana Attila.
long_description.en: Germanic heroic legend uses Nibelung (German), or Niflungr in Old Norse, as a personal or family name in several rival and even contradictory senses. Its etymology is unclear, though often tied to German Nebel ('mist'). It gives its name to the Middle High German epic Nibelungenlied. The most widespread use names the Burgundian royal house, also called Gibichungen or Gjúkingar: royal brothers led by Gunther or Gunnar, who bring about the hero Siegfried's (Sigurd's) death and are themselves wiped out later at Attila's court.

long_description.id: Dalam bahasa Jerman abad pertengahan, Nibelung juga merujuk raja dan penghuni negeri mitos yang didiami kurcaci dan raksasa dalam paruh pertama Nibelungenlied, yang memberi nama "harta Nibelung". Menurut artikel es, nibelungo adalah bangsa mitos legenda Jermanik yang dipimpin pangeran Nibelung: kurcaci gelap yang tinggal di dalam bumi, menambang logam mulia terutama emas, dan memiliki harta besar di dasar sungai Rin; Sigfrido (Siegfried) membunuh pangeran Nibelung dan Schilbung setelah bertengkar soal pembagian harta. Richard Wagner kemudian menggubah siklus empat opera El anillo del nibelungo berdasarkan legenda ini.
long_description.en: In medieval German, Nibelung also names the king and people of a mythical land of dwarfs and giants in the first half of the Nibelungenlied, which gives its name to the 'hoard of the Nibelungs'. According to the es article, the Nibelungs are a mythical people of Germanic legend ruled by prince Nibelung: dark dwarfs living deep in the earth, mining precious metals, above all gold, with a huge treasure at the bottom of the Rin (Rhine); Sigfrido (Siegfried) killed the princes Nibelung and Schilbung after quarrelling over how to share the hoard. Richard Wagner later wrote a cycle of four operas, El anillo del nibelungo, based on these legends.
