long_description.en: The term Nibelung (German) or Niflungr (Old Norse) is a personal or clan name with several competing and contradictory uses in Germanic heroic legend. It has an unclear etymology, but is often connected to the root of German Nebel, meaning 'mist'. The term in its various meanings gives its name to the Middle High German heroic epic the Nibelungenlied. The most widespread use of the term Nibelung denotes the Burgundian royal house, also known as the Gibichungen (German) or Gjúkingar (Old Norse). A group of royal brothers led by king Gunther or Gunnar, the Gibichungs are responsible for the death of the hero Siegfried or Sigurd and are later destroyed at the court of Attila the Hun (called Etzel in German and Atli in Old Norse). This is the only use of the term attested in the Old Norse legends. In medieval German, several other uses of the term Nibelung are documented besides the reference to the Gibichungs: it refers to the king and inhabitants of a mythical land inhabited by dwarfs and giants in the first half of the Nibelungenlied, as well as to the father and one of two brothers fighting over a divided inheritance. This land and its inhabitants give their name to the "hoard of the Nibelungs" (Middle High German der Nibelunge hort). In the late medieval Lied vom Hürnen Seyfrid, the name, in the form Nybling or Nibling, is given to a dwarf who again gives his name to the treasure. In Richard Wagner's opera cycle Der Ring des Nibelungen (1848–1874), Nibelung denotes a dwarf, or perhaps a specific race of dwarfs.

short_description.id: Setengah-elf adalah makhluk mitologis atau fiktif yang lahir dari elf abadi dan manusia fana; asal-usulnya ada dalam mitologi Nordik, dengan contoh Skuld dan Högni.
short_description.en: Half-elves are beings of myth and fiction whose parents are an immortal elf and a mortal human; they go back to Norse mythology, where Skuld and Högni are examples.

long_description.id: Setengah-elf adalah makhluk mitologis atau fiktif yang lahir dari elf yang abadi dan manusia yang fana. Mereka sering digambarkan sangat rupawan dan memiliki kekuatan gaib, kadang terbelah di antara dua dunia yang mereka huni. Makhluk ini dikenal luas di masa modern terutama lewat tulisan J. R. R. Tolkien tentang Dunia Tengah, tetapi berakar pada mitologi Nordik.
long_description.en: Half-elves are beings of myth and fiction whose parents are an immortal elf and a mortal human. They are often portrayed as very beautiful and gifted with magic, sometimes torn between the two worlds they belong to. Today they are familiar above all from J. R. R. Tolkien's Middle-earth books, yet their roots lie in Norse mythology.

long_description.id: Dalam mitologi Nordik, setengah-elf adalah keturunan elf dan manusia; contoh utamanya Skuld dan Högni. Högni adalah pahlawan dalam Thidreks saga yang lahir dari seorang ratu manusia setelah elf mendatanginya saat raja pergi. Skuld adalah putri Denmark dalam saga Hrólf Kraki, anak Raja Helgi dengan seorang perempuan elf yang ia bebaskan dari kutukan; nama Skuld berarti "apa yang harus kaulakukan".
long_description.en: In Norse mythology a half-elf is the child of an elf and a human; the main examples are Skuld and Högni. Högni, a hero of Thidreks saga, was born to a human queen whom an elf had visited during the king's absence. Skuld was a Danish princess in Hrólf Kraki's saga, daughter of King Helgi by an elf-woman he had freed from a curse; the name Skuld means 'what you should do'.

long_description.id: Sarjana Hilda Ellis menggambarkan Skuld sebagai tokoh jahat yang memakai sihir untuk membangkitkan pasukan melawan saudara tirinya, Hrólf; prajurit Skuld yang terbunuh terus bangkit kembali. Högni juga dipandang tokoh yang pada dasarnya bersifat iblis, dan Alexander Krappe menilai statusnya sebagai putra elf sesuai dengan peran itu.
long_description.en: The scholar Hilda Ellis describes Skuld as evil, using magic to raise an army against her half-brother Hrólf; Skuld's slain warriors kept rising again. Högni too is seen as essentially demonic, and Alexander Krappe considers his elf parentage to suit that role.

long_description.id: Dalam fiksi Tolkien, setengah-elf adalah anak Elf dan Manusia yang dapat memilih keabadian Elf atau kefanaan Manusia. Sejak dipopulerkan Tolkien, setengah-elf menjadi umum dalam permainan peran, misalnya Dungeons & Dragons, dan dalam fiksi fantasi pada umumnya.
long_description.en: In Tolkien's fiction half-elves are children of Elves and Men who can choose Elvish immortality or the mortal life of Men. Since Tolkien popularised them, half-elves have become common in role-playing games such as Dungeons & Dragons and in fantasy fiction generally.

claims.quote: In Norse mythology, a half-elf is the offspring of an elf and a human. Major examples include Skuld and Högni. Högni was a hero in Thidreks saga, born to a human queen when an elf visited her while the king was away. Skuld was a Danish princess, as told in Hrólf Kraki's saga.

claims.statement: King Helgi, sleeping alone, let in a ragged person on a midwinter night; she said he had freed her from a curse, and three years later the elf-woman returned and left a daughter at his door named Skuld, meaning 'what you should do'.

claims.quote: King Helgi, sleeping alone as he had not been invited to King Adils's wedding, let in a ragged person on a midwinter night. ... She told him he had freed her from a curse and asked to leave. ... three years later the woman, an elf, returned and left a daughter at his door. She told him that the child's name was Skuld, which means "what you should do".

claims.statement: She said the King would be rewarded for breaking the curse, but his people would suffer because he had not done as she asked; she never returned, and Skuld was always angry.
claims.statement_id: Ia berkata raja akan mendapat imbalan karena mematahkan kutukan, tetapi rakyatnya akan menderita karena raja tidak menuruti permintaannya; ia tak pernah kembali, dan Skuld selalu marah.
claims.quote: She said that the King would gain the reward for breaking the curse, but that the King's people would suffer as the King had not done as she had asked. She never came back, but Skuld was always angry.

claims.statement: The scholar Hilda Ellis describes Skuld as evil: in the saga she used magic to raise an army against her half-brother Hrólf, and her men sprang up again as fast as they were killed, fighting harder.
claims.statement_id: Sarjana Hilda Ellis menggambarkan Skuld sebagai jahat: dalam saga ia memakai sihir untuk membangkitkan pasukan melawan Hrólf, saudara tirinya, dan prajuritnya yang dibunuh segera bangkit dan bertarung lebih kuat.
claims.quote: The scholar Hilda Ellis describes Skuld as evil, recalling that in the saga, Skuld used magic to raise an army against Hrólf, her half-brother. As quickly as Hrólf's warriors kill Skuld's men, they spring up, fighting more strongly than ever.

long_description.en: A half-elf is a mythological or fictional being, born of an immortal elf and a mortal human. They are often depicted as very beautiful and endowed with magical powers; they may be presented as torn between the two worlds that they inhabit. Half-elves became known in modern times mainly through J. R. R. Tolkien's Middle-earth writings but have origins in Norse mythology. A half-elf appeared in Lord Dunsany's 1924 book The King of Elfland's Daughter. In Middle-earth, half-elves are the children of Elves and Men, and can choose either Elvish immortality or the mortal life of Men. The elf-maidens Lúthien and Arwen in Tolkien's works both chose mortality to be with the Men that they loved. Scholars have noted that this enabled Tolkien to explore several key themes, including love and death, time and immortality. As a Catholic, he believed that Men, freely choosing to let go, gain release from the world's limitations; whereas if they tried to hold on to life and material things, they would end in darkness. His Elves – except for half-elves – were unable to gain this release. In On Fairy-Stories Tolkien wrote that since men write fairy-stories, these concern the escape from death; and conversely that Elves would tell human-stories about the escape from deathlessness. Since their popularisation by Tolkien, half-elves have become widely known in role-playing games, and in turn in video games and spin-off films. The role-playing game Dungeons & Dragons features its own race of half-elves, including the character Tanis Half-Elven.

short_description.id: Durinn adalah kurcaci dalam mitologi Nordik, yang kedua diciptakan setelah Mótsognir menurut Völuspá, dan dalam Hervarar saga ikut menempa pedang ajaib Tyrfing.
short_description.en: Durinn is a dwarf of Norse mythology, the second created after Mótsognir according to the Völuspá, who in Hervarar saga helped forge the magic sword Tyrfing.

long_description.id: Dalam mitologi Nordik, Durinn atau Durin adalah kurcaci yang disebut dalam bait ke-10 puisi Völuspá dari Edda Puisi, dan disebut lagi dalam Gylfaginning dari Edda Prosa. Ia kurcaci kedua yang diciptakan, setelah Mótsognir, kurcaci pertama dan terkemuka. Terjemahan Völuspá oleh Karl Simrock menyebut para dewa bermusyawarah tentang siapa yang akan menciptakan bangsa kurcaci dari darah Brimir.
long_description.en: In Norse mythology Durinn or Durin is a dwarf named in stanza 10 of the Völuspá in the Poetic Edda and again in the Gylfaginning of the Prose Edda. He was the second dwarf created, after Mótsognir, the first and foremost. Karl Simrock's translation of the Völuspá tells of the gods taking counsel over who should make the race of dwarfs from Brimir's blood.

long_description.id: Dalam Hervarar saga, ia menempa pedang ajaib Tyrfing dibantu kurcaci Dvalin; dalam varian teks saga itu namanya Dulinn. Menurut satu uraian, Durin dan Mótsognir terbentuk ketika dunia diciptakan dari tubuh raksasa Ymir, lalu para dewa memberi mereka akal dan rupa manusia.
long_description.en: In Hervarar saga he and the dwarf Dvalin together forged the magic sword Tyrfing; in variant texts of the saga he is called Dulinn. One account says Durin and Mótsognir formed when the world was made from the body of the giant Ymir, and that the gods then gave them reason and human likeness.

long_description.id: Dalam legendarium J. R. R. Tolkien, Durin menjadi nama beberapa raja kurcaci, termasuk Durin yang Abadi, yang tertua dari Tujuh Leluhur bangsa mereka.
long_description.en: In J. R. R. Tolkien's legendarium Durin is the name of several dwarf kings, including Durin the Deathless, eldest of the Seven Fathers of their race.

note.en: The first dwarf, made before Durinn.
Helped Durinn forge Tyrfing.

description.en: Dwarf king in Tolkien's legendarium.

statement.en: In Karl Simrock's translation of the Völuspá the gods take counsel over who should make the race of dwarfs from Brimir's blood and limbs; Modsognir became the mightiest and Durin after him.

statement.en: Durin and Mótsognir formed spontaneously when Odin and his brothers Vili and Ve made the world from the body of the cosmic giant Ymir; the gods then gave them intelligence and human appearance.

In variant texts of the saga Durinn is known as Dulinn.

short_description.id: Eitri atau Sindri adalah kurcaci pandai besi dalam mitologi Nordik, saudara Brokkr, yang menempa babi emas Gullinbursti, cincin Draupnir, dan palu Mjöllnir.
short_description.en: Eitri or Sindri is a dwarf smith of Norse mythology, brother of Brokkr, who forged the golden boar Gullinbursti, the ring Draupnir and the hammer Mjöllnir.

long_description.id: Dalam agama Nordik Kuno, Eitri, juga disebut Sindri, adalah kurcaci dan saudara Brokkr. Menurut Skáldskaparmál, setelah Loki menyuruh para Putra Ivaldi membuat rambut Sif, kapal Skidbladnir milik Freyr, dan tombak Gungnir milik Odin, ia mempertaruhkan kepalanya sendiri dengan Brokkr bahwa Eitri tak akan mampu membuat benda yang menandingi mutu karya itu.
long_description.en: Old Norse religion knows Eitri, also named Sindri, as a dwarf whose brother is Brokkr. The Skáldskaparmál tells how Loki, after the Sons of Ivaldi had crafted Gungnir, the spear of Odin, Skidbladnir, the ship of Freyr, and golden hair for Sif, staked his own head with Brokkr on Eitri being unable to equal that craftsmanship.

long_description.id: Eitri bekerja di tungkunya sementara saudaranya memompa ububan, tetapi seekor lalat, yang kadang dianggap Loki sendiri, menyengat Brokkr untuk menggagalkan pekerjaan itu. Eitri tetap berhasil membuat babi emas Gullinbursti, cincin emas Draupnir, dan palu Mjöllnir sehingga saudaranya memenangkan taruhan, walau gagang palu itu lebih pendek dari semestinya.
long_description.en: Eitri worked at his furnace while his brother pumped the bellows, but a fly, sometimes thought to be Loki himself, stung Brokkr to spoil the work. Even so Eitri produced Gullinbursti, a boar of gold, Draupnir, a ring of gold, and Mjöllnir, a hammer, so that his brother won the wager, though the hammer's handle turned out too short.

long_description.id: Dalam Marvel Cinematic Universe, Eitri tampil sebagai tokoh pendukung yang diperankan Peter Dinklage, terutama dalam film Avengers: Infinity War, sebagai pandai besi yang tinggal di Nidavellir.
long_description.en: In the Marvel Cinematic Universe Eitri is a supporting character played by Peter Dinklage, chiefly in Avengers: Infinity War, as a smith living on Nidavellir.

did_you_know.id: Gagang palu Mjöllnir lebih pendek dari semestinya karena seekor lalat, mungkin Loki, mengganggu saudara Eitri saat memompa ububan.
did_you_know.en: Mjöllnir's handle came out short because a fly, perhaps Loki, pestered Eitri's brother at the bellows.

summary.id: Loki mempertaruhkan kepalanya bahwa Eitri tak bisa menandingi karya Putra Ivaldi; meski diganggu lalat, Eitri menempa Gullinbursti, Draupnir, dan Mjöllnir.
summary.en: Loki bets his head that Eitri cannot match the Sons of Ivaldi; despite a stinging fly, Eitri forges Gullinbursti, Draupnir and Mjöllnir.

short_description.id: Nachzehrer adalah mayat hidup dalam cerita rakyat Jerman yang dari dalam kuburnya menyedot daya hidup kerabat dan tetangganya, kerap dengan mengunyah kain kafannya.
short_description.en: The Nachzehrer is a revenant of German folklore that, from inside its grave, drains the life of its relatives and neighbours, often by chewing its own shroud.

long_description.id: Dalam cerita rakyat Jerman, Nachzehrer (harfiah "pemakan sesudah", juga Nachtzehrer, "pemakan malam") adalah sejenis Wiedergänger atau mayat hidup yang diyakini dapat menyeret orang hidup menyusulnya ke dalam kematian, entah karena dengki atau karena ingin dekat dengan orang yang dicintainya. Kata ini mulai dipakai pada abad ke-19, tetapi kepercayaannya jauh lebih tua.
long_description.en: In German folklore the Nachzehrer (literally 'after-consumer', also Nachtzehrer, 'night-consumer') is a kind of Wiedergänger or revenant believed able to drag the living after it into death, whether from malice or a wish to be near its loved ones. The word came into use in the 19th century, but the belief is several centuries older.

long_description.id: Kepercayaan ini dulu umum terutama di Mark, dan berbeda dari anggapan lama para ahli folklor, sebarannya tidak terbatas pada wilayah timur dan timur laut Jerman, tetapi sampai ke Rheinland. Nachzehrer berkerabat dekat dengan vampir. Tanda yang sangat umum ialah kain kafan dan pakaian yang dimakannya sendiri, dan bahayanya dianggap paling besar bila orang hidup memberi jenazah barang miliknya sebagai bekal kubur.
long_description.en: The term was once common especially in the Mark, and contrary to an older folklorists' view the belief was not confined to Germany's east and north-east but reached the Rhineland. The Nachzehrer is closely related to the vampire. A very common sign was a shroud and clothing it had eaten itself, and the danger was thought greatest if the living had given the dead their own belongings as grave goods.

long_description.id: Menurut tradisi, berbeda dari vampir yang harus meninggalkan kubur, Nachzehrer berbaring atau duduk di bawah tanah sambil menyedot daya hidup orang yang ditinggalkannya. Untuk mencegahnya, benda logam seperti gunting atau paku diletakkan di dadanya, dan kacang kering atau kerikil dituang ke peti, karena ia harus menghitungnya lebih dulu dan tak bisa melewati angka dua.
long_description.en: According to tradition, unlike a vampire that must leave its grave, the Nachzehrer lies or sits underground draining the life-force of those it left behind. To prevent this, metal objects such as scissors or nails laid on its chest, and dried pulses or pebbles poured into the coffin, since it had to count them first and could never get past two.

role.en: Drags its kin after it into death.

long_description.en: In German folklore, a Nachzehrer (German: [ˈnaːxˌt͡seːʁɐ] , literally "after-consumer" (a creature that consumes from the afterlife) in German; also spelt Nachtzehrer, literally "night-consumer") is a type of Wiedergänger (revenant), which was believed to be able to drag the living after it into death, either through malice or through the desire to be closer to its loved ones through various means. The word Nachzehrer came to use in the nineteenth century, but belief in the creature the label is applied to precedes this by several centuries. The nachzehrer was prominent in the folklore of the northern regions of Germany, but also in Silesia and Bavaria, and the word was also used to describe a similar creature of the Kashubes of Northern Poland. The nachzehrer was similar to the Slavic vampire in that it was known to be a recently deceased person who returned from the grave to attack family and village acquaintances.

short_description.id: Fossegrim adalah roh air atau troll dalam cerita rakyat Skandinavia, pemain biola ulung di air terjun dan sungai yang dapat mengajarkan keahliannya dengan imbalan persembahan.
short_description.en: Fossegrim is a water spirit or troll of Scandinavian folklore, a master fiddler of waterfalls and streams who can teach his skill in return for an offering.

long_description.id: Fossegrim, juga disebut grim saja dalam bahasa Norwegia atau Strömkarlen ("Lelaki Sungai") dalam bahasa Swedia, adalah roh air atau troll dalam cerita rakyat Skandinavia. Ia sering digambarkan sebagai lelaki tampan tanpa busana yang bermain biola di sungai dan air terjun, dikaitkan dengan roh penggilingan kvernknurr dan berkerabat dengan roh air nokken, sehingga di Swedia kadang disebut näcken.
long_description.en: Fossegrim, also simply the grim in Norwegian or Strömkarlen ('the Stream Man') in Swedish, is a water spirit or troll of Scandinavian folklore. He is often shown as a handsome naked man playing the fiddle in streams and waterfalls, linked with the mill spirit kvernknurr and related to the water spirit nokken, so that in Sweden he is sometimes called näcken.

long_description.id: Ia pemain biola yang luar biasa: bunyi hutan, angin, dan air bermain di senar biolanya. Lagu strömkarl Swedia konon punya sebelas variasi, dan yang terakhir disimpan untuk roh malam.
long_description.en: He is an exceptionally gifted fiddler: the sounds of forest, wind and water play over his strings. In Sweden the strömkarl's tune reportedly comes in eleven variations, of which the last belongs to the spirits of the night.

long_description.id: Ia mau mengajarkan keahliannya dengan imbalan persembahan makanan pada Kamis malam secara rahasia, seperti kambing jantan putih yang dilempar ke air terjun yang mengalir ke utara atau daging domba asap. Bila dagingnya kurang, ia hanya mengajari cara menyetel biola. Pemain biola terkenal seperti Myllarguten dan Ole Bull dikabarkan belajar darinya.
long_description.en: He will teach his art for a secret food offering on a Thursday evening, such as a white he-goat thrown into a north-flowing waterfall or smoked mutton. If there is too little meat he teaches only how to tune the fiddle. Famous fiddlers such as Myllarguten and Ole Bull were rumoured to have learned from him.

role.en: Teaches music in return for an offering.

did_you_know.en: The statue of the violinist Ole Bull in central Bergen shows a fossegrim playing his harp beneath falling water.

note.en: Fossegrim is related to the water spirit nokken.

statement.en: Fossegrim is linked with the mill spirit (kvernknurr), related to the water spirit (nokken) and sometimes called näcken in Sweden; he is tied to watercourses (Swedish Strömkarlen means 'the man of the stream'), especially those with waterfalls (Norwegian foss).

claims.statement: Fossegrim is described as an exceptionally talented fiddler whose strings carry the sounds of forest, wind and water; he can be induced to teach, and the Swedish strömkarl's lay has eleven variations, the last reserved for the night spirits.
claims.statement_id: Fossegrim digambarkan sebagai pemain biola yang luar biasa berbakat, yang senarnya memainkan bunyi hutan, angin, dan air; ia dapat dibujuk mengajarkan keahliannya, dan lagu strömkarl Swedia konon punya sebelas variasi, yang terakhir disimpan untuk roh malam.
claims.quote: Fossegrim is described as an exceptionally talented fiddler: the sounds of forest, wind and water play over his fiddle strings. Fossegrims can be induced to teach the skill. The Swedish strömkarl's lay is said to have eleven variations, the final one being reserved for the night spirits

claims.statement: Fossegrim will teach his skills for a secret food offering on a Thursday evening: a white he-goat thrown into a north-flowing waterfall, or smoked mutton (fenalår); if there is too little meat, he teaches only how to tune the fiddle.
claims.statement_id: Fossegrim konon mau mengajarkan keahliannya dengan imbalan persembahan makanan pada Kamis malam secara rahasia: kambing jantan putih yang dilempar ke air terjun yang mengalir ke utara, atau daging domba asap (fenalår); bila dagingnya kurang, ia hanya mengajari cara menyetel biola.
claims.quote: Fossegrim is said to be willing to teach away his skills in exchange for a food offering made on a Thursday evening and in secrecy: a white he-goat thrown with head turned away into a waterfall that flows northwards, or smoked mutton (fenalår). If there is not enough meat on the bone, he will only teach the supplicant how to tune the fiddle.

claims.statement: Famous fiddlers rumoured to have learned from the fossegrim include Torgeir Augundsson (1801–1872), known as Myllarguten, and Ole Bull (1810–1880), whose statue in central Bergen shows a fossegrim playing his harp under falling water.
claims.statement_id: Pemain biola terkenal yang dikabarkan belajar dari fossegrim antara lain Torgeir Augundsson (1801–1872) alias Myllarguten dan Ole Bull (1810–1880), yang patungnya di pusat Bergen menampilkan fossegrim memainkan harpa di bawah air terjun.
claims.quote: Famous fiddlers who were rumored to have learnt from the Fossegrim include Torgeir Augundsson (1801–1872) known as Myllarguten and Ole Bull (1810–1880) whose statue in the centre of Bergen depicts a fossegrim playing his harp under the falling water.

claims.statement: Fossegrim is linked with the mill spirit (kvernknurr), related to the water spirit (nokken) and sometimes called näcken in Sweden; he is tied to watercourses (Swedish Strömkarlen means 'the man of the stream'), especially those with waterfalls (Norwegian foss).
claims.statement_id: Fossegrim dikaitkan dengan roh penggilingan (kvernknurr), berkerabat dengan roh air (nokken), dan di Swedia kadang disebut näcken; ia terkait aliran air (nama Swedia Strömkarlen berarti "lelaki aliran air"), terutama yang berair terjun (foss dalam bahasa Norwegia).
claims.quote: Fossegrim è stato associato allo spirito del mulino (kvernknurr) ed è imparentato con lo spirito dell'acqua (nokken) ed è talvolta chiamato anche näcken in Svezia. È associato ai corsi d'acqua (il nome svedese "Strömkarlen" significa "L'uomo del corso d'acqua") e in particolare ai corsi d'acqua a cascata (foss in norvegese)

long_description.en: Fossegrim, also known simply as the grim (Norwegian) or Strömkarlen (Swedish), is a water spirit or troll in Scandinavian folklore. He is often depicted as a handsome, nude man playing the fiddle in streams and waterfalls. Fossegrim has been associated with a mill spirit (kvernknurr) and is related to the water spirit (nokken) and is sometimes also called näcken in Sweden.

short_description.id: Litr, "warna, rupa", adalah nama seorang kurcaci dan seorang raksasa (jötunn) dalam mitologi Nordik; kurcaci Litr ditendang Thor ke api pembakaran jenazah Baldr.
short_description.en: Litr, 'colour, appearance', is the name of a dwarf and a giant (jötunn) in Norse mythology; the dwarf Litr was kicked by Thor into Baldr's funeral pyre.

long_description.id: Litr (juga Lit; dalam bahasa Nordik Kuno berarti "warna, rupa") adalah nama yang disandang seorang kurcaci dan seorang jötunn dalam mitologi Nordik. Namanya diterjemahkan sebagai "warna", "corak", atau "rupa", dan berasal dari bentuk Proto-Jermanik yang direkonstruksi *ulituz.
long_description.en: Litr (also Lit; Old Norse for 'colour, appearance') is the name of a dwarf and of a jötunn in Norse mythology. The name has been rendered 'colour', 'hue' or 'appearance', and comes from a reconstructed Proto-Germanic *ulituz.

long_description.id: Dalam Gylfaginning karya Snorri Sturluson, ketika Thor menyucikan api pembakaran Baldr dengan Mjöllnir, seorang kurcaci bernama Litr berlari di depan kakinya; Thor menendangnya ke dalam api dan ia terbakar. Litr juga tercantum sebagai kurcaci dalam Völuspá, dan seorang kurcaci bernama Litr muncul dalam Áns saga bogsveigis, dipaksa tokoh utamanya membuat busur.
long_description.en: In Snorri Sturluson's Gylfaginning, as Thor hallowed Baldr's pyre with Mjöllnir, a dwarf named Litr ran before his feet; Thor kicked him into the fire and he burned. Litr is also listed as a dwarf in the Völuspá, and a dwarf of that name appears in Áns saga bogsveigis, forced by its hero to make him a bow.

long_description.id: Dalam bait Bragi Boddason yang dikutip dalam Skáldskaparmál, Thor disebut "penantang tarung orang-orang Lit"; karena Thor musuh para raksasa, Litr di sini umumnya dianggap raksasa. Hal ini membuat John Lindow menduga mungkin semula hanya ada satu Litr, seorang raksasa.
long_description.en: In a stanza by Bragi Boddason quoted in the Skáldskaparmál, Thor is called 'Lit's men's fight-challenger'; since Thor is the giants' foe, Litr here is generally taken to be a giant. This led John Lindow to suggest there was probably originally only one Litr, a giant.

short_description.id: Vardøger adalah roh pendahulu dalam cerita rakyat Skandinavia: penampakan langkah, suara, atau rupa seseorang yang tiba lebih dulu sebelum orang itu sendiri datang.
short_description.en: The vardøger is a spirit predecessor of Scandinavian folklore: the steps, voice or likeness of a person arriving ahead of the person themself.

long_description.id: Vardøger, juga disebut vardyvle atau vardyger, adalah roh pendahulu dalam cerita rakyat Skandinavia. Kisah-kisahnya mirip déjà vu yang terbalik: roh dengan langkah kaki, suara, bau, atau rupa seseorang tiba lebih dulu di suatu tempat, sehingga para saksi mengira telah melihat atau mendengar orang itu sebelum ia benar-benar datang. Dalam cerita rakyat Finlandia, gagasan ini dikenal sebagai etiäinen.
long_description.en: The vardøger, also called vardyvle or vardyger, is a spirit predecessor of Scandinavian folklore. Its stories are like déjà vu in reverse: a spirit bearing someone's footsteps, voice, scent or looks reaches a place first, so witnesses think they have seen or heard the person before he or she actually arrives. In Finnish folklore the idea is known as etiäinen.

long_description.id: Berbeda tipis dari doppelgänger, vardøger tidak bermakna seram, dan disamakan dengan kembaran gaib atau bentuk bilokasi. Kata Norwegia vardøgr berarti bunyi atau penampakan pertanda seseorang sebelum ia tiba, dan berasal dari bahasa Nordik Kuno varðhygi, dari vǫrð, "penjaga", dan hugr, "pikiran, roh"; di Swedia gagasan yang sama disebut vård.
long_description.en: Subtly unlike the doppelgänger, the vardøger has no sinister overtone and is likened to a phantom double or a form of bilocation. The Norwegian word vardøgr means a premonitory sound or sight of a person before arrival, from Old Norse varðhygi, from vǫrð, 'guard', and hugr, 'mind, spirit'; in Sweden the same idea is called vård.

long_description.id: Menurut cerita rakyat Norwegia, melihat vardøger seseorang sering hanya berarti orang itu sedang dalam perjalanan. Karena vardøger semacam roh pelindung, orang yang memilikinya biasa dianggap orang baik yang dijaga roh baik; semula ia dianggap sejenis fylgja.
long_description.en: According to Norwegian folklore, seeing someone's vardøger often just means that person is on the way. Because the vardøger is a kind of guardian spirit, those who have one are commonly called good people protected by a kindly spirit; originally it was considered a kind of fylgja.

note.id: Vardøger disebut lawan dari doppelgänger yang lebih seram.
note.en: The vardøger is called the counterpart of the more sinister doppelgänger.
The vardøger was originally considered a fylgja.
The name vardøger comes from vǫrð, 'guard'.

statement.en: Vardøger, also known as vardyvle or vardyger, is a spirit predecessor in Scandinavian folklore.

claims.quote: nearly déjà vu in substance, but in reverse, where a spirit with the subject's footsteps, voice, scent, or appearance and overall demeanor precedes them in a location or activity ... This bears a subtle difference from a doppelgänger, with a less sinister connotation. It has been likened to being a phantom double, or form of bilocation. In Finnish folklore, the concept is known as etiäinen.

statement.id: Kisahnya mirip déjà vu terbalik: roh dengan langkah, suara, bau, atau rupa seseorang mendahuluinya di suatu tempat; berbeda tipis dari doppelgänger dan kurang seram, ia disamakan dengan kembaran gaib atau bilokasi, dan dalam cerita rakyat Finlandia disebut etiäinen.
statement.en: Its stories are like déjà vu in reverse: a spirit with a person's footsteps, voice, scent or looks precedes them; subtly different from the doppelgänger and less sinister, it is likened to a phantom double or bilocation, and in Finnish folklore is called etiäinen.

claims.quote: Vardøgr is a Norwegian word defined as ‘‘premonitory sound or sight of a person before he arrives’’. ... The word vardøger is from Old Norse varðhygi, consisting of the elements vǫrð, "care taker, guard, watchman" (akin to "warden") and hugr, 'the mind, will, thought, spirit'. The same concept exists in Sweden but under the name of vård

statement.id: Vardøgr adalah kata Norwegia yang berarti "bunyi atau penampakan pertanda seseorang sebelum ia tiba"; asalnya bahasa Nordik Kuno varðhygi, dari vǫrð ("penjaga") dan hugr ("pikiran, kehendak, roh"); di Swedia gagasan yang sama disebut vård.
statement.en: Vardøgr is a Norwegian word meaning 'premonitory sound or sight of a person before he arrives', from Old Norse varðhygi, of vǫrð ('guard') and hugr ('mind, will, spirit'); in Sweden the same concept is called vård.

claims.quote: Si ves un vardøger, según el folclore noruego, eso significa que te estas cruzando en el camino de una persona. A menudo solo quiere decir que esa persona de la cual has visto su vardøger está en camino.

statement.id: Menurut cerita rakyat Norwegia, melihat vardøger berarti kau berpapasan di jalan seseorang, dan sering hanya berarti orang itu sedang dalam perjalanan.
statement.en: According to Norwegian folklore, seeing a vardøger means you are crossing someone's path, and often only that the person is on the way.

claims.quote: originalmente, un vardøger era considerado un fylgja, una especie de espíritu guardián de esa persona.

statement.id: Semula, vardøger dianggap sebuah fylgja, sejenis roh pelindung orang itu.
statement.en: Originally a vardøger was considered a fylgja, a kind of guardian spirit of that person.

claims.quote: Debido a que el vardøger es un tipo de espíritu guardián, se suele decir de aquellos que tienen un vardøger que son buenas personas, ya que un espíritu benéfico les protege. En resumen, podríamos decir que un vardøger es la contraparte de un doppelgänger.

statement.id: Karena vardøger sejenis roh pelindung, orang yang memilikinya biasa disebut orang baik yang dilindungi roh baik; singkatnya vardøger adalah lawan doppelgänger.
statement.en: Since the vardøger is a kind of guardian spirit, people who have one are usually called good people protected by a kindly spirit; in short, the vardøger is the counterpart of a doppelgänger.

claims.quote: Debido a que el vardøger es un tipo de espíritu guardián, se suele decir de aquellos que tienen un vardøger que son buenas personas, ya que un espíritu benéfico les protege. En resumen, podríamos decir que un vardøger es la contraparte de un doppelgänger.

long_description.en: Vardøger, also known as vardyvle or vardyger, is a spirit predecessor in Scandinavian folklore. Stories typically include instances that are nearly déjà vu in substance, but in reverse, where a spirit with the subject's footsteps, voice, scent, or appearance and overall demeanor precedes them in a location or activity, resulting in witnesses believing they have seen or heard the actual person before the person physically arrives. This bears a subtle difference from a doppelgänger, with a less sinister connotation. It has been likened to being a phantom double, or form of bilocation. In Finnish folklore, the concept is known as etiäinen. Originally, vardøger was considered a fylgja and/or vǫrð, a sort of guardian spirit. Thus, a vardøger is the representation of a human's inner essence, which manifests as an animal that most closely resembles the personality of the human.

short_description.id: Askafroa, "istri pohon ash", adalah roh penjaga pohon ash dalam cerita rakyat Skandinavia yang berbahaya dan harus ditenangkan dengan persembahan pada Rabu Abu.
short_description.en: The Askafroa, 'wife of the ash tree', is a dangerous guardian spirit of the ash tree in Scandinavian folklore who must be appeased with offerings on Ash Wednesday.

long_description.id: Askafroa (bahasa Swedia, "istri pohon ash"), dalam bahasa Denmark Askefrue, adalah makhluk legenda dalam cerita rakyat Skandinavia yang mirip hamadryad Yunani. Ia penjaga pohon ash dan dianggap makhluk jahat yang banyak menimbulkan kerusakan, sehingga orang perlu memberinya persembahan pada Rabu Abu.
long_description.en: The Askafroa (Swedish 'wife of the ash tree'), Danish Askefrue, is a legendary creature of Scandinavian folklore similar to the Greek hamadryads. She guards the ash tree and was considered a malicious being that did much damage, so people had to make offerings to her on Ash Wednesday.

long_description.id: Ia tinggal di pohon ash di wilayah Skåne, Swedia, dan merupakan jiwa pohon itu; bila pohonnya ditebang, ia akan membalas dendam. Sarjana Swedia Hyltén-Cavallius mencatat dalam Wärend och Wirdarne bahwa di Ljunit Hundred para tetua menuang air ke akar pohon ash sebelum matahari terbit pada Rabu Abu sambil berkata: "Kini aku berkorban, agar kau tidak mencelakai kami". Mereka juga percaya siapa pun yang mematahkan dahan atau ranting pohon ash akan jatuh sakit.
long_description.en: She lives in ash trees in Skåne in Sweden and is the tree's soul; if the tree is felled she takes revenge. The Swedish scholar Hyltén-Cavallius recorded in Wärend och Wirdarne that in Ljunit Hundred the elders poured water on the ash's roots before sunrise on Ash Wednesday, saying: 'Now I sacrifice, so that you do us no harm'. They also believed anyone breaking branches or twigs from the ash would fall ill.

long_description.id: Pohon ash memiliki tempat penting dalam mitologi Nordik: bersama pohon ek, ia pohon paling sakti yang diberi kekuatan khusus, seperti menghentikan darah atau menangkal bisa ular, dan pohon mitologis Yggdrasil pun pohon ash. Askafroa tetap makhluk yang cukup samar dan jarang tampil dalam fiksi modern, walau muncul dalam gim daring Dark Age of Camelot.
long_description.en: The ash tree holds a prominent place in Norse mythology: with the oak it was the most magical tree, credited with powers such as stopping bleeding or countering snake venom, and the mythological tree Yggdrasil was an ash. The Askafroa remains a rather obscure creature, rarely seen in modern fiction, though she appears in the online game Dark Age of Camelot.

long_description.en: The Askafroa (Swedish: wife of the ash tree), also known as the Danish Askefrue is a type of legendary creature in Scandinavian folklore, similar to the Greek Hamadryads. The Askafroa is the guardian (tutelary deity) of the ash tree. The Askafroa was thought to be a malicious creature that did much damage, and to appease her, it was necessary to make a sacrifice to her on Ash Wednesday. The Askafroa lives in ash trees in the Scania region of Sweden, and is said to be a very dangerous creature. She is the soul of the tree and if it is cut down, she will exert revenge. To appease her, one must provide offerings every Ash Wednesday by pouring water on her roots and declaring: "I am offering to you so that you do us no harm". The ash tree has a very prominent place in Nordic mythology. It was, together with the oak tree, the most magical tree to which special powers were assigned, such as the ability to stop blood flow or as an antidote to snake poison. The mythological tree Yggdrasil was also an ash tree. The Swedish scholar Hyltén-Cavallius recorded in his ethnographic work Wärend och Wirdarne a belief of a female creature living in the ash tree, in Ljunit Hundred. The elders sacrificed to the Askafroa on the morning of Ash Wednesday. Before the sun had risen, they poured water over the roots of the ash tree. While doing this, they said: "Nu offrar jag, så gör du oss ingen skada", meaning "Now I sacrifice [to you], so that you do us no harm". Hyltén-Cavallius further writes that they believed that if anyone broke branches or twigs from the ash tree, they would become ill.

short_description.id: Slattenpatten, "payudara kendur", adalah makhluk perempuan dalam cerita rakyat Denmark, sejenis perempuan elf yang berpayudara sangat panjang dan dikejar Kong Volmer setiap malam.
short_description.en: Slattenpatten, 'flaccid-breasts', is a female being of Danish folklore, a kind of elf-woman with extremely long breasts who is chased every night by Kong Volmer.

long_description.id: Slattenpatten atau slattenlangpat (harfiah "payudara kendur" atau "payudara panjang yang melorot") adalah makhluk perempuan dalam cerita rakyat Denmark, terutama dikaitkan dengan Suså. Ia juga disebut ellekvinde atau ellekone (perempuan elf), tetapi berbeda dari ellepige yang biasanya digambarkan sangat cantik, ia dicirikan oleh payudara yang amat panjang.
long_description.en: Danish folk tradition, especially around Suså, tells of Slattenpatten or slattenlangpat, a female being whose name means roughly 'flabby breasts' or 'long sagging breast'. She is also called ellekvinde or ellekone (elf-woman), but unlike the ellepige, usually described as very beautiful, she is marked by extraordinarily long breasts.

long_description.id: Payudaranya menjuntai sampai ke pinggang, tetapi dapat dilempar ke atas bahu agar anak yang digendong di punggung bisa menyusu; saat dikejar, ia melempar payudaranya ke bahu agar tidak menghalangi larinya. Di Sjælland selatan ada sejumlah legenda tentang ia yang diburu "Kong Volmer" (sebenarnya Valdemar Atterdag) atau "Wojens Jæger" dengan anjing-anjingnya; menurut legenda, Kong Volmer menembaknya setiap malam, tetapi ia kembali keesokan paginya.
long_description.en: Her breasts hang down to the waist, but can be thrown over the shoulder so a child carried on her back can feed; when chased she flings them over her shoulders so they do not hinder her running. In southern Zealand several legends tell of her being hunted by 'Kong Volmer' (really Valdemar Atterdag) or 'Wojens Jæger' with his hounds; by legend Kong Volmer shot her every night, yet she came back the next morning.

long_description.id: Slattenpatten mencuri dari manusia di malam hari, tetapi tak bisa mencuri roti yang digoresi tanda salib. Orang yang dikejarnya bisa lolos dengan berlari menyeberangi alur bajak, karena ia hanya dapat berlari searah alur yang dibajak dengan bajak baja, atau dengan melompati air mengalir. Menurut legenda lain, payudaranya panjang agar ia dapat menyusui anak-anak ikannya di dalam air, sehingga ia juga dikaitkan dengan air dan dianggap dewi air, khususnya di Sjælland menurut sebagian arkeolog.
long_description.en: Slattenpatten steals from people at night, but cannot take bread scored with a cross. Someone she pursues can escape by running across the plough furrows, since she can only run along furrows ploughed with a steel plough, or by jumping over running water. Another legend says her breasts were long so she could suckle her fish-children under water, so she is also linked with water and seen as a water goddess, particularly in Zealand according to some archaeologists.

claims.statement_id: Slattenpatten atau Slattenlangpat adalah makhluk perempuan dalam kepercayaan rakyat Denmark, terutama dikaitkan dengan Suså; ia juga disebut ellekvinde, ellekone, atau elverkone, dan berbeda dari ellepige yang biasanya sangat cantik, ia dicirikan payudara yang amat panjang.
claims.quote: Slattenpatten eller Slattenlangpat er et kvindeligt væsen i dansk folketro, især knyttet til Suså. Væsnet betegnes også som en ellekvinde, ellekone eller elverkone. I modsætning til en ellepige, der i reglen beskrives som meget smuk, er Slattenpatten karakteriseret ved at have overordentligt lange bryster.

claims.statement: Her breasts hang down to the waist but can be thrown over the shoulder so a child on her back can feed, and when chased she flings them over her shoulders; in southern Zealand legends tell of her being hunted by 'Kong Volmer' (really Valdemar Atterdag) or 'Wojens Jæger' with hounds.
claims.statement_id: Payudaranya menjuntai sampai ke pinggang tetapi dapat dilempar ke bahu agar anak di punggung dapat menyusu, dan saat dikejar ia melempar payudara ke bahunya; di Sjælland selatan ada sejumlah legenda ia diburu "Kong Volmer" (sebenarnya Valdemar Atterdag) atau "Wojens Jæger" dengan anjing-anjingnya.
claims.quote: Brysterne hænger "helt ned til bæltestedet", men de kan kastes op over skulderen, således at et barn kan die, selvom det bæres på ryggen. I situationer, hvor Slattenpatten jages, slænger hun blot brysterne over skuldrene ... På Sydsjælland findes en række sagn, hvor Slattenpatten jages af "Kong Volmer" (egentlig Valdemar Atterdag) eller "Wojens Jæger" med sine hunde.

claims.statement: Slattenpatten steals from people at night, but cannot steal bread scored with a cross; those she pursues can escape by running across plough furrows, since she can only run along furrows cut with a steel plough, or by jumping over running water.
claims.statement_id: Slattenpatten mencuri dari manusia di malam hari, tetapi tak bisa mencuri roti yang digoresi salib; orang yang dikejarnya bisa lolos dengan berlari menyeberangi alur bajak, karena ia hanya bisa berlari searah alur yang dibajak dengan bajak baja, atau dengan melompati air mengalir.
claims.quote: Slattenpatten røver fra menneskene om natten. Men ridses et kors i ens brød og bagværk, kan hun ikke stjæle det. Følger hun efter én, kan man undslippe hende ved at løbe ud over markerne og tværs over plovfurerne, for hun kan kun løbe langs med furerne, når de er pløjet med stålplov. ... Man kan også hoppe over rindende vand

claims.statement: Another legend says her breasts were long so she could suckle her fish-children under water; slattenlangpat is therefore also linked with water and considered a water goddess, especially in Zealand according to some archaeologists.
claims.statement_id: Legenda lain menyebut payudaranya panjang agar ia bisa menyusui anak-anak ikannya di bawah air; karena itu slattenlangpat juga dikaitkan dengan air dan dianggap dewi air, khususnya di Sjælland menurut sebagian arkeolog.
claims.quote: Another legend tells us that her breasts were so long so that she could breastfeed her fish-children under the water. Slattenlangpat is therefore also associated with water and considered a water goddess, in particular according to certain archaeologists, in the Danish region of Zealand.

claims.statement: In the 2010 renovation of Axeltorv in Næstved, the old fountain was replaced by a statue of Slattenpatten by Bjørn Nørgaard.
claims.statement_id: Dalam renovasi Axeltorv di Næstved pada 2010, air mancur lama diganti patung Slattenpatten karya Bjørn Nørgaard.
claims.quote: I forbindelse med renovering af Axeltorv i Næstved blev det hidtidige springvand i 2010 erstattet af en statue af Slattenpatten, udført af Bjørn Nørgaard.

long_description.en: Slattenpatten or slattenlangpat (literally “flaccid-breasts” or “saggy-long-breast”, is a female creature in Danish folklore. The beast is also referred to as an “ellekone” (elf-woman), but unlike an “ellepige” (elf-girls or wood nymphs), which are generally described as very beautiful, Slattenpatten is characterized by having extremely long breasts. Similar to the dangerous "ellepiger" who stole the souls of men by way of their sheer beauty, "slattenlangpat" also was a haunting woman. The legend goes that Kong Volmer chased and shot her every night, only to see her return the next morning The breasts hang "all the way to the knee area", and they can be thrown over the shoulder so a child can feed, even if it's carried on her back. In situations where Slattenpatten is chased, she simply throws her breasts over her shoulders so they are not in the way when she has to run The legendary figure slattenlangpat is supposed to have symbolized fertility, her long breasts bearing evidence to all the children she had given birth to and nourished. Another legend tells us that her breasts were so long so that she could breastfeed her fish-children under the water. Slattenlangpat is therefore also associated with water and considered a water goddess, in particular according to certain archaeologists, in the Danish region of Zealand.

short_description.id: Fairy Queen atau Ratu Peri adalah penguasa perempuan para peri dalam cerita rakyat dan sastra, kadang berpasangan dengan raja; Titania dan Mab adalah nama yang sering dipakai.
short_description.en: In folk tradition and in literature the Fairy Queen, or Queen of the Fairies, rules over the fairies, sometimes alongside a king; Titania and Mab are common names.

long_description.id: Dalam cerita rakyat dan sastra, Fairy Queen atau Queen of the Fairies adalah penguasa perempuan para peri, kadang tetapi tidak selalu berpasangan dengan seorang raja. Tergantung karyanya, ia bisa bernama atau tanpa nama; Titania dan Mab adalah dua nama yang sering dipakai. Tuatha Dé Danann dan Daoine Sidhe dalam mitologi Irlandia (Irish) memiliki banyak raja dan ratu setempat; Oonagh (Una, Nuala) adalah istri Finvarra, raja peri Irlandia (Ireland) barat. Ratu peri Irlandia lainnya termasuk Clíodhna dari Munster, Aibhell, dan Ainé.
long_description.en: Folk tradition and literature know a Fairy Queen, also called Queen of the Fairies, a woman ruling over the fairies, at times though not always beside a king. Some works name her and some do not; Titania and Mab are two names used often. The Tuatha Dé Danann and Daoine Sidhe of Irish myth had many local kings and queens; Oonagh (Una, Nuala) was wife of Finvarra, fairy king of the west of Ireland. Other Irish fairy queens include Clíodhna of Munster, Aibhell and Ainé.

long_description.id: Tokoh Arthurian Morgan le Fey memerintah pulau gaib Avalon dan kadang digambarkan sebagai ratu peri; dalam Vita Merlini ia Morgen, kepala sembilan ratu bersaudara yang sakti. Ratu peri muncul dalam beberapa Child Ballads: yang baik hati dalam Alison Gross, dan yang kejam dalam Tam Lin, yang membayar upeti kepada Neraka setiap tujuh tahun. Dalam Thomas the Rhymer, ratu peri tanpa nama menjadikan Thomas kekasihnya dan meninggalkannya dengan kemampuan bernubuat. Menurut artikel es, Child Ballads adalah kumpulan 305 balada rakyat dari Inggris (Inglaterra) dan Skotlandia (Escocia) yang dihimpun Francis James Child.
long_description.en: The Arthurian Morgan le Fey ruled the otherworldly island of Avalon and was at times shown as a fairy queen; in the Vita Merlini she is Morgen, head of nine magical sister queens. Fairy queens appear in some Child Ballads: a kindly one in Alison Gross and a cruel one in Tam Lin, who pays a tithe to Hell every seven years. In Thomas the Rhymer an unnamed fairy queen takes Thomas as her lover and leaves him able to prophesy. According to the es article the Child Ballads are a set of 305 folk ballads from England (Inglaterra) and Scotland (Escocia) gathered by Francis James Child.

short_description.id: Brown Lady of Raynham Hall adalah hantu yang konon menghantui Raynham Hall di Norfolk, Inggris, dan menjadi terkenal lewat foto majalah Country Life tahun 1936.
short_description.en: The Brown Lady of Raynham Hall is a ghost said to haunt Raynham Hall in Norfolk, England, made famous by a 1936 Country Life photograph.

long_description.id: Brown Lady of Raynham Hall adalah hantu yang konon menghantui Raynham Hall di Norfolk, Inggris (England). Ia menjadi salah satu kisah hantu paling terkenal di Britania Raya (United Kingdom) setelah fotografer majalah Country Life mengaku memotretnya. Julukan "Brown Lady" berasal dari gaun brokat cokelat yang konon dikenakannya. Menurut legenda, penampakan itu adalah Dorothy Walpole (1686–1726), saudari Robert Walpole, yang umumnya dianggap Perdana Menteri pertama Britania Raya; ia istri kedua Charles Townshend, yang konon mengurungnya di kamar di Raynham Hall setelah mengetahui perselingkuhannya dengan Lord Wharton.
long_description.en: The Brown Lady of Raynham Hall is a ghost reputed to haunt Raynham Hall in Norfolk, England. It grew into one of the best-known hauntings in the United Kingdom after Country Life photographers said they had caught it on film. She takes her name from the brown brocade gown she is said to wear. Legend holds she is Dorothy Walpole (1686–1726), sister of Robert Walpole, who is usually counted Great Britain's first Prime Minister; Charles Townshend, whose second wife she was, reportedly locked her in her rooms at Raynham Hall on learning of her affair with Lord Wharton.

long_description.id: Penampakan pertama yang tercatat dilaporkan Lucia C. Stone tentang perayaan Natal 1835 di Raynham Hall: Kolonel Loftus dan seorang tamu bernama Hawkins mengaku melihatnya, dan malam berikutnya Loftus melihat rongga matanya yang kosong. Pada 1836 Kapten Frederick Marryat, sahabat Charles Dickens, juga dikatakan melihatnya. Menurut artikel de, tidak ada bukti keaslian foto 1936 maupun penampakan lainnya, dan para ilmuwan skeptis masa kini, termasuk Joe Nickell, berpendapat foto itu dipalsukan, mungkin dengan pencahayaan ganda.
long_description.en: The first recorded sighting was reported by Lucia C. Stone of a Christmas party at Raynham Hall in 1835: Colonel Loftus and a guest named Hawkins said they saw her, and the next night Loftus noticed her empty eye sockets. In 1836 Captain Frederick Marryat, a friend of Charles Dickens, is also said to have seen her. According to the de article there is no proof that the 1936 photo or other sightings are genuine, and modern sceptics including Joe Nickell think the picture was faked, perhaps by double exposure.

claims.quote: The Brown Lady of Raynham Hall is a ghost that reportedly haunts Raynham Hall in Norfolk, England. It became one of the most famous hauntings in the United Kingdom when photographers from Country Life magazine claimed to have captured its image. The "Brown Lady" is so named because of the brown brocade dress it is claimed she wears.

claims.quote: According to legend, the apparition is that of Dorothy Walpole (1686–1726), the sister of Robert Walpole, generally regarded as the first Prime Minister of Great Britain.

statement.en: Legend says the ghost is Dorothy Walpole (1686–1726), sister of Robert Walpole, first Prime Minister of Great Britain.

claims.quote: The story says that when Townshend discovered that his wife had committed adultery with Lord Wharton, he punished her by locking her in her rooms in the family home, Raynham Hall.

statement.id: Charles Townshend mengurungnya di Raynham Hall karena berselingkuh dengan Lord Wharton.
statement.en: Charles Townshend locked her in Raynham Hall for adultery with Lord Wharton.

claims.quote: Loftus and another guest named Hawkins said they had seen the "Brown Lady" one night as they approached their bedrooms, noting in particular the dated brown dress she wore.
